reviews.title: Beautiful Interface - Updated Review
reviews.comment:
I left a 2 taco review for over branding. But...

This was  an issue with my site being cached and still showing the original SkillPlate branding. SkillPlate resolved the caching issue and now I have a beautifully laid out course app - nice surprise.

With the minimal branding in the footer, we are all in now and I have to give a full 5 tacos. 

Excellent support and thank you for getting this sorted.

children.comment:
I am really sorry you feel that way. But you have to understand this is a lifetime campaign with a 92% discount. If you really use the app we will lose money over time. So if we do not get at least 1 customer from referrals the whole campaign doesn't work. That branding pays for the app being so cheap. It makes it possible to make such an incredible lifetime deal possible. Otherwise it is mathematically impossible to provide so much value for $60 (Tier 3 Price - the Appsumo fee). You get lifetime hosting, video streaming, website builder, AI, email marketing, free API usage and a ton of other tools. The cost of this is real. Even if you don't use your account at all.
To be fair there is no page where you can see 5 skillplate logos. The maximum you can see is a logo in the player and a powered by skillplate link in the footer. 
We had promised to provide white-label at $999. (Remember this is not just a small tool but an all-in-one platform that includes a big number of apps that you would otherwise have to pay a monthly fee for. And you can't vibe code them because they have real costs involved.) 
We finally finally figured out a way to provide the white-label at the lowest price possible in order to make sure the platform will not go bankrupt from this deal. This is the absolute maximum we can give. 
I would give more but the math doesn't allow it.
Every action we have taken up to this point backs that statement completely. Everything that can be free is free. The "powered by Skillplate" We even pays you a 30% commission for the referral. Indefinitely. So you can get more than the app and the white-label from 1 referral.
On the other hand, absolutely any business that has customers and really needs a white-label can afford to pay $299 to hide the platform they are using if they need to. Most don't need to do that.
We have taken your feedback, discussed it and even took action on it. 
We also have to be fair that about calling this over branding. If a small link in the footer is over-branding what is minimal branding? The only 2 places where users can see Skillplate is the video player (which you can change if you want) and the link in the footer. On most pages it is really just a link in the footer. So if that is over-branding what is minimal branding? Remember this link basically pays for the 92% discount and if we get 1 customer from it we will even pay you more than you paid us. 

I fully understand that you think it should be cheaper. But it just cannot be because the business model mathematics do not allow it. If they did it would have been cheaper I swear it.

reviews.title: Caution : Communities are to be hosted externally on Discord
reviews.comment:
Wanted to start a community (à la Skool) and maybe start selling courses afterwards. My #1 reason for getting this deal was unlimited communities.

I got the Tier5 deal with the no commission add-on and the white label (not refundable) option.

Now, the interface is really good and I'm sure the platform is fine, but just when starting to explore the platform, I created one test community, it brought be to a button that forwards me to Discord. I thought I missed something... but I didn't, it seems. Communities, as of now, are only on Discord.

When coming back here to look at reviews/questions, I noticed that people talked about this before, the founder explained the reasons they went that way at first and that they are also developing internal communities. It's on the roadmap. Still, I we have no idea when that will be live and it could years in the future, who knows. At that time, I would be out of my refund window.

This little fact was a deal breaker for me and I refunded, but I had the "white label" for 299$ that is not refundable so that is a frustrating loss for me that I regret taking. I feel that it was not that clear in the app description that communities were only on Discord at the moment. I'm not sure why I would pay that much when I could just start a Discord server by myself. I don't understand who would want to have a community type platform and host the community on another one requiring another login. It's a head scratcher to me.

Still, I believe the platform seems awesome in many other ways and I'm sure course makers will get very good value out of it. The founder seems great. I still feel like the Discord communities part should be made a lot clearer. That confusion just cost me 299$.

children.comment:
Yes you are correct. Communities use Discord right now. And again as I have said many times Discord is a much better community and communication platform. The reason is people use it a LOT MORE. Not 1 or 2 times more ... 20 times more than Skool. That is why it is worth more than all the rest of the course and community platforms combined. 

We will make an internal a la Skool type community quite soon but it will never be better than discord objectively. You will be able to have your branded members area with all the community features like Skool and hope people will come to your website to be a part of the community and lose money in the process until you realize that people actually communicating in the community is where the value is. 

When we finish the AI website builder in the next 1-2 weeks we will begin work on the next projects.
(New roadmap video coming up in the following days) Go to youtube and search for it on the skillplate channel.

You will get an email to be notified when the new features are released (even though you refunded) so if you don't unsubscribe from that list you will see when the community feature is released.
If you decide to come back we will honor your whitelabel purchase and you won't need to buy it again.

reviews.title: A promising tool, userfriendly and easy to integrate
reviews.comment:
I had been using a German course platform for the past eight years. Over time, more features were added—but the price went up significantly.
Initially, I was simply curious and wanted to explore alternatives for some smaller offers. Skillplate immediately caught my attention. After watching a YouTube tutorial and setting it up for my business, I was genuinely impressed. Just to keep in mind, I am not a technical person, and often I fail during the set-up process…
Skillplate is intuitive, easy to use, and straightforward to connect with the tools I need. The setup process was smooth, and it already offers everything I need to create and manage new offers and ideas, without unnecessary complexity.
Most importantly, Skillplate feels like a tool I can grow with. It has a lot of potential for expanding my small business in the future, while remaining simple and practical today. Especially when I am testing new, small offers, I do not need all the bells and whistles. I am more than satisfied with my decision and look forward to continuing to build with Skillplate.

children.comment: Thank you! You nailed the core value really well :) Everyone should be able to set it up. And do it fast so they can focus on selling not on setup.

questions.title: I’m considering Skillplate for a multi-year Tai Chi school.
questions.comment: I need: (1) Drip to advance only during active paid membership. If someone receives Months 1–3, cancels for 6 months, then rejoins, they must resume at Month 3/4—not unlock Months 4–9 because time elapsed. Does cancellation pause the drip clock and rejoining resume it? What happens after failed payments? (2) Free courses, subscription Core Training and separately sold standalone courses, with different memberships granting different course combinations and manual access control. (3) Can permissions differ for modules/lessons within one course?

children.comment:
Currently the drip feature works like a standard drip. Meaning if your course starts on September 5th and the next lesson is sep 12 and then sep 17 you can do that. It works as if you are doing things live.
The feature you are asking for is cool but we do not have it.
There are workarounds that you can do to unlock different products with each month's subciption payment with a simple automation with the API. Some creators do it already and it works quite well.
This way with each payment people get something new and this keeps them hooked.

Free courses yes - just make a free plan.
Granting different sets of products with different subscription plans also yes - just make a bundle for each plan and add to the bundle whatever you want to give access to.

on your third question I am not sure what you are asking exactly but you cannot grant access to a modules separately that would be a different product.

questions.title: Will the core infrastructure features promised in the Feb. 2026 roadmap actually be delivered by the end of 2026?
questions.comment:
Hello Skillplate team,

I bought the Skillplate LTD on AppSumo in Nov 2025. I cannot launch my product yet because core features (Community, Product Types, Calendar) promised for 2026 are still missing. Comparing the Feb and Sep 2026 roadmap videos, these are still listed as future projects. Aside from AI, there is hardly any tangible development. 

Overlapping promises in the roadmap videos: 
1. Checkout 2.0
2. Members Area 2.0
3. New product types
4. Affiliate Tracking. 

Critical question: Can you confirm these features will be delivered by the end of 2026, as communicated in the early 2026 roadmap? Or will we see another video in 8 months presenting these same features as future projects again? I need transparency. 

Thanks!
Melanie

References: 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBPJ3OVjLSM 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uhM76SU823Y

children.comment:
Hello, Melanie, I first want to clarify that our roadmap is not a promise. It is our intention on what we plan to do next, there is no guarantee that we will succeed in completing it by the end of 2026.

Now that said in order to build those features and have the ability to read and control them with AI a lot of invisible infrastructure had to be built so we can later give the AI superpowers that will really give you a competitive advantage.
Now that we have the AI infrastructure the first AI superpower coming in is the AI website builder which allows you to do landing pages and funnels with AI with insane quality and speed. It is in testing phase coming in a week or 2.

The affiliate tracking is ready and will come in the same update.

Some of the checkout features are coming immediately after - Order bumps, thank you pages, 1 click upsells. They are already in development.

The members area 2.0 we will not be able to complete before the end of 2026 for sure.

And right after the checkout features new product types and email marketing features are coming next. These are also already in development.

I hope this clarifies the situation. 
We are doing our best to push everything out but it is not simple and has a lot of dependencies and we are also trying to totally reinvent how some of these things will work for the AI era.

questions.title: Own payment providers?
questions.comment: Can I integrate my own payment providers such as PayPal or others to avoid the Skillplate commission fee?

children.comment:
Hello and thanks for the question.
You can use external payment providers.
All you need to do is to set your landing page buttons in the website builder to send people to your external checkout links. 
Then you need an automation with zapier or n8n to catch the webhook your payment provider sends with the payment information. And then you use that and the Skillplate API to register the user and give them access.
You can find the skillplate API here : https://skillplate.com/docs/api
And you can give it to any ai agent and it will tell you how to do the automation.

But keep in mind most payment processors are more expensive than Skillplate and it is extremely likely you will be better off just getting the 0% commission addon.

Using external payment providers is a hassle, it is costly, and you lose critical tracking information that can be used by the skillplate Overmind AI agent to help you grow your business later.
Skillplate analytics and our 24/7 AI agent growth mode are coming soon. So this data will become very relevant very soon.

questions.title: Can Skillplate integrate with a Bangladesh payment gateway such as SSLCOMMERZ?
questions.comment: I’m based in Bangladesh and want to sell courses locally. Can Skillplate integrate with a Bangladesh payment gateway such as SSLCOMMERZ, bKash, or Nagad through API/webhooks? If yes, can a successful payment automatically create/enroll the student in the correct course, and are there any Skillplate fees, limitations, or required third-party tools?

children.comment:
Yes you can use any external payment provider.
You use the website builder. Set the buy buttons to send to the external checkout.
Then use the webhook from the payment provider and the Skillplate API https://skillplate.com/docs/api to register the user.
You can give both api's to any ai and it will tell you how to set it up.

reviews.title: I have used it for over a year. Here is my honest review
reviews.comment: I highly appreciate the team behind this software. They have created an innovative meeting environment and constantly update their software. Most importantly, their customer support is outstanding. Every time I report a software issue or a bug, they respond and take full responsibility for resolving it. If you are looking for a stable, long-term meeting tool with excellent customer support, I highly recommend using it.

reviews.title: Works well, active dev team!
reviews.comment:
My use of GoBrunch is for hosting live chats with various members of my own development team. It allows me to invite strangers to sit in a room that feels like a comfortable business lounge versus inviting them to a platform like Google Meets. There is a clear distinction between people on the stage and people who are listening in the audience. I think if I did this via Google Meets, fewer people would show up because it would feel as though they are more involved with the call than they really are, or that they are comfortable being. So that is the use case for me.

Initial setup did take some onboarding, but thankfully, this team has a lot of content around helping you craft the perfect space for what you need it to be. The setup wizard for each room could probably be more polished, but it works as is once you've spent some time clicking through all the buttons to learn how each can affect the space you're trying to build. It's not exactly Photoshop-level complexity, so I believe an hour or two of messing around with the settings while trying to create your space would do the trick.

I spent some time looking over their content, which showcases other creators and the unique and interesting ways they are utilizing this platform to form the space that they want. By doing so, it gives me a little bit of an idea and context on how I can grow my own if I choose to go that route. Some of the community members seem to really go all in to a level that I am not comfortable spending my time. So, I believe my use of this software is pretty basic, but it serves the use case that I need it for, and I do not regret buying into this project.

I highly recommend it for individuals that work with online crowds or anyone trying to build a community with a tool that adds a sense of presence to the entire experience without making the participants feel pressured or uncomfortable while being at an event because you can design your spaces in a way that makes it appropriate for each social interaction.

reviews.title: Fun alternative to Zoom squares
reviews.comment: Honestly the thing that appealed to me most about GoBrunch was the fact that it doesn't look like a traditional "online meeting room," and in that, it does not disappoint! I love that I can change the backgrounds and that every face (or avatar) is visible. I also like the way meeting rooms can be kept open and the links reused. It makes sharing meeting info a lot easier to prep in advance! Add in unlimited recording space and no meeting time limits, and getting GoBrunch is a decision that I would make again and again.

reviews.title: A Must-Buy, Fresh Concept, But Latency, Recording, and a Few Other Issues
reviews.comment:
I absolutely love GoBrunch 😊 My usecase is a fun meeting space for my community's monthly meetups, and I used it for two recorded courses, but that didn't go well (will explain more below). The concept is great, it's easy to use, the permissions features are granular, and branding options and customization are amazing. The concept itself is really fresh and fun, and makes me feel like I'm actually meeting with my community members, rather than get "Zoom fatigue" from another video meet with big boxes. ❤️

There are a few big issues for me though:
- Latency and freezing audio and video are an issue in sessions. Myself and attendees get dropped from rooms sometimes

- Using a locked room is not a fun experience. I love the knocking sound and notification, but if you miss the device dialogue box that pops up in your system tray (PC) to let an attendee in a room, it's gone forever until they try again, for some reason. I seriously cannot find an "admit" button in the actual GoBrunch meeting room itself; it just shows a message someone is trying to get in in the chat. Really annoying. I switched it to public or use an access code as a workaround. They need to add a clear, *on screen* button that admits people to the room if using the approval workflow, not just the system alert

- For scheduled GoBrunch rooms, you can't edit details about a meeting if it's too close to start time, or already started, so I only use the perpetual meeting room, just in case

- Recording quality and ease of use is terrible; the dialogue box that pops in Chrome for permissions won't got away, and since it's embedded in the Chrome UI, it warps the aspect ratio of the recording, so it makes my head look like a hotdog 😂 If you do record, there's isn't a clean, easy way to keep your aspect ratio and present things like slides or share your screen. It will mess up the recording beyond saving, again, because it warps the aspect ratio and squishes everything. So, I can't use this for classes or recording like I'd planned and tried. I have to redo the live classes with attendees that I've already recorded in another video meeting solution, because GoBrunch's recordings are unusable

- Trying to use the screenshare function in Chrome will mess up your session, so don't plan on using the screenshare function with GoBrunch. It will put in a permissions dialogue box that will persist until you close the tab or window, even if you stop screensharing. It's really annoying, and removes visible space/warps the aspect ratio of the GoBrunch room

They are a MVP for sure, but I hope they fix these issues! Again, concept, ease of use for the most part, and customization are fantastic. Fresh concept I haven't seen anywhere else. But my user experience has has some challenges.

reviews.title: All in all great, but I miss 1 feature
reviews.comment: I loved gobrunch. But it misses a really easy, yet profound feature: Meeting participants cannot react with emojis to posts in the chat. Therefore, my community is not using it at all, and we went back to Zoom. If that feature ever came. I would love to come back..

questions.title: 100 Active Community Members Limit (even if not actually active)
questions.comment:
Hi,
I'm somewhat confused by the limit on active community members at 100. 
Do I understand correctly that if a community member posts or comments once, and never does again, they are counted towards the 100 active community members, and this never resets?
So in other words, once any member has posted or commented, that is counted towards the 100, and after 100 is reached, the community cannot have more posts or comments from members (tother than this 100)?
If what I have said is correct, this is an odd limit  It is making this a very hard deal to buy. What is the way out of it, other than manually banning / removing community members? A new subscription? 
Thanks.

children.comment:
Hello Mike,

Thank you for writing in.

Yes, that is correct. The first 100 members to post or reply to comments become the active members, and they are still counted towards the total active members even when they are not posting; it does not reset. 

When one of the 100 users is banned or removed from the community, the first person to make a post or comment automatically replaces the banned member. Others above 100 will only be able to react to posts and comments.

The only way out would be to ban or remove members or purchase the unlimited plan, which comes with unlimited active community members. 

Kind regards,

Thanks for replying. Can I ask what is the purpose of this limit? It is an unusual limit. 

Why not allow 100 active users within a month. Keeps resources low, puts the deal in line with AppSumo standards, without appearing just to make the lifetime deal of limited use. 

Or is the idea to encourage lifetime users not to use the community side? If so, can other communities be connected?

questions.title: Purchasing Questions
questions.comment:
The 9 Course Limit: I am looking at buying 3 codes on AppSumo for $297. To confirm, does this strictly cap my entire account at 9 courses total across the 3 websites, or is it 9 courses per website? Community Active Users: Regarding the 100 active user limit on the community feature if I reach 100 users who have commented, does it automatically lock out the 101st user from commenting, or does the limit reset monthly? Can I delete inactive users to free up spots?
I understand Stripe works for recurring monthly subscriptions. Is there any timeline on the roadmap to support PayPal for recurring subscriptions, or is it strictly limited to one-time purchases permanently? If I buy the lifetime deal but decide later I don't want to use external video hosting, what is the exact cost to add native video hosting to my lifetime account?

children.comment:
Hello there, 

Thank you for writing in. Below are the answers to your questions:

1. It depends. 3 codes give you access to 3 courses per website (3 websites), but if you redeem all the codes on one website, you get 9 courses on 1 website. 

2. Yes, it stops users above 100 from commenting or making posts, and it does not reset per month. When one of the 100 users is banned or removed from the community, the first person to make a post or comment automatically replaces the banned member. Others above 100 will only be able to react to posts and comments. 

3. Yes, you can remove inactive users or ban them if it is a paid or invite-only community, but for a free community, you can only ban users. 

4. No, there is no timeline for this. PayPal is strictly for one-time purchases, while Stripe is for both one-time payments and subscriptions. 

5. Native video hosting is available for lifetime deals. You will have to upgrade to one of our subscription-based plans at a discount to upload videos. 

Kind regards,

questions.title: Community users not unlimited?
questions.comment:
Hi,

When I first bought OnlineCourseHost I didn't know that the number of active community members is limited to 100 or so. Now months later on my community page, I see a new panel displaying how many community users I can have: only up to 100. Is there a way to redeem the unlimited community users feature?

children.comment: How does this work? How does the system track the number of active members at a time and what do members see when that limit is reached and how do we curate which members are given active membership and which ones are not? How do we monitor this and all?

Hello Joyful, 

Thank you for writing in.

The number of active community members has always been capped at 100 for the PRO and AppSumo plans.

Under the community, you can have unlimited members, but under your plan, you can only have 100 active members. This number is determined by the first 100 members to comment, post, or react to posts. The other members will be passive - they will only be able to react to posts; they won't be able to comment or make posts.

Members will not see this on their end, but you, as the course creator, will get a tag underneath the right panel like this, so that you can monitor it: https://prnt.sc/H0KZYtxzACLd

When the number is filled up, other members become passive members. When one of the 100 leaves the community or is banned, the first member to make a post or comment becomes active in their stead.

Unfortunately, you cannot decide on the active members. It just depends on who posts and comments first, until the available slot is filled. And when the slot is filled, your community will remain active, so no issues with that.

Kind regards,

questions.title: Revoke Button and Waiver of Withdrawal Period
questions.comment:
The EU regulation or regulatory framework grants every buyer a 14-day right of withdrawal, which also generally applies, for example, to download products - unless the customer is explicitly informed about the waiver of the right of withdrawal and must confirm this, for example, by checking a box. Does Forento offer the possibility to implement such waiver declarations on the customer's part?

Second thing: Since this year, product providers must offer a simple revoke/withdrawal button on their website that allows buyers to withdraw from products for which they have a right of withdrawal. Again, the question: Does Forento provide the possibility of such a withdrawal button?

children.comment:
Hi cameyer,

Thanks for your question. Forento supports both.

1. Waiving the right of withdrawal

Forento has a built-in withdrawal function that you can turn on under Settings → Legal in your dashboard. Once it's on, buyers of courses, videos, downloadable products, and digital-only bundles see a checkbox at checkout. It isn't ticked by default, and the purchase can't be completed until the buyer ticks it. By ticking it, the buyer:

- asks for the content to be made available immediately, during the withdrawal period, and
- confirms that they lose their right of withdrawal once the content is made available.

The text appears in your academy's set language. We store the exact wording the buyer accepted with the purchase and email the buyer a confirmation of the waiver.

Event bookings for a specific date are already exempt from the right of withdrawal, so they don't need a waiver. Memberships and 1:1 sessions keep the full 14-day right of withdrawal.

2. Withdrawal button

The same setting also turns on the withdrawal button required since 19 June 2026. Students see a "Withdraw from contract here" button on their billing page for every purchase still inside its withdrawal period, along with the deadline. A notice with the button also appears on their dashboard. When a student withdraws, they automatically get an acknowledgement by email.

You'll see every withdrawal you receive in the same settings section. From there, you can refund it through Stripe or PayPal with one click, or mark it as handled if you settled it another way.

Please note that the function is off by default, so you'll need to turn it on yourself. We also recommend having your legal advisor review the wording before you do, since we can't give legal advice.

Feel free to reach out through the live chat on our website if you have any other questions or concerns. We're happy to help.

/Adrian at Forento

That's great! Most platforms do offer good features but pay little attention to legal requirements. It's fantastic that Forento takes care of implementing current legal regulations! Just bought Tier 6 👍

questions.title: Yelp, Thumbtack, Homeadvisor, Angies
questions.comment:
The tool does seem to be outdated; general contractors/businesses have moved to these platforms, and those platforms have people who are willing to spend on their marketing. 

Are there any plans to add support for these?

children.comment:
A few of these have gone in and out of LocalScraper over the years. We had HomeAdvisor in the past and then they redesigned their website and removed ALL business details except for a few paid results. Making their data completely useless and inaccessible. HomeAdvisor only makes money if you hire a contractor through their leads funnel. They have done everything possible to remove any business data not in this paid funnel to keep you from getting any useful details to contact them. 

Another issue is that these sites Yelp and HomeAdvisor have paid for very high levels of anti-scraper/bot protections. This requires the use of paying for advanced proxy services which many customers are not familiar with and don't want to pay for. The program supported these services and the ReadMe page told customers which ones to use but it was hard explaining to customers while some scrapers can work easy out of the box with no extra costs, not all of them could. One easy solution is that Yahoo Local uses data from Yelp and TripAdvisor so if you wanted Yelp data you can use Yahoo Local as your target and get the same data. 

I am of course always looking at adding and removing sites as things change, the data scraping world is very dynamic and I try to always provide the best product I can to customers through these changes.

reviews.title: Community, courses and real-time chat in one place
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What I like about EzyCommunity is that it doesn't make the community feel like an extra feature attached to a course platform. The community itself is at the center, with a feed for posts and discussions alongside real-time chat that feels more like Slack or Discord.

From there, you can add courses, events, paid channels, memberships and gamification without sending members through a collection of different tools. I can see that being especially useful for someone running a coaching program, membership or paid community where the course content is only one part of why people joined.

I liked the chat experience during testing. Members can move between community discussions, channels and direct conversations, while points, badges and leaderboards give them another reason to participate. For me this is one of the big differentiators of the platform because getting people to participate reularly is one of the hardest things of running an online community. 

Courses are inside the same environment, so someone can go from a lesson to a conversation with the rest of the community without leaving the platform.

Members can also use EzyCommunity through its iOS and Android apps, which is useful for a community where you want people checking in regularly rather than only when they are sitting at a computer. A fully branded app under your own name is available separately.

You can monetize different parts of the community too. Channels and courses can be restricted or paid, and EzyCommunity takes 0% of your sales, outside of the normal payment processor fees. This becomes more valuable as a paid community grows. And most other platforms take a % commission so this is a good value proposition from EzyCommunity.

There were still some unfinished areas when I first tested it. Course certificates were marked as coming soon at the time, but the team completed them and I verified that they had been added.

Email marketing is the one area I would still check before buying if it is important to you. During my original test, the Marketing section was not yet available even though email marketing was advertised as included. The team said it was close to completion. The current pricing still lists monthly marketing email allowances, while another part of the current website continues to describe email campaigns as coming soon, so I would confirm exactly what is available today.

Overall, I think EzyCommunity works particularly well when the course, community and conversation need to feel like one product rather than three separate services stitched together. For a membership where people are there as much for each other as they are for the content, that combination makes all the difference.

questions.title: Is this use case valid?

children.comment:
Yes, this is a valid use case for Twidget

The workflow would look like this:

1. Use AI or an automation to collect discounted items and populate your Google Sheet.
2. Connect Twidget to Google Sheets and create an API that returns those items, with filters such as shop or category.
3. List your Twidget API on RapidAPI and configure paid access plans. RapidAPI supports listing and monetizing APIs.

Twidget would host and run your API, while RapidAPI would provide the marketplace and subscription billing.

reviews.comment:
This app excels at generating PDFs and images from various sources, such as markup or HTML, and now also supports creating PDFs from widely used office formats (e.g., Google Docs or Sheets).  

With its API-driven functionality, it’s a must-have tool for anyone automating processes via Make.com. One standout feature is the precise control over the final appearance of the PDF. questions.title: can it automate generate pdf report with dynamic content?
questions.comment:
Hi, may I check if MarkupGo can support this online quiz workflow?

Can MarkupGo receive quiz answers as JSON data via API?
Can those answers be inserted into a saved template as dynamic content?
Can the output be generated as a PDF report?
Does the API return a hosted PDF URL that I can save and send to the user?
Is this suitable for personalised reports that may contain user-submitted information?
Are there any limitations around long text fields, multiple pages, tables, or conditional sections in the PDF?

The intended workflow is:

Online quiz 
→ capture user answers
→ send answers and results to MarkupGo via API
→ generate personalised PDF from template
→ return PDF URL
→ send PDF report link to the user

Would this be possible, and what API endpoint or documentation should I refer to for this use case?

children.comment:
Hi WinWin,

Thanks for reaching out — and yes, MarkupGo is a great fit for exactly this kind of quiz-to-PDF workflow. Here's a point-by-point answer:

Can MarkupGo receive quiz answers as JSON via API?
Yes. You send your quiz answers and results as a plain JSON object in the API request body (under source.data.context).

Can those answers be inserted into a saved template as dynamic content?
Yes. You design and save a template in the dashboard, then reference it by its template ID. We use Handlebars syntax ({{name}}, {{score}},
etc.), so any value you pass in the context object is rendered into the template at generation time.

Can the output be a PDF report?
Yes. The endpoint is:
POST https://api.markupgo.com/api/v1/pdf
Example request:
{
  "source": {
    "type": "template",
    "data": {
      "id": "YOUR_TEMPLATE_ID",
      "context": {
        "name": "John Doe",
        "score": 87,
        "answers": [ ... ]
      }
    }
  }
}
Authenticate with your API key via the x-api-key header (generate one in your dashboard).

Does the API return a hosted PDF URL?
Yes. The response is a JSON object containing a hosted CDN url you can store and send straight to your user:
{
  "id": "26a4ebd91745f1755df615ba",
  "url": "https://files.markupgo.com/tasks/.../1725057544064.pdf",
  "format": "pdf",
  "size": 1048576
}
(If you'd rather receive the raw PDF binary instead of a URL, use POST /api/v1/pdf/buffer.)

Is this suitable for personalised reports with user-submitted info?
Absolutely — personalised, per-user reports are one of the most common use cases for this exact endpoint. You can also set an expiration on
the file (anywhere from 60 seconds up to 90 days) if you'd like generated reports to auto-delete after a period.

Limitations around long text, multiple pages, tables, conditional sections?
- Long text & multiple pages: Fully supported — content flows and paginates automatically.
- Tables: Fully supported (standard HTML/CSS tables render as expected).
- Conditional sections: Supported via Handlebars helpers like {{#if}} / {{#each}}, so you can show/hide sections based on the answers you
pass in.
- There's no hard limit on page count or text length. The main thing to keep an eye on is your plan's monthly credit allowance (each PDF
generation uses 3 credits). The default API rate limit is 100 requests/minute.

Your intended workflow — Online quiz → capture answers → POST answers to MarkupGo → generate personalised PDF from template → get back the
hosted PDF URL → send to user — is fully supported end-to-end.

Documentation to refer to:
- API overview: https://markupgo.com/docs/api
- PDF endpoint (your main reference): https://markupgo.com/docs/api/pdf
- Templates: https://markupgo.com/docs/api/templates

Can the session use my Mac as a **Tailscale exit node**? How do I select it? If unsupported, can I combine `TailnetProxy` with an HTTP forward proxy running on that Mac?
My goal is to route research traffic through my own internet connection without using your residential proxy pool.

children.comment:
Thanks for the detailed report. You're right: today `TailnetProxy` only routes traffic addressed to tailnet devices, so anything public still leaves from our cloud IP. There's currently no way to pick an exit node, and `TailnetProxy` can't be combined with another proxy in the same session.

Workaround for now: run an authenticated HTTP forward proxy on your Mac, make it reachable from the internet (for example a port forward on your router), and pass it as an `ExternalProxy` instead of `TailnetProxy`. Public sites will then see your home IP, and none of our residential pool is used.

We're adding exit-node selection to `TailnetProxy` so you can name your Mac directly. When it ships, your Mac will need to be an approved exit node, and your tailnet policy will need to let `tag:notte` reach `autogroup:internet`. I will ping you once this is out
Excellent! So far I'm loving the tool. People need this tool more than they realize if they plan on doing any amount of ongoing research with their agents.  Great job.

questions.title: Is this approach incorporated?
questions.comment:
This seems to be another optimisation. Is this tactic already incorporated into Headroom?

https://medium.com/@maahisoft20/we-wasted-84-of-our-claude-tokens-the-fix-took-10-minutes-41035e87677a

children.comment:
Hi Gareth,

Thanks for the question! That article is mostly about servers that call the Claude API directly, not Claude Code sessions, so it doesn't 100% apply to Headroom. Where it does apply, it's already covered.

The tactic is prompt caching. Claude Code and Codex already do it themselves: they mark the part of each request that doesn't change (instructions, tool definitions, earlier turns), so Anthropic and OpenAI read it from cache at a big discount. Headroom compresses each part of the conversation once, then sends that same compressed version again on every later turn, so the cache keeps matching. You get the cache discount on what was already sent, plus fewer tokens on everything new like tool output, logs and file dumps. The savings Headroom shows come on top of caching, since cache reads aren't counted in them.

Let me know if you have any further questions or thoughts!

questions.title: Team plan compatibility + Anthropic ToS compliance
questions.comment:
Hi Garm, I’m on a Claude Team plan and use Claude Code with my Team seat. Your tiers only list Pro/Max. Is Team supported, and which tier would I need?

Also, Anthropic’s docs say subscription OAuth is for ordinary use of Claude Code, and third parties may not route requests through plan credentials. Since Headroom proxies Claude Code traffic and modifies requests, how does it comply?

Does any data go anywhere besides Anthropic (incl. your analytics)?
Do you change headers, client IDs or the system prompt, or only tool output?
Has Anthropic confirmed this is allowed, or have any Team/Enterprise accounts been flagged?

Thanks!

children.comment:
Thanks for the detailed questions!

Team: yes, Team seats are supported. Headroom reads your seat type when you connect Claude Code. A Standard seat matches the Pro tier, and a Premium seat matches the Max x5 or Max x20 tier, depending on its limits.

ToS: technically speaking, Headroom does not route requests through your plan credentials. Claude Code makes every request, signed in with your own seat, and Headroom never sends a prompt to Claude of its own. Headroom is a local proxy on your own machine (127.0.0.1), hooked up through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, which is the setting Claude Code documents for gateways and corporate proxies. It compresses Claude Code's requests on the way, and they go from your machine straight to Anthropic. Headroom also never logs in to Claude for you and doesn't offer Claude access. The app makes only two calls of its own with your login, and both are read-only: it reads your plan type and your usage level, to match your license. 

By designing the tool in this way, there is effectively no risk of non-compliance here. We're also not aware of any account, Team, Enterprise or otherwise, ever being flagged for using Headroom.

Data: your prompts and code never touch our servers. We receive your email, a hashed device ID, your plan type and account ID, savings counts, anonymous usage events and crash reports without content. You can turn analytics and crash reports off in Settings. Details: https://extraheadroom.com/privacy

What changes in a request:

Tool output (file reads, logs, JSON, search results) and older history get compressed.
A short instruction asking for concise replies is added to the end of the system prompt. On routine tool-result turns, the reasoning effort Claude Code asked for is lowered. HEADROOM_OUTPUT_SHAPER=0 turns both off.
One tool is added so Claude can fetch the original of anything that was compressed.
Your auth token, user agent and client ID headers pass through unchanged.

Let me know if you have any further questions or thoughts!

The switch: I believe I can see your attempts in our error reports. Headroom can't turn it on because it can't read your OpenCode config file, ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json. Fix that line, flip the switch again, and it should stay on.

If you can't spot the typo, email the file to [email redacted] with your API key removed and I'll take a look.

questions.title: Software Clarification Questions
questions.comment:
Hello Support Team,

1.) Great product! Does your software work with WordPress Gutenberg or just WordPress Elementor? 

2.) If your software currently doesn't work with Gutenberg websites, is this on your road map?

3.) Can your software be used with Non- WordPress website builders? If so, which website builder softwares?

4.) What capabilities & features will AI agents be able to do within your software and their limitations? 

5.) Can additional API credits be purchased before the credits renew the following month?

6.) If additional API credits can be purchased, do you have a bulk discount price or an Appsumo price for early investors of your software?

children.comment:
Hi,

Thanks a lot! Answers below.

1–2. Gutenberg
Not yet, but it's coming. We add new builders all the time: Elementor and Bricks shipped recently, and Gutenberg is next on the list. Until then, you can export any section as HTML and paste it into a Custom HTML block.

3. Non-WordPress builders
Yes. MiroMiro exports Tailwind, HTML, React and Vue. The HTML export also works in any builder with a custom code block, like Webflow, Framer or Wix.

4. AI agents
Connect MiroMiro to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Codex or any agent through our MCP server. Then just paste a URL and ask. Your agent can:

-Rebuild any section as clean code, an Elementor template or a Shopify section, using the site's real colors, fonts and spacing (no guessing from screenshots)
-Grab the brand: logo, color palette and fonts
-Pull the full design system as ready-to-use tokens
-Download every asset: images, SVGs, fonts, videos and Lottie animations

Every rebuilt section comes with a live preview and a download link, so you can check it before you use it.

All of this runs on our own extraction engine, and we test its output against real websites on an ongoing basis to keep improving it.

Limits: public pages only (no logins), and a few sites block automated browsers. For now it works one section at a time, but whole-website extraction is on our roadmap.

5. Extra credits
Yes. Credit packs are a one-time payment and never expire. They're only used once your monthly credits run out: 500 for €5, 1,500 for €10, 5,000 for €25, or 15,000 for €60.

6. Bulk / AppSumo pricing
Bigger packs cost less per credit, and for higher volumes you can contact us at [email redacted]. With an active AppSumo license, you also get 30% off every credit pack and the Developer and Growth subscription plans, applied automatically at checkout.

I'm also happy to put together a custom setup for AppSumo buyers, whether that's the API, credits or anything else. We ship updates all the time, and we're adding MiroMiro to n8n soon so you can run it in your automations.

Best,

Hi! Thanks for reaching out, and sorry for the confusion. Your 2,000 one-time credits are there; they're added to your account the moment you create your first API key.

questions.title: Hmm, re:add on
questions.comment:
Why isn’t this included in Tier 3?

Website Change Monitoring is a separate PeekShot Pro add-on, along with exact-time scheduling and Google Drive integration.

children.comment:
Thanks for the question! 

Website Change Monitoring is currently a separate PeekShot Pro add-on because it requires a significantly different processing pipeline from regular screenshot capture — including webpage content extraction, comparison, OCR/processing, and additional recurring infrastructure.

The same applies to some of the advanced features such as exact-time scheduling, where allowing everyone to schedule captures at arbitrary times can create large traffic spikes instead of distributing the workload evenly.

That said, I completely understand why you'd expect these features in the higher AppSumo tier. We're actually considering introducing a higher tier that would bundle these advanced features together, so customers who need the full automation/monitoring functionality can get everything in one package.

I'll definitely take this feedback into account as we finalize the AppSumo tiers.

For the price, it delivers a lot of value. It’s honestly hard to find an environment that gives you both a testing setup and a terminal for this cost, especially as a lifetime deal. If your goal is to quickly spin up an environment to run code, experiment, and learn, it does that very well.

That said, there are some areas where the product could improve—especially around documentation and clarity.

It takes time to understand how things actually work. For example, files from the “Drive” can be seen in the terminal, but you can’t modify or open them through the online desktop. At the same time, you can’t save files into /mnt, which creates confusion.

Because of that, you start running into questions like: if I can use Git, but I can’t write to /mnt, where should I work from? If database support is listed, how am I supposed to use it in practice? Should I create SQL scripts, or use Python or PHP to interact with a database? When I open an HTML file, it seems to bundle CSS and JS together—are these actually separate files? If I want to add images, where do they go? The /mnt directory shows everything mixed together without a clear folder structure—is that expected? Is there even proper support for assets like images?

Another example: how exactly am I supposed to use the Monaco editor with Drive files? Is that possible or not? These are small but important details that aren’t clearly explained, and the user ends up “hitting a wall” multiple times trying to figure out things that would normally be trivial.

The system works—but sometimes in ways that feel a bit patched together. Once you understand its quirks, you can make good use of it, but getting there isn’t always straightforward.

So here’s the bottom line: if your goal is to have a fast, simple environment for testing—running single-file scripts in Python, PHP, or HTML with inline CSS/JS—you’ll probably love it. It’s very convenient and always available.

However, if you expect a more complete development environment with flexibility, structure, and scalability, you may feel limited or even frustrated.

I believe the team could significantly improve the experience by adding better documentation, tutorials, and practical examples showing how the system actually works—especially how the desktop, terminal, and drive interact with each other. That would make a huge difference and help users fully understand what the platform is designed for.

Five tacos!

children.comment:
Hey Sumo-ling, thanks for your thoughtful review!

- Yes, /mnt is intentionally read-only, and the lack of a visible folder structure is also by design— the directories you see in the IDE are virtual.
- The HTML editor bundles CSS and JavaScript together, rather than storing them as separate files.
- In the Interactive Desktop, you can open a terminal alongside the IDE drive, which is one of its main advantages for workflow flexibility.

Your feedback is solid and appreciated. The platform was originally built for research use, and we later expanded it with features like the HTML editor—so it’s still evolving. Interactive Shell actually has a lot of powerful capabilities, and we’re gradually improving the documentation here: https://help.interactiveshell.com/

Both worked well without needing any extra libraries or files. reviews.title: So far so good
reviews.comment:
I have been testing this for a while and everything seems to be functioning well. However, there are several areas that require additions or improvements:  
- Establish a Discord channel for feedback, package requests, and support.  
- The UI/UX feels like the old days.  
- The Pro Shell packages are quite limited, they should encompass all common languages and packages.  
- The IDE design could be improved, consider using open-source options like Code Server (https://github.com/coder/code-server).  
- Should be able to set /mnt as default location.
- Support for creating files and folders from Pro Shell is needed, as I currently cannot initialize a virtual environment using the command python3 -m venv venv.
- It should support multiple terminal sessions. 
- Ability to open Pro Shell in new tab.
- The session durations are too short, requiring frequent logins.  
- There needs to be tagging, searching, and filtering features, as there will be many files in the future.  
- Implement public sharing with password protection.  
- Include an option to upload files and folders.  

By the way, great job to the team! I give you 5 tacos and hope these suggestions lead to innovative changes and enhancements for Shell.

children.comment: Thanks for your informative review, we are working on many of the recommendations above as we speak. Thanks again, exactly what we needed!

reviews.title: Bought the Highest Tier Immediately
reviews.comment:
I created my first website from scratch in less than 15 minutes. I really enjoy the interface of this app.

It would still be incredibly useful to have more robust project-level import workflows (for example, importing full folders where files can properly reference one another). In the past, I tried importing a folder exported from Brizy Cloud so that I could tinker with the code, but while uploads appeared to work, the files rendered blank and couldn’t communicate with one another. This made it difficult to work with fully functional exported sites or multi-file projects.

That said, I want to update my original rating based on long-term use and—more importantly—the responsiveness of the development team.

I previously suggested that the platform add support for the Exercism CLI, since Exercism allows users to submit and work through coding exercises locally and is widely used for learning programming. I felt this tool would be a perfect fit for the educational use cases this platform already enables.

The developer listened directly to that feedback and implemented Exercism CLI support in a month or less.

That level of responsiveness genuinely matters. Many tools promise to “listen to users,” but few actually ship features that directly reflect user suggestions—especially on such a short timeline.

Because of this, I’m updating my review to 5 stars. I’m a bit addicted to the tool (especially when using it inside a minimalistic browser like Zen Browser), and I still believe this product is a steal, particularly considering that it delivers Replit-like functionality as a lifetime deal instead of a subscription.

I sincerely hope the product continues to improve, and based on my experience so far, I’m confident the team is actively moving it in the right direction.

reviews.title: Found real issues I had missed
reviews.comment:
I ran a scan on my site through MCP from my AI assistant: start it, poll the status, read the report. The report sorts findings by severity. Medium were a DMARC policy still on “none” and a missing X-Frame-Options header. Low ones included missing DNSSEC, COOP and CORP headers, and HSTS without includeSubDomains and preload. It also flagged a missing og:image on two pages, no structured data on my article index, no llms.txt, no terms of use and no accessibility statement.

Each finding names the affected URL, so I could check it against my source before changing anything. I’m fixing them now and will post the rescan result here. DNSSEC has to wait for me.

Making each finding easy to check against your own source is a big priority, so I really appreciate you highlighting the affected URLs and evidence.

reviews.title: Security checks with fixes your AI coding tool can use
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

One of the problems with vibe coding is that you can get an app working long before you know whether it is safe to put in front of users.

Vibe App Scanner gives you a way to check the app you have deployed by entering its URL. It runs more than 150 checks, including exposed API keys, authentication issues, database permissions, and other security problems that can easily go unnoticed when you're focused on getting the app working.

What I particularly like is how it handles the findings. Each issue comes with an explanation, supporting evidence, and suggested fixes you can give to your AI coding tool. You can take those instructions back to Lovable, Cursor, Claude Code, or your developer, make the changes, and scan again to check the results.

For someone developing software with AI, I can see this becoming part of the development process. You make changes to your app, deploy them, run a scan, and address anything new that comes up. It also supports MCP, so you can connect it to your AI coding tools without having to manually copy everything between applications.

In my test, the scanning and suggested fixes worked well. I initially flagged a couple of things that would make the product more useful, particularly PDF reports for sharing findings with clients and a REST API for connecting scans and reports to other tools. The team added both, and I confirmed they were available in my retest.

I would still want a proper security review for an application handling sensitive data, but Vibe App Scanner gives founders and developers a way to catch common issues during development and after deployment.

Overall, I like the direction of this product, particularly for people using AI to develop software who may not have a security background. The ability to scan a deployed app, get specific instructions for addressing the findings, and check the results after making changes is what makes Vibe App Scanner worth considering.

children.comment: Thanks for the thoughtful review, Abe, and for coming back to retest the issues you flagged. I’m glad the findings and fixes were useful in your workflow. I also appreciate you pointing out that automated scans complement, rather than replace, a proper security review for sensitive apps. Feedback like yours helps us keep improving VAS.

questions.title: Hello, can scans reach sites behind Cloudflare? Are there fixed scanner IPs or a user agent to allow?
questions.comment: Some scan checks end as "could not finish" on a site behind a CDN/firewall. I want to know whether this can be fixed before buying.

children.comment:
Hi KimchiDee, Cloudflare’s interactive CAPTCHA challenges can prevent some checks from completing, and we don’t currently guarantee getting through those challenges.

For apps with that protection, we generally recommend scanning a staging environment that closely mirrors production, with access configured to let the scanner reach the app without an interactive CAPTCHA. This avoids weakening your live site’s protection. Production-specific settings may still need separate checks.

We’re also working on code repository scanning, coming soon, to expand coverage by examining the source code directly. It will complement live-site scanning rather than replace it.
If you email your scan ID to [email redacted], I’ll review which checks couldn’t finish and help you work out the best setup before buying.

Jacob

questions.title: Code Repository Scanning
questions.comment: I saw the message in my account saying “Code repository scanning is coming soon” and that it is planned for my existing plan. Could you clarify the expected scope? Will it include SAST/insecure code patterns, vulnerable dependency/lockfile scanning, secret detection, and GitHub repository scanning? Also, will repository findings be available through MCP/API in the same way as live-app scan findings?

children.comment:
Hi Joe, yes, the planned scope includes:
- SAST-style checks for insecure code patterns
- Known vulnerable dependency checks using supported lockfiles, initially npm.
- Secret detection for credentials and private keys committed to your code.
- GitHub repository scanning, including private repositories you explicitly grant access to.

This will complement the live-app scans by checking the underlying code for issues that external scanning cannot see.

API and MCP access to repository findings is part of the roadmap, but I don’t want to promise full parity with live-app findings on day one. We’ll confirm the supported integrations and your plan’s repository-scan allowances when we announce the rollout.

questions.title: given you very little meaningful response to date
questions.comment:
When you say it integrates with Google, does that mean it directly integrates with Google AI Studio (which I have used to create a SaaS desktop application using Next.js, Typescript, Cloud Firestore & Firebase SDK v12, etc.).

How does VAS help to fix security issues that it identifies?
Does it make recommentations or changes to improve auth/user architecture or payment plans/user levels/registration process?

children.comment:
Hi Ben, thanks for the detailed questions!

To clarify, VAS scans your deployed web app rather than connecting directly to your Google AI Studio project. You provide the app’s publicly accessible URL, so you can use it with an app built using Next.js, TypeScript and Firebase. If yours is packaged as a desktop application, we can assess its publicly accessible web components, rather than the desktop installation itself.

VAS looks for issues such as exposed secrets, publicly accessible database data, and security misconfigurations. A lot can be checked without needing to log in, although a URL scan cannot fully assess every private workflow or permission rule.

For the issues it finds, the report explains the risk, shows supporting evidence and provides remediation guidance. You can export the findings in an AI-friendly format and bring them into Google AI Studio to help implement the fixes.

VAS makes recommendations, but it does not automatically modify your code, Firebase rules, authentication setup or payment plans. It can flag relevant security issues it detects, but it is not a complete review or redesign of your registration, user-role or subscription architecture.

Is your app already available at a public web URL, or is it currently desktop-only? That would help us clarify which parts VAS can assess for you.

I haven't actually published it, insofar as being operational. However, Google AI Studio has provided (maybe two months ago) the ability to add a URL. So I wouldn't say that it is "live" yet, as I don't think it is publicly accessible. However, I could make it public, if required for Vibe App Scanner to operate effectively, if that is what you are referring to?

Hi Ben, yes! VAS needs a URL it can access without a Google login, but your app doesn’t need to be officially launched. A public test deployment with dummy data is fine. Keep normal authentication and security controls in place; VAS checks the publicly accessible parts. Send the URL privately to [email redacted] and I can check whether it’s suitable. No passwords needed.

reviews.title: Turn GitHub repos into docs that stay synced
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

GitDoc is an essential tool in every developer's toolkit out because it does the one thing every developer says they will do later: write proper documentation.

I tested it by connecting GitDoc to a GitHub repo for a web app I built a couple of years ago. What impressed me is that it read the actual source files, not only the repo name, filenames, or README, and generated documentation that was substantively correct. I was able to publish the docs, and the result looked polished enough to share.

The bigger value is that GitDoc connects the parts of documentation that are usually split across different tools. It can generate docs from a repo, API spec, files, URLs, or prompts, then let you edit visually or in MDX, publish to a branded domain, and keep the documentation synced as the project changes which is a key differentiator in my opinion.

The AI side is also more interesting than a basic doc generator. GitDoc includes Ask AI search for visitors, plus API and MCP access, so tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or other AI workflows can query or work with the docs directly. This is extremely useful because more people now ask AI tools for answers instead of digging through documentation page by page.

I also like that GitDoc is using its own LLMs rather than relying entirely on the usual third party AI providers. The team said Gemini is only used as backup or for high availability, which should give them more control over cost, availability, and how the product develops.

One thing I would still clarify is BYOK access. The team said BYOK is already supported through MCP and that every app function can be used through your own key that way. 

Overall, GitDoc is an easy recommend if you build projects and push code to GitHub. It gives you a fast way to go from repo to published documentation, while also making those docs easier for users and AI tools to query.

reviews.title: AI coding that makes sure you understand the code
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

AI coding tools can help make software much faster, but there is an obvious downside. It becomes very easy to accept a change because it works without really understanding what the AI changed or why.

That is what Contral is trying to address. It adds a teaching layer to the coding process, explaining functions, patterns and decisions as you vibe code. You can also highlight code and ask for an explanation when you want to understand a particular section in more detail.

I think Defense Mode is one of the more interesting ideas here. Instead of simply showing you an explanation, Contral can ask you to explain the code back in your own words and give you feedback on whether you actually understood it. For someone learning to code, or even an experienced developer working in an unfamiliar codebase, I can see that being much more useful than simply accepting whatever the coding agent produced.

I can also see this being useful beyond learning. If you're a founder using AI to help build your product, there may come a point where an investor, technical advisor or due diligence reviewer starts asking questions about your codebase. You should be able to explain how the important parts work, why certain decisions were made and what the risks are. A tool that keeps pushing you to understand the code as you go can help you be much better prepared for those conversations.

You also don't have to replace the coding tools you already use. Contral can work alongside agents such as Claude Code and Codex through its editor extension. Your coding agent continues doing the coding, while Contral watches the changes and explains what happened. That separation makes a lot of sense to me because I can keep using the coding tool I prefer while adding the learning layer around it.

I did run into a couple of problems during testing. The Explain feature in the VS Code extension originally kept spinning without returning anything, and a link inside the desktop IDE was broken. The team fixed both issues, and I rechecked them successfully.

There are some current limits. The structured Learn Mode curriculum currently teaches Java only, although Build Mode and the code explanation features can work with other languages. On macOS, the desktop IDE currently requires Apple Silicon, while Windows and Linux versions are also available.

Overall, I think Contral is most interesting for people who want to use AI to code without becoming completely dependent on it. The AI can still help you move faster, but Contral keeps asking the question that most coding assistants don't: do you actually understand the code you're about to ship? A very useful tool for any founder or coder’s stack, with a lot of potential.

children.comment: Hi AbeChallah, thanks for such a careful review. Glad Defense Mode and the teaching layer came through, and that Contral can sit alongside the coding agents you already use. Appreciate you flagging the VS Code Explain and desktop IDE link issues and confirming the fixes. You're right that structured Learn Mode is Java-only today; Build mode and the explanation features work across languages. Thanks again for giving Contral a real look.

Open an empty folder, describe what you want, and it creates the files, writes the code, and can run install and dev-server commands with your approval. Bigger apps may take a few messages. Usage is tracked per feature rather than as one shared credit pool, and each message you send counts once no matter how many steps the agent takes: AI (Build) messages are 500 per day on Tier 1, 1,000 per day on Tier 2, and unlimited on Tier 3. Learn Mode explanations are unlimited on every tier. Teaching cards on Kilo Code or Cline edits follow the same daily numbers (500 / 1,000 / unlimited). Deep dives are 10 / 20 / 200 per day, and codebase analyses are 5 / 10 / 100 per month. Messages that use your own API key are unlimited on every tier. Premium models are included on Tier 3. questions.title: Contral.ai vs condemate.ai
questions.comment: Apart from the teaching feature, how much Contral.ai is different from codemate.ai app?

children.comment:
Hi cikandar, thanks for asking!

Beyond the teaching layer, here's how Contral is set up today:

Build mode is a repo-aware coding agent with Plan, Fast, Deep, and Recursive modes. Plan starts read-only and ends in a plan you approve or reject; Recursive can draft, critique, and revise its own output. Contral never writes files silently. Edits show up as hunks you accept or skip (or apply all), and terminal commands ask first.

The VS Code–compatible extension also watches edits from agents you already use (Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cline, Windsurf, and others) and explains those changes, so you can keep your preferred agent. You can use the extension or the Contral IDE (public beta on Apple Silicon Mac, Windows, and Linux) with the same account and plan. Models are included with no API key required; optional BYOK (including Ollama for local models) is available. Contral is local-first: it doesn't store your source code, and with Ollama BYOK prompts can stay on your machine.

Happy to go deeper on any of these if useful!

Contral comes with hosted AI models included, so you just sign in and start using Build mode and the teaching features, and usage counts against your plan's daily allowances. If you'd like, you can optionally bring your own key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, xAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, Ollama for local models, or any OpenAI-compatible provider). BYOK messages are counted separately, are unlimited on every AppSumo tier, and are billed directly by your provider. Thanks for checking out Contral!

Hi GDR, thanks for asking! Yes, you can build with it. Contral's Build mode is a coding agent: it reads your project and proposes edits as a review card, and you accept, skip, or apply them all. It never writes to your files without your review. It can also create new projects (Next.js, Vite, Express, FastAPI, Django, Go and more) and open a live preview of web apps.

If something's wrong in your code, just ask Build mode to fix the bug or improve the approach, and it'll propose the corrected code for you to apply. Every change also comes with a teaching card explaining what changed and why.

On usage, there isn't one single credit pool. Each plan has separate allowances: messages to the Build agent count as AI messages, while explanations like Explain selection, Ask Tutor, Deep dives and teaching cards have their own allowances. And if you'd rather fix things yourself, Learn Mode and the teaching features point out what's wrong and explain the better way without editing your code.

reviews.title: Everything other Forms gave us, without the yearly bill, plus support that actually answers
reviews.comment:
I picked Bit Form up on the previous AppSumo deal, so this is not a first impression. It has been running the enquiry flow of our website for months, and since the deal is back I thought the honest long version might be more useful than another five star line.

We run a small education and therapy centre in Zagreb. Our website is the main way people reach us, so the forms are not decoration. They are the business. We came from WPForms. It worked, but every renewal cost more for capabilities we had long stopped considering advanced, and that was the reason we started looking.

The forms themselves were never the point. Anyone can put a name and an email field on a page. What we needed was the logic behind them.

Our forms decide what to show depending on what the person selects. They send a different confirmation depending on which programme someone signs up for. They notify the right person on our side, separately and with different wording from what the visitor receives. They carry a hidden field so we know which page an enquiry came from, which turned out to matter far more than we expected. None of that required a separate paid add on per capability, which is precisely what we were escaping.

Four things turned out better than expected.

Conditional logic is genuinely conditional. Fields, sections and entire email templates respond to what the user selected, not merely field visibility.

Autoresponders and admin notifications are separate templates, and each carries its own conditions. One form, several outcomes, no duplicated forms to keep in sync.

Dynamic options. Our course dropdown is populated live from the events we publish on the site. We change a date in one place and every form reflects it at once. There is no list to maintain by hand and nothing goes stale, which for a centre that reschedules courses is worth the price on its own.

The builder is quick and stays out of your way. Duplicating a form and adapting it is a matter of minutes.

Support deserves its own paragraph. I opened a ticket about a narrow limitation: filtering an imported post list by taxonomy term. The answer came quickly, from someone who had clearly read the question, tested it, and sent working code instead of a link to a generic article. When it turned out the capability did not exist yet, they said so plainly and logged it for a future release rather than talking around it. Fast, technical and honest at the same time is rarer than it should be.

So no, it is not perfect. That taxonomy filter is still on my wish list. But everything our enquiry flow actually stands on works, works reliably, and no longer arrives with an invoice every year.

What I value most, after months of it, is that Bit Form was clearly built by people who use forms themselves. The capabilities are the ones you actually reach for, the defaults are sensible, and the team answers like engineers who care whether your site works. It has quietly become one of the few plugins on our site that I never have to think about, and for a tool that carries every enquiry we receive, that is the highest compliment I can pay it. Thank you to the Bit Apps team for building it properly and for standing behind it.

I can't even begin to think about building another Wordpress site without Bit-Form or without Bit-Flows, and I'm not joking. 

I recommend Bit-Form 110% to anyone and everyone with a WordPress site. You cannot go wrong with this purchase, and I wish the BitApps Team the absolute best...I need you folks to stick around forever and to flourish and build even more incredible WordPress apps.

reviews.title: MetaSurvey: a fresh, interactive take on surveys
reviews.comment:
Full review here:
https://youtu.be/q-eZ-NMTmdM

I took an initial look at MetaSurvey, a survey builder available on AppSumo. Its standout feature is the swipe-style survey experience: respondents move through questions one at a time, a bit like using a dating app. It gives surveys a more interactive feel than a conventional form and could be a good fit when you want to make answering quick and engaging.

I explored several question formats and tried creating a survey with the AI generator. My first prompt produced a survey in German, so I had to refine the instructions and specify that I wanted English. After that, it created a useful survey about lifetime deals. The AI can be a helpful way to get started, but I’d check the output and be specific about the language and content you need.

I also connected the survey to Google Sheets to see how responses are collected, and looked at the customisation and sharing options. The product includes ways to share or embed a survey, create a QR code, randomise questions and use conditional logic. Those options give you room to adapt a survey to different audiences and workflows.

My first impression is that MetaSurvey is straightforward to explore and offers a distinctive presentation style. The swipe format is its clearest point of difference, while AI generation and Google Sheets integration can help with creating a survey and working with responses.

This was an initial hands-on look rather than an in-depth or long-term review, so I can’t speak to how it performs at scale or how reliable every feature is in regular use. I’d recommend trying the builder with a real example, checking the AI-generated questions carefully, and making sure the survey and response workflow suit your needs before committing.

Overall, MetaSurvey looks like an interesting option if you want surveys to feel more interactive than a standard form. The AI gave me a language hiccup at first, but a clearer prompt improved the result. Worth exploring if the swipe-style experience appeals to you; just treat this as an early impression rather than a full product verdict.

questions.comment:

For example:

* Score 0–20 → Thank You Page A
* Score 21–40 → Thank You Page B
* Score 41–60 → Thank You Page C
* Score 61+ → Thank You Page D

Can I use Skip Logic, Display Logic, or another feature to automatically route someone to a specific Thank You Page based on their total assessment score?

If so, what is the best way to set this up, especially if I want each score range to have different messaging, resources, and calls to action?

children.comment:
Hi Ryan,

Yes, you can create multiple Thank You screens.

To navigate to the preferred Thank You screen, you should:

1. Add a calculated field (or use the default Score field): https://getmetasurvey.com/help/calculated-fields

2. Add conditional logic to change the Score during the survey, and then add skip logic to the last question to navigate to the appropriate Thank You screen based on the Score value: https://getmetasurvey.com/help/conditional-logic

reviews.title: One of my best Appsumo Deals ever!

I run a small agency in Zurich and we were looking for a form builder we could use across client projects without paying per seat, per form, or per submission. Deftform turned out to be exactly that.

We currently use it for two things: course registrations and contact forms. Every submission is stored in Deftform, not just fired off as an email, that alone solved a problem we'd been living with for years. If a notification mail gets stuck in spam or never arrives, the entry is still there. Our client can open the dashboard, see every registration in one list, and export it as CSV or PDF for the participant list or invoicing. No more "did we miss an enquiry?"

The builder is genuinely quick. Multi-page forms, conditional logic, file uploads, e-signatures, 20+ field types — I had the first live form built in under 15 minutes. AI Builder works also perfectly!

The part that closed it for us: data sits on servers in Germany, uploads stay in the EU. For European clients, GDPR compliance isn't a nice-to-have, and being able to say that in a client meeting is worth real money.

Unlimited forms and responses, one payment, no per-form pricing creeping up as we add clients. For an agency, that's the whole value proposition.

Easy 5 tacos. If you handle client forms at any volume, grab it.
