reviews.title: Great product with lots of potential
reviews.comment:
I had purchased Formly back in 2022 and had trouble using it. Since it was only a Tier 1 AppSumo offering and I couldn't refund due to negligence on my part, I chalked it up as a learning experience. I saw it once again last year and noticed many improvements so this time I  made a Tier 3 purchase. I played around with it but didn't put it to the test until one of my client's WeForms market registration form failed and we couldn't get it fixed. 

So I decided to finally get serious with Formly and recreated the form for my client. With support help from the Formly folks I now had a form completed and ready to try out. Connecting it to Stripe just basically required me adding the client's Stripe email address to the form. Instantly, the form was working flawlessly. Using one of their templates allowed me to mimic the design of my client's website. The receipt generated and sent to the user is well laid out and clearly indicates the user's choice of markets they wished to attend along with the booth size, cost of each booth and the total. 

So here are a couple of suggestions to the Formly folks from my recent experience using their product. 
1. I got stuck when trying to connect the pricing to the booth size and location. I couldn't figure out what I had done wrong. I immediately went to their "Help" section where a list of Hep articles gave me a choice of subjects to choose from. After reading through them, nothing was helpful.
2. When the "Help" section didn't actually help, I looked for any "support@" email address in my account. Couldn't find any email contact form or "chat box" at all.
3. That led me to YouTube to see if they had any videos I could watch. My search for "Formly Forms" produced a list of videos, but they were either competitors or AppSumo marketers creating their own videos. Scrolling down the page I finally found one that Formly created just two months ago. It was a well done 13 second video highlighting "Hidden Fields", but didn't show how to add a hidden field. Again, showing how easily they added field that would be a better sales approach. That was all I could find. Still stuck with my problem.
4. Went to CHATGPT and asked it if Formly had a support email address. It displayed it right away and I was now able to write for some help. They responded immediately with an explanation of what to do. I tried it but still had trouble. I wrote back for more clarity and they encouraged me to try once more and make note of the "@" symbol placement. That's when I discovered that I had not hit my space bar to provide one space between the text and the field calculator. Once I did that, everything started working. One strike with my space bar on my keyboard was all I needed to finish my work.

This is my experience with Formly Forms. Now that I have a better understanding how everything works, I'm up and running ready to replace all my current forms Formly Forms. Good folks with a great product. Some videos like the one you just made and an easier way to communicate would be the icing on a nice cake!

reviews.title: MetaSurvey: a fresh, interactive take on surveys
reviews.comment:
Full review here:
https://youtu.be/q-eZ-NMTmdM

I took an initial look at MetaSurvey, a survey builder available on AppSumo. Its standout feature is the swipe-style survey experience: respondents move through questions one at a time, a bit like using a dating app. It gives surveys a more interactive feel than a conventional form and could be a good fit when you want to make answering quick and engaging.

I explored several question formats and tried creating a survey with the AI generator. My first prompt produced a survey in German, so I had to refine the instructions and specify that I wanted English. After that, it created a useful survey about lifetime deals. The AI can be a helpful way to get started, but I’d check the output and be specific about the language and content you need.

I also connected the survey to Google Sheets to see how responses are collected, and looked at the customisation and sharing options. The product includes ways to share or embed a survey, create a QR code, randomise questions and use conditional logic. Those options give you room to adapt a survey to different audiences and workflows.

My first impression is that MetaSurvey is straightforward to explore and offers a distinctive presentation style. The swipe format is its clearest point of difference, while AI generation and Google Sheets integration can help with creating a survey and working with responses.

This was an initial hands-on look rather than an in-depth or long-term review, so I can’t speak to how it performs at scale or how reliable every feature is in regular use. I’d recommend trying the builder with a real example, checking the AI-generated questions carefully, and making sure the survey and response workflow suit your needs before committing.

Overall, MetaSurvey looks like an interesting option if you want surveys to feel more interactive than a standard form. The AI gave me a language hiccup at first, but a clearer prompt improved the result. Worth exploring if the swipe-style experience appeals to you; just treat this as an early impression rather than a full product verdict.

I have wanted an app that was simple but had the features I wanted. I tried Fuzen to build the app and was very happy with the results.

The Ai got stuck getting a feature to work right, but a ticket to support and they had things running in less than 24 hours.
I was sent an email offering an online meeting if I still had trouble or questions. I had hit another issue with my app so I set a meeting. The meeting was quite helpful in learning more about Fuzen and when they found out how long and the amount of credits used trying to get my current issue solved, they jumped right on it. The next day my app was again running and they had replenished some of my credits.

I have run into an issue with Ai in general and Fuzen does it too. If you are running a test on you app that generates a report or results and there is no data to work with Ai's will create data from the "cosmos" and then generate your answer. I have had this happen with multiple Ai models, even after telling the model Not to create fake data. I think in general Ai is taught to deliver a positive answer, stating there is no answer is negative so the Ai creates data to give a positive answer.

I would say to give Fuzen a try if your looking to build an app of your own, it's simple to use and you get the app features you want with none of the add on bloat.

I am looking forward to building a couple other apps I have been thinking about with Fuzen.

reviews.title: Absolutely Worth It, BUT...
reviews.comment:
UPDATE:
I was initially quite impressed with Fuzen, but after diving more deeply into its architectural approach, I'm not so certain. I'm building a solution from scratch with a pretty detailed craft prompt. While the initial build looks good on the surface, it falls apart under the hood. Granted, the calculations and workflows in use are fairly intricate, but the issue is simple data flow from page to page. I've tried several times to get the tool to embrace the concept of global calculations and variables to use throughout, but it continues to generate code to recalculate on each page. So the issue becomes correct values on one page, incorrect or missing data on others for the exact same data. It also tends to generate mock code, calling it fully implemented. When requested to test, it will essentially fabricate results, and even though the actual and expected results don't match, it will denote test cases as passed. The other issue I've seen is relative to security vulnerabilities (I.e. storing app keys in the browser rather than server side). The cost of resolving the architectural missteps has far outweighed the speed with which fuzen can spin up a working solution. I do realize that the niche and complexity of my project may push the limits of what the tool is capable of, but the default architectural/security gaps noticed seem to be a bigger issue with the potential to affect other builds, not just my own. Also notice the AI overstepping my requests by proceeding with implementation of steps I explicitly stated not to make or to await approval before implementing. I'm torn on whether keep fuzen, hoping it will improve, or throw in the towel. After three failed attempts and exhausted credits trying to shore up the porous infrastructure generated, I'm deducting two stars.

Original Review:
Chose fuzen to essentially build out a few app ideas I've had floating around for a while. I'm crafting a calendar journal of sorts from scratch that will eventually be shared to my broader community. The build process was initially a bit of a learning curve, but I've adapted quickly. You really want to start with a very detailed craft prompt. I was able to get a working iteration up in no time; less than an hour. The challenge has been working through a few more complex mathematical and celestial calculations. No fault of the tool, just complex mathematical things based on planetary and geographical positioning/alignments. Overall I'm impressed with Fuzen, its been up for the task of creating something a bit unconventional. The tool makes coding a breeze. And as a former engineer, I love that I can go behind the scenes when necessary to do some more custom things. 
I went with the highest tier, because I love that the credits refresh for life; which means I'll have more than enough credits to flesh out all of my ideas at least to some degree. I also love that hosting and all of the backend details are handled by the tool, so I don't have to worry about it. The credit usage is extremely fair and the AI is really fast and accurately responsive. The only thing missing, if I had to pick something I would like to have, is the ability to export/sync the code to GitHub, just to be able to maintain my own code backup in the event something were to happen to the tool. But overall I'm more than happy with my purchase. And I'm looking forward to all that I will have the ability to create. Thank you to the Fuzen team for this offering!

questions.title: Who owns client data, and can Fuzen use it for marketing, outreach, AI training, or resell it?
questions.comment:
Hi,
I'm considering Fuzen to build, white-label and resell SaaS apps to businesses, including EU/EEA clients. After reading your data privacy & Terms, please clarify:

1. Do I own and control my apps, databases and client data?
2. Can Fuzen access, share, sell or use client data for its own marketing, direct outreach, lead generation or AI training?
3. Do you provide a GDPR-compliant DPA? Where is data stored and processed?
4. Can I resell or transfer complete SaaS apps, including customer accounts and data?
5. Can I export all data and migrate to another provider without restrictions?
6. Are private app data and customer records excluded from your broad content licensing terms?
7. What happens to data if I cancel or Fuzen shuts down?

Please confirm these rights and restrictions in writing.

children.comment:
Hi, thanks for the detailed questions. 

Your apps and data are yours. The apps you build and all the client data inside them belong to you and sit under your account. You control who has access.

We don’t touch your client data. We don’t access, share, sell, or use it for our own marketing, outreach, lead generation, or AI training. The only exception is if you explicitly ask us to, in writing, through a support ticket.

GDPR: being upfront, we don’t have a GDPR DPA in place right now, and apps are hosted in the US. If EU/EEA compliance is a hard requirement for your clients, that’s worth a direct conversation before you commit.

Reselling: yes, you can resell the apps you build with Fuzen to your own clients. The one thing that can’t be resold or transferred is the AppSumo lifetime deal itself.

Export: you can export your data to CSV or Google Sheets at any time. There’s no source-code or app-structure export, since Fuzen is a managed platform, so you own the data, not the underlying code.

“Private apps” just means invite-only: nobody can sign in without an invite. There’s no content-licensing claim over your apps or customer records.

If you cancel, or if an app shuts down for any reason, you can download your data.

Thanks for your questions!

Templates: all the free templates are included on every tier. The paid ones (Manufacturing ERP, School, Solar) aren't free, but Tiers 2 and 3 get 50% off them. That discount is part of the lifetime deal, not a public sale.

Branding: removing Fuzen branding isn't a Tier 3 extra, it's on every paid tier. Your app runs on your own domain, with your name and logo and no "Built with Fuzen" badge.

One app per client: each app is fully separated, its own data, users and permissions, walled off from your other apps. It runs on our managed multi-tenant platform rather than a dedicated database per app.

MCP / export: you can export your data to CSV or Google Sheets today. There's no app-structure or source-code export, and MCP isn't available yet, and not planned in the next few months.

reviews.title: A desktop AI builder for turning ideas into apps
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

I took Friday Code for a deep dive and was genuinely impressed. It's a robust desktop AI builder that turns plain language prompts into websites, web apps, backends, and small tools you can actually deploy. What I like about it is that it gives you more than a chat window for code. You can describe what you want to build, work through the project inside the desktop app, refine it through conversation, and export the full codebase if you want to keep building elsewhere.

In my early test, I used Friday Code to build and deploy a to do app and a landing page. It did not get everything right on the first try, but it responded well to follow up instructions and improved the output over a few rounds until I got what I wanted. That is what I expected from this type of application. After a few rounds, I got a better feel for how to guide it, what level of detail to give it, and how to get to the expected result faster. The best way to use Friday Code is to see it as a faster way from idea to working version, with room to keep improving the output through iteration. The important part is that it gives you the tools to do that without starting from a blank codebase or having to manage the whole process manually.

Friday Code also supports templates, local project storage, and different AI model options. The OpenRouter support is especially useful because you can use your own OpenRouter API key, which gives you more control if you already have a preferred AI setup.

There were a few launch readiness glitches in the first build I tested, especially around Intel Mac compatibility and the Windows install experience. The team has been addressing these ahead of launch (the Intel build and a couple of experimental features have been cleaned up). I retested again with the new launch build, and those concerns are no longer an issue. App generation worked well, the early issues were resolved, and the product now feels much closer to what buyers should expect at launch. It also keeps getting better.

Overall, Friday Code is worth considering if you want a desktop AI builder for quickly testing ideas, building tools, and getting projects deployed without starting from a blank codebase. It sits somewhere between a no code builder and a terminal based AI coding tool like Claude Code. You still need to guide the AI through a few rounds, but you do not have to live in the terminal, manage a local dev setup, or think like a developer from the first prompt. It's a solid solution for helping non technical users turn ideas into working apps in a more guided desktop environment.

We have made the agents much better, and the windows issues are resolved as well. Appreciate you sharing inputs on how we can continue to make the product better!

reviews.title: Good but ... **UPDATED**
reviews.comment:
********* UPDATE 02/09/26 *******
This is an update to the original review below. I had direct dialogue with Amogh, the developer and sent over my log file and several of my concerns were addressed and QUICKLY (which matters massively with this type of software).

I am now updating my review from 3 stars to 4 stars because the credit system has been adjusted and I can confirm, credit burn is much slower (I am hoping it will be refined evern further - Amogh has assured all users this is the case) and the software is good and very quick.

I could also really do with the ability to copy responses (so a copy button) so I don't have to constantly highlight and press ctrl+c.

I also get a server busy response or a try again (granted FAR less frequent than before but still more so when using "Friday GO") and when it has to go over old checkpoints again, there is still credit usage.

Another small thing would be a terminal inside of Friday - it's just one less app I need to open but this in no way effects my usage of the software.

Again, I just want to reiterate, I really, really like this software and think it's on its way to 5 stars. 

I will update again as more changes happen.

**************************************************************************************

I like the software, first and foremost. It’s lacking some refinement, though, and I’m hoping this improves and, in time, it will replace Devin and Cursor in my stack.

A few things I think could be improved massively:

Credits get burned through, and I mean QUICK. Ask a question or two and the credits start decreasing before any work has even really begun.

Terminal commands and functions like a full Pytest run (that can be run from Windows PowerShell) also use credits, and I’m not sure why. This doesn’t use any model reasoning, etc., and as stated, I can run these for free from my own PowerShell.

I used almost all 250 credits in six hours, doing no more than I usually would in Codex/Cursor. For comparison, I only pay for the lowest tiers per month and never run out (so circa £40 per month). With how quickly Friday’s credits burn, I’ll also be spending on credits for OpenRouter. At some point, I’ll have to look at the overall cost and see which makes more financial sense. On a plus note, the actual Friday coder is excellent.

Every now and again, we’ll get halfway through working on a prompt for Friday to suddenly report, “This AI agent is available, please try again,” and every time I’ve had to restart. And yep, you guessed it, the redo uses even more credits.

There’s no ability to copy or paste without keyboard shortcuts. I use Grok/ChatGPT/Claude as the orchestrator and then Friday/Devin/Cursor to implement, so having to constantly scroll up and down to copy things is a pain.

There’s no ability to change the theme. It’s black with white text and a splash of green. Unbolded text looks more grey and can be a real pain to read, so being able to change to a light background with black text would be good.

You constantly have to have a browser open to remain signed in?

These are just things I’ve noticed from using it for the last day or so.

children.comment:

1. Credit burn: We're actively working on it, and this will be much more credit efficient in the next couple of releases.
2. Theme: You absolutely can switch to light theme. Hoverover on your name on bottom left, you'll see an icon to switch between dark and light theme. I personally love the light theme a lot more, easier to read during the day.
3. Model unavailable. We're working on switching cloud providers, the one we're currently using has low capacity sometimes. This issue will be resolved.
4. Copy/Paste - Dint quite follow the feedback, do you need a copy icon in the responses? Or in thr files editor. Please post your feedback on our Slack.
I hope we turn this into a 5 star experience for you!

reviews.title: Early-stage potential contender for Cursor's throne
reviews.comment:
First off, for everybody complaining about Friday being an early-stage product with some bugs / features in development: You know we're on Appsumo, right? It's not called "Perfectly-finished-product-sumo". We're investing in early stage products because of the dream of what they can become; not always for what they do right now. 

Now, Friday is working towards becoming a contender for the throne. It's a good product, with good capabilities already (built + shipped a MacOS native Swift project in less than a day's work). It has a long way to go before it can challenge Cursor in its own right, but - let's be honest - Cursor literally sold for 60 BILLION DOLLARS. It's been in development for years, with a large development team, and tons of money behind it. The fact that Friday is as good as it is, at the stage that it is, is a major hats-off to Amogh. 

New features are shipping regularly, and genuine feedback is taken and acted upon quickly and with proper consideration. He's not shipping half-baked here, he's shipping well-considered + thoughtful additions. 

Full disclosure; I did refund my purchase, but that's a personal situation & financial decision more than a product decision. I think Amogh, especially as responsive / invested as he is in the development, will no doubt make this an even more incredible product over time.

I'm keeping Friday linked in my bookmarks so I can check in from time to time, and - should I end up with more development time available in my life - I'll gladly rejoin as a paid subscriber. 

Amogh is a passionate, committed developer, building an incredibly ambitious project, and he's doing it: He's winning. Kudos to him, sincerely.

reviews.title: Took my time on this one...
reviews.comment:
So I have now used Friday to make a chrome extension, an app, and a couple websites over that last couple of weeks.

This thing is good. It is hovering on an interesting line between Lovable's ease of use and Openclaw's agentic power and it really feels nice to use.
It solves Openclaws worst aspect, which is a complicated setup. 

Now it isn't quite as powerful as either of those apps for what they do, but if you are wanting a hybrid that can do both jobs realistically about 90%+ as good, Friday is your software.

The founder is 10/10 as far as "in the zone" dealing with issues and people while juggling 2 projects. I am very impressed with Amogh, I am not sure I could do anywhere near as good of a job handling things.

Now lets get into the "bad". Friday Go which is the base model and is not very good. I am assuming this is the cheap model's fault more than the prompting itself and just like all AI models I think this will improve with time. Even "bad/cheap" models are getting better crazy fast. I did move away from this model quite quickly and might not have given it a fair shake on more simple tasks.

The agent made automations work but I had some issues with them deleting themselves after a few runs. I didn't test a lot so this may have been random and caused by the automation being broken so the agent decided to remove it but I was never able to find out what happened to it. Thank you so much for the detailed review and for taking the time to share your feedback!

We’re currently completely reworking the default end screen to make it much more user-friendly and flexible. This update will be live soon and should address the issue you mentioned around defaults and end-screen behavior.

Regarding spam protection, we already have a honeypot system integrated to help block automated spam submissions. We’re also actively working on giving you much more design flexibility within the form editor, including more control over buttons, text, typography, colors, sizing, and other form elements, so you can customize your forms as much as possible.

Really appreciate your patience, detailed feedback, and continued testing. Your feedback helps us make Kiwiform better!

reviews.title: A Phenomenal SaaS - Ideal for Creating Quiz Funnels - My top purchase for where it is now, and for where it's heading
reviews.comment:
***The Pros****
Very rarely am I compelled to leave this level of feedback.  KiwiForms has become my number one purchase on AppSumo. This is due to its versatility, functionality and the productivity and professionalism of the team behind it.

I’m a top tier purchaser, and have invested in some AppSumo lifetime powerhouses.  I’ve recently completed stress testing KiwiForms, and it is extremely intuitive, with a very extensive feature set.  I’ve found team Kiwi, especially receptive to my feature suggestions, and the issues I’ve had with system glitches were swiftly ironed out.  This product started strong but it’s now an absolute beast, and the direction its development team are heading, makes this one of my greatest investments on AppSumo.

My preference, is to construct my branching logic forms manually.  That said, even without it's AI functionality, I’d still say tier 3 is priced extremely competitively as a lifetime product.  However, with its AI features, such as its MCP server, I can utilise ChatGBT via Codex and dramatically lessen my workload when doing less bespoke projects.

It has so many potential uses, but as a quiz funnel it is phenomenal. The following are just three of the many features that make KiwiForms absolutely powerful for my use case:

Black listing
* Able to black list respondents by their form outcome.

Email verification
* Respondents are prevented from going any further in a form until they verify their email.

Stripe Payments
* Adding a payment field to your forms, so form respondents can make a payment.

***The Cons****
The only real drawback is that you can only map a total of 5 subdomains.  After speaking with their leadership team, this current restriction is understandable.  In my opinion, not offering unlimited domain mapping, is a drawback for agencies wanting to offer a tailored bespoke service to their clients.

***The workaround ****
That said, a great work around is purchasing a unique generic domain and then using their 'custom link' feature, where you can put your clients' business names as the slug (e.g. just4.you/client’s business name).  You can then give your clients an exclusive service without using up your domains.  You can also use their ‘embed form in webpage’ feature, to help towards offering a premium service to your clients.

Also, when possible, it would be great to have a pay-as-you-go domain mapping model, to support our clients, where we pay per month for each extra domain, only when needed.  That way, we can provide a service for some clients who want bespoke forms presented on their chosen domains.

***The conclusion****
This is an extremely versatile and valuable piece of technology, that allows you to create intricate forms with advanced branching logic, easily.  It has superb ergonomics and a very self-explanatory user-interface.  This makes it apparent that their team has put a lot of time and effort into providing a great user-experience.  Which makes it easier for us to create forms that also give respondents a great user experience.

Bespoke quiz funnels are the future, and to have an instrument like this that creates the bones of these intelligent forms, so seamlessly, is a must.  My advice is to go unlimited with tier 3, and get KiwiForms whilst you can.  I’m pretty certain that you’d never get it for this price again, and I'd be surprised to see it show up as a lifetime deal once this offer ends.

To get an idea of how powerful this piece of software is, go to their 'Help center' (https://kiwiform.com/help), and manually browse or use their search function.

questions.title: How do I add redirect URL as next step when a form is submitted?
questions.comment: I can't delete the end screen or make the redirect the default. How do I do this?

children.comment: I can fix this in the logic screen but I can't change the default from the end screen. How do I change the default to the redirect and delete the end screen?

You can't delete the default End Screen, as we include it for a better user experience. However, you can create different types of End Screens based on your requirements and bypass the default End Screen using Logic Flow.

For redirecting users, Kiwiform provides two options:

1. Button Redirect: The End Screen includes a button, and you can set your desired URL for that button. When the user clicks it, they'll be redirected to your specified URL.

2. Automatic Redirect: Use the "Redirect to Link" End Screen. Once the user completes the form, they will be automatically redirected to your specified URL without needing to click anything.

If needed further clarification you can drop your message on our support email: [email redacted]

questions.title: Code IMPORT after editing externally
questions.comment:
I understand the security reasoning behind “code goes out, never in,” but this is probably my biggest concern about keeping my PlugThis LTD. Will it will remain competitive and time-saving long term?

AI coding is evolving incredibly fast. If I export an extension and use Codex, Claude, Cursor, etc. to fix or improve something PlugThis couldn't; I can no longer bring that improved version back and continue working in PlugThis. That may work today, but I'm worried a one-way workflow could become limiting rapidly.

Is “code never comes in” a permanent principle, or are you considering safe alternatives such as comparing/syncing external changes or other ways to work alongside external AI coding tools?

And related to that, as models improve so quickly, what is the plan for keeping PlugThis's actual coding capabilities competitive long-term?

children.comment:
Your real question is whether this ages badly, so let me answer that.

Start with what the one-way door actually does for you. You own the source outright and nothing of ours runs inside your extension. If we disappeared tomorrow, everything you have built keeps working and you carry on with it somewhere else. The export is not the trap. It is the thing that means you can never be trapped.

What you lose is the round trip, and that is real. But look at what the round trip requires. You can already change code by hand inside PlugThis, save, and keep chatting on top of your own edits. 

Why it is not there today. Everything we generate goes through checks before you download it, ending in a headless Chrome run that actually boots the extension and confirms it works. Code arriving from outside has been through none of that. So the question is not whether we can accept it, it is what we are still able to promise you about it once we have. That is the honest reason, and it is a solvable one rather than a principle.

It is not planned, yet. The shape you described is the right one. Compare incoming changes against the version we hold and show you what changed, rather than overwriting blind. If this is the thing that decides whether the product works for you, pls say so. We will think about this. 

On models. We are not tied to one.

But the model is not where our advantage sits. We only build Chrome extensions, which means we see how they fail. Thousands of real builds, in real browsers, breaking in real ways. Every one of those failures becomes a rule the generator follows the next time somebody builds something similar. A general model will write you something that looks correct and quietly does not work, because it has never watched what happens after a person installs it. We have, and we keep watching.

Models will keep changing. That library of known failures only grows, and it is the part that makes this worth having in two years.
Sounds like you're on top of it. Thanks for this.

questions.title: Long-term roadmap, model quality, and platform independence
questions.comment:
Hi Udaya, 

I'm evaluating PlugThis for production Chrome extensions and commercial products.

1. Will you support multiple AI models, model choice, and model-agnostic build verification to maintain quality as models evolve?
2. Are monthly generation limits guaranteed for LTD users, or could infrastructure costs reduce build capacity?
3. What's planned for Firefox, GitHub workflows, code import, and advanced debugging?
4. How will development, infrastructure, and support be funded after the AppSumo campaign? Will LTD allowances and core features remain available without mandatory subscriptions?

Please distinguish firm commitments from planned features. Thanks!

children.comment:
Hi, thanks for the clear questions. I'll split each answer into what's true today, what I can commit to, and what isn't decided.

1. Models and verification
Today: PlugThis already uses several models, chosen per step (planning, writing, repairing), and we swap them as better ones come along. We don't let you pick the model yourself.
Verification doesn't depend on the model. Every build goes through our own checks before you see it: the code has to bundle and load, and it's opened and clicked through in a test browser. Where a build needs your real logged-in page, which our test browser can't open, the result says "Built. Not yet checked on your page" instead of claiming it works. Test copies have a "Something's wrong?" button that sends what happened on your page back, so it can be fixed from what actually went wrong.
Commitment: whichever models we use, the checks stay ours and stay on.

2. Generation limits
Commitment: your tier's monthly generations are part of the deal you bought and stay as listed on this page. We won't lower them.

3. Firefox, GitHub, code import, debugging
Today:
- Code import: yes. Import a .zip or a folder of an existing Manifest V3 extension (up to 5 MB) and keep building it in PlugThis. It counts as one of your projects.
- GitHub: you can push your extension's code to GitHub. Importing straight from a GitHub repository isn't available.
- Debugging: a "Fix an error" panel for pasted errors and for "nothing happens, no error", the "Something's wrong?" button in test copies, an editable Code tab, and version history to go back.
- Firefox: not available today, and I won't give a date.

4. After the campaign
Commitment: lifetime plans keep their monthly generations and the features in your tier without a mandatory subscription. 
PlugThis is a business that keeps selling after AppSumo, and support is me and the team, as it is now.

Please let me know if you have other questions

questions.title: sanebox.com
questions.comment:
Hey,
is it possible to create something like this:

https://www.sanebox.com

children.comment:
Hi, good question. Some of it yes, some of it no.

The key difference: SaneBox runs on its own server, connected to your mailbox. A PlugThis extension runs inside Chrome, in a side panel next to Gmail, and only while Chrome and Gmail are open.

Probably possible, with the side panel open in Gmail:
- Sort what's in your inbox into "Important" and "Later" in the panel, based on senders you've replied to before (like SaneLater, but shown in the panel).
- Move a sender's mail to a "Later" or "Blocked" label in one click (close to SaneBlackHole, but on your click, not automatic).
- A list of emails you sent that have had no reply after X days (like SaneNoReplies / reminders).
- A "today" summary in the panel of what came in and from whom (a digest you look at, not one emailed to you).
- Remember your choices, so the panel gets better at sorting the senders you've already marked.

None of these are tested yet. Gmail's page is complex and loads in pieces, so each one needs to be built and tried on a real inbox first.

Not possible, for sure:
- Sorting when Chrome is closed or your computer is off.
- Sorting on your phone or in other mail apps (Outlook desktop, Apple Mail).
- Filtering mail on the server before it reaches your inbox.
- A digest emailed to you every morning.
- Acting on its own in the background: the extension acts when you click.

My suggestion: pick the one feature you use most and build that first. Tell me which at [email redacted] and I'll test it on my own Gmail and send you the result and the exact prompt.

How does that sound?

Happy Building :)

With Supabase, Google Sheets, external APIs, MCP servers, and AI models, you could build a cloud-connected solution that handles email sorting, monitoring, and scheduled automations even when Chrome is closed. The extension would simply serve as the interface. So yes, something like SaneBox is technically possible, potentially with even more features! Of course, building this would be more complex

reviews.title: Great secure sharing tool
reviews.comment:
I've been using InPrivy instead of emailing sensitive files, and it's a solid fix for a problem most of us just tolerate. Attachments in email never expire and sit around in inboxes, waiting for a mail admin or the mail hoster to look into your information. InPrivy replaces that with a link that self-destructs after viewing (or on a timer), and I can see exactly when something was opened.

From my research I would say that the solution looks GDPR-complaint, which is important to me. It is built by ivy.mayhem GmbH, a Hamburg-based company, with data stored on German servers (via Hetzner) rather than mixed international infrastructure. The data is AES-256 encrypted, with the company stating it has no access to the encrypted content itself.

From my point of view, this InPrivy lifetime deal is a no-brainer. I would highly recommend it to everyone.

reviews.title: Focused secure sharing without forcing us into a full client portal
reviews.comment:
We use InPrivy for a narrow job: securely sharing information when a full client portal or collaboration platform would be unnecessary.
That focus is what we like about it. Sometimes the right experience is not “create an account, join a workspace, learn a portal.” It is simply “here is the protected information you need, through a controlled sharing surface.” InPrivy fits that use case well.
We also value the ability to use our own branded custom domain for the sharing experience. That makes a focused secure-share tool feel like part of our normal client-facing workflow instead of sending someone to an unrelated third-party URL.
We are intentionally not trying to make InPrivy our document-management system or client-operations platform. We already have broader tools for those jobs. Its value is that it stays comparatively simple and gives us a purpose-built option when secure sharing is the actual requirement.
The biggest improvement for our use would be deeper automation and audit integration: an API/webhook path to create and expire shares, retrieve current state, and read view/access events would make it much easier to use InPrivy inside a governed workflow while keeping the provider as the secure execution layer.
For the focused job it solves, InPrivy has been a useful addition to our stack. I would rather have a small tool that does this job cleanly than force every occasional secure exchange into a much heavier portal.

reviews.title: Adaptive forms are the real differentiator — useful for discovery, not just data collection
reviews.comment:
We use Dashform for project discovery and guided follow-up rather than as another generic form builder.
The feature that made us keep it is the separation between a normal logic-based intake and an AI-assisted follow-up funnel. A fixed form is great when you already know every question you need to ask. In discovery work, however, the useful next question often depends on what the person just told you. Dashform gives us a practical way to test that adaptive layer without replacing the deterministic intake underneath it.
We ran a synthetic discovery proof across multiple scenarios and retained a production Logic Funnel plus a production AI follow-up Funnel afterward. That was important for us: the product had to prove that it could add decision-useful clarification, not simply make a form feel more conversational.
I also like the direction around MCP, webhooks, integrations, analytics, and agent-assisted form creation. Direct create/readback from ChatGPT has been useful, and the product is much more interesting to us because the form can participate in a broader workflow rather than remain an isolated survey.
The main area I want improved is least-privilege integration. During our testing, the MCP/OAuth path exposed rough edges around scope/resource interoperability before the direct ChatGPT path became usable. For an automation-oriented product, the ideal experience would be very explicit read-only vs. write scopes, no unnecessary offline access, and documentation that always matches the live authorization behavior.
I would also love more explainability around adaptive questioning: for each generated follow-up, expose why the system decided the question was worth asking, what missing/ambiguous fact it is trying to resolve, and the stopping reason. That would make the AI funnel easier to audit and safer to use in structured business discovery.
Overall, Dashform has earned a real role in our stack because it solves a different problem from Tally or Google Forms. We still prefer deterministic forms when fixed branching is enough, but when we genuinely need guided clarification, Dashform gives us a useful adaptive layer instead of forcing a human to manually conduct every follow-up conversation.

children.comment:
Thank you for such a thoughtful review and for testing Dashform across multiple discovery scenarios. Hearing that you kept both a Logic Funnel and an AI follow-up Funnel in production means a lot to us.

Your point about asking questions that provide useful clarification captures exactly what we want adaptive discovery to achieve.

We also appreciate your specific suggestions on permissions and explainability. We plan to complete the related MCP improvements by the end of October, including clearer permission boundaries and more consistent authorization behavior and documentation.

The adaptive-questioning explanations are coming sooner: we plan to release them in the next couple of days. These will help you understand why a follow-up was asked, what missing or ambiguous information it aims to clarify, and why the funnel decided to stop.

Thank you for helping us make Dashform more useful and easier to trust in real business workflows. We would love to hear how these improvements work for your discovery process once they are live.

reviews.title: So much more than a basic quiz builder
reviews.comment:
I came to Dashform with a fairly complex assessment in mind. I didn’t want to simply tally a score or put people into generic personality types. I wanted different answers to work together to create a genuinely personalized result across several sections.

I pushed the platform pretty hard, and what impressed me most was how Jake and the team responded when we reached the edges of the existing functionality. They listened to what I was trying to accomplish and actually expanded features to support the more complex backend logic my quiz required.

My 12-question quiz is now live and embedded directly into my website, producing individualized results that would have been difficult to create with other platforms I explored.

The AI-assisted builder makes sophisticated forms possible without needing to be a developer, and the support has been outstanding. Dashform is still evolving, but the team clearly listens to its users and actively improves the product.

If you’re looking for more than a basic form or cookie-cutter quiz, I warmly recommend Dashform. I’m very happy I grabbed the lifetime deal.

reviews.title: More Than a Form Builder, It’s a Workflow Front Door
reviews.comment:
I bought Dashform with a pretty clear vision of how I wanted to use it, and after testing it in real workflows, that vision has been validated.

The moment it clicked for me was when the branching started working the way I expected. Once I understood how Dashform handles branches, groups, and conditions, the product became much more intuitive. More importantly, I stopped seeing it as just a form builder.

For me, Dashform is a workflow front door.

I’ve already used it to build a business systems assessment for my consulting work and a Shift Change Culture Audit for convenience-store managers. The same form can send people to completely different outcomes and next steps based on their answers. That opens up a lot of possibilities for consulting, training, education, community groups, operational audits, course follow-up, and more.

The AI-generated starting point was useful and appreciated, but the real value shows up after the form is built. Lead scoring, response analytics, branching, different endings, and the ability to identify patterns in replies can help determine what services, training, or tools people actually need.

That service-intelligence piece is especially important to me. Instead of guessing what to build next, I can use actual responses to identify recurring problems and opportunities.

I also see strong potential in Dashform’s agent/MCP direction. I have not fully tested that piece yet, so I won’t pretend I have, but the idea that AI agents could discover, understand, and interact with these workflows is a major differentiator.

There was a learning curve, and I initially misunderstood parts of the branching logic. I also ran into a routing issue that the founder investigated and addressed. What stood out to me was that he did not rush out a polished response. He investigated, fixed the issue, and then responded.

The flexibility is what earns the 5 tacos for me. I can see using the same underlying system across consulting, training, C-Store Center, education, and community projects without needing a different platform for each use case.

I came into this already expecting to upgrade to Tier 3. Testing Dashform did not change my mind. It validated the vision and instinct I had when I first saw it.

I’ve seen a lot of software described as “more than a form builder.” In this case, I think that description actually fits.

And if you think you see a use case for Dashform, don’t leave it sitting in your cart too long. My wallet practically opened itself once I saw what I could build with it.

5 tacos.

questions.title: Is this HTML or javascipt form? Will it have to load or embedded instantly on our Wordpress website?

children.comment:
Hi Jake,

Dashform uses a JavaScript embed to display your hosted form inside an iframe on your WordPress page.

You can paste the embed code into a Custom HTML block or your page builder’s HTML widget, provided your WordPress setup allows scripts and iframes.

The embed script loads asynchronously, so the rest of your page can continue loading. The form still needs to load over the network, so it is not an instant, zero-loading-time HTML form. Visitors can complete it directly on your website without being redirected.

questions.title: Can Dashform expose why each adaptive AI follow-up question was asked?
questions.comment: For structured business discovery, we want every adaptive follow-up to have a decision-useful reason rather than conversational curiosity. Can the response/submission data expose a machine-readable reason for each AI-generated follow-up, such as the missing or ambiguous fact it was trying to resolve, plus the final stopping reason? That would make adaptive funnels easier to audit, compare with fixed forms, and use safely in repeatable intake workflows.

children.comment:
Thank you for spelling this out. A follow-up should help resolve something that matters to the discovery process, and its purpose should be available for review.

We are preparing an explainability update that we plan to release in the next couple of days. The intended output includes machine-readable metadata alongside each adaptive follow-up:

• The missing or ambiguous fact the question is intended to clarify.
• The relevant earlier answer or discovery requirement that prompted it.
• A concise explanation of how the clarification supports the assessment.

We also plan to expose a final stopping reason, distinguishing between sufficient information collected, the configured follow-up limit reached, or the respondent ending the conversation with information still unresolved.

These explanations will be separate from the respondent-facing question text, so they can support auditing and downstream workflows without adding clutter to the intake experience.

This capability is part of the upcoming update, so we do not want to imply that the complete metadata is already available today. We will document the output structure and provide a sample submission when it ships.

Thank you again. Your examples are helping us make adaptive discovery more useful for repeatable business workflows.

questions.title: Can MCP OAuth be limited to read-only/per-resource scopes without offline access?
questions.comment: During our integration testing, the live MCP/OAuth path exposed broader/coarser authorization behavior than we expected from the published granular-scope model. For an agent that only needs to list/read forms or submissions, can the live connection request only those exact read scopes and omit offline access? If granular least-privilege scopes are supported now, could you publish a current example for ChatGPT/Codex/Cursor showing the expected consent screen and revoke path?

children.comment:
Thank you for testing this carefully and calling out the mismatch.

The current live MCP connection uses a broader “mcp” scope. It does not yet provide the granular, resource-specific read-only authorization you described. The published documentation should make that limitation clearer.

Offline access is a separate permission for maintaining access through refresh tokens. Our configuration does not include it in the default registration scope, but we still need to verify the complete authorization behavior in each client before promising an end-to-end connection without it.

We plan to complete the related MCP authorization improvements by the end of October. The goal is to let read-only workflows request only the permissions they need, with write access and offline access requested separately when needed.

As part of that release, we will publish tested examples for ChatGPT, Codex, and Cursor covering the requested scopes, resource boundaries, expected consent screen, and revocation steps. We will also document any client-specific limitations.

Until those changes are live and verified, please do not treat the current MCP grant as a narrowly scoped read-only connection.

Thank you again. Your feedback gives us a clear standard to build and test against.

reviews.title: A must-have LTD for any website owner, agency, or ecommerce business! A+++ Super-easy to setup and start using it. An amazing CYA to protect your website and business from legal headaches as well!
reviews.comment:
I’m extremely happy I found WebAbility.io on AppSumo. Good accessibility SaaS tools are surprisingly hard to find, especially ones that are affordable, easy to install, and built for people who do not have a full accessibility team or a huge compliance budget.

The setup was quick and straightforward. You can add it to sites on platforms such as WordPress, Shopify, Wix, and Webflow, or ANY kind of website since you can just drop the snippet right before your </body> tag, and then scan your website for accessibility issues. The widget offers useful visitor controls and accessibility profiles, including screen-reader support, keyboard-navigation improvements, text-to-speech functionality, contrast and visual adjustments, focus support, and options that help people with visual, cognitive, hearing, and motor-access needs.

I also appreciate that it does more than just place a widget on the site. It helps identify issues across content, navigation, forms, and media; automates certain safer fixes where possible; flags items that need human review; and provides an accessibility statement. It is designed to support work toward standards and requirements such as ADA, WCAG 2.1/2.2, Section 508, AODA, EN 301 549, and IS 5568. Of course, no tool should be treated as a guaranteed legal shield or replacement for a proper accessibility review, but this is a very practical layer of support and a strong starting point.

Support has been excellent. Every time I have reached out with a question, the team has been fast, responsive, and helpful in getting things resolved. That matters a lot with a product connected to accessibility and compliance.

This topic is much more important than many website owners realize. There are attorneys and automated systems actively looking for websites that appear to lack accessibility support, and businesses of every size can face complaints, demand letters, or legal costs. Search Google or Reddit for recent accessibility-related legal issues and you will quickly see why this deserves attention. With AI making automated website analysis easier, that risk may only increase.

More importantly, accessibility is not only about reducing risk, it is about making your website usable and welcoming for real people with disabilities. That should be the main reason to take it seriously.

In my view, this is becoming as essential as a cookie banner: something businesses should put in place early instead of waiting until there is a problem. Between the easy installation, scans, automated assistance, custom accessibility statement, useful widget controls, responsive support, and LTD pricing, the value is hard to beat.

Honestly, nearly every AppSumo buyer who owns, manages, builds, or maintains websites should consider owning this tool. 

Thanks SO MUCH to the WebAbility.io Team for making such a fantastic disability tool so easy to deploy on all my websites and to get my fully compliant very quickly!!

I want to love TransferChain Pass. The blockchain-based security and zero-knowledge encryption are top-tier and exactly what I’m looking for in a secure vault. However, there is a massive elephant in the room: Mobile usability is non-existent.

It has been over a year since a mobile solution was announced/teased, and yet we are still waiting. Currently:

The Web Interface is NOT responsive: Attempting to access the vault via a mobile browser is nearly impossible. The UI doesn't scale, making it useless when you're away from a desk.

No Mobile App: For a password manager, mobile access isn't a "bonus feature"—it is a core requirement. We need our passwords on the go for apps, mobile banking, and travel.

Broken Promises: The team mentioned mobile updates long ago, but the roadmap seems to have stalled in favor of other features.

The interface is "basic" enough that it could work well, but until the team makes the web version responsive or releases the dedicated app, this remains a desktop-only tool. In a mobile-first world, this is a deal-breaker for daily use.

Message to the Dev Team: Please, stop adding secondary features and focus on the core experience. A password manager you can't use on your phone is like a car without wheels. We need a concrete release date for the mobile app and an immediate CSS fix for mobile browser responsiveness.

children.comment:
Hi Michael,

First of all, thank you for taking the time to write such a detailed and constructive review. I genuinely appreciate you recognizing our unique security foundation.
Let me address your points in detail.
 
1) SOC 2 & Independent Verification
You are absolutely right that SOC 2 is a widely recognized benchmark.

To clarify, our security controls, logging mechanisms, access management and encryption standards, are already designed in alignment with the SOC 2 Trust Service Criteria. In several areas, particularly around data custody, our zero-knowledge and client-side architecture structurally exceeds the assumptions of traditional centralized systems typically evaluated under SOC 2.
What we have not yet completed is the formal third-party SOC 2 certification process itself. That is a matter of timing and audit engagement, not the absence of controls.

It is also important to clarify that we conduct third-party penetration testing annually in addition to continuous internal security testing.
 
2) GDPR, DPA, and Compliance Documentation
I would also like to also clarify this point:

We do provide a Data Processing Agreement (DPA), and it is contractually referenced in our Services Agreement. Where TransferChain acts as a processor, processing is governed under that DPA in accordance with GDPR requirements.

Our Privacy Policy and Services Agreement (https://transferchain.io/servicesagreement) clearly outline data subject rights and provide contact mechanisms for exercising those rights. We also operate with defined internal procedures for handling GDPR requests within regulatory timelines.

Regarding data transfers and SCCs:
By default, all TransferChain data is stored within the European Union. We are a Swiss-based company operating under European data protection standards, and EU storage is the default configuration.
For enterprise customers, data residency is configurable. 

Organizations may choose:
• EU-based storage
• A specific regional zone
• Private cloud
• Fully on-premise deployment

If data remains entirely within the EU, Standard Contractual Clauses are not required.

If enterprises select a non-EU region, data is strictly stored within the customer-selected zone and does not move outside that environment.

In fully on-premise deployments, data never leaves the customer’s own infrastructure.

Additionally, due to our client-side end-to-end encryption and zero-knowledge architecture, TransferChain does not have access to decrypted customer data. This significantly reduces processing exposure compared to traditional custodial SaaS models.
 
3) Regarding Features
• Mobile apps are currently in active testing.
• We already provide 2FA for the Admin Panel. For end users, each account is protected by mnemonics, which act as a strong security layer since no one can access data without the mnemonic, even if email and password are compromised. That said, we will also introduce 2FA/TOTP for end users.
• We are expanding note types and will continue introducing additional data types.
• Safari and Firefox support are planned for deployment later this year.
• Based on user feedback, we are introducing a major team collaboration upgrade. The redesigned Collections structure will significantly enhance collaboration capabilities.
• Regarding breach detection: Traditional password managers can perform breach monitoring because they store password hashes. In our case, since passwords are client-side encrypted and fragmented, we do not have visibility into hashes either. This has required dedicated R&D. Our approach is to run breach checks on the client side, and we expect to introduce this capability later this year.
 
4) Additional Notes
• You can follow our quarterly product updates here:
https://blog.transferchain.io/tag/product-updates/
We continuously improve both TransferChain Drive & Pass.
• It is also important to note that we are fundamentally a security and privacy company. We work with large enterprises managing highly sensitive data across sectors such as finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and defense. In our industry, discretion is part of the security model.
• We can always improve support, and we take that seriously. We provide live chat and also arrange calls with customers when needed. Please feel free to reach out to [email redacted] and we would be happy to review anything together with our team.
 
As you mentioned, TransferChain runs on a unique protocol. Because of this architecture, adding features sometimes requires additional engineering time, as nothing is built on a traditional centralized architecture. This is because the utmost priority for us is the security and privacy of your data.

If some of the points above provide additional clarity, we would be grateful if you would consider updating your review to reflect the corrected information. We genuinely value fair and accurate feedback.

Thank you again for your thoughtful feedback.
Kind regards,
Mert

children.comment:
Hi CCPLInd,

Thank you for your review and for choosing TransferChain specifically for its security. That’s exactly what we are built for.

First of all, you are absolutely right. When a password is filled on a login page, the browser (Chrome, Edge, etc.) may show its own “Save password?” prompt. This popup is generated entirely by the browser, not by TransferChain. Every password manager has to deal with this behaviour, and most of them do not block it at all.

We have just implemented a new upgrade in our browser extension that will:
disable the browser’s built-in “save password” prompts and instead show TransferChain’s own prompt apply this improvement not only in Chrome, but across all major browsers
This change will be included in our next extension release, so your users will no longer see the browser’s save-password popup during login. It is also important to highlight that this is a user-facing security layer, not a protocol-level security mechanism.

How your passwords are actually protected at TransferChain. Regardless of the browser prompt, your passwords are protected at all times by our patent-pending protocol:

Client-side and end-to-end encryption:
Your passwords are end-to-end encrypted (and split into fragments) on your device before they ever touch the internet.

Data fragmentation and distributed storage:
Encrypted data is split into fragments and stored across multiple storage locations in a distributed manner. No single provider, ever holds all of the chunks together.

Blockchain-based authorization:
Every time you save or access your passwords you're authorized through the blockchain network, preventing unauthorized access and providing an immutable system.

Because of this design, no one can access your passwords unless you grant them the rights. This includes our engineers, our servers, or any storage providers. For example, all traditional password managers store and keep password hashes, but in TransferChain your password is first encrypted end-to-end on your device and then fragmented into small chunks. As a result, there is no trace of a full hash stored anywhere. In other words, yes, with TransferChain you benefit from the highest protocol-level security.

At the same time, we know that backend security alone is not enough. Just as you pointed out, we continuously improve the user-facing side as well, and disabling the browser’s password saving prompt is one of these improvements.

We really appreciate your attention to detail, your focus on security.

Kind Regards,

reviews.title: Great support
reviews.comment:
With most cookie plugins ditching their free plans and requiring annual renewals, I decided to buy a lifetime plan for Consently. I installed it on a few websites without any issues at all.

Seriously, especially with WordPress, the process is very simple. Add the plugin to the site, add the site to Consently, create an API key, add the API key to WordPress, set up the banner, and run the scan. Then review the cookies it found, add them as needed, and confirm that the categories are correct.

But then I ran into a problem with one particular installation where the site had hundreds of pages and hosting resources were limited. The scan kept completing with warnings, saying the crawler couldn’t access the pages even though it could read the sitemap and see that those pages existed.

I worked with both the hosting company and Consently, running support tickets with each and sharing their replies back and forth until we finally got to the bottom of it. We whitelisted Consently’s crawlers, adjusted the caching and CDN settings, and gave the cached pages time to build up before running the scan again. This time, the crawl completed successfully.

Both the hosting company and Consently provided awesome support and stuck with me until the issue was completely sorted out. I highly recommend Consently for handling the cookie consent requirements that websites have to deal with in so many countries.

Thank you so much for the detailed review, and for sticking with us through the troubleshooting. We’re glad the whitelisting and caching changes got your scan completing successfully. We really appreciate your patience in coordinating between us and your host, and we’re happy you chose the lifetime plan. 

Please reach out anytime if you need anything else!

reviews.title: Not usable for terms & conditions
reviews.comment:
I answered every question in the Policy Generator to create Terms and Conditions for our SaaS, and the output was unusable.

Some of what it produced:

- "We offer a [object Object]-day free trial" appears three times - a raw code error that made it into the legal text.
- Governing law, jurisdiction and the company's state of organization all read "United States," which isn't a legal jurisdiction.
- Many section headings are blank, including Amendment, Content Removal, Service Warranties and International Data Transfers, and a Data Processing Agreement link points to nothing.
- Two sections are both numbered 9, and the survival clause cites the wrong sections.

It would take longer to find and fix everything than to write the terms from scratch. For legal documents, a generator that fails like this is worse than none, because you can't trust what it left in. 

I don't know how it does with Cookies or Privacy Policy because I stopped using it and refunded it after the T&C failures.

children.comment:
Hi, 

Thank you for such a detailed review, and we are sorry the Terms & Conditions generator let you down. You were right on every point. Your examples let us find and fix each problem, and   the fixes are now live:    

"[object Object]-day free trial": fixed. The trial length now shows correctly ("We offer a 14-day free trial") and appears once, in the Free Trials section.

"United States" as the jurisdiction: the State/Province field in your company details now lists real states. The Terms now say, for example, "organized under the laws of Delaware, United States", and governing law and jurisdiction use the state too.

Blank headings: Amendment, Content Removal, International Data Transfers, and the DPA link were blank because the generator never asked the questions behind them. It now asks, and the DPA link uses the URL you enter. Service Warranties has been removed. Any section that doesn't apply to your answers is now left out entirely rather than shown as an empty heading.

Numbering: the duplicate section 9 is gone, the survival clause cites the correct sections, and subsections are numbered without gaps.

We also fixed a few related issues we found while testing, such as free services getting billing clauses they don't need. 

If you'd like to try again, open the Policy Generator, check that your company details include your state, and click Regenerate on Terms & Conditions. Documents generated before the fix don't update on their own. 

If anything still looks wrong, please email us at [email redacted], and we'll look at it right away.    

Thanks again for taking the time to spell this out. It made the product better.

Himel, 
Consently Support Team.

reviews.title: Bug report in, feature out. In less than 2 weeks. That earns some tacos!
reviews.comment:
I build WordPress sites for clients, most on theme.co's Pro theme with the Cornerstone builder. Consently's plugin conflicted with and errored out the builder. Every element threw a markup error when Consently was active. That's a dealbreaker. I'm in the builder daily.

Emailed support. Was expecting the usual "we'll pass it along." Al Amin replied the next day asking for screenshots. Himel came back with a workaround through Tag Manager. That didn't fit me or my clients since we run GA4 directly. I said so. Instead of leaving it there, they put it on the roadmap. Two days later it was in testing. Nine days after that, Himel emailed to say they'd added a data-exclude-paths attribute to the embed script. Dropped it in my child theme, builder works, banner works. Done.

I've bought a lot of deals on this site over the last decade. Support that listens, keeps you posted without being asked, and turns a bug report into a product change in under two weeks is rare. Taco worthy. Al Amin and Himel, thank you.

The product itself: easy setup, easy to customize the banner to match the site, clean and simple. No bloat, no gimmicks. Exactly what a consent tool should be.

One thing to know for other WordPress builder Sumolings: the exclusion attribute only works with the embed script, not the WordPress plugin (yet). I deployed via child theme. Super simple.

Glad I bought it. Now rolling it out to client sites.

children.comment: This made our day! Passing it along to Al Amin and Himel. Really glad we could actually fix this instead of just working around it. Thanks for pushing back on the Tag Manager option and for the detailed writeup for other WordPress builder users — that'll help a lot of people.

questions.title: elementor's built-in recaptcha support?

children.comment:
Hi, 
Elementor’s built-in CAPTCHA is primarily a form-level spam protection feature for Elementor Forms. WP Captcha is a broader security plugin with many more CAPTCHA-related features.

For example, Elementor will help you protect only its forms, whereas WP Captcha allows you to place CAPTCHA on any form you want.

Also, Elementor only offers Google reCAPTCHA v2/v3, while WP Captcha gives you reCAPTCHA v2/v3, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, Icon CAPTCHA, and built-in CAPTCHA.

As the latest addition, WP Captcha offers AI analysis and reports, where AI will analyze your site and suggest everything that needs doing, as well as keep an eye on your site

WP Captcha also allows you to use country blocking, manage blacklists/whitelists, and manage your licenses if you're an agency.

reviews.title: A Permanent Tool in my WordPress toolbox!
reviews.comment:
My agency manages and hosts 300+ WordPress websites for clients large and small. We've configured the usual automated server-wide backups, daily server-level db backups, rsync for offloading site backups to private cloud storage, etc. - all in an effort to minimize our reliance on WordPress plugins.

Sure, some "hands-on" clients feel as though they simply must install a WP backup plugin, so they can visually SEE it running (and subsequently fill up their server's disks with outdated backup files for us to remove when they forget...).

But what about when they login to wp-admin and get prompted to update WordPress, a plugin, or a theme to the latest version. And click it the "Update" button with nary a thought how it may affect their live website. Or when it's Taco Tuesday, and an hour before lunch, I'm starving, cranky, and distracted...and forget that I'm not on the staging server, I'm running updates on the PRODUCTION server! 

The stress of unraveling update/installation errors, incompatibilities, and panicked theme code comparison is now a thing of a past for WordPress websites! WP Reset Pro calmly stays in the shadows, automatically creating snapshots prior to any WP core or plugin update. Plus, it saves space by backing up only the affected files/db tables and makes it a breeze to quickly rollback to a known good state if a  WP or PHP error/incompatibility occurs. 

In these scenarios, WP Reset Pro functions beautifully as an extra safety net as part of our overall backup/version control strategy. It quite literally helps me sleep better, and I'm very thankful that the talented folks at WP Reset and AppSumo teamed up for this excellent lifetime deal!

children.comment:
Hi, 
Wow, that's one heck of a review, thank you very much!! :)

reviews.title: Just woooow! Buy it, believe me!
reviews.comment:
WP Reset is not a backup plugin, it's so much better than that!
Included in my hosting, I have an automated backup system so I thought that Wp Reset was not for me, that it was useless.
It's complicated to understand how useful this tool can be.
Let me explain you the 4 tools included into it :

First of all, there is the "reset tool" which gives its name to this tool. For me, it's a useful option but much less than the others. It will allow you to do a total or partial reset of your site, your plugins, your theme, ... It will also allow you to clean some directories or to go back to a previous version of wordpress.

The second tool proposed by WP reset is the snapshots tool. This one is a real killer!
Indeed, by activating it to run automatically, it will allow you to make a kind of incremental backup (like MacOs Time Machine) at each modification / activation / deactivation / deletion / addition of plugin or theme. I don't know about you, but I don't systematically bother making a manual backup when I install or test a new extension. Don't worry, the tool will do it for you now!

The third tool is even more awesome for all those who, like me, often install wordpress sites : collections.
You will be able to configure collections of plugins and themes that can be installed with a single click. Unlike the same option on Softacoulous, you will be able to add your own zip files and even fill in your license numbers so that the pro versions can be installed with a single click.
It's an incredible time saver!

The last tool is just indispensable: the "emergency recovery script".
This tool will install a script that will work outside of your wordpress environment and will therefore not be sensitive in case of an attack.
It will allow you to restore your site in case of hack, deletion of files, databases, users, ... in a few clicks!

**UPDATE**
Due to a smooth refund experience of mcp, I have changed my rating from 1Star to 4Star. Unfortunately the product didn't fulfill my needs. Having said that I am sure the product can be a good fit for others. 

The native website builder is good and actually gave an aesthetic design, but it consumes a lot of credits.

______________________________________

I had high hopes for this but unfortunately I experienced some issues:

> Only after one purchases the tool is it revealed that MCP is not included and can be purchased for an additional fee.  I contacted customer service to ask what is going on - who provide you with a "separate 49$ pay link". 

> Opaque credit system: I made an entire website on my end using ChatGPT, and then just needed to publish it via Grigora. This operation alone deducted a whopping 15.000 AI credits which is a lot!! I checked the entire trace and the only build operation given to Grigora was to "create an empty html shell", that could serve as a shell for a pre-built page I wanted to upload.

> After having transferred the entire website, I wanted to try and use the Grigora native website builder to make some tweaks. But the builder couldn't recognize any of the work even though I myself could see the webpage in the Grigora editor. Even after multiple tries it said "The current page is an empty shell, with nothing to repair. Can you add the reader HTML or point me to where it is".

children.comment:
Hello,

I understand your concern about AI credit consumption, and I appreciate you sharing your feedback. However, I'd like to explain how we've structured our AI credit system and why.

1. AI Credits and Lifetime Access

Let's take Tier 5 as an example. It includes approximately 1 million AI credits per month, which is enough to create 60+ websites from scratch, depending on their complexity. These credits are replenished every month, so you can continue building new websites without purchasing additional credits.

Offering truly unlimited AI usage under a lifetime deal is economically challenging because every AI operation has a real cost. We need to balance generous usage limits with a sustainable business model that allows us to support our customers for the long term.

2. Website Creation and Editing Costs

Currently, creating a new website costs approximately 15,000 AI credits, while an edit costs around 1,000 credits. Even if you want to rebuild or significantly modify an existing website, you can make substantial changes within the editing cost, depending on the scope of the changes.

Regarding your example of creating an empty HTML shell, I understand why the credit consumption might seem high for something relatively simple. Our current pricing is based on the website creation workflow rather than just the amount of HTML generated.

3. Our Long-Term Commitment

We've been working in this industry for the past three years, and our goal is to build a product that customers can rely on for life. Maintaining reliable hosting, infrastructure, and product development requires a sustainable business model. Our pricing and credit limits are designed with that long-term commitment in mind.

4. Improving AI Efficiency

AI models are becoming more affordable and efficient, and we intend to pass those improvements on to our customers wherever possible. We've continuously improved Grigora over the past year, and you can review our changelog to see how much the platform has evolved.

We genuinely want to make AI website building more accessible and affordable. Your feedback is valuable, and we'll continue looking for ways to reduce credit consumption while delivering better results.

Thank you for being part of Grigora and helping us improve the product.

Best regards,  
Pratik
