reviews.title: Super website builder.
reviews.comment:
I used to host my site on WordPress. For sure, WordPress can give you all the bells and whistles you need to build anything from your first to your 500th website. But the cost starts to ratchet up once you factor in additional plugins and hosting. 

So, I decided to try the Grigora lifetime deal a while back. It's a pretty intuitive website builder, and it includes newsletter capabilities, though I'm still using VBOUT for this because I don't think Grigora can generate nurture sequences yet. Hopefully that's in the pipeline, because I find VBOUT really unintuitive and clunky, even with Claude helping me. 

Grigora also has an MCP connector that lets me use Claude to create and add webpages and posts. So I can use the built-in AI to help generate webpages, or I can use my Claude subscription, which I tend to do because it can generate posts by referring to my Karpathy-style wiki on my hard drive. 

Recently, Grigora added new SEO and GEO analysis to help identify issues; it is in beta but already helpful. 

The AI features are useful. You can easily link pages, and it can also help generate alt image text. Grigora AI can also generate blog posts (though I haven't used it for that), and it has an AI image generator, which I also haven't tried in a while because I use Nano Banana with my Gemini Workspace account. That's less convenient, but it helps me maintain brand consistency. The AI tools can also generate FAQs or turn a video into a blog post for you. 

The team is very responsive to feedback and super helpful when you contact them about issues with your sites. They're also frequently building new features and improving the user interface.

It was a great deal when I bought it, and it still is.

I just wish the Grigora team would use their AI to help work on their own copy and training, because I think it could help with identifying benefits rather than features and improve their marketing. Right now, it's a super little gem but it's more of a secret than it ought to be.

Client Approvals: Tradies require a formal quote to secure budget approval from their clients before buying.

Custom Trade Discounts: Our sales team manually reviews the order volume and Business Number to apply the correct trade discount.

Heavy Freight: Concrete sleepers require delivery via a forklift and trailer. Shipping costs must be calculated manually post-submission.

Can Grigora's cart be configured so customers submit an order purely as a quote request without paying?

children.comment:

Grigora doesn't currently support converting the standard e-commerce checkout directly into a quote-request flow with no upfront payment.

However, you can use a custom form to collect the required details, such as products, quantities, Business Number, and delivery address. Your sales team can then review the request, apply the appropriate trade discounts, calculate freight costs, and send a formal quote manually.

With our lead notification system, your team will receive automated notifications whenever someone submits a form on your website, allowing you to follow up and manage the quoting process.

Best regards,  
Pratik

questions.comment:
1. Does this support multi currency? 
Is stripe and PayPal easy to connect? Or require website dev/coding knowledge? 
2. Ability to send order confirmation email? 
3. How easy is it to migrate from Webwave to you? Esp for non developer or coder? 
4. Can it work with print on demand as well as Etsy or other platforms such as kofi? 
5. Membership? Donation based purchase? Course sales? What file types can be uploaded as digital downloads (would like to sell 3d model files) 
6. Can I set up shipping profiles, shipping restrictions to certain countries?

children.comment: Sorry one more question- is it possible to edit site on the go, such as from my phone?

Hello,

Here are the answers to your questions:

- Multiple currencies: We don't support multiple currencies at the moment.
- PayPal and Stripe: Both are easy to connect. You just need to add your API keys and configure webhooks. No coding or developer knowledge is required.
- Order confirmations: Automated order confirmation emails are supported.
- Webwave migration: You can export your website from Webwave and ask our AI to migrate the content and design. It can handle most of the work. If you need help with anything specific, reach out to our support team, and I'll guide you through it.
- Print-on-demand: Not supported at the moment.
- Memberships: Membership-based selling isn't supported. However, you can offer donation-style purchases using a "Pay What You Want" option.
- Courses and LMS: We don't currently support selling courses or LMS functionality.
- Digital downloads: You can attach the files you want to sell as digital downloads.
- Shipping: You can configure shipping profiles for different countries, but restricting orders based on specific countries isn't currently supported.
- Customer categorization: Filtering customers by category isn't available yet.
- Mobile responsiveness: Most AI-generated websites are responsive by default. If anything needs adjustment, you can simply prompt the AI to fix it.
- Changing templates and designs: Grigora isn't like WordPress, where you can switch templates whenever you want. Each website is custom-built, so changing templates isn't straightforward. However, you can ask the AI to modify the design and layout to suit your needs.
- Unlimited products: On the lower-tier plans, you can purchase the $49 add-on to unlock unlimited products. There's no minimum tier requirement; you can choose Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3, and the add-on will unlock unlimited products.
- Custom fonts: You can upload your font directly in the chat and ask the AI to use it.
- Mobile editing: Yes, you can comfortably prompt our AI Website Builder from your phone.

I hope this clarifies everything. If you have any other questions, feel free to reach out!

Best regards,  
Pratik

reviews.title: The best product needs more improvement.
reviews.comment:
These add-ons provide a lot of useful features. However, I do have a few criticisms:

1. Support
Many people claim the support is good, but my experience was quite different. I didn't receive any email replies from the support team, even after reaching out to Appsumo for help. As of now, I still haven't heard back from the developer. It's important to have fast and accurate support in this business, and I noticed that many others are disappointed with the lack of responses. I hope this issue gets more attention.

2. URL Authorization
As someone who can use these addons on unlimited sites, I noticed a feature that allows me to activate the plugin based on a specific URL I enter in the dashboard. However, I found out that this URL activation only applies to automatic updates and doesn't lock the widgets. This means that once the pro plugin is installed, all the pro elements become available, regardless of whether a license number is entered or the website URL is registered. This can be a problem because anyone who installs the pro plugin can use it on any website and access all the pro elements without needing to register. My suggestion is that if a URL is not activated or removed from the authorization list on the dashboard, the pro elements should remain locked and inaccessible.

3. Web Bugs
I noticed some issues with your website. Myself and other users often encounter unrelated websites opening when we type your web URL, like this one: https://tuto.ateliers-achats.fr/Wnu61Q9o. Additionally, I found some irregularities in the Google search results, such as links with Chinese writing. It's important to check and fix these problems.

While these addons offer a wide range of functionality, there are a few areas that require improvement, as I wrote above. I give you 5 tacos because your product is really good, and I believe that you will continue to improve the quality of this product and service as well.

As soon as I installed the plugin I could see there was a great bunch of really useful features that were either not found elsewhere, better than others or great that's all under one plugin rather than having to install multiple ones. So far everything is working as it should.

Additionally, and this one the main benchmarks I use to determine the value of any plugin, the customer and tech support are not only quick to respond but listen to your ideas and questions. When I submitted a feature request, I didn't just a polite reply that the will add it to their list. Instead, I got a follow up email asking me some very specific questions about what I would want, what it would be used for, and how I would use it. This clearly shows how serious they are about continually trying to improve their product to meet the needs of its users.

Money well spent.

reviews.title: Great potential, but suffers from bugs
reviews.comment:
I went all in on this one knowing how useful it could be. Unfortunately, Editor.do does not deliver. Not yet at least. There are serious bugs but what's worse, bug reports go unanswered. Something as simple as incorrectly set or missing caching policies for images means that to replace images, you need to rename them. The editor requires manual upload of files. Something that breaks and requires a browser reload. The UI feels unpolishes and so does the UI text. It's an unfinished product which I hope they'll give more attention to fix some of the most glaring issues.
I'd love to be able to hook this up to a repo on Gitlab or Github and simply have it pull changes so I can manage a website without using the browser. 
To the founders: I'd be happy to offer feedback and recommendations.

reviews.title: A cloud-backed coding platform!
reviews.comment: As someone coming from an MS-DOS, Turbo Pascal/Turbo C IDE background of some 35 years ago, I value having my source files backed up to a hopefully secure cloud. I found the editor preferences difficult to set and not intuitive. For instance, I want to disable dark mode, but can't figure out how or where! Also, are there any keyboard/keystroke shortcuts available while editing, I can't tell? I do like the keyword syntax highlighting and that multiple languages are supported. A printable PDF cheatsheet with editor/keystroke shortcuts and settings would be helpful. As several reviewers have stated, this version is a good start, but lacking in several basic user UI needs. Support is good, and they are quick to reply.

reviews.title: There's no product development, it doesn't seem like it. It stopped two years ago.
reviews.comment:
1) Default templates
These aren't very nice templates. They look very archaic.
I feel like they're old examples of websites that existed 10 years ago.
They lack the modern look of current websites.
Artificial intelligence can now generate nicer ones.
A few really nice templates would be useful so I can start with something nice.

2) The file management method and the lack of any form of external file upload (e.g., FTP).

3) I lack support for PHP and a SQLite file database.

4) AI
The AI ​​BYOK assistant works, but it seems independent. It's just a simple chat.
When I ask it to change something in the file code, it says it doesn't have access.
This seems unnecessary if it doesn't correct the files in Editor.do.

5) No external backup system. If I'm working on this, I'd also like to automatically backup, for example, to an external FTP.

6) No response to questions on Appsumo. Occasionally, only.

.
Maybe one day I'll change my mind when I see it develop.

reviews.title: Nice product for small projects
reviews.comment:
This is a useful tool for building small web tools and static pages. I wouldn’t use it for a full website project, but it works well for smaller tasks.

What I really dislike is the lack of support. I've reached out multiple times but never received any reply.

Another issue is that you cannot drag and drop or rearrange files and folders in the navigation bar. You also can't move files into folders 🤦🏻‍♂️ Drag and drop should be a core function.

The AI assistant doesn’t work. I tried it with multiple GPT keys, and it seems broken. Even if it worked, it would be very limited since it’s just a simple input-output AI with no connection to the code.

Drag-and-drop website builder feels useless (in my opinion)

Overall, it’s nice, but the lack of support and missing core features make it frustrating to use.

reviews.title: Not what it appears
reviews.comment:
I was hoping this tool could rival codepen or vscode.dev but instead it is exactly like a modern geocities.  

Editor.do is a basic tool that reminds me of putting notepad++ on the web. In addition to a basic notepad it provides urls to serve your site, but hosted projects can only be HTML, CSS, js, and media files. You're allowed to have other files but they cannot be served. 

You are not able to create a project without a valid domain or using up one of your allotted subdomains. I am not allowed to use this tool for editing files unless I have it tied to one of my 5 *free* subdomains. This means no backups, archiving, or dummy projects. 

The way files are maintained is really where this tool fails hard. You are not able to move files into different directories. You cannot drag and drop files to upload. You cannot sort your files at all. You cannot change file types. You are limited in what file types you can add (SQL, htaccess, typescript, manifest, etc are not allowed). There's no auto save, github sync, versioning, trash/recovery, undo/redo, or creating .bak(backup) files. It's also not possible to search across files or for file names. 

It's not mentioned anywhere that AI requires BYOK unfortunately and only from OpenAI.

It has some nice looking templates and the admin dashboard caught my eye. It also allows for quick importing of libraries. 

There's a bug where saving MD files crashes the site and logs you out.

I will say on a positive note the tool is visually appealing and makes for easy storage and editing sites. I'm using it to edit my php site on the go. Just means I am copying and pasting or moving files to where my php site is actually hosted. Also switching between projects is fast and smooth and open files are remembered.

reviews.title: The Best AI Dark Mode for WP (With a Few Minor Tweaks)
reviews.comment: DarkMySite is a game-changer for WordPress, offering a sleek, "set it and forget it" solution that instantly modernizes any layout with AI-powered color inversion. The performance optimization is impressive, keeping the plugin lightweight without dragging down my Core Web Vitals. However, it’s not without minor flaws; the learning curve for custom CSS overrides can be steep if the AI misses a specific element, and I’ve noticed occasional glitches with certain third-party slider plugins that require manual tweaking. Despite these small hurdles, the ability to replace images specifically for dark mode and the professional floating switch designs make it an incredible value, especially if you grabbed the AppSumo lifetime deal. It is easily the most polished dark mode tool available in 2026.

reviews.title: Nice plugin for WordPress
reviews.comment: I evaluated the plugin on WordPress 6.8 before using it in production. Very easy to install and configure, it has many advanced settings. I evaluated it in a BerqWP and LiteSpeed Cache environment without any apparent problems. I highly recommend this product, which is also offered at a very reasonable price. Is there a changelog? Are any updates planned? But for now, it's a great little gem! Go for it!

The toggle in the menu is not working, and there's no way to put the shortcode on the menu either. And after sending these questions through their email, I'm still waiting for their feedback.

reviews.title: What a great deal.
reviews.comment:
Great is not really a strong enough word sometimes. This deal is more than great for WordPress developers, price-wise. Sure, as an agency I wish there was an unlimited sites stacking level, but 100 sites for $18 - that's EIGHTEEN CENTS per site - that's a stupendous, amazing, shocking, huge, crazy can't miss, great deal. 

Furthermore, I suppose holding back an unlimited option helps to keep the developers selling the plugin, which keeps them eating, which only helps to keep them developing this plugin! So that's a sort of bittersweet bonus to me, but a bonus nonetheless!

No matter how it ends, I know I've paid much more for many less beneficial or user-pleasing plugins. Even ones the developer abandoned. STILL, I would have kicked myself had I missed this deal.

But I didn't miss the deal. I got in with two codes and I'm super-excited by the features, the level of customization, the options, and just the fact that DarkMySite gives my clients another upgrade to make their visitors happy. It also just seems to be a quality plugin.

I don't know what more I could say to to get you to jump on this opportunity, so I'll just say it again... 

This is a great deal! Why kick yourself later for missing out?

reviews.title: An excellent product at a price that is hard to believe...
reviews.comment:
I have been a WordPress user for a very long time and I have two rules:

1. Install as few plugins as possible
2. In a production environment, installing only top-quality, proven plugins

At first, I didn't expect much from DarkMySite, but out of curiosity, I tested it quite intensively, because I need the dark mode functionality on several sites where themes do not have such functionality built-in.

Summary: I am very impressed with this plugin!

1. It is light and fast (plugin file is only less than 400kB)

2. It has a very nice UI and professionally built backend based on AJAX technology

3. It has a very large amount of functionality and customization - whatever you want in dark mode area

4. Dark mode works great right out of the box, but also it can be personalized in any way you can imagine

In short: take it while you can - an excellent, high-quality product almost for free.

REDEEMING CODES: 
Bad: I bought 3 codes and wasn't able to redeem them myself. 
Good: I submitted a ticket and the WP Dev team took care of it quickly.

PLUGIN ITSELF:
I really like this plugin. When I purchased it, I wasn't aware of the required work needed to setup the auto posting to social media. It's ALOT of work. Which really blows when you start looking at providing this plugin as part of your services to clients. It was fairly easy to setup Facebook and Linked In. Twitter is another story. I'm also shocked that Instagram isn't included. 

Overall, I'm glad that I've purchased this plugin, but I seriously hope that the implementation becomes easier for clients. I also hope that they can include IG as it's now a product of Facebook. 

I would've given 5 tacos, but it's really a pain to setup those social media integrations. Which technically brings it (for me) down to 3, but the plugin UI / UX brought it back up to a 4 for me.

children.comment: Instagram will not allow any 3rd party auto publishing tools -- their API restricts it specifically. They want to be a mobile only platform. One possible work around would be set your facebook account to relay all posts to instagram automatically so that you c an schedule posts to FB and then have those posts CC'd to IG basically.

reviews.title: Very cheap deal, limited, unclear Node.js support
reviews.comment:
This is a very cheap price, AppSumo got a great deal here. If you need a domain name, you are effectively getting the rest for free.  So I was unsure how to rate this.  I chose 3 tacos because I am unsure if this provides enough benefit for my use-case versus spending more with more long-term stability.

One thing about the credit card requirement. I'm not clear on what happened re. card details. It accepted an address without asking for the card number. saying my card was stored. So I don't know what details Hostinger has. The account / billing information doesn't say what card is stored.  Will ask their support, but odd process.

For those interested in web app deployment, the deal page explicitly states Node.js, but the plan itself doesn't list it. It only lists frameworks built with Node.js. I got it working as I could add an Express.js layer and select 'Express'. So not sure what would happen if you are not using a framework.  I don't think Hostinger are helping themselves with this lack of clarity.

To connect web apps, via GitHub or Zip, you need a very specific app setup. Without that, it fails, with zero information as to why it failed. So that was a lot of trial and error and back and forwards with their documentation.

For the hosting, if you are used to cPanel or Plesk, Hossinger dashboard is  limited. 

If you need a domain name or need one-click setup, this is a really good deal, for you would be an easy 5 tacos. 

One thing I would have like to do but it is not an option is add users with restricted access permissions. This is not possible. You can add users as Admin or Collaborators, but they see everything and can change anything. 

If you are used to setting things up yourself, deploying web apps or AI agents elsewhere, or familiar with popular website hosting panels, this may be too limited, even at this price.

reviews.title: Kind of great, but still a work in progress
reviews.comment:
THE BASIC CONCEPT IS GREAT

o Give it a Google sheet, whose cells refer to a collection of images, Google Docs, etc. 
o Choose a website template.
o And it will pull together the referenced resources and create an attractive, useful, 1-page website based upon the chosen template.

STRENGHTS AND WEAKNESSES OF THIS APPROACH

The strength of this approach is that you can quickly and easily create and update attractive, functional 1-page websites.  The weakness is that someone else has made all the design and layout decisions for you, and very litte customization thereof is possible.

They say that you can fully control styles with custom CSS, and they give you a big text box where you can paste whatever CSS you want, but they don't document their CSS classes and selectors, so in effect very little custom stying is possible.

THE TEMPLATES ARE UNEVEN

Of the 29 templates, some are very useful.  For example the Documentation template will compile a list of Google Docs into an online "book", where each Google Doc is a chapter.  And the Blog template looks pretty useful.

On the other hand, some are not really useful, such as the eCommerce template, which doesn't handle sales tax, and applies the same, fixed shipping charge to all purchases.

And there are some that are in-between, such as the Table template, which produces a very attractive table layout, but only of four columns.

And the Landing Page template is totally useless.  It basically gives you your own copy of the Sheetany home page, but doesn't let you create your own content.

GETTING STARTED IS HARDER THAN IT SHOULD BE

The basic process of creating a 1-page website from a template is fast and easy — once you learn all the tricks.  But they don't have a simple explanation of all these tricks, so it took a lot of frustrating experimentation, and some back and forth with support, to be able to figure it out.

THE DOCUMENTATION IS LACKING

Of the 29 templates, there are only explanations in the online documentation for 14 of them, of which six are actual explanations, and the rest just contain copies of the explanation for the Waitlist template, so are effectively meaningless.

ONE SPECIAL PAGE, PLUS MULTIPLE GOOGLE-DOC PAGES?

An architectural oddity is that after using a template to create a 1-page website, you can add additional pages to the website by specifying one or more Google Docs, each of which will become an additional page in the website.  So you end up with one "fancy" homepage, maybe a blog, and an arbitrary number of additional "plain" pages that are generated from Google Docs.

CLOSING COMMENTS

There is a lot more that could be said, but the above gives the big picture.

In my opinion, for those  who want to be able to create clean, attractive, functional 1-page websites, such as a documentation site, or a blog, but don't know how to design, code and test them, and if Sheetany has a working template that fulfills their needs, then Sheetany is an excellent product, and the lifetime deal is an incredible value.  I bought tier-3.

We truly appreciate the way you highlighted both what works well and what still needs improvement. Your feedback is extremely valuable to us, especially regarding documentation, template consistency, customization flexibility, and the overall onboarding experience.

Sheetany was built with the goal of helping people create clean, useful, and attractive websites from simple data sources without needing to design or code everything from scratch. At the same time, we fully understand that there are still areas where the product can be clearer, more flexible, and more polished.

We take your comments seriously and will use them to guide our upcoming improvements. Better documentation, clearer template instructions, more practical templates, improved customization options, and a smoother getting started experience are all areas we will continue to work on.

Thank you again for your support, your honesty, and for choosing the Tier 3 lifetime deal. Feedback like yours helps us make Sheetany better for everyone, and we are committed to improving the product step by step!

reviews.title: Great for creating web content directly from Google Docs and Sheets
reviews.comment: I recently gave Sheetany a shot, and honestly, it just works. For those blogs with other content management systems (CMS), you likely know the effort of not just writing but also spending excessive time arranging individual elements to make your posts visually appealing and formatted well. Sheetany addresses this issue by transforming your Google Docs and Sheets into an actual website or blog, and I truly value this simplicity. reviews.title: A good security addition to our agency stack and a quick reality check on licensing
reviews.comment:
WP Login Lockdown is a good addition to our agency tech stack. The centralised dashboard makes managing multiple client installations painless, the interface is clean, and the Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) works wel. In an environment where brute-force login attempts and automated credential stuffing are constant threats, having frictionless, reliable 2FA deployed across client sites is an absolute no-brainer.

It is surprising to see highly upvoted reviews criticising this product due to licensing limitations and support response times. Those criticisms stem from a fundamental misunderstanding of both commercial software licensing and standard agency operations.

How Agency & White-Label Licences Actually Work
There is a distinct legal difference between an agency white-label licence and Master Resell Rights (MRR):

The Agency Model: An agency licence permits you to rebrand the plugin and install it across client sites as part of a comprehensive service offering, such as website design, secure hosting, or ongoing maintenance and care plans. The client pays for your managed service and security oversight; the white-labelling simply ensures a clean, bespoke experience without third-party vendor clutter.

The Resale Fallacy: No software company sells a lifetime licence that allows a purchaser to turn around and resell individual licence keys, setup standalone purchase links, or distribute raw downloads to the public. You cannot buy a stock photograph and sell it on your own stock library; you integrate it into a client project. Expecting distribution rights to run an independent software resale business off the back of an agency tier is completely detached from industry reality.

A Realistic Look at Support Turnaround
Complaining that technical support responded in "a few hours" is equally misguided. In the software industry, standard developer Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for non-emergency tickets typically sit between 24 and 48 hours. Receiving a direct, effective resolution within several hours is well above industry standard, it is an agile, responsive development team that deserves applause, not docked stars.

The plugin delivers precisely what it advertises: robust login security, rock-solid 2FA, intuitive remote dashboard management, and fair, transparent licensing terms that protect both the developer and the agencies building value on top of it. Highly recommended for any serious web professional.

reviews.title: Huge Time Investment, But Licensing Limits Make It Hard to Recommend
reviews.comment:
I went into this purchase with high expectations because the white-label and rebranding features looked perfect for my business model. I spent hours setting everything up, honestly most of an entire weekend, customizing branding, configuring settings, and preparing it for client use.

Only after all that effort did I discover important licensing restrictions that significantly reduce its value:

You can’t sell it directly to clients.
You can’t include purchase or download links.
Even when fully white-labeled, it can only be bundled into a broader service, not offered as its own solution.

That’s a major issue for consultants, agencies, or service providers who believed white-labeling meant flexible commercial use.

Why this is frustrating

The setup and branding process takes serious time.
The licensing limitations weren’t obvious early enough.
The practical use case for agencies is far more limited than expected.

What needs improvement

Clarity around licensing and resale rights should be front-and-center in the product description so buyers don’t invest significant time before realizing the limitations.

I don’t mind putting in work, but spending an entire weekend setting up a tool only to learn it can’t be used the way I planned is extremely frustrating.


I would like to add that their support is very slow.  It says they will get back to you in a FEW hours.  Not acceptable.

reviews.title: WP Login Lockdown: Say Goodbye to Brute Force Attacks 👋💻
reviews.comment:
I’ve been using WP Login Lockdown for a while now, and I can confidently say it’s one of the most reliable WordPress security plugins I’ve tried. 🔒

The main feature I appreciate is how it automatically limits the number of login attempts. This simple yet powerful function drastically reduces the risk of brute force attacks, which are unfortunately very common. 🚫👨‍💻 Knowing that my site is being actively protected gives me peace of mind and allows me to focus on growing my content instead of worrying about hackers.

Another big plus is how easy it is to set up. ⚙️ Even if you’re not very technical, the interface is straightforward, and you can get everything running in just a few minutes. I also like the detailed logs, which let me see exactly when and where failed login attempts are happening. This extra transparency is invaluable for tracking suspicious activity.

On top of that, the plugin runs smoothly in the background without slowing down my website. Speed and performance are crucial for SEO, so that’s a huge win. 🚀

Overall, WP Login Lockdown is a must-have tool for anyone serious about protecting their WordPress site. Highly recommended! 👍

questions.title: How exactly does it work for multisites?
questions.comment:
Hello Scrollsequence team:

Before purchasing, I need clarification on how your licenses work with WordPress Multisite (subdomain mode).

My situation:
- I have a WordPress Multisite installation with more than 10 subsites in subdomain mode.

- Main domain: mydomain.com
- Subsites: client1.mydomain.com, client2.mydomain.com...

My questions:

1. Does the "Pro Plan (10 sites)" license cover:

A) Only one site (the main domain mydomain.com), allowing unlimited subsites?

B) Each subsite separately (i.e., I would need a license for more than 10 sites)?

2. If I purchase Level 1 (10 sites) and activate it across the entire network, will all subsites have access to Scrollsequence features using only one license, or do I need to purchase a license for each subsite separately?

Thank you for your clarification!

children.comment:
Hi Rickmark,

Thanks for reaching out! 

1. Site counting: Each subsite in a multisite network counts as a separate “site” toward your license. So, the Pro plan would cover up to 10 domains or subsites in total. For example, if you have the main site plus 10 subsites, a 10-site license would not cover all of them.

2. Network-wide activation: You can activate Scrollsequence across your network, but the license will only cover up to the total number of sites included in your plan. Any subsites beyond that limit will not have full Pro features and may display license warnings.

If your network exceeds 10 sites, we recommend upgrading to the Business Plan license to ensure all subsites have access to Scrollsequence features.

You can do so here: https://scrollsequence.com

I hope this helps. Feel free to reach out if you have other questions.

questions.title: Translation, AI Dependency, Remediation, Custom Code
questions.comment:
First of all, I must congratulate you on the thoughtfulness with which you built your explainer video. Most SaaS launches show the cracks right there hinting support would be little. So that is a confidence builder, from the beginning. I have a few questions: 

A) Translation: 
i) does it translate onlly the Accessibility widget or the whole site? 
ii) What translation tool does your app produce the translations from? 
iii) What if we need to improve some of the translations? 

B) What are the things that cannot be done without using a paid AI API key? 

C) I see on your site in comparison table there is no automatic remediation. Does it mean remediation is suggested for every issue but we have to manually accept the suggestion? 

D) Custom Code: 
What if I am not a good coder? Does your plugin assist with identifying which code snippet ?

children.comment:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions! Here are the details you are looking for:

A) Translation:
i) The translator functions as a widget. When a user selects a language, it translates the current page they are viewing, rather than processing the entire website at once.
ii) It utilizes Google's on-the-fly translation service. It is designed to instantly assist visitors who don't speak your website's native language, rather than acting as a permanent, full-site localization tool.
iii) Currently, you cannot manually edit the translations, as they are generated automatically by Google.

B) AI Dependency:
The AI feature allows you to resolve website accessibility problems with a single click. Without it, you would need to go through the scanner's report and fix each detected issue manually.

C) Automatic Remediation:
Yes, if you integrate your AI API key, the system can automatically fix the identified issues for you without requiring manual approval for every suggestion.

D) Custom Code:
We do not currently have a feature that points out specific code snippets. However, we are actively logging this feedback and plan to add it in the future if there is strong user demand.

reviews.title: Misleading Overage Information
reviews.comment:
If you don’t plan to grow, scale, or increase traffic to your website, this AppSumo deal might work for you. But if you do plan to grow, you will eventually be forced into their subscription plan.

We made the decision to purchase this lifetime deal based on the information provided to questions on AppSumo, by the VanChat team:

1. Nov 30, 2025: “Currently, the price for each response beyond the plan limit is $0.09.”
- Ref: https://appsumo.com/products/vanchat/questions/cost-when-exceed-monthly-limits-1446588/

2. Oct 3, 2024: “Don't worry if the estimate is not accurate. We will soon launch an add - on. After the add - on is launched, even if the GPT response limit is reached, the responses will not stop. Excess GPT responses will be charged separately.”
- Ref: https://appsumo.com/products/vanchat/questions/what-counts-as-a-reply-1209749/

These statements strongly implied that exceeding the reply limit would simply result in overage charges, not a hard stop, and not a forced subscription upgrade.

However, after contacting support, we were told:
“Currently, we do not have an option to increase the reply quota specifically for lifetime plans.”

Instead, we were directed to their subscription plan. When I asked about the discrepancy between the AppSumo answers and the currently provided information, their response was:

“His response came prior to our development of the add-on. Once the feature was finalized, we discovered that it could not be made available for AppSumo's lifetime plans.” - another discrepancy.

The Nov 30, 2025 answer on AppSumo clearly says "Currently," meaning after development. That wording indicates an active, existing pricing structure, not a pre-development assumption.

I understand that business models and product functionality can change. However, publicly stated information that directly influences purchasing decisions must be updated when policies change. Changing the terms in practice while the original statements remain publicly visible creates confusion and undermines trust.

reviews.title: High hopes but just too many basic email features need fixing & testing...
reviews.comment:
I had really high hopes for AI Emaily, but I've asked for a refund. The main problem is that I never got to test the AI features properly, because basic email functions on iOS and Windows simply didn't work:

- Forwarding dropped images. I forwarded my wife's boarding pass at the airport and she never got the QR code boarding pass graphic she needed (I had to open forward the email again from another email program)
- No address suggestions in the To: field, not even recent contacts.
- No select or swipe after searching, so you can't search for emails and then delete them.
- Stray "\n" characters appeared in a draft after I saved it and reopened it.
- Image and email resizing was buggy - not possible to zoom into the render as it would only zoom from left side...

I reported these to support here as questions and later by email (there is no way to log issues from within their clients). They replied to the first issues here, but I heard nothing after my detailed email on 11 Oct, a week before I asked for the refund. In that email I'd said I'd ask for a refund if the next version wasn't significantly better. I noticed no improvement...

My advice to the team is simple: have basic tests for every release, covering composing, sending, forwarding, searching and selecting, etc. before it is released. It's not my job as an AppSumo buyer to test basic functionality. There is no point having bells and whistles - Ai xyz - if the core functionality is just lacking.

questions.title: Email alias
questions.comment:
I use a Google Workspace business account that has many verified 'Send mail as' aliases configured inside Gmail. If I connect that account to AI Emaily, will all of those aliases automatically appear as selectable From addresses in the compose window? Specifically: 

(1) does it pull the 'Send mail as' list from Gmail automatically, or do I have to add each identity manually? 
(2) when I send from an alias, does it go through Gmail's SMTP so the recipient sees the alias and not my primary address? 
(3) does it preserve per-alias display names and signatures? 
(4) can Autopilot send on behalf of an alias, or only my primary address?

children.comment:
Yes to all four, once you turn it on. Go to Settings → Mailboxes → Click 3 Dots for any of your Workspace mailbox and switch on "Sync send-as aliases". It's off by default. 

Pulled automatically. AI Emaily reads your verified "Send mail as" list straight from Gmail, so there's nothing to add by hand. It refreshes every 6 hours, and you can untick any alias you don't want in the From menu.

Yes. Alias sends go out through Gmail itself, so the recipient sees the alias, not your primary address.

Yes. Each alias keeps its Gmail display name and its own Gmail signature.

Yes, on the Autopilot tiers (T3/T4). It replies from the alias the email arrived on, and checks the alias is still verified right before sending.

This works for Gmail and Workspace only for now. Outlook and IMAP mailboxes send from their primary address. however you can change the send as email for any reply. 

— Nafiul

questions.title: Spoofed Incoming Emails Incorrectly Classified as Sent
questions.comment:
I received a spoofed extortion email with my address in both From and To. Thunderbird confirms it is in my IMAP INBOX, but AI Emaily incorrectly shows it in Sent.

The headers show SPF softfail and DMARC fail.

Does AI Emaily determine Sent status based on the From address rather than the actual IMAP folder? If so, could this be fixed?

children.comment:
Hi, thank you for such a precise report. 

AI Emaily marks a message as "sent by you" when it comes from your Sent folder, and also when the From address matches your own mailbox address. Your spoofed email had your address in From, so it was treated as your own mail even though it arrived in your INBOX. That's also why it showed under Sent. It shouldn't trust the From address alone, especially when SPF and DMARC failed, as in your headers.

We will look into that and if we found the issue we will resolve it for sure. 

— Nafiul

questions.title: Can be linked to an external agent and Generate a Link for it?
questions.comment: If there is an agent in Make or Tiny Command or N8N, can we connect Release0 to it and have Release0, generate a URL link for it, so that the functions of that External Agent can be accessed through the link generated by Release0. If this can be done, please explain how.

children.comment:
Hi Neebyen! 👋 Great question.

Yes, you can use Release0 as the conversational interface for an external agent or automation, provided the external service exposes an API or webhook that Release0 can communicate with.

For example, if you have an AI agent or workflow running in **Make or n8n**, you can connect it to Release0 using the **HTTP Request block**.

Here's how it would work:

1. Create your external agent or workflow in Make, n8n, or another platform that provides an API/webhook endpoint.
2. Create a conversational agent in Release0.
3. Add an **HTTP Request block** to send user inputs to your external endpoint.
4. Capture the response and display it to the user within your Release0 conversation.
5. Publish your Release0 agent to generate a **shareable URL** that users can open to interact with it.

This way, Release0 handles the user-facing conversational experience, while your external system handles the processing, AI logic, or automation.

You can also embed the Release0 agent on a website or use a custom domain, depending on your plan.

**One important distinction:** Release0 doesn't directly import or host an external agent. Instead, it connects to that agent through its API or webhook. For multi-turn conversations, the external integration must also handle any conversation context it requires.

Documentation: [https://docs.release0.com](https://docs.release0.com)

Hope this helps! 🚀

Hi kawashopon,Thank you for the detailed questions!

Release0 does not currently have a native LINE Official Account integration. However, Release0 supports HTTP requests, webhooks, Make.com, Zapier, and API-based integrations, so if your LINE setup can exchange messages/data through the LINE Messaging API or an automation layer such as Make, you can build a custom integration around Release0.

reviews.title: Build the WordPress site, then manage it after launch
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

There are plenty of AI tools that can make a website, and plenty of tools that can manage WordPress sites after they have been made. SiteSkite tries to cover both sides.

On Tier 2 and above, AI Site Studio can take a description of the site you want and generate a real, editable WordPress site in its own sandbox. You can explore different directions, refine the site through conversation, and then publish or export it to your own WordPress host. Because the result stays in WordPress, you are not moving the client onto a proprietary website builder just to use the AI generation.

After launch, the same platform handles the work that comes with maintaining WordPress sites: backups, plugin and theme updates, uptime monitoring, security checks, staging, rollbacks and client reports. For an agency or freelancer, I can see the appeal of using the same system to create the first version of a client site and then continuing to use it for the maintenance contract afterwards.

The sandbox side is useful even if you are not using the AI builder. You can create a fresh environment or clone an existing site from a backup, test plugins or updates away from production, and only push changes once you are comfortable with them.

SiteSkite also supports MCP, so you can connect tools such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor and use them to work with your connected WordPress sites and SiteSkite operations. During my original test, the Cursor setup asked me to copy my active browser login cookie into the configuration, which I wasn't comfortable with. The team replaced that method, and I rechecked the change.

I also ran into an issue with AI Site Studio during my first test. It spent 1,625 credits and more than 11 minutes generating a site before checking whether I had an available sandbox slot. The generation finished, but it couldn't publish. The team added the capacity check before generation, and I verified that the change is working well.

Backups were the one area where my experience was less straightforward. A full backup of my test site repeatedly stopped at 13%, even after I updated and disabled the other plugins and tried again in incognito mode. The partner was eventually able to back up the same site and traced the problem to restrictions or caching at the 20i host that I was using for my test site. So this turned out to have been specific to that hosting environment, but I was never able to get that particular full backup to complete myself. I would test backups early on the hosting providers you use most.

You can also store backups in your own cloud storage instead of relying entirely on SiteSkite's included storage, which is useful if you already have your own backup setup or want more control over where those files are kept.

For me, the main advantage is the full WordPress workflow. You can create or clone a site, test it away from production, publish it, and then continue managing, monitoring, backing up and reporting on that same site afterwards. For agencies in particular, that can replace several separate tools used at different stages of a client's website.

children.comment:
Thank you for giving SiteSkite such a thorough test—and for coming back to check the changes we made. I really appreciate the time you put into this.

You’ve described something that matters a lot to me: what happens after the website is built.

Having spent years working with WordPress, I know how much work continues after launch. Clients need changes, plugins need updates, something needs testing, and you need a backup you can rely on. That everyday work is a big part of why I’m building SiteSkite. I want the journey from the first idea to ongoing site management to feel easier for the people responsible for it.

Keeping the site in WordPress is central to that. You should be able to edit it, choose your hosting, and keep developing it as your client’s business grows. The sandbox supports that same idea—giving you room to try things before making changes to a live site.

I also appreciate you being direct about where we fell short.

Your concern about the original MCP authentication method was fair. We replaced it with OAuth 2.0, and thank you for checking the updated setup yourself. Feedback like this helps us improve the details that make a real difference when someone starts using the product.

The backup experience deserves that same honesty. Our investigation pointed to restrictions or caching in that particular 20i environment, and we managed to complete the backup on our side.

I’m glad you mentioned bringing your own cloud storage, too. We also support bringing your own AI model. Giving people more control over the services they use with SiteSkite is something I care about.

Thank you again for sharing both what worked and what needed attention. It’s encouraging to see the wider workflow resonate with you, and equally useful to understand where the experience needs more work. I’m grateful you gave us the chance to respond, improve, and earn your confidence.

questions.title: How is data protection handled?
questions.comment: In this time where every company big or small can get hacked, how is the protection on your end handled? What if a hacker get acces to your system, will he get acces to all websites connected? En how are backups stored? Encrypted on EU servers or only US?

children.comment:
Good question.

Backups
SiteSkite-powered backups are stored on EU servers and are encrypted. You can also use Bring Your Own Cloud (Google Drive, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, pCloud, Amazon S3, etc.) if you want backups in your own account / region.

Site access isn’t a simple API key call
Connected sites use the SiteSkite plugin with a request-signing model, not “anyone with a token can freely call the site.”

Requests are protected with Ed25519 digital signatures
The signing key is handled server-side (it doesn’t get handed to the browser as a free-for-all site password)

WordPress verifies the signature before accepting the action
On top of that we run strict validation (auth checks, request integrity, and action-level controls)

So access is designed as signed + validated commands, not open remote control.

If someone compromised SiteSkite?
No security system is “unhackable,” and we won’t pretend otherwise. In practice:

We use secure transport (SSL/TLS), access controls, signed API requests, and encrypted backup storage

A breach of one customer account is not designed as “open access to every website on the platform”

The meaningful risk surface is the compromised account / credentials for that customer’s linked sites — which is why strong account security and key rotation matter
Extra control for you

Prefer maximum data ownership → use BYO cloud storage for backups
Sandbox / staging environments are kept separate from production workflows
Help Center: https://knowledgebase.siteskite.com/

Happy to answer any follow-up.

— Muhammad / SiteSkite

Thanks for the answer. I understand that a compromised account does not affect other accounts. But my worry is when your main system is hacked, does it have acces to all sites connected to distribute malware so to say?

"But my worry is when your main system is hacked, does it have acces to all sites connected to distribute malware so to say?"

You mean a breach of SiteSkite itself. We use account-specific access tokens for connected sites, protect the platform with a firewall, and can revoke all connection tokens centrally in seconds if needed.

Because of GDPR, there's no master account listing.

I was debating the 5-llama rating on this, truth be told. Five stars, for me, would normally be a fully finished and ready-to-go product. This isn't quite there yet; it works, the bones are there, they just need to be fully fleshed out first.

The thing is, and what made me keep the 5-burrito rating on it, is the pure ambition and complexity of what they're working on here.

If you're looking at this, I'm assuming you've used agents to do parts of things in your work life. You've probably got one running in the background right now (Claude, how's that plugin going anyways?). What's missing, though, is the brain that's holding all the bits and pieces together. 

I know, ideally, I'm supposed to be that brain in my world. The problem is, between the 'tism, the ADHD, and the wildness of my 20s, the brain doesn't do so hot when it comes to retaining context. Heck, I'm not even good at sharing context -- my totally disjointed stories are proof of that (just ask my wife). 

So what do we do when the flesh-brain doesn't work too well? 

Up til now, I've segmented off parts of it to hand off to robot brains. They used to be very bad robot brains, because robot brains couldn't point out things like "maybe the toaster isn't a good bath bomb," but now they're smart enough to be like "maybe something in a soothing lavender instead?"

Where was I going with this

Oh right, anyways, Agently is setting out to be that robot brain in the centre of things -- the one that knows what's going on so your fleshy brain doesn't need to. The one you can turn to and be like "Hey Jarvis, I hit my head and don't remember who I am, what do I need to do next?" and it'll list off the five top emails you need to reply to, what meetings you have, and your local hospital's average emergency wait time so you can hopefully get that concussion checked before those meetings.

So, for overall product *readiness*? 3/5 guacamoles. 
But, for project ambition and *where it's going*? 7/5 puppies wearing sombreros. 

Overall score: 5/5 freshly baked apple pies.

children.comment:
Hi Dion, thanks for the detailed questions.

1. Gmail: The help page is right. Gmail is send-only today. We submitted the CASA review, it will be around 3-4 weeks until the whole process is completed. Outlook works fully today, including inbox reading and Outlook in Needs you.

2. Token usage: These are per-run medians from real usage over the last two weeks, counting every model turn in the run:
- Jarvis chat: about 50K input and 1.1K output tokens. About three quarters of the input is read from cache.

4. Background costs: No. Needs you ranking, routine checks, the brain's syncing and extraction, and search indexing all run on our keys, never yours. Your key is only used for runs you start: chats, Draft reply, and routine runs that actually go ahead. A routine that is skipped because nothing changed doesn't touch your key.

5. Future versions: Yes, your license includes future updates to your plan.

reviews.title: Solid omnichannel platform with huge potential—needs deeper CRM customization, contact sync, and thread controls
reviews.comment:
We have been using AnyChat integrated with our custom CRM for several months to manage client communications across WhatsApp (QR), Instagram, and Facebook Messenger from a centralized dashboard.

The core system delivers well on basic messaging aggregation and webhook architecture. However, to become an indispensable, top-tier solution for sales teams, there are a few key feature gaps and workflow friction points that need to be addressed:

1. Better Thread Management (Stop Auto-Archiving Bot Chats!):
When the automated bot interacts or replies to a lead, the conversation often gets archived or displaced from the main active inbox. Bot-handled threads must stay explicitly visible in a dedicated status tab (e.g., "Bot Active" or "Pending Review") until a human agent manually marks the lead as resolved or archived.

2. Contact Identity & Google Contacts / Gmail Sync:
There is a strong need for direct integration with Google Contacts / Gmail API to resolve raw phone numbers or social handles (@username) against our team's contact address book. Syncing contact names automatically would make the inbox experience significantly more personalized and organized.

3. Native Support for @usernames (Phoneless Messaging):
As WhatsApp and social platforms shift towards username handles without exposing traditional phone numbers, AnyChat should seamlessly support starting chats, sending attachments, and linking leads using handles alone, without hard-requiring a numeric phone number.

4. Deeper CRM Customization & Automated Follow-Up Engine:
We would love to see more native customization for CRM workflows:

Automated Sequences: Triggering scheduled follow-ups (e.g., sending an automatic re-engagement message 24–48 hours after a quote is sent if the customer hasn't replied).

Flexible Auto-Replies & Snippets: A more customizable auto-responder system supporting rich media (PDFs, images, and quick-reply templates) tailored to specific lead stages.

5. Transparent Monthly Reports on System Stability & Product Improvements:
As AnyChat continues to mature, it would be extremely valuable for agency owners and team leads to receive a monthly report or digest. Having a structured breakdown covering platform uptime/stability metrics, newly deployed feature improvements, and upcoming roadmap items would help us keep our clients informed and demonstrate the ongoing value of the system.

Verdict:
AnyChat is a robust product with a great foundation. If the roadmap includes Google Contacts integration, better thread preservation for bot interactions, deeper automated follow-up tools, and regular improvement reports, it will easily become the ultimate gold standard for omnichannel client management.

questions.title: Can Foyer be used on Brilliant Directories?
questions.comment:
The site is built on Brilliant Directories, which allows custom HTML/JavaScript widgets. Can Foyer be embedded using a script tag or similar code on a Brilliant Directories website?

Please also confirm:

1. Does Foyer support both voice and text chat, or voice only?
2. Can it be branded with my name/logo/colors as AION from AI Hub?
3. Can I give it custom instructions about my business and marketplace categories?
4. Can it route visitors to specific pages such as Request AI Help and Apply as Provider?
5. Can it collect lead details or push visitors toward a form?
6. Does it work properly on mobile?
7. Are there conversation, visitor, credit, or usage limits on the AppSumo deal?
8. Are there any required monthly fees after the AppSumo purchase?

Thank you.

children.comment:
Hi Tag36575! Sohazur here, one of Foyer's founders. Brilliant Directories supports the script-embedding method Foyer uses, so you don't need a separate plugin.

Install your Foyer snippet once under Settings → Design Settings → Custom CSS / HEAD → Additional Footer Code. We've added Brilliant Directories to our in-app setup guide and Help Center: https://app.tryfoyer.ai/dashboard/help#faq

To answer each question:

1. Voice and text: Visitors can speak or type through “Show chat.” Currently, typing is part of the connected voice session, not a separate microphone-free chatbot. Starting the session requires microphone permission.

2. AION branding: You can use “AION from AI Hub” in your brand instructions, customize the launcher text, and change colors, position, shape, and font. Tier 1 includes basic styling; Tiers 2–3 add more detailed styling. All AppSumo tiers remove the Foyer watermark. Custom-logo upload isn't currently available, and the active-call heading still says “Agent,” so I wouldn't describe it as fully white-label.

3. Custom instructions: Yes. Add your business context, marketplace categories, tone, and rules under Brand & Instructions, alongside the relevant website pages in your knowledge base.

4. Page routing: Yes. Provide the actual URLs for “Request AI Help” and “Apply as Provider,” then explain when the agent should suggest each. Install Foyer on the destination pages too.

5. Lead capture: Yes. Foyer can display its own contact form and save details in your dashboard, or guide visitors to your existing form page. This doesn't automatically create member or lead records inside Brilliant Directories.

6. Mobile: The widget has a responsive mobile-web layout. Voice requires HTTPS and microphone permission. Your particular theme and any overlapping mobile controls should still be checked after installation.

7. Usage limits: Tier 1 includes 50 minutes/month, 1 agent, and 100 indexed pages per agent. Tier 2 includes 150 minutes, 1 agent, and 260 pages. Tier 3 includes 400 minutes, up to 3 agents, and 550 pages per agent. Minutes are shared account-wide, reset monthly, and don't roll over. Connected session time counts, including typing or muting; simply visiting a page doesn't consume minutes. Conversations pause when the allowance and purchased minutes are exhausted.

8. Monthly fees: There's no required Foyer subscription beyond your AppSumo purchase for the included allowance. Optional AppSumo top-ups cost $18 per 100 additional minutes and $10 per 100 additional indexed pages. Purchased minutes don't expire, but don't renew monthly. Your Brilliant Directories subscription and any optional BYOK provider charges remain separate.

For your marketplace, I'd start with the category guidance and those two destination pages, then check the visitor journey before rolling it out across the site.

reviews.title: A Game-Changer for Customer Support – Just Needs a Few Tweaks!
reviews.comment:
I’m honestly loving Bit Assist! This plugin has been a fantastic addition to my online store and my personal blog as an electrical repair specialist. It really feels like it was made to bring me closer to my customers – but hey, there are still a few things I’d love to see improved.

Pros (+):
All-in-One Contact Hub: Bit Assist lets me connect WhatsApp, Telegram, and even Facebook Messenger, all in one neat little widget. My customers now have their pick of how to reach out, and honestly, it's been a game-changer for reducing those abandoned carts! Getting questions answered fast means people actually stick around to buy. Love it!

Simple, Customizable Widget: The widget looks great on my site. It’s super easy to set up and customize with colors, welcome messages, and business hours. It just feels more professional and welcoming, and my customers appreciate it.

Easy as Pie to Use: Setup was smooth, no complicated steps – just install, connect, and go. Everything is so user-friendly, and I can handle messages from all channels in one place. No technical skills needed – major plus!

Boosts Trust and Connection: Having this little widget on my site adds that personal touch. In my blog, readers reach out more often, which feels great. I can respond quickly, build relationships, and make them feel valued. It’s perfect for that!

Cons (-):
Analytics Could Be Better: The analytics are pretty basic. I’d love more insight into which channel gets the most traffic, peak hours, and popular topics. This would help me make my support even better.

Lacks Message Filtering: In my store, I get lots of questions, and it would be amazing if I could filter them by keywords or topics. Right now, it takes a bit of digging to find specific messages, which can slow things down.

Setting Up Multi-Site Feels Tedious: I use this on multiple sites, and I wish I could just clone my settings. Setting up the widget from scratch for each site feels like extra work.

Wishlist:
Advanced Analytics: It’d be awesome to have deeper reports to see how I’m doing and what customers are asking for.
Better Notification Options: If there were notifications for unanswered messages after a certain time, that’d be a lifesaver for staying on top of support!
All in all, Bit Assist is an awesome tool that has already made a huge difference for me. It’s easy, professional, and my customers love the quick contact options. If the team can add a few more features, it would be just perfect!

questions.title: #1: AI for chat? #2: Auto-responses? #3: Booking a meeting?
questions.comment:
#1: AI for chat? 
#2: Auto-responses? 
#3: Booking a meeting?

children.comment:
1. Bit assist not have any AI integration or AI chat bot feature.
2. Bit-Assist has tawk.to and other live chat platforms that can be embedded within Bit Assist as a channel. In those particular platform, auto responses feature are available. reviews.title: Simple Solution for Customer Feedback & Roadmaps
reviews.comment:
As a SaaS startup owner, managing user feedback was becoming a chaotic mess. We were drowning in feature requests scattered across emails, Slack threads, and support tickets. FeatureShift has been the perfect tool to bring order to that chaos.

What makes it brilliant:

• Unbelievably Easy to Set Up and Use: We had our public roadmap portal live and embedded in our app in under an hour. The interface is so intuitive that our entire team—from developers to support—adopted it without any training. This simplicity is its superpower.

• Transparency Builds Trust: The public roadmap has transformed our relationship with our users. Instead of their suggestions vanishing into a black hole, they can now see, vote, and comment on ideas. We've noticed a significant drop in frustrated support queries and an increase in constructive, collaborative feedback.

• Focuses on What Matters: It cuts through the noise. The voting system automatically surfaces the features our users genuinely care about, making prioritisation data-driven and easier to justify. It's stopped the "squeaky wheel" from getting all the grease.

• Excellent Value for Money: Compared to clunky, enterprise-grade tools that cost a fortune, FeatureShift offers exactly what a growing product team needs at a sensible price. It's a lean, focused tool that delivers immense value without unnecessary complexity.

A Minor Consideration:

If you're a massive enterprise requiring deep, custom integration with Jira on a field-by-field level or complex permission schemes, you might find it a bit lightweight. However, for most small-to-medium-sized businesses and product teams, its feature set is spot-on.

FeatureShift has become an indispensable part of our product development cycle. It has made us more organised, our process more transparent, and our users feel heard. For any UK product team looking to professionalise their feedback loop without overcomplicating things, I cannot recommend it highly enough.

reviews.title: Good tool, but missing a key piece for local businesses
reviews.comment:
Spokk does what it says — generates nice reviews. No complaints there.

The problem? Customers don't actually copy and paste those reviews onto Google Business Profile 😅 As a local business owner, I need reviews to show up on Google, not sit inside Spokk. The generated reviews are basically useless if they never make it to the platform that actually drives foot traffic.

Would be a game-changer if there was a way to push reviews directly to Google Business Profile, or at least a smoother nudge that actually converts.Good concept, just needs that last mile for local businesses like mine 🇮🇪

children.comment:
Hey there,

Thank you for your honest review. It really means a lot to us that you took the time to give us your honest feedback.

Here's a few things that other businesses do:
1. Set up the automation -> it helps increase the number of responses you get -> also has reminders and referrals built it.
2. We recently released a new review reminder automation that follows up with customers who left feedback but never clicked the Google review link. This is essentially the nudge you mentioned in your review.
3. Make the thank you message in the classic form more detailed, this is something other companies do - "We’d greatly appreciate a Google Review. When the Google page opens, paste your review into the text box (right-click or Ctrl + V) and click Post. Thanks!"
4. Another important fact is that you can incentivise feedback via Spokk but you cannot incentivise google reviews (against policies). People would already take a step towards giving you feedback so the push from the feedback to leaving a review is much smaller than getting a review written from scratch.

Here are a few reasons why people don't post on Google from Spokk
1. They think the review has already been posted after submitting their feedback. In this case, the reminder automation can help. We recommend mentioning that their review is already written for them and just needs to be copied and pasted.
2. They just didn't want to - honest brutal truth. People are willing to give feedback but leaving a public review is kind of a civic responsibility. Maybe they had something lacking in their experience that stopped them from leaving the review. Use Spokk internal follow ups to try and find the root cause or give them a coupon to get them to come back and provide an even better experience.

Final thoughts
Detailed reviews tend to perform much better for Google Maps rankings than short generic reviews. Spokk helps generate those higher-quality reviews. The automations also help maintain review velocity, which is another important ranking factor for local businesses.

If you have a minute, please try and set it up with automations + our new review nudge. I'm sure your reviews will blow up. We have a wellness company in Malaysia that's killing it with Spokk, I can't disclose the name because it's white-labeled.

If you have any ideas to further improve the conversion rates, please send me an email at [email redacted]. We are all about feedback at Spokk haha.

children.comment:
Hi there!

Memberships let you offer customers a recurring subscription, either monthly or yearly, in exchange for ongoing perks. For example, a salon could offer a membership that gives customers 10% off every visit, or a car wash could offer a monthly plan with a set number of washes included.

The idea is to encourage repeat business by giving customers a reason to keep coming back to you, while providing your business with more predictable recurring revenue. It's a win-win!

We do take a 10% platform fee on membership sales for AppSumo users. If you subscribe directly to one of our monthly or yearly plans, there’s no additional platform fee.

Our direct subscription plans also include onboarding, video call support, a dedicated SMS number with SMS costs covered, and custom integrations built for your business at no extra charge.

Memberships are completely optional, so you can decide whether they make sense for your business. Spokk's other features can be used independently of them.

questions.title: How does Spokk protect a Google Business Profile from this?
questions.comment:
I like Spokk, but I am worried Google will penalize my business because of what I found online: 

1. Spokk’s default feature relies on generating an AI review for the customer to copy and paste. Google’s guidelines explicitly prohibit giving users wording to copy-paste, and their systems are trained to flag and delete AI-generated text patterns.

2. Because the customer only opened the feedback screen to get a reward, Google considers the foundation of that review incentivized—regardless of when the reward is paid out.

3. When multiple users claim a reward on Spokk and immediately click through to Google Maps to paste text, it creates an identical technical referral path that Google flags as rating manipulation.

Have you had any businesses get reviews deleted. Not including review gating cuz that's obviously not allowed

Best regards,

children.comment:
Hey Justin,

Fair question. I went back and read Google’s current policy pages before answering rather than relying on assumptions.


On the AI-generated draft:
There’s no rule in Google’s current policies that prohibits AI-assisted reviews. I checked both the Business Profile and Maps policies, and the key requirement is that a review reflects the customer’s genuine experience.

That’s exactly how we designed Spokk. We don’t provide a generic template or invent content. The draft is generated only from what that specific customer tells us through the feedback form — their ratings, their own words, the services they selected, etc. The model is also explicitly instructed not to invent staff, products, or experiences that weren’t provided.

So the AI is really just helping someone who had a genuine experience but doesn’t want to spend five minutes writing a paragraph. The customer sees the result in an editable box labelled “AI Generated Review” and decides whether to edit it and post it themselves from their own Google account.

People already use ChatGPT to write reviews themselves. Blocking all AI reviews just does not make sense because people don't write anymore, Spokk just does it better and easier than ChatGPT.


On the reward:
Google’s policy prohibits offering incentives *in exchange for posting a review*. In Spokk, the reward is tied to submitting feedback, not leaving a Google review.

The reward is triggered as soon as the customer submits their feedback, regardless of their rating, before the Google review step is even shown. They can take the reward and close the page without ever visiting Google.

The important part is the wording. You should say something like **“Share your feedback and get X”**, rather than **“Leave a review and get X.”** The latter would create a policy issue with both Google and the FTC.


On the referral path:
I couldn't find anything in Google's policies that treats the customer's click path or referrer as a policy signal. Spokk sends customers to `search.google.com/local/writereview`, which is Google's own review URL — the same destination used by the review link and QR code Google provides through Business Profile. The reward is for the feedback, this is just an additional ask without any incentive for the user.


What actually seems to cause problems:
The bigger risks are unusual review velocity and soliciting reviews while customers are physically on your premises.

For example, Sterling Sky published data in February showing a business that went from roughly 72 reviews per month to 235 and subsequently lost 342 of 595 reviews and received a posting block.

So our recommendation is straightforward: send the request **after the visit**, via SMS or email, rather than asking customers to review while they're at the counter. And don't suddenly go from your normal review volume to 10× that amount.


Have we seen reviews deleted?
None so far. Infact most of the reviews generated from Spokk have been showing up at the top in the recommended section because it's just well written and the customer's real experience. This can change but if it does, we will adapt.


And if you’d rather not use the AI feature:
That's completely fine. You can turn off AI drafts in your form settings and use Spokk purely for review-request automation with your direct Google review link. This would be identical to other review platforms like Birdeye.

You'd still get the automation, timing, and click tracking, so you'd know how many customers actually clicked through to Google. If you send the Google link yourself from your own phone or email, you don't get that visibility.



I hope that answers all your questions. 

Best,
Samesh

questions.title: Automated agency onboarding via API or MCP

children.comment:
Hi, if you write into support I will work with you on building what's missing. But here's what you can and cannot do right now:

Can be automated today:

- Create a new agency client project (Agency API or Agency MCP)
- Invite the client by email (Agency API or Agency MCP; resend invite supported)
- Create locations (Project API; a default location is created when the project is created)
- Build the review page URL from the project slug returned at creation, plus optional location slug from List Locations
- Retrieve that project's API key via Agency API for further Project API calls
- Adjust project limits and feature flags via Agency API overrides
- Notify Make or Pabbly when your automation finishes (your scenario after the last successful API call)

Cannot be automated today:

- Client accepting the portal invitation on their own account
- Google Business Profile connection and OAuth (someone with Google access must complete this)
- A single API field that returns the full public review page URL (you construct it from slug and your domain setup)
- A platform webhook for project created or onboarding complete (webhooks only cover reviews and messages)
- Provisioning new agency projects from the in-app Stripe integration (Stripe in MGR is per project for customers and review requests; use your Stripe webhook plus Agency API for new clients)
- Creating locations or managing reviews and customers using only Agency API or Agency MCP (use Project API or Project MCP for that)

I definitely want to improve the agency flow via MCP, so I'll start on some new endpoints and skills to do so.
thank you for your quick reply

reviews.title: What! Another AI Writing app

I hate writing and my writing skills show it! (Which you are about to experience below :o) 

This is why I'm in search for the ultimate AI writing app. This is actually the 5th AI writing app I've bought on AppSumo. 

I've just had all 5 open in a separate window (Rytr, ContentBot.AI, Typli.ai, Thundercontent, and this one WordHero) and tried writing the same article about 'Meditation tips for beginners'. 

In a nutshell this is what I've found:
- Rytr - too complicated
- ContentBot.AI - way too complicated
- Typli.ai - a bit random in the content it generates, e.g. I'm not a girl from Arizona who is trying meditation for the first time! Seriously what!! The expansion tools seem limited and no control over the tone of voice. Initially I liked this as it has a chrome extension and a wordpress plugin .. but what's the point if the content is a bit off!
- ThunderContent - generates good content, even straight out of the box, but the editor is a bit limited. They need to improve the UI in my opinion.
- WordHero - the most user friendly of the lot and the long editor actually follows the way I would want to write, e.g. Title > Outline > Create paragraph for each title (from the outline) > expand the text if needed. The content it generates is also really spot on. I've also just discovered it has a lot of writing tools for specific uses, e.g. reviews, book descriptions .. nice. The road map is also worth a check as it looks like more in on it's way, e.g. SEO.

So in a nutshell ... in my opinion ... WordHero is not all the bells and whistles ... but it's pretty close and I can see in time it's going to be the ultimate AI content app I've been looking for. Very exciting!!

And to think I almost didn't open that AppSumo email thinking "What! Another AI writing app" .. so glad I did. Keep up the great work!!
