reviews.title: Hands down this is The best AI writer out there !
reviews.comment:
Yes, now this might be a bold claim but once you try it you will see why!

I have tried Jarvis, Outranking, Longshot and others And whist they have some good features, especially for the SEO side of writing content, when it comes to generating good quality content they don't even come close to wordhero. 

Now let me first just clarify this, I am not a friend, employer or anyone that has any other interest or motives to give wordhero a good review. Also, unlike many other companies on Appsumo, there are no incentives from wordhero to leave a good review. 

This review of mine is as genuine as it can be.

Ai content writing has come a long way. You can now get a decent piece of content out of most ai software. But, there will always be the human editing part to it. At the end of the day, the software does not know what is in your head and what you truly want to be 

Hence a lot of the time, the ai will write gibberish and nonsense. You might ask it to write about how to understand a scientific table and it might write a paragraph on wooden dining tables!

But all in all, Ai writers are and can be a very good tool in unlocking writer's block and help guide your article in a better direction.

And this is where I think, wordhero excels in comparison to the others. Not only have I noticed that its ai writer is more accurate to the topic I am writing about, but it also has the ability to generate three different types of content at once on any blog intro or section you ask it to!

This is a real game-changer! 

The three generated pieces of text and the actual AI real-time writer nearly always give you something you can really work with and if needed expand. 

Its algorithm seems to be very well programmed in understanding the requirements for the content.

It also has som many different types of content it can write. In fact, it has over 40! Including listicles, product descriptions, emails, blog intros/summary/conclusion, sentence expander and more!

This software is also much cheaper than most of the rest! 

You also get free unlimited characters whilst the others only offer 50000 for around the same price.

I have written so many more articles since I've started using this, usually multiple articles pr day when before just completing one or two good ones would take me a week or so.

There is also a road map which shows some really exciting things to come.

Longshot, Jarvis and Outranking are more SEO optimised. So I do hope that at some stage wordhero will also introduce this, once it does there will b no need for me to check my articles in the other software.

If anyone out there has any question they would like me to answer in regard to my experience with wordhero please do not hesitate to ask.

children.comment:
Thanks for such a well written response! Great timing too because I was just researching WordHero. I don't think Jarvis is something I am going to check out right now in light of the Lifetime deals on AppSumo. But Rytr and WordHero are catching my eye the most. 

I saw that Rytr does the 50,000 credits. WordHero immediately became more attractive lol (although admittedly that's because I'm thinking in a cheap way right now lol). 

So would you mind comparing the two, Rytr and WordHero? Namely, the writing quality (Grade A-F), features, and how much time it takes to go from idea to publish-ready content

Thanksssss! So much for your review!

Hi, I'm glad you found my review helpful.

The advantage that word hero has over Rytr, and in fact even over longshot and outranking is the text generation.
Rytr doesn't offer much in other features, so wordhero is ahead in that regards too. They both use GPT-3 technology, but they also have their own algorithms which help their software understand the technology. With rytr you will get the ai to write, but with wordhero not only will it write for you, but it will also generate three boxes of text on the exact same topic,  yet they will all be different. Hence you can copy and paste, cut and change so your copy sounds much better.

Longshot may have better headline generation, but when you generate the text, in my opinion, wordhero is more accurate and true to the headline. Now all ai software that I have tried, including Jarvis, do stray away from the subject now and then, but I find word hero more accurate. The funny thing is I was just trying this comparison today with Longshot and wordhero when I noticed your message!

Outranking is probably the best all-rounder. Meaning it has on-page SEO and ai writer in one. It checks the top results in google to search for the best type of headlines, metadata, title tags etc. It also optimises your text by notifying you of how many keywords, h2 tags and other analytical information you need for SEO. It gives your page an SEO score too. 
However, the problem with outranking is that it does take a long time to get started with. You have to go through each process before you can start the blog. It is also a bit confusing at times. Admittedly it has excellent potential, but at the moment the ai writer is no better than wordhero, in fact, I would edge the word hero output, and ultimately that's what it is about - the content.

Even though we would love software to write everything perfectly, it's just not gonna happen, so most of us want the content to unstick us and help direct us, therefore I feel word hero is the best for this.

Word hero can be asked to write different types of content for your needs. I.e if you need a product description, or a sentence expander, blog intro or conclusion, book titles, blog ideas, emails, letters, rewrite, poems and more! Around 54 different types of content. None of the others can do the same. So this is the one-stop software for all your content needs. 

Now to compare, word hero cost $69 for life! outranking has a monthly subscription, starting at $39, with limited outputs on SERP analysis etc.

How to use? I generate the headlines from longshot then I plug it into word hero, I write the article in word hero and then I optimise it in outranking. There are so many features in outranking when trying to generate the blog that it takes up a lot of your credits. So i just plug in the finished article and then check the optimisation of it. I take on board the results and edit it back in worhero. Soon with the new wordhero update planned i will do all of it in wordhero

Also just to let you know that at the end of the day it's just my opinion, and opinions are subjective. The best way to know which software is best for you is to try as many free trials as possible and then make a decision that suits your needs best.

reviews.title: A solid offering for product reviews (updated)
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I’m a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give. 

Update to my original beta test score:
The issues and concerns I discovered during my testing (see Cons) seem to have all been appropriately addressed since my original testing. I now believe ProductBridge to be a valuable platform for anyone needing to track feedback and keep users updated with changes. I have changed my 3 taco score based on initial testing prior to the Appsumo launch to 5 tacos. Welcome to Appsumo ProductBridge!

After a thorough beta testing session of ProductBridge, I am giving this tool a solid 3 out of 5 tacos. ProductBridge is a versatile client portal and feedback management software that allows you to collect, analyze, and act on user feedback to improve your product or service offerings. The platform centers around three core modules: Feedback, Roadmap, and Changelog. These features are incredibly beneficial for finding out what users want in a product, tracking bug submissions, and keeping customers updated on improvements and new features.

What truly differentiates ProductBridge from many other platforms in this category is its AI agent. The AI automatically collects feedback for you by pulling data from public review sources like Trustpilot and the App Store, monitoring support channels such as Intercom and Zendesk, and listening to team channels like Slack and Discord. This means you don't have to manually gather feedback. Furthermore, the AI works very well when tasked with creating posts and determining the proper next course of action after reviewing the provided feedback.

However, the product is not without its flaws. The onboarding experience lacks sufficient resources, leaving new users without adequate guidance on how to effectively utilize the platform and its workflows. Additionally, the UI's monochromatic gray background with black text lacks vibrancy. Despite these hiccups and a few bugs, the tool is definitely ready for an AppSumo launch. With a few fixes, more integrations, and expanded user limits, this could easily be a 4- or 5-taco deal.

Pros:
Modular Flexibility and Automation: ProductBridge provides significant value through its modular approach, allowing you to enable specific tools like Feedback, Roadmap, and Changelog based on your specific communication needs.  
Easy Setup and Navigation: The platform stands out for being easy to set up and use overall, enabling users to get started with minimal effort. The layout is intuitively designed, providing a clear structure that makes it easy to locate and interact with features across the different modules.  
Versatile Portal Deployment: ProductBridge provides multiple deployment options for making its customer portal accessible. You can easily choose from a popup, sidebar integration, iframe embedding, or direct link sharing, which ensures compatibility across various use cases and user preferences.

Cons: (please note that these cons have all been addressed since initial beta testing, but have been left here for reference)
Restrictive Team Limits: The 15-member maximum per organization for tiers 3 and 4 may be significant limitation for some, especially for organizations with larger teams. 
File Upload Issues: A frustrating bug prevents the uploading of larger documents to the knowledge base. Users are only able to upload small file sizes, forcing them to break documents down into smaller sizes to bypass the restriction. (Please note that this limitation and others may have been corrected since my beta testing).

children.comment:
Thank you for taking the time to test ProductBridge so thoroughly and for sharing such detailed feedback.

We’ve already acted on several of the points you raised during beta testing:

Guided onboarding — new users now get step-by-step guidance from the moment they sign up and create their organization.

Make & Pabbly integrations — both were built and launched based directly on your suggestions. You also mentioned wanting more integrations, and we’d genuinely love to know which other platforms you’d like to see us add next.

File upload issue fixed — we resolved the Knowledge Hub upload issue and increased the supported file size limit to 5 MB.

Higher team limits — during beta testing, the limit was 10 team members. Based on your feedback, we increased it to 15 members for each organization for Tier 3 and Tier 4.

UI improvements — we’ve taken your feedback about the visual experience seriously. We’re adding more color where it improves clarity and usability. For example, we’ve already introduced more visual differentiation across Analytics and Insights, and we’ll continue refining other parts of the product as well.

Full documentation — every major feature is now documented at https://docs.productbridge.io, with documentation linked throughout the product to make it easier to find help when needed.

Since your review was based on the beta version and most of the concerns you raised have now been addressed, we’d really appreciate it if you could take another look and consider updating your review and rating based on the current version of ProductBridge.

Thanks again for helping us make ProductBridge better.

Hi Sumo-ling,

Thank you for your thoughtful review. We’ve denied this submission because it includes an explicit admission of receiving something of value in exchange for the review — e.g., “I’m a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free…” — which violates our policy prohibiting incentivized reviews. That statement alone requires us to reject the review regardless of its content or score.

We’d love to publish your feedback if you can resubmit a version that removes any mention of payment, free access, gifts, or other incentives. If you were actually compensated or received the product for free as part of a program, you should not submit a review. If you weren’t compensated, simply rewrite the review to focus on your firsthand experience (details like onboarding, AI agent behavior, pros/cons, and your updated taco score are helpful) without referencing compensation. Once you’ve posted a compliant review, we’ll reevaluate it. ❤️ & 🌮 - ModBot

reviews.title: WordPress plugin not working?  The "404 Not Found"
reviews.comment:
WordPress plugin not working?

The "404 Not Found" error is an HTTP status code that indicates that a web server could not find the resource requested by the client. OpenResty is an Nginx-based platform for managing web applications and APIs. This error usually occurs when a URL is incorrect or the resource has been deleted or moved.

children.comment:

Thank you for submitting your review. We’ve denied it because it reads as a general explanation of a “404 Not Found” error rather than reporting on your firsthand experience with the plugin. Our “Reviews without use” guideline requires that reviews demonstrate actual use—details like your WordPress version, plugin settings you tried, specific error messages or screenshots, and any troubleshooting steps you took.

We’d love to approve a new review that walks us through how you installed or configured the plugin, what went wrong in your environment, and what you’ve tried so far to fix it. Once we see that hands-on feedback, we’ll be happy to reevaluate! 💪

❤️ & 🌮 – ModBot

reviews.title: Great AI writing tool with lots of useful features
reviews.comment:
Writeseed has been a very useful tool for creating content quickly without compromising too much on quality. I particularly like the long-form article writer, SEO optimization, paraphrasing tools, AI image generation, and the wide range of templates.

The ability to work with different AI models and create content in multiple languages is also a big advantage. The WordPress integration and Chrome extension make the workflow even easier.

Overall, Writeseed is a solid all-in-one AI writing platform for bloggers, marketers, and businesses that need to create content efficiently. The interface is easy to use, and having so many features in one place saves a lot of time.

reviews.title: Solid product that keeps getting better
reviews.comment:
I bought Writeseed with mixed feelings and it has turned out to be a solid product. The developers keep adding new features, and the quality has clearly improved with each one — it's not one of those tool that shipps and then goes quiet.

What I use it for most is content and article writing, and it handles that well. The template library is broad enough that I rarely start from a blank page, and the Brand Voice feature makes the output sound like us rather than like everyone else. Working in German and Spanish as well as English, the multi-language support matters to me and it holds up.

The Keyword Research tool was a nice surprise — a single search returns around a hundred keywords with search volume, CPC and difficulty, which is more than I expected from a writing tool.

Not everything is unlocked on my tier, some output still needs a human edit before it goes anywhere near a client. But for what I paid, it earns its place in the stack.

children.comment: Thanks for the kind words. We are constantly making improvements. We hope to bring up more features. Please let us know what features you'd like to see.

reviews.title: A promising tool
reviews.comment: Writeseed is a promising tool. Unlimited GPT Image 2 generation at tier 6 is potentially an unbeatable deal for most people; the image output quality is great, as expected. However, its resolution options are not suitable for my workflow. ChatGPT free offers higher-resolution output at 1254 x 1254 or 1024 x 1536px, while Writeseed appears limited to 1024 x 1024 or 720 x 1280. That may be perfectly adequate for many users, and in many cases the smaller image sizes could even be beneficial for site speed, but it is a limitation for my needs. I will reconsider purchasing again once the resolution is increased, although I would understand the cost sustainability concerns. Wishing the team continued success.

reviews.title: The best AI book-writing tool I’ve tried so far
reviews.comment:
Updated review — 5/5 (from 4.5/5)

I have updated this review after receiving a helpful reply from the author and learning more about how to use the tool through videos, platform updates, and additional features.

After trying five AI book-writing tools, AIWriteBook is currently the best one I have used. It is not perfect, but it has the strongest combination of readable writing, story consistency, author-voice control, and a workflow that can take a book from an idea to a polished, print-ready result surprisingly quickly.

What I corrected from my first review
- I originally thought chapters were limited to around 1,200–2,000 words. I later learned that chapter targets can be set up to 5,000 words, which is much better for longer books. However, the target is not always reached exactly: even when I request 5,000 words, I sometimes receive around 3,500-4000. I would like more consistent word-count delivery and maybe even going over 5000.
- It is possible to expand chapters in the AI Editor or regenerate them at a higher target length. That helps, although optional scenes or sub-chapters would still make long chapters easier to structure.
- I also learned that DOCX export is available before a book is finished, once a cover has been added. This is useful for writers who want to edit their manuscript in Word, Google Docs, Scrivener, or elsewhere.

What I like
-    Story consistency: In my testing, the plot, characters, and overall direction stayed coherent much better than in most competing tools.
-    Readable output: The writing generally flows well and does not feel like disconnected AI text.
-    Voice of Author: One of the platform’s strongest features. It does a convincing job of following a chosen writing style.
-    Complete workflow: With proper outlining, character details, editing, and guidance, it is possible to create a finished and polished book very quickly.
-    Writing credits: Longer chapters do not cost more than shorter ones, which makes longer projects more economical.
-    Audiobook flexibility: Audiobooks can be generated chapter by chapter over time. There is also an ElevenLabs BYOK option, which may be a more affordable alternative for longer books. But using platform credits it's very expensive (10k credits for 70k words)

What I would improve
-    More reliable chapter lengths: A 5,000-word target should consistently produce something closer to 5,000 words.
-    More control over non-fiction research: The search feature is useful, but it is hit-or-miss. I would like to tell it exactly what to search for, define research questions or keywords, and have more clarity about the sources it uses.
-    More reference uploads: The 10-file limit is restrictive. I may have many short studies or articles, even while staying below the 100,000-word limit. More files and a larger word allowance (200k - 300k) —even as more expensive credit option —would be valuable.
-    Version history: Regenerating a chapter can permanently remove an earlier version once you leave the page. A proper history system would make experimentation much safer.
-    Duplicate book option: If version history is not available, the ability to duplicate an entire book would be very useful before testing another model, new editorial guidelines, or major rewrites.
-    Optional locations/settings section for fiction: I would like an optional “Spaces” or “Locations” section in the Story Bible. For relevant stories, users could define locations such as Place A, B, and C, including descriptions, atmosphere, characters present, goals, events, and what the protagonist does there. This could improve continuity when characters travel and ensure settings are described consistently.
-    Audiobook cost: A full-length book can still be expensive to narrate—around 10,000 credits for a typical 70,000-word book. The ElevenLabs API option may help, but the standard cost remains high.
-    Security warnings: Bitdefender has repeatedly blocked threats when I visit the site, mentioning Launchpadly and Foundrlist. I do not know whether these are false positives or third-party scripts, but this should be checked.
-    Minor bugs: I have reported a few issues related to additional notes not showing. Other than that, the platform works well overall.

Overall
AIWriteBook still needs improvements, especially around research controls, reference limits, version backups, and word-count consistency. But its core product is very strong.

If you are willing to properly guide the tool—build the outline, develop characters, review output, and edit the manuscript—it can create coherent, readable books that do not feel like mumbled or disconnected AI output.

My rating: 5/5.
It is currently the best AI book-writing tool I have tried.

children.comment:
This is the most useful review we have had, so let me pay it back with numbers,
including one place where the app misled you.

Chapter length. 1,200 to 2,000 words is not the ceiling, it is what the outline AI
filled in for you. Every chapter card on the Outline step has a Target Words field,
and the same field sits in the Story Bible rail of the writing screen. The range is
100 to 5,000 words on fiction, 200 to 5,000 on non-fiction, and the writer is held
to within about 10 percent of whatever you type. Our published print sample runs
284 words to a 6x9 page, so a 5,000-word chapter is 17 to 18 pages, not two. Your
80,000-word novel is 16 chapters at 5,000, not 53. The sample is downloadable if
you want to measure it yourself:
https://aiwritebook.com/samples/echoes-of-the-silicon-soul-6x9-print.pdf

The economics run your way too - a chapter costs the same credits at 5,000 words as
at 500, so long chapters are the cheaper way to reach a page count.

Expanding what you already have. Open the chapter and use the AI Editor panel on
the right, 5 credits a request: "expand the arrival scene, add 400 words of
description before the dialogue". It inserts new paragraphs as highlighted
suggestions you accept or reject one by one. If you would rather have the whole
thing rewritten longer, raise Target Words in the Story Bible rail and hit
Regenerate Chapter, at the normal 15/20/30 credits. That one replaces the chapter,
so do it before hand edits you care about.

Scenes and sub-chapters we do not have. Someone has already put it on our roadmap
in almost your words, and it is open for votes right now at
https://aiwritebook.com/app/public-roadmap - your vote on that one is worth more to
me than my opinion of it.

DOCX. Half right. DOCX export does not wait for the book to be finished and it is not tied to publishing - it sits on the Export step and works with a partial draft. The one condition is that the Export step opens once the book has a cover, so generate or upload one first, then DOCX is available right away, however much of the manuscript exists.

Audiobook. The price is 1 credit per 12.5 characters of narration, plus 20 percent
when the book is cast with multiple voices, and a 75 percent launch discount is
running until 6 October. Your 1,500 credits works out to roughly 62,500 characters,
about 11,000 words - so it was your page estimate that was low, not the quote. A
real 200-page book is around 57,000 words, which comes to roughly 7,800 credits
multi-voice at today's rate, closer to 6,500 single-voice. Worth knowing the
discount is temporary: after 6 October those numbers are four times higher.

Your idea about splitting it over months is already how it behaves. Credits come
out per chapter as each one renders, never upfront for the whole book, so you can
narrate three chapters this month and the rest after your Tier 3 credits refresh.

And yes on ElevenLabs. Tier 3 includes bring-your-own-key, and audiobook is one of
the actions it covers - connect your own ElevenLabs key in settings and narration
costs 1 credit on our side while ElevenLabs bills you directly for the audio. For a
200-page book that is the difference between thousands of credits and almost none.

Thank you for the Voice of Author line especially. Tell me how the consistency
holds if you take one past 60 chapters - that is the test I want to see.

I hope it helps!

Hi AnthoN, Artem here, Mykyta's co-founder. Thanks for coming back and updating your review. Answers to the new points, and one correction to our earlier reply.

Chapter length. Mykyta wrote that the writer stays within about 10 percent of Target Words. That's what we ask the model for, but nothing checks the length afterwards, and at 5,000 words it often stops short, exactly as you saw. Two things help today: remove any old word-count line from the Additional Instructions To AI box, since it competes with Target Words, and top a chapter up with the AI Editor (5 credits), for example "add a 1,000-word scene where...". We're looking at making long targets land properly.

Research. The search is built from your title and description, so put your research questions and keywords into the description before you run it. Search again adds sources to the ones you have, and you can delete any that miss. Your own studies go in as reference files.

Reference files. The limit is 10 files and 100,000 words per book. Merging several short studies into one document saves file slots, though the word total stays the same.

Version history and duplicate book. Neither exists yet. Undo after a regenerate only lasts until you leave the page, so copy a chapter first if you might want it back. "Version history and chapter lock" is on the roadmap at https://aiwritebook.com/app/public-roadmap, and a duplicate-book request belongs there too.

Locations. Each outline card has a Locations field for that chapter. For places that recur across the book, add them on the Characters step with the description in Background, and the AI treats them as canon. A real Locations section is a good roadmap idea.

Audiobook. Your math is right: 1 credit per 50 characters, plus 20 percent with several voices. With your own ElevenLabs key it costs 1 credit per render on our side and ElevenLabs bills you for the audio.

Bitdefender. Launchpadly and FoundrList are "listed on" badges on our homepage, loaded from those directories' sites. Thanks for flagging it, we're checking both.

I hope it helps!

reviews.title: I Spent Years Talking About My Personal Finance Book. Aiwritebook Got It on Amazon
reviews.comment:
For years I gave the same advice at kitchen tables and after work — how to get out of debt, how to build a first emergency fund, how to stop feeling ashamed of money. Everyone told me to write the book. I agreed with them every time and then did nothing, because I had no idea how to turn a hundred scattered conversations into chapters that actually built on each other.

Aiwritebook is what finally broke that loop. It didn't hand me a book; it helped me interrogate my own material. What does the reader already know by chapter four? Which story earns its place and which one am I keeping out of sentiment? Within days I had a structure that made sense, and the writing stopped feeling like guessing. The vague ambition I'd carried for years turned into a table of contents I could work through one section at a time.

As I write this, my book is live on Amazon. Not in a drawer, not in a folder called *ideas* — published, with my name on it, being read by people I've never met.

**Aiwritebook gave me the clarity to see the book I already had inside me, and the structure to finally finish it.**
Also ran into some issues not from Arwritebook but from Amazon when I was publishing my book but their support chat helped solved my issue and walked me through it and got it fixed.

Congratulations, Sunflow. Years of kitchen-table advice becoming a book that strangers are now reading is the outcome that matters, and you did the hard part of it.

"It helped me interrogate my own material" is the best description of the outline step I have read. Which story earns its place is exactly the question it is built to make you answer before you write a word.

reviews.title: Turned my biggest hangup (the cover!) into my favorite surprise, and gave my audience a real audiobook option
reviews.comment:
I came to AIWriteBook with one goal: turn a full draft I'd already written into an audiobook. I uploaded the manuscript as is, figuring that was the whole test. What I didn't expect was to end up poking around the writing tools too, and being genuinely pleased with what I found. It doesn't try to rewrite everything or bury you in suggestions. It stayed pretty quiet on my already finished draft, but what it did flag was actually useful, not just noise for the sake of having something to say.

The real shock for me was the cover design studio. I'm a designer by trade, so I was fully prepared to be unimpressed. I only tried it because I'd been stuck on my own cover for longer than I want to admit. The imagery it came up with was spot on, exactly the mood and composition I'd been trying to land on myself. I'll tweak the fonts to match my own style before I use it, but as a starting point it saved me hours of trial and error.

Then there's the audiobook feature, the reason I signed up in the first place. You take a finished manuscript and, with essentially the push of a button, it produces a full, professionally narrated audiobook. Natural sounding narration, real voice options, and it's all built for a distribution ready result, not just a rough recording.

The one hiccup I ran into was downloading the finished audiobook as a single file. It wouldn't let me pull the whole thing at once, and that one is still being worked out. What made it a non issue for me in the meantime is that I could still download it chapter by chapter, which actually worked out well since one of my reviewers needed to listen to the book rather than read it, and chapter files were easy for her to work through. I also want to give credit where it's due: the owner personally jumped in to help me troubleshoot, and is still actively working the problem rather than brushing it off. That kind of hands on attention is rare, especially from the person actually running the company.

Between a genuinely one click path to a full audiobook, a cover design tool that held its own against an actual designer, and writing help that knew when to stay out of the way, AIWriteBook delivered a lot more than I expected. Highly recommend.

children.comment:
Skye, thank you for this. The line I keep rereading is that you came in as a designer fully prepared to be unimpressed by the cover studio. That is the hardest audience it has.

One pointer, since you said you will tweak the fonts: once you have your version, upload it back on the Metadata step. Then the cover that goes into your exports is yours, not ours.

And you are right about the merged audiobook file. It is not the size of your book, it is a bug on our side, and it is still open. Chapter by chapter keeps working while I sort it out, and I will follow up when it is fixed.

I hope it helps!

reviews.title: A Great Way to Keep a Nonfiction Book Under Control
reviews.comment:
I am currently using the Tier 3 plan to create a nonfiction book, and after planning the project and completing the first two chapters, my experience with AIWriteBook has been positive.

What I like most is the feeling of having the entire book under control. The synopsis, target audience, tone, outline, chapter order, and word-count goals are all kept together in one project. I can easily see what has been completed, what remains to be written, and how each chapter fits into the overall structure. For me, this is much easier than managing a complete nonfiction book through separate conversations with ChatGPT or Claude.

The ability to choose between different AI models is also useful. Claude produces more natural narrative prose, while Gemini works well for explanatory and structured content. Tier 3 provides a generous credit allowance, giving me enough room to revise or regenerate chapters when necessary.

The process is not fully automatic. Nonfiction content still requires careful fact-checking and human editing. I have encountered some inaccurate details, repeated passages after AI revisions, confusing tracked changes, and one chapter generation that stopped before completion.

Overall, AIWriteBook is a very useful workspace for planning, organizing, and drafting a nonfiction book. Its greatest advantage is helping me keep the whole manuscript under control while AI assists with the writing. Based on my experience so far, I would give it 5 stars**.

children.comment:
Hi gestodedios,

Two chapters into a nonfiction book is where you actually find out whether something is a workspace or a slot machine, so thank you for reviewing it from there rather than after one prompt. Your read on the models matches ours: Claude is better in narrative passages, Gemini is steadier on explanatory and structured material.

On the four problems you hit.

Inaccurate details. Nothing in the writing pipeline searches or browses the web, so a chapter is the model writing from your brief plus what it already knows, and for nonfiction that is where wrong dates and invented specifics come from. The way to bind it down is the Details step: upload reference files (first one free, 10 credits after that, up to 10 files) and switch the citations toggle on. That routes chapter writing to Claude at 30 credits per chapter, and the AI places numbered markers inline with an APA 7 reference list per chapter, carried into the EPUB, PDF and DOCX. Every source in it is one you handed over, which is the point: it cannot cite something you did not give it.

Repeated passages after revisions. The AI editor reads the whole chapter rather than only the part you asked about, so a narrow request comes back with broader proposals more often than it should. That one is on us and the precision is not where we want it. What helps today is pasting the exact sentence into the request in quotes and asking for the single change. It narrows what the model touches.

Tracked changes. Every proposed change has a green check and a red X on it, and the bar at the top has Accept all, Reject all, and a Next change button that walks you through them one at a time. Reject all puts the chapter back exactly as it was, so trying an edit costs you nothing. One thing that is not signposted anywhere: clearing the chat also throws away any changes still pending, so resolve the diff before you clear.

The chapter that stopped early. Credits only come off after a chapter is saved, so a run that dies before that costs nothing. If it saved short and still charged you, that is the case I want to see. Send me the book title and chapter number, or write from the support chat in the app, and I will pull the server log for that generation.

Editor precision is the item I would most like ranked by people actually writing books, so if you want to push it up the list: https://aiwritebook.com/app/public-roadmap

I hope it helps!
Mykyta

children.comment:
Hi Hermannn,

The line I keep re-reading is the one about it knowing the difference between a chapter that carries an argument forward and a chapter that just fills space. That is the exact failure mode the outline step was built around, and almost nobody names it out loud. People feel that an outline is thin and move on without being able to say why. So thank you for saying why.

That part is not the model being lucky, for what it is worth. The outline step never asks for a table of contents. It first proposes three whole-book structures where every part has to state what job it does and over which chapters, then a chapter template where every section has to state its own purpose, and the chapter outlines are written against that template. A chapter that exists only to fill space has nothing to put in those fields, so it usually does not survive the step.

On your scope note: you spent your sessions on planning and outlines, so that is what you speak to. That is the right way to do it, and I am glad the foundation held up. When you do take a manuscript all the way through, I would like to hear where it holds and where it does not, the export side especially.

Cheers,
Artem

questions.title: Can Tier 3 auto-generate and place relevant infographics, diagrams and illustrations throughout a book?
questions.comment:
Hi,
I'm considering Tier 3 for creating professional, commercially sold 30–50-page business, AI, UX and educational ebooks.

I need more than decorative images. Can AIWriteBook:

1. Analyse chapter content and automatically generate relevant illustrations, conceptual models, frameworks, flowcharts and accurate infographics?
2. Let me specify the number, type and placement of visuals across chapters or pages before generation?
3. Generate and insert these visuals during initial book creation, without manually prompting or positioning each one?
4. Edit or regenerate individual visuals while maintaining consistent branding, accurate text and labels?
5. Preserve visual positioning and readability in PDF, EPUB and DOCX exports?

Please clarify which features work today in Tier 3, which require manual work and which are unsupported.

Thanks

children.comment:
Hi ZevsMatic,

Here is where Tier 3 stands on each point today.

1. Visuals generated from chapter content: not supported. Chapter images are made one at a time in the image panel of the chapter editor. You write the prompt, pick one of 14 styles and an aspect ratio, and each image costs 15 credits. It draws illustrations and conceptual scenes well. It does not build accurate flowcharts, frameworks or data infographics, and text inside a generated image is not reliable enough for a labeled diagram. What the chapter writer does produce by itself is structure in the text: headings, numbered steps, lists, and small tables where data reads better as a table.

2. Planning the number, type and placement of visuals before generation: no. There is no visual plan step. Images go in after a chapter is written, at the spot where you put your cursor.

3. Visuals generated and inserted during book creation: no. Each image is its own step. The only flow that plans and draws a picture for every page is the visual book studio, which Tier 3 includes. It is built for picture-led books like children's books and cookbooks, though: the page text is lettered onto the artwork, and in EPUB and Word each page is an image. For a 40-page business ebook I would not use it.

4. Editing one visual at a time: yes. You can regenerate an image, or use "Edit with AI" on it to keep the picture and change only what you describe. There is no brand kit, so consistent colors come from repeating them in your prompts, and exact labels are not guaranteed.

5. Exports: yes. Images stay where you placed them in the chapter, with their size and left, center or right alignment, in PDF, EPUB and DOCX. In an EPUB the text reflows to the reader's screen, so an image keeps its place in the text but not a fixed page position. That is how every EPUB works.

For business and educational books, here is the setup that gets you accurate visuals: build the frameworks, flowcharts and infographics in Canva, Figma or a similar tool, then upload them into the chapter. Your own uploads are free, labels stay exactly as you made them, and your branding stays yours. Use the AI for the writing and for illustrative images.

You can check this before buying. A free account lets you write one full chapter, upload your own images into it and export a watermarked PDF, so you can see how one of your diagrams looks in the export.

If diagrams generated from the chapter text would decide it for you, please add it to our public roadmap and vote. That is where we measure demand: https://aiwritebook.com/app/public-roadmap

I hope it helps!

questions.title: Custom domains
questions.comment:
Hi,

Is it possible to place my ebook on a custom domain instead on your domain, to collect subscribers for my ebook?

Second, can i decide per book if i want a registration or not. For example: give a non-fiction book for free but they need to register for the free workbook.

Looking forward to hear from you.

Best regards

children.comment:
Hi,

1. Custom domain: no. Book pages live on aiwritebook.com, or on nanoreads.com if you pick that on the Author dashboard, at an address like aiwritebook.com/author/your-name/your-book. You can't point your own domain at them. What works is linking to the book page from your own site. The subscribers are yours either way: the list sits on the Author dashboard and exports to CSV, so you can move it into whatever email tool you already use. You can also email them from inside the app.

2. Registration per book: yes. Each book has its own "Free chapters via email" number in the Distribution step, Author Page tab. Chapter 1 is always free to read. The number you set is how many of the chapters after it unlock when a reader enters their email. Set it to 0 and that book has no form at all.

One limit matters for your workbook idea. The book page shows chapter 1 plus the gated chapters and nothing more, so you can't publish a whole book openly and put only the workbook behind the form on the same page. Two setups that do work:

- Make the workbook its own short book, gate it, and link to it from the free book.
- Export the free book as PDF or EPUB and offer it on your own site, and use the gated book page for the workbook.

The author page and book pages are included from Tier 2 up.

I hope it helps!

questions.title: Foreign languages/Swedish
questions.comment: Hi, English  language works well but I tried this in Swedish language, it wasn't good at all. It wasnt how we talk or how we write, we dont build up our sentences like that and the words was something AI came up with. Will you improve this majorly or is this mostly for English books?

children.comment:
Hi,

Thanks for being direct about it. Swedish is a fully supported book language, but English is where most of our prompt tuning and testing has gone, so that's where the prose is strongest today. These settings change the Swedish output the most:

1. On the Basics step, check that Book language is set to Svenska. That setting decides which language rules the AI writes with, so a book left on English with a Swedish description gets the wrong ones.

2. Paste 6 to 10 paragraphs of your own Swedish writing into the Writing Style field on the Details step. The chapters then follow your sentence structure and word choice instead of the model's defaults.

3. Write chapters with Claude instead of the default Gemini. You pick the model per chapter. Claude costs 30 credits a chapter instead of 15, and it is our best model for prose. Regenerate one chapter with it and compare.

4. Use the chapter's Additional Instructions field for house rules, for example: "korta meningar, vardaglig svenska, inga anglicismer".

5. On Tier 3 or 4 you can also connect your own OpenRouter key (BYOK) and write a chapter with any model OpenRouter offers, at 1 credit per chapter, so you can test which one writes the most natural Swedish.

For single clunky paragraphs, the AI chat in the editor rewrites them and shows the change before you accept it.

If a chapter still reads wrong after that, send it to [email redacted] with the book's settings. A real Swedish example helps us more than anything when we tune the prompts.

I hope it helps!
Thank you for all the tips!

reviews.title: Follow.it Tier 2 Review
reviews.comment:
Follow.it funciona como una gran herramienta para empezar el día recibiendo un resumen personalizado de fuentes de noticias directamente en la bandeja de entrada, lo que evita visitar múltiples sitios web o distracciones en feeds infinitos.

La plataforma ayuda a rastrear noticias, sitios web, blogs, canales de YouTube y otros contenidos en un solo lugar, facilitando la búsqueda de información relevante mediante filtros de palabras clave y de inteligencia artificial sin necesidad de comprobaciones manuales.

Resulta especialmente útil para creadores de contenido que buscan descubrir temas en tendencia, investigar competidores y encontrar ideas para publicaciones, artículos y vídeos.

La mayor ventaja radica en su simplicidad: la configuración es directa, añadir fuentes es sencillo y automatiza el trabajo para ahorrar tiempo, reducir la sobrecarga informativa y evitar el desplazamiento innecesario por contenido negativo.

La oferta en AppSumo ofrece una buena relación calidad-precio por un servicio útil que se integra rápidamente en la rutina diaria y ayuda a ahorrar tiempo al juntar todo el contenido nuevo en un solo lugar y en un solo mensaje diario.

Usa filtros automáticos para mostrarte solo los temas que te importan mediante palabras clave.

Es muy útil tanto para personas que quieren mantenerse informadas sin distracciones como para creadores de contenido que buscan ideas nuevas o investigan qué está pasando en su sector.

Tengo muchas ganas de ver cómo avanza éste proyecto en el futuro. Muchas gracias a todos los desarrolladores por el esfuerzo que le dedican a ésta aplicación.

children.comment:
¡Muchas gracias por esta reseña tan completa! Nos alegra mucho que follow.it se haya convertido en parte de tu rutina diaria, y que el resumen diario te ayude a mantenerte informado sin distracciones. Eso es exactamente lo que buscamos.

Seguimos mejorando follow.it cada semana, así que cualquier sugerencia es más que bienvenida. ¡Gracias por tu apoyo!

reviews.title: Really nails it as a solid Inoreader replacement
reviews.comment:
(Note: This review focuses on the desktop browser version, where I spend most of my time.)

I've used and promoted my favorite RSS reader, Inoreader, for years, and even had a paid subscription for a while. I eventually settled on the free version, mainly because I felt that the paid features weren't worth it. After using Follow.it for a while, it really exceeded my expectations. It is both familiar yet still unique in some nice ways. 

As an RSS reader, Follow.it is very solid and capable. It's laid out logically and thoughtfully, with nuances that other RSS readers often overlook. Overall, it's very polished and modern-looking. I found every feed I had set up in Inoreader except one. Not bad! You can't add a custom feed yet, but that appears to be in development. Definitely not a deal-breaker for me.

EDIT: Yes, you CAN add custom feeds without issue. I think I fat-fingered the original URL, so I tried again, and it worked perfectly.

Beyond being an RSS reader, Follow.it includes many other features, including publishing content and pushing notifications and content to a myriad of services. And I haven't even scratched the surface of what it can do.

This lifetime deal is quite affordable in comparison to Inoreader, nicely extending features above and beyond the free tier. Don't get me wrong, the free version is amazing. This deal just amps it up.

I've tested and used countless programs and services, so I hope to really put Follow.it through its paces and provide some solid feedback. So far, highly recommended!

children.comment:
Thank you so much for this thoughtful review! Hearing that follow.it holds up against Inoreader, from someone who has used it for years, means a lot to us.

About custom feeds: you can already add sites that don’t have an RSS feed on https://follow.it/feeds. We’ve reached out to you to look into the one feed that didn’t come over, so it should be sorted soon.

And you’re right, there’s a lot more to discover beyond the reader. We’re looking forward to your feedback as you put follow.it through its paces!

reviews.title: A great way to stay informed without endless scrolling!
reviews.comment:
Follow.it has become a great way for me to start my day. Instead of visiting multiple news websites and getting distracted by endless feeds, I now receive a clear, personalized summary of my favorite news sources directly in my inbox every morning.

The biggest advantage is its simplicity. Setting everything up is straightforward, adding news sources is easy, and once configured, Follow.it does most of the work for you. It saves time, reduces information overload, and puts an end to unnecessary doom-scrolling. A convenient overview of the news that actually matters to me.

The AppSumo deal offers value for money. For a very reasonable price, you get a genuinely useful service that can quickly become part of your daily routine.

Is Follow.it perfect? Not yet. There are definitely areas that could use further improvements and refinement. However, the foundation is solid, the concept works well, and I believe this product has potential to become even better. I'm particularly looking forward to the expansion of the Find Feeds feature with Company Feeds and Topic Feeds. These additions would make it even easier to discover and follow relevant content, taking the platform's usefulness to the next level.

Overall, a smart, affordable, and easy-to-use solution that already delivers real value. A promising product with a bright future. Highly recommended!

questions.title: Does follow.it support non-RSS website monitoring, page-change detection, and automated integrations?
questions.comment:
Hi follow.it team,

I'm evaluating your AppSumo lifetime deal and would appreciate clarification on a few capabilities:

1. Can follow.it monitor websites without RSS feeds, including specific webpages?

2. Can it detect changes to existing pages, such as updated text, pricing, or features, rather than only newly published content?

3. Can updates be delivered through webhooks, RSS, Pabbly Connect, or other automation integrations?

4. Does the lifetime license permit commercial use of information obtained through the platform, without reselling or sublicensing the software?

5. Which capabilities are currently available, and are there differences between license tiers?

Thank you for your clarification!

children.comment:
Sorry for the late response! It seems AppSumo's notifications aren't working properly at the moment.

Thanks for your questions! Let me address them one by one:

1. Monitoring websites without RSS: Yes! There are two ways to do this:

a) Regular feeds: If you enter a URL on https://follow.it/feeds that doesn't have an RSS feed, you can ask our system to identify the structure of the website and detect new posts. Once configured, it works just like a regular RSS-based feed: whenever a new entry is detected, you'll get alerted.

b) Website Changes Tracker: Alternatively, you can use our Website Changes Tracker (https://follow.it/website-changes-alert), which monitors webpages for changes of any kind, with various configuration options to control what gets detected and when you're alerted.

2. Detecting changes to existing pages: Yes, that's exactly what the Website Changes Tracker is designed for. It can detect changes to existing content, such as updated text, pricing, or features, rather than just newly published posts.

3. Integrations: We currently support delivery through email, Telegram, browser push, and other channels. Webhooks are on our roadmap, with an initial target of around 2 months. We're also working on API/MCP access, which we hope to launch in the coming weeks. A direct Pabbly Connect integration isn't currently available.

4. Commercial use: Yes, using follow.it for commercial monitoring and business purposes is fine. However, rights to the underlying content remain with their respective owners, so redistribution or commercial exploitation of third-party content may require additional permissions.

5. License tiers: All four AppSumo tiers support website monitoring and change detection, but higher tiers allow you to monitor more pages and offer higher tracking frequencies.

You can see the detailed comparison here: https://follow.it/special-feeds-features

And the overall AppSumo tier comparison here: https://appsumo.com/products/follow-it/

I hope this clarifies things! If you have specific websites or automation workflows in mind, feel free to share them. I'd be happy to look into what's possible.

Hi Nick,

Thank you for your detailed and transparent response. I appreciate the clarification on current capabilities and upcoming integrations. Your answers have been very helpful in evaluating Tier 4, and I'm looking forward to exploring follow.it further.

Best regards,

I'm looking for a tool like Feedly, but now it's kinda costly. I stumble upon your app and it seems to do what I want, and I saw Web Change. Does it work like Visualping? 

My goal is to create a Trend center and monitoring competition. Does this tool fit the case use?

Thanks :)

children.comment:
Sorry for the late response! It seems AppSumo's notifications aren't working properly at the moment, which highlights the importance of a reliable alert service like follow.it ;)

Thanks for your question! Yes, I think follow.it could be a great fit for your use case :)

Our Website Changes Tracker (https://follow.it/website-changes-alert) works similarly to Visualping: you enter a webpage URL, and follow.it checks it regularly for changes. You can configure what kind of changes to detect and use filters to avoid unnecessary alerts.

However, follow.it goes well beyond website change monitoring. For your trend center and competitor monitoring, you could combine several types of feeds:
- Regular website feeds: Monitor competitors' blogs, news sections, and other websites for new content, even if they don't offer RSS.
- Website Changes Tracker: Detect changes to existing pages, such as pricing, product features, or other important information.
- Other monitoring feeds: Track relevant keywords, social media discussions, product launches, news, and much more.
You can find our available monitoring feeds here: https://follow.it/feeds

All updates can be collected in My News, where you can read and organize information from different sources in one place. You can also apply filters to reduce noise and focus on what matters.

One difference from Visualping: our tracker focuses on detecting changes in webpage content rather than providing detailed screenshot-based visual comparisons.

If you share a little more about the competitors or trends you want to monitor, I'd be happy to help you find the best setup. Feel free to reach out to us at help (at) follow (dot) it so we can discuss your use case in more detail!

questions.title: Is there one machine-readable aggregate feed for all followed sources after filtering?
questions.comment: My News is a useful human reading surface, but we have not found a documented machine-readable equivalent for the whole account. Is there an API or aggregate RSS/JSON endpoint that returns all matched items across followed Reader feeds after each feed's filters are applied, while preserving source identity and stable item IDs? That would let us consume one deterministic stream while still managing noise and filtering at the individual-feed level.

children.comment:
Thanks for this question as well! It's closely related to your previous one, so much of my answer there applies here too.

We don't currently offer a documented API or aggregate RSS/JSON endpoint that provides all filtered items across your subscriptions.

However, this is exactly the kind of use case we're planning to support with our upcoming API/MCP functionality. The idea is to let external systems retrieve items across your subscriptions, including those that passed your filters.

As mentioned in my other response, we're hoping to have the first version available in the coming weeks. The exact endpoints and metadata are still being worked out, but I'll share your requirements with our developers.

Thanks again for the detailed feedback!

reviews.title: Powerful, flexible, and a founder who actually answers - with some rough edges
reviews.comment:
I’ve been setting up and testing KeyShift for a few weeks on Windows 11 (v1.7.2), plus the new Android app (v1.0.1), and I upgraded to Tier 3 because I plan to use it heavily on a second computer. Here’s the honest picture.

What I like:

Custom actions and a custom AI prompt. I built about 30 actions in Spanish for my businesses (fix writing, reply to clients, format for WhatsApp, cost calculators) and each one is a shortcut away. This is the real value.
“Review before inserting” lets me check the result before it replaces my text.
Credits are transparent and cheap in practice. Short actions cost about 1 credit, just as the founder describes.
Bring-your-own-key and local model support, so sensitive text can stay on my machine.
Workflows work well, and the founder confirmed they’re in Tier 2 without a price increase.
Support is excellent. I reported a bug, and the founder investigated and replied within a day, with a clear test to run. Updates ship every few weeks.
My custom actions sync to the Android keyboard.

What needs work:

Some secondary windows (feedback, new action, prompt context) open behind the main window and don’t come to the front when clicked.
The window opens small on every launch.
Localization is incomplete in Spanish: the tray menu, trigger descriptions, “Check” button in About, “Quick Actions”, and the “1 of 4” tour counter are still in English.
On one occasion the Markdown action cut its output mid-name when the text came from Windows Notepad, while the same text worked from a browser. I’ve reported it with my tests.
The Android app is fully in English with no interface language option. Its feedback box doesn’t scroll to follow the cursor while typing, and the keyboard lacks autocorrect and accelerated delete.
Built-in modes can’t be edited or removed, and I’d love to choose which mode the double-space trigger runs.

Verdict: a genuinely useful tool with a responsive founder. Most issues are polish, not missing core features, and I expect it to keep improving.

children.comment:

Status: the windows opening behind, the small launch size, the Spanish strings you listed and the Notepad cut-off are all fixed and ship in the next desktop update. On Android, the feedback box scrolling and faster delete are fixed too. Spanish interface for Android is on the list.

Choosing the action for double-space is a good idea and I want to add it. Autocorrect is off on purpose for now while I tune the keyboard feel.

Thanks again for testing on both platforms.

AI Flows (we call them Workflows in the app) chain several AI steps into one shortcut, so you select text once and get the finished result. Three examples:

questions.title: Markdown action output cuts off mid-generation - reproducible pattern found
questions.comment:
Bug: my custom "Markdown" action cuts the response off mid-generation, intermittently, with the exact same input.

Pattern: when input has real names in ALL CAPS with no accents, and the AI tries to add them (e.g. "JOSE MARIA" -> "José María"), it cuts off mid-name in 3/4 tries. Same text/size with clearly fake names, or with accents already present, always completes (4/4).

Example that fails:
POSITION ONE
HOLDER JOSE MARIA HERNANDEZ PEREZ
ALTERNATE MARIA GUADALUPE JIMENEZ GOMEZ

With a real 6-position list needing this correction, it cut off 3 separate times mid-name. Same text re-run sometimes completes fine, so not 100% deterministic.

Q: Is there a time/step limit per generation that could interrupt output instead of retrying? Different handling for spelling correction vs. plain reformatting?

children.comment:
Thanks for the careful testing. I checked the request on our side: the text reaching the AI already ends at "ROMERO CASTILL", so nothing is cut during generation. The AI formats exactly what was selected, and the last letter wasn't in the selection. The fake-name runs were complete selections, which is why they always finished.

There's no time or step limit per generation, and correction and reformatting use the same path.

One check would help me rule out a bug on our side: select the same text, copy it yourself, and paste it somewhere plain. If the name is whole there but not in KeyShift, it's on us and I'll fix it. Also, which app are you copying from, and Windows or Mac?

Thanks for looking into it. I ran the tests, including the one you asked for:

1. Updated to v1.7.2. Selected the full text in Windows Notepad using Ctrl+A, and ran the Markdown action again. Same result: the name still comes out cut off at "CASTILL".

2. Copied that exact same text from Notepad, pasted it into the browser (into Claude's chat input box), selected it there, and ran the same action

reviews.title: One piece of content, published everywhere from one place
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

I actually bought StoryChief when it first appeared on AppSumo back in 2018 and used it for a while, so I already knew the basic idea behind the product. What is different now is how much more of the content process it covers. This updated version fits much more naturally into the way I publish content today.

You can start by looking at website performance, Google Search Console data and competitor research to decide what is worth creating or updating. StoryChief can also run weekly content audits to find older articles that are losing traffic and suggest what needs attention.

Once you have something worth publishing, you can take that main piece of content and repurpose it for your website, social channels, email and other destinations. StoryChief supports publishing across more than 30 channels, so you are not treating every version of the same idea as a completely separate piece of work.

This solves a problem I run into with content all the time. The article ends up in WordPress, the social posts are somewhere else, the newsletter is in another tool, and then the performance data is somewhere else again. StoryChief brings the planning, writing, approvals, publishing and reporting into the same workflow.

The AI side also goes beyond generating a first draft. It can use your company knowledge and brand voice, help optimize content for SEO and AI search, and repurpose approved content into other formats. You can also connect ChatGPT or Claude through MCP and create or manage StoryChief content from the AI assistant you already use. According to the current Q&A, a regular Claude Pro account works for this without needing separate Anthropic API billing.

I also like the Broadcasts feature. Approved content can be shared through email, Slack or Microsoft Teams, which gives companies another way to get more reach from content they have already created.

If you already have a library of WordPress content, that doesn't have to stay outside StoryChief either. Existing articles can be imported through its WordPress plugin, and there is also an API if you need a more customized setup across multiple sites.

One thing worth understanding about the AppSumo tiers is that the main platform features are available across them. What changes most is how many workspaces, users, articles, social channels and AI credits you get. The AI Visibility feature starts at Tier 3, and AI image and video generation is a separate add-on rather than part of the recurring LTD credits.

Having bought StoryChief during its first AppSumo run, this version feels like a much more complete product than the one I originally purchased. It now fits very nicely into my current publishing workflow because it can help me decide what to create, produce it, repurpose it, publish it across my channels, see how it performs, and then identify what needs to be updated next. That's what makes me excited to start using StoryChief more seriously again.

You've perfectly captured what we've been building towards: AI has made content creation easier than ever, but turning that content into coordinated, multichannel campaigns is where the real challenge lies.

It's great to hear that StoryChief now fits even better into your workflow. We've come a long way since our first AppSumo launch, and there's plenty more to come!

reviews.title: A month of content planned around your brand
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What caught my attention about Vocable is how it approaches content planning. I can get ChatGPT to write a LinkedIn post or an article whenever I want. Planning a month of content that fits my brand, covers the right subjects, and gives people a reason to keep reading takes more work.

Vocable starts by learning about your business. It can scan your website and existing social content, analyze your writing patterns, and use your brand guidelines to develop a profile that informs the content it generates. From there, you can create a 30-day campaign around a topic or business goal and organize the posts in a calendar or Kanban view.

I particularly like the idea of having that brand information available throughout the writing process. You can work on individual drafts in the editor, revise sections, keep earlier versions, and check whether the finished content still matches your brand guidelines. That last part is especially relevant when you are producing content for several channels or managing more than one brand.

The MCP connector is another interesting addition. It gives Claude access to Vocable’s content planning and publishing tools, so people who already work inside AI assistants can use them with their Vocable projects.

Vocable is primarily a written content tool, so you will still need something else for graphics and videos. I would also treat the generated campaign as a plan to work from. You still need to bring your own experience, examples, opinions, and final edits to the content.

Overall, I like the direction Vocable has taken. For founders, consultants, agencies, and small businesses that regularly publish articles, newsletters, and social posts, having the brand information, content calendar, drafts, editing, and publishing in one place is appealing. I would consider it especially if you already know what you want to talk about but need help turning those ideas into a consistent publishing schedule.

But that's not how everyone does content, so we know we aren't for everyone :) 

We are an AI content management system so we help you plan, organize and draft mutli channel content at scale instead of needing to prompt back and forth countless times using chatbots, which isn't practical for marketers and businesses looking to be efficient and consistent, and looking to scale their output across multiple channels.

Now if you create one of posts here and there, I think your customGPT will work fine if you just want to create and post on the fly, instead of planning ahead and organizing strategic cohesive campaigns across multiple channels in one one sitting and in batches.

reviews.title: A serious branding tool if you bring your own judgment
reviews.comment:
We ran Branding 5 end-to-end for our own marketing agency: intake questions, inspiration links, ICP, competitor analysis, brand values, and the full archetype flow. Honest breakdown below.

What we liked:

- The wizard structure is genuinely good. The intake questions, ICP builder, and values step walk you through defining a brand in a sensible order, and the character limits allow real answers, not snippets.
- Inputs carry forward faithfully. The description, audience, and USP we wrote early showed up verbatim in the final review, and the AI summary read our positioning back almost word for word. Consistency between what you type and what it concludes is the core promise, and it delivers.
- The refinement feedback loop actually listens. When we told it our tone should be calm and warm rather than combative, the next pass fixed exactly that.
- The website analyzer impressed us most. It read our site and concluded, quoting evidence from our actual copy, that we already execute our intended tone. That matched our own internal assessment, which is rare for an automated read.
- The competitor research is real, not invented. It blends live SERP overlap data with AI reasoning, filters out aggregators, and lets you edit everything. The final landscape summary gave us a positioning statement we will actually use, and the insights section produced two product ideas we are keeping.
- The trait sliders re-rank the archetype shortlist based on your weightings, and our final result landed exactly where our messaging points.

What we had issues with:

- The archetype suggestions misread us completely. The AI reasoned from our company name (it literally cited "Blitz" implying bold action) instead of the detailed questionnaire we had just completed, and proposed Hero, Magician, and Outlaw. Worse, all four suggestions arrived pre-selected; clicking Next without looking bakes the wrong personality into your report.
- The ICP generator invents statistics. A precise gender split, an income range, a decision timeline, all presented like research findings. None of it came from us or from any data. The qualitative persona underneath was solid, but fake precision is a real flaw in a tool whose reports may be shown to clients.
- The "Help me with AI" buttons on text fields push generic agency-speak. Every time we used our own copy instead, the downstream output was better.
- One radar chart contradicted its own written analysis, scoring a competitor high on a dimension its own bullet points called weak.

What was insightful:

- The three suggested brand directions were thought-provoking and composable rather than competing options.
- The per-competitor insight blocks (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats) were specific enough to inform real positioning work, not filler.

Who this is for:

Agencies and founders who already know their positioning, or are willing to review every AI suggestion before accepting it. Treat it as a structured workshop with a helpful, occasionally overconfident assistant, and you get real value. Click through on autopilot, and you will inherit its mistakes as your brand.

Verdict:

The engine underneath is better than the defaults it serves. Bring your own judgment, and Branding 5 earns its place in the workflow.

children.comment:
Thank you for such a thorough and fair review. It's rare to get feedback this specific, and it's exactly what helps us improve.

We're glad the core of the product worked for you.

reviews.title: Promising concept, but limited features and stalling roadmap
reviews.comment:
Pros:

* Decent UI: The user interface is clean, functional, and workable for basic navigation.
* Basic formatting: It functions okay if you just need a quick tool to import and format final text.

Cons:

* No style copying or consistency: The AI completely lacks the ability to match or mimic my own unique writing style. It also struggles heavily with long-term consistency, completely forgetting character details and world elements from one chapter to the next.
* Limited cover generator: While the covers look okay at first glance, the generator is highly limited. There are no editing options to tweak the results, and the final quality lacks the polish needed for professional publishing.
* Robotic voices: The audio generation is disappointing. The Italian voices and most others sound highly robotic and do not justify the price jump to higher tiers.
* Low prose quality: The AI writing model requires heavy manual editing. The translations are imperfect, and the text requires a lot of restructuring to sound natural.
* Stalling roadmap: While the founder seems nice and responds to feedback, actual product improvements have stalled since launch.
* Pricing shifts: Adding a Tier 4 feels like a cash grab that hurts customer trust, rather than improving the core features for early backers.

Verdict:
I originally started at Tier 3 for the audio voices and higher limits, but due to the low prose quality, robotic audio, lack of cover editing, and poor character/style consistency, I decided to downgrade to Tier 1. For me, it's a 2-3-taco deal at the moment. It has potential, but it needs serious updates to the core functionality before it is truly useful and better support and progress.

reviews.title: For best results, you need to make it work for you.
reviews.comment:
Inkfluence AI can be a helpful tool or a disappointing one, depending on how you use it. Many of the negative reviews seem to come from users who have taken the app builder’s claims too literally. For example, the Influence AI page on AppSumo states, “Generate complete books and eBooks from a single prompt, with structured chapters, covers, and branded layouts.” This promotion suggests you can create an entire e-book by providing just one simple prompt. While this may be the app builder’s selling point, it should not be interpreted literally.

I subscribe to several apps for writing both fiction and non-fiction e-books. Each has its strengths, but the reality is that no writing app—Inkfluence AI included—can produce a polished, professional-quality book from a single prompt. If you try, the result will almost certainly be unsatisfactory.

To get the best outcome, you need to actively guide the app rather than expecting it to do all the work. You cannot simply hand over the entire book creation process—outlining, chapter generation, and writing—to the app and expect a polished book. Instead, you must develop the book concept yourself, create a detailed outline, decide on the number of chapters, and come up with chapter titles before feeding this structured information into the app.

Giving only a one- or two-line prompt in hopes of generating a complete e-book will likely produce unprofessional results. I’ve tested this myself, and the quality fell short of expectations. This is because even the most advanced large language model (LLM)- based apps start to “hallucinate,” generating inaccurate or irrelevant content when pushed with repeated corrections or vague instructions. Writing apps that rely on LLM technology share these limitations.

What I’ve found to work better is preparing a comprehensive outline, including chapter titles and summaries for each chapter, before using the app to flesh out the content. While this might sound like a lot of upfront work, it’s actually quite manageable, especially with tools like ChatGPT or Google Gemini.

Influence AI is no exception—it performs much better when approached with this strategy. I have used this method myself, and the results were very satisfying.

Inkfluenceai can give you higher-quality writing when you apply this strategy. This applies not only to non-fiction but also to fiction.

children.comment:
Thank you for taking the time to write this, it's a very useful review, and a very fair read of what these tools can and can't do.

You're right that a one line prompt only gets you so far, and your outline first approach is exactly how the best results come out of Inkfluence AI too.

The one thing I'd add is that you can do all of that inside the app rather than prepping it in ChatGPT first: On the dashboard, choose "Choose a format and add detail" instead of the quick prompt box. It builds the outline and then stops so you can go through it properly, rewrite chapter titles and summaries, add or remove chapters, reorder them, and only then does it write. Given how you already work, I think you'd get on well with it.

Really appreciate you laying all this out, we're actively working on improving the ability to outline & draft so say tuned for more updates.

Sam
