reviews.title: Influencer marketing without hiring an agency
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Jem Social is built for brands that want to find, contact, and manage creator relationships without hiring an influencer marketing agency.

What I like about the product is that it makes influencer discovery feel more accessible. A lot of influencer marketing tools seem built for large brands with large budgets, or they push you toward a managed service. Jem Social feels more useful for smaller brands, ecommerce companies, agencies, and founders who want to run creator outreach themselves and keep the process organized.

The value is in having creator discovery, outreach, campaign management, and relationship tracking in one place. Instead of manually searching social platforms, keeping creator lists in spreadsheets, and trying to remember who replied where, Jem Social gives you a more structured way to build and manage influencer campaigns.

I also like the positioning. It does not need to compete with expensive enterprise influencer platforms, instead, it focuses on helping underserved buyers get into influencer marketing with a more intuitive and affordable workflow.

On the first review, most of my notes were around polish and trust. There were leftover template pages, missing legal and help pages, creator database size numbers were inconsistent on different pages, and case study details that needed clearer attribution. The team has since addressed those, which is good to see and shows fast responsiveness.

I found the ‘Invite’ option in settings still did not work in my retest. Clicking it did not open anything. That does not affect the main creator discovery use case, but it is something I would still like to see fixed, especially for users who plan to bring others into the account.

Overall, Jem Social is worth considering if you want a more approachable way to discover creators, manage outreach, and run influencer campaigns. Its best fit is a brand or agency that wants to make influencer marketing more organized, measurable, and manageable in house.

children.comment:
Thank you for the detailed retest, and glad the earlier fixes landed well.

On the Invite option, clicking it should open your operating system's own share dialog, so it's odd that nothing opens at all for you. Could you tell us the device, operating system and version you tested on, and the browser if you were on web? That should let us reproduce it and get it sorted.

Really appreciate the thoroughness here, it's genuinely useful.

reviews.title: Great Concept and UI, But the Creator Base Isn't There Yet
reviews.comment:
I really wanted this tool to work out for my brand. The interface is clean (although I hate the pink), the overall idea is solid, and the developers have been receptive to feedback on minor UI issues. The core issue isn't the software itself—it's the quality and activity level of the platform's creator network.

Key Issues Experienced:
Direct Outreach Silence: I spent hours searching creators and pitching dozens of direct offers. After two weeks, I received zero replies. Because there are no 'last active' statuses or read receipts, it's impossible to know if these influencers are inactive or simply ignoring messages.

Unqualified Marketplace Applicants: I posted a public offer with explicit, basic criteria. Out of 20+ applications received from creators, not a single person met the requirements. It was clear the applicants didn't read the brief, and many relied on generic, copy-pasted AI scripts.

An influencer platform is only as effective as the community using it. Right now, the lack of creator vetting and activity standards makes it nearly impossible to get actual campaign ROI. I ended up refunding for now, but I hope the developers focus on curating and pruning their creator directory moving forward.

children.comment: Thank you for your feedback we are actively working on the key areas addressed. These are great points and area's we can improve in Q4. We hope you are willing to try us again after we address the rest of the issues you mentioned. We're expecting these concerns to be fixed by end of month.

reviews.title: Strong creator-marketing foundation with room to become a complete partnership platform
reviews.comment:
I purchased Jem Social at License Tier 2 because I wanted a more organized way to find creators and manage campaigns without relying on spreadsheets, scattered DMs, separate contracts, and disconnected payment systems.

What I like most is that Jem brings several important parts of creator marketing into one workflow. Users can search by platform, niche, location, follower count, engagement, activity, language, and other criteria. Creators can also be found through the AI Assistant, AI Shortlist, URL-based matching, or added from outside the platform.

The Opportunity Board is another feature I appreciate. Instead of depending entirely on cold outreach, a business can publish a detailed campaign brief and allow interested creators to apply. This gives campaign owners an opportunity to evaluate people who have already expressed interest in the work.

Jem also includes Gmail-connected outreach, direct conversations, offer negotiation, contracts, escrow payments, collaboration pipelines, production tracking, revisions, approvals, creator rebooking, and analytics. These features address a genuine buyer need by reducing the number of separate systems required to manage a creator campaign.

The analytics capabilities are especially useful. Campaigns can be organized around sales, conversions, leads, website traffic, engagement, app installs, or brand awareness. Jem can generate creator-specific tracking links that direct audiences to a selected landing page, helping businesses evaluate performance beyond views and follower counts.

I also found the documentation well organized. It walks users through brand setup, creator discovery, outreach, campaign briefs, bookings, production, and analytics. This is valuable for businesses that understand the potential of creator marketing but need a clear operational process.

There are some areas I would like to see improved. During my testing, the Influencer Finder returned “No influencers found” and displayed an “External API call failed with status: 400” error. Since creator discovery is one of Jem’s primary features, the search needs to be reliable and explain clearly when an external request fails.

My dashboard also shows 20 monthly Creator Bookings, while the AppSumo listing advertised 50. I would like that discrepancy corrected or explained.

Creator activity and responsiveness should be easier to evaluate. Last-active dates, average response times, invitation-response rates, read receipts, completed-campaign history, missed deadlines, and a verified-active badge would help users avoid spending credits and time contacting inactive profiles.

The Opportunity Board would benefit from stronger applicant screening as well. Campaign owners should be able to add required questions and filter applicants by niche, audience location, engagement, availability, relevant experience, and whether they meet the campaign requirements.

The largest opportunity I see is for Jem to expand into ongoing creator product partnerships. Many creators have trusted audiences and valuable expertise but no ebook, course, guide, workbook, template package, coaching offer, membership, or other digital product to sell. Marketers and product-development partners could help those creators identify audience needs, develop suitable products, and launch them through the creator’s platform.

Jem already has much of the infrastructure needed for this model: discovery, communication, agreements, deliverables, tracking links, analytics, and payments. Adding product-ownership terms, intellectual-property agreements, milestones, affiliate commissions, hybrid compensation, recurring revenue-share tracking, and automated commission payouts could extend Jem beyond one-time UGC campaigns.

What would motivate me to purchase the highest level is not only a larger booking allowance. I would want more Finder Credits and AI Searches proportional to that allowance, reliable active-creator verification, advanced screening, team and client workspaces, higher Autopilot limits, API or webhook access, advanced attribution reports, and support for continuing creator partnerships and revenue sharing.

Overall, Jem has a strong and thoughtfully organized foundation. It already addresses several real problems in creator discovery and campaign management. Correcting the Finder and account-limit issues would strengthen my confidence, while expanding into long-term creator partnerships would make the platform considerably more valuable and provide a compelling reason to upgrade.

questions.title: Can Jem support ongoing creator product partnerships and revenue sharing?
questions.comment:
Many creators have engaged audiences and valuable expertise but no clear product to sell. Marketers and product developers can identify these opportunities and help creators turn audience needs into ebooks, courses, guides, coaching offers, and other digital products. What is missing is a platform where both parties can safely manage the partnership.

Could Jem support this through custom agreements, ownership and usage terms, fixed-fee or revenue-share arrangements, commission tracking, launch deliverables, and automated payouts?

This could expand Jem beyond one-time UGC campaigns into long-term creator partnerships that generate recurring transactions, improve retention, and attract marketers, agencies, and product developers who want to build sustainable products with creators.

questions.title: Affiliate marketing?
questions.comment:
Hi there, does Jem.Social works with affiliation marketing or only paid per content?
What I mean is, can I sign up the creators on our affiliation program and pay them commissions based on sales performance?

children.comment:
Hi! Yes for running the campaigns, no for tracking the sales.

Affiliate is a built-in offer type. You can set the offer as Affiliate or Gifted + Affiliate with your commission percentage, so creators see the terms before they apply. Once booked, creators get a unique trackable link that redirects users to your provided destination, so you'll see clicks and content performance per creator in your Jem analytics section (views, likes, comments etc).

We don't connect to your store though, so we can't see your sales or pay commissions. That side stays in your existing affiliate program. Jem Social finds, manages and tracks the performance of your creators. Your own program handles the sales tracking and commission payouts.

Happy to walk you through setting one up. And if there's anything that would make this work better for you, tell us. User requests drive a good part of our roadmap.
You should make youtbe tutorial walk-through videos for this.

questions.title: Pre-booking messaging: How to negotiate with applicants?
questions.comment:
I currently have an active opportunity live and am receiving creator applications. Many applicants submit custom rates or requirements that don't align with my exact offer terms out of the gate.

I need a way to open a dialogue and message applicants directly to negotiate before committing, but right now I only see rigid "Accept" or "Decline" options on the application cards. Is there an existing way to message applicants before making a decision, or is a pre-booking chat feature on your roadmap?

children.comment:
Hi, thanks for this. You're right, and it's a fair gap. It's on our roadmap and we're actively working on opening chat directly from opportunity applications. It should ship very soon, and we'll keep you posted here as it progresses.

Appreciate you raising it, this is exactly the kind of feedback that helps us prioritise.

questions.title: Are these 250 M creators registered with JemSocial?
questions.comment:
There are 2 types of "influencer software".

1. The platform is a search tool. Where it openly search social platforms based on criteria. These are NOT creators registered with the platform. We'll be reaching out to creators as strangers.

2. The platform is a marketplace. Means, all of the creators registered with the platform and fully aware they're contacted by brands through the platform. Think of upwork or Fiverr, all freelancers are registered through the platform.

May I know which one is JemSocial? Because if it's a search tool, we already have plenty of that, we're looking for platforms.

Thank you very much.

children.comment:
Fair question. Jem is both, so let me be precise about which part is which.

The large database figures are your type 1: public social accounts indexed from across the platforms, where outreach is cold.

The marketplace side is separate and real. Creators sign up with Jem Social, build a media kit, set their rates, apply to the opportunities/jobs you post and pitch brands directly. Bookings, agreements and escrow payments all run through the platform, and those creators expect to hear from brands. It's a smaller pool than the search index, and I'd rather say that up front.

Thank you!

questions.comment:
Hi,
I've purchased Tier 2 for my two brands but encountered several issues:

1. Workspaces: Both workspaces share the same social media connections. How can I assign separate accounts to each brand and prevent publishing to the wrong channels?

2. AI images: Tier 2 explicitly includes 20 AI images/month and maps to Pro, yet I'm prompted to upgrade to Pro. Why isn't this feature available?

3. Email: I see "Mailgun Not Configured." Is Mailgun mandatory, and does it cost extra? Your website advertises using existing email accounts. Why can't I configure standard SMTP?

4. License limits: Are the 35 generated posts, 75 scheduled posts, 400 AI credits and email campaign allowances shared or per workspace?

Please clarify whether these are configuration issues, missing features or additional paid requirements.

Thanks,
Marcus

children.comment:
Hi Marcus, thanks for the detailed questions! Running two brands from one deal is exactly what Tier 2 is built for, so here's how it works:

1) Separate social accounts per brand
Each workspace is its own brand with its own Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn and X connections. Switch to a brand's workspace, connect that brand's accounts in Social accounts, and its posts only ever go to its own channels. Using the same LinkedIn or X profile for both brands? Just connect it in each workspace.

2) AI images
Tier 2 includes 20 AI images every month in each workspace. Turn them on in Settings → "Allow AI-generated images" (or with the toggle in the media picker) and they're ready to go.

3) Email: no Mailgun required
Mailgun is optional. Without it, you send straight from the email account you already use: Orchestra splits your list into BCC batches and opens each one ready to send in Gmail, Outlook or your mail app, with the subject and message already filled in. If you'd rather send fully automatically from your own domain at higher volume, connect a Mailgun account (Mailgun bills its sending directly). "Mailgun Not Configured" only means you haven't picked that option.

4) Limits
Monthly allowances apply in full to each workspace: 35 generated posts, 75 scheduled posts, 20 AI images and 4 email campaigns each, so two brands get double. Your 400 AI credits belong to the licence, are shared by both workspaces, never reset, and only kick in once a workspace has used its monthly allowance.

Happy to help you set up both brands. Just reach out to [email redacted] with your AppSumo order email.

The Orchestra Technical Team

children.comment:

Good question, and the good news is that the allowance works the other way round. On Tier 5, the monthly limits apply to each workspace, not to all ten combined. Each of your 10 brands gets its own 50 post generations, 30 AI images and 100 scheduled posts every month, and they reset monthly.

On top of that, the tier includes a one-time pool of 4,000 AI credits shared across all your workspaces. If a brand runs out of its monthly post or image generations, Orchestra draws from that pool automatically, so you aren't stopped mid-month. Scheduled posts are the one exception: they're a fixed monthly limit per workspace that credits don't extend.

You can also create one post and send it to several channels at once. Orchestra adapts the format for each platform.

If you'd like to compare tiers, the full breakdown is on the AppSumo listing, and I'm happy to answer anything else before you decide.

children.comment:
Hi,

Each workspace gets its own monthly allowance (posts, images, briefs, audits, AI visibility checks, ad plans, email campaigns), which resets every month. Separately, your plan includes a one-time pool of AI credits, shared across all your workspaces: 150, 400, 1,000, 2,000 or 4,000 depending on the tier. The pool doesn't refresh.

reviews.title: From brainstorming an idea to a coherent book draft
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Writing a few pages with AI is easy. Keeping an entire book consistent from the first chapter to the last is a different problem.

Aivolut Books can start even earlier than that. If you don't have the book idea figured out yet, you can give it some direction and have it brainstorm several concepts for you. You can also bring your own idea instead. I generated several book ideas, chose one I liked, and turned it into a full brief with a title, subtitle, premise, target reader and chapter outline.

From there, it generated a coherent multi-chapter nonfiction draft of several thousand words. What I like is that the book is treated as one project rather than a series of unrelated prompts. Aivolut keeps the brief, outline, writing style and source material together and uses that plan to guide the chapters as the manuscript is written. Which means less time reminding the AI what the book is supposed to be about every few chapters.

There is quite a bit around the writing itself too. I generated a cover that matched the book and could choose from different styles. It also produced the Amazon description and keywords without using additional credits. Once the manuscript is ready, you can export it as DOCX, EPUB or PDF and continue editing or prepare it for publishing.

Digital products are live too, so the platform can also be used for things like workbooks, guides, checklists and lead magnets. BYOK is available on tiers 3 and 4, which is useful for something as AI-heavy as generating and revising entire books.

During my original test, children's picture books and audiobooks were still marked as coming soon. Those features are now available on the Pro tier, along with manuscript import, translation and deeper research.

Additionally, during my first test, the saved ideas count updated but the actual list did not refresh until I reloaded the page. The team said they are addressing that issue.

Overall, I like that Aivolut Books doesn't assume I already have everything figured out. I can start by brainstorming book ideas, choose one worth pursuing, turn it into a structured brief and outline, and then generate the manuscript while keeping the whole book connected. This is much more useful than opening a general AI tool and trying to piece together a book one prompt and one chapter at a time. For self-publishers who want a guided path to a KDP-ready draft, it delivers.

questions.title: Output after verification is useless for my platforms can it be the same as input?
questions.comment: Hi when i enter my CSV file with the correct headers like NAME WEBSITE EMAIL ADRES, the output after the verification is useless there are so many added fields and entries and additional tekst that i can't use it on my platforms, is it possible that the input file stays the same ? without adding additional headers / text to it? so it only says NAME WEBSITE EMAIL for example

children.comment:
Thanks for the query. When a list is verified, our system preserves all of your original columns and appends about 20 verification detail columns (such as status, score, deliverability, and the verified email) so you have full insight into the results.

Currently, there is no option to automatically strip out the verification columns upon export. The reason you are seeing two email columns during import is that your original file contains an email column and our system appends its own verification columns as well, which can confuse import mappers like SendFox.

To resolve this easily for SendFox:

    Download the clean segment you want (such as Safe Only or Safe + Role).
    Open the downloaded CSV in Excel, Google Sheets, or any spreadsheet software.
    Delete the unwanted verification columns on the right, keeping only your original columns (such as NAME, WEBSITE, EMAIL).
    Save the CSV and import it into SendFox.

Have a wonderful day and a great week ahead!

questions.title: Catch All
questions.comment: when are you planning to release a feature for "catch-all" verifier?

children.comment: Thanks for the query. If an email is a true catch-all and drops rejected emails silently, the status of that email cannot be detected. Some email server accepts the email regularly and later they send a reply email for the invalid ones saying that the address does not exists. Some companies send real email and wait up-to a certain time (max 24 hours) to check if they receive any such emails. However, sending a real email for verification is one kind of spamming and not legal. So we do not have any plan to take this route. However, if there is a good way to detect catch-all addresses for any specific email providers, we will do that. In fact, we can already detect the status of catch-all addresses for some specific companies (without sending any email).

reviews.title: Good basic email service, but needs a few improvements

Like: The user interface is reasonably easy to use and understand (though the videos need updating as it has changed slightly since they were made). The automation builder was straight forward and I really liked how the emails could be cloned and made into templates. The email builder itself was also easy to use if you just want to create simple emails. It's great that SendFox is also able to directly integrate with Book Funnel and Story Origin.

Dislike: No text wrapping in email builder. This gives less flexibility in design layout and while there are workarounds, they don't look good for both desktop and mobile. I also wish there was an 'or' feature in the automations, especially for triggers, so new subscribers could enter a flow by being added into this group OR this group OR this group. Having said that, I'm not sure it is a regular feature in any ESP, but it would be great. Forcing double opt in is also a little problematic, as subscribers may have already completed double opt-in before they hit Send Fox. This creates extra friction and annoyance for subscribers, and means I need to manually follow up or manually cull them so they don't weigh my list down. Once inside, I also discovered that someone unsubscribed cannot resubscribe later if they want to. That could be a problem.

Overall though, it is a very affordable and easy to use platform and I am mostly satisfied so far.

questions.title: Multiple sender addresses on Lifetime Tier 1
questions.comment:
I'm considering purchasing the $29 SendFox Lifetime Tier 1 plan through AppSumo.

I publish under two author names, each with its own domain and email address.

Can I use one SendFox account to send automated welcome sequences from two different verified sender email addresses, with separate contact lists and automations for each author identity?

Does the Lifetime Tier 1 license support this without additional fees?

Thank you!

children.comment:
Hello, thanks for reaching out!

Yes, one SendFox account can do this. The sender isn't set once for the whole account: every email and every automation email has its own From name and From email, so each author's welcome sequence can go out under its own name and address.

To send from your own addresses, verify each domain under Settings > Sending > Email domains by adding three CNAME records to its DNS. You can verify both domains on the same account, and that's included in the lifetime plan at no extra cost. Verification is per domain rather than per address, so any address on a verified domain sends as itself.

Lists and automations aren't limited on the lifetime plan either. An automation is triggered by a list, so you can keep one list and one welcome sequence per author.

Two things are shared, because it is a single account. The plan's contact limit and send pool cover both authors together, and the company name and postal address in the email footer are set once for the account, so the same footer appears under both names.

Domain setup guide: https://help.sendfox.com/article/279-how-do-i-validate-my-domain

If you have any other questions, feel free to reach out to us at [email redacted] and we'll be happy to help!

reviews.title: We're really happy with SalesBlink

We are using SalesBlink for email outreach and it was really easy to set up and understand. We are new to email outreach, but the bot answered all of my questions and I had it running when the live agent checked in.

First, the app runs the lead verification when you first import the list. Some of the verified leads could go bad while waiting in que to be sent. I think that the verification should be closer to when the email is sent this way it is more accurate for the automation.

Second, there is no way to manipulate or filter the lists when organizing them in the Lists section. I have to export the list to Sheets to change capitalizations and I also can't manually reorder the list categories, when I'm going through them. I wanted to filter them according to whether they were good, bad, or maybe but I was limited to them automatically going into the regular folder or the archive folder. There is limited manipulating in the Lists area, so I had to export and do work arounds to try and get the best out of our list. 

Overall, we are happy with the program. Hopefully there will be improvements and it will get even better!

reviews.title: Essential Tool That Replaced Three Monthly Subscriptions
reviews.comment:
Before grabbing SalesBlink on AppSumo, my outreach stack was expensive and fragmented. I was paying recurring monthly fees for cold email automation, a separate per-mailbox warm-up tool, an AI writing assistant, and a third-party calendar scheduler. SalesBlink consolidated everything into one clean platform on a lifetime license.

The setup was seamless across my sending accounts. The automated email warm-up and smart sender rotation protect domain health without needing manual intervention. Inboxes scale safely, keeping messages out of spam filters and landing right in primary inboxes.

BlinkGPT is a huge time-saver. Instead of spending hours writing copy and pacing follow-ups, I input a quick summary of my offer and audience, and the AI generates a multi-step sequence in minutes. The drafts are punchy, conversational, and avoid generic sales fluff.

Day-to-day management is equally smooth with the Master Unibox, which aggregates replies from all sending domains into a single inbox. The integrated calendar scheduler lets leads book meetings directly from messages, automatically halting ongoing sequence touches so nobody gets redundant follow-ups.

For founders, freelancers, and agency teams wanting to scale outreach without getting hit by recurring per-seat fees, SalesBlink delivers outstanding reliability and value. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Great tool for cold email outreach
reviews.comment:
I’ve been using SalesBlink for cold email outreach and overall I’m very satisfied with the platform. Setting up email sequences is straightforward, and having follow-ups, personalization and campaign management in one place makes the outreach process much easier.

I especially like that the platform combines several tools that would otherwise require separate services. This saves time when managing multiple campaigns and email accounts.

There is still some room for improvement in the interface and certain workflows could be more intuitive, especially when setting things up for the first time. However, once everything is configured, the platform is practical and easy to work with.

Overall, SalesBlink offers very good value for money for businesses and teams doing regular cold email outreach.

reviews.title: Fantastic tool
reviews.comment:
I've used Instantly, SalesHandy, and several other tools that are usually considered the go-to options for cold email outreach.

Surprisingly, Mystrika has outperformed all of them for me. I've been using it for over two years, and it's been consistently reliable throughout. I even ran side-by-side tests comparing its warmup network with Instantly's, and Mystrika delivered noticeably better results. Within a month, my email deliverability improved significantly compared to what I was seeing with Instantly.

The UI still feels a bit clunky, even after the V2 update, and it doesn't have the polished look of some competitors. But when it comes to the things that actually matter - deliverability, reliability, and getting emails into inboxes - it simply gets the job done, and it does it exceptionally well.

P.S. Writing this after two years of using the product, simply because I appreciate what the founder has built and consistently delivered.

reviews.title: Unfortunately, the interface is very outdated and highly illogical.
reviews.comment:
Update to my review following the team's reply:

1. This is not my first experience with this type of service. I am well aware of how these tools operate.
2. I genuinely tried multiple times to add a domain for emails in your system. But your interface never once showed the actual reason for the errors.
3. Instead of making the service actually workable, you almost immediately sent me a link to buy ready-made mailboxes tailored for your platform.
4. I can only conclude that selling this LTD (Lifetime Deal) is nothing more than a bait-and-switch tactic to upsell and lock in paying customers.
5. For several days, the service was completely down. You sent a screenshot showing a massive spike in server load, and only after that did the service come back online. This means you either don't monitor your uptime at all, or you do a very poor job of tracking performance. That is definitely not what I expect from a B2B tool.
6. I got tired of trying to find a workaround for your service and ended up paying for SalesBlink. Compared to yours, everything there is running perfectly so far. It took me less than 15 minutes to connect multiple email providers and set up 30 mailboxes simply by connecting my Hermes agent via MCP. I don't know how it will perform in the long run, but I can say right now that it has a much more intuitive and user-friendly interface, highly detailed and clear documentation, and highly functional API and MCP integrations. These allow you to drastically expand the platform's capabilities, as well as manage and interact with it remotely.
7. And yes, your support did respond to my ticket, but after that, I had no desire to return to your platform. I even tried to find your roadmap, hoping that the necessary, modern updates might be on the way. But all I saw were endless user complaints about your confusing interface, making me realize that you are intentionally ignoring the problem. I left an honest, objective review stating exactly what was missing (and I didn't even mention a competitor right away).
8. Instead of taking this feedback on board—from someone who spent a significant amount of time testing your app and reporting the issues found—you decided to blame your customer. Objectively speaking, because of your platform, my campaigns are now launching two weeks late.

Unfortunately, the interface is very outdated and highly illogical. It provides no feedback when errors occur, and sometimes it throws error messages for issues that definitely don't exist. I spent a lot of time trying to add sending domains, but nothing worked out, and it's impossible to figure things out without support. The API integration is also very weak. I was highly disappointed by the lack of integration with modern AI agents, including the ability to connect and configure via MCP. I didn't even get to test the actual functionality—honestly, it was just a massive waste of time.

Because the sentiment and the 5-taco rating don’t match, we had to deny the review until the rating and content are consistent.

Once you’ve edited the review to align rating and sentiment, resubmit and we’ll approve it.

Hi There,

We’re sorry to hear you’re encountering difficulties in using Mystrika at maximum capacity for your business growth.

Let me explain how email campaigns work in Mystrika, and why sometimes your campaign takes longer than expected. 👇

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗽:
• 100 prospects to email
• 3 sending emails - emailA, emailB, emailC
• Sequence: Email 1 → wait 3 days → Email 2 → wait 5 days → Email 3
• Campaign daily limit: 30 emails/day
• Each sending email address limit: 20 emails/day

𝗗𝗮𝘆-𝗯𝘆-𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝗕𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗱𝗼𝘄𝗻:

Day 1, 2, 3 → 30 new prospects get Email 1 each day. (90 prospects done, 10 remaining)

Day 4, 5, 6 → The first 90 prospects have waited their 3 days. Mystrika always by default prioritizes sending the NEXT email to prospects already mid-sequence (option available in campaign to override default behaviour). So 30 prospects per day get Email 2. The last 10 new prospects still wait.

Day 7 → The final 10 new prospects get Email 1. The remaining 20 daily slots sit EMPTY because no prospect has completed their 5-day wait for Email 3 yet. Those slots cannot be filled by anyone.

Day 8 → Nothing sent. Everyone is still in the 5-day waiting period.

Day 9, 10, 11 → 30 prospects per day finally get Email 3.

Day 12 → Last 10 prospects get Email 3. Campaign complete!

So what felt like it should finish in 6 days actually takes 12. The delays between emails + daily sending limits are the #1 reason campaigns run longer than expected. Your schedule settings (weekdays only, specific hours etc.) also affect this.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝗶𝗳 𝗮 𝘀𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗹 𝗴𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗱?

Say emailA gets disabled on Day 4 due to an error. Every prospect assigned to emailA is now paused - extending your timeline further.

Mystrika intentionally keeps each prospect tied to their assigned sending email address throughout the entire campaign. This is by design - receiving emails from the same address looks natural and professional.

You have two options:
✅ Fix and re-enable emailA → Mystrika automatically resumes exactly where it stopped. No manual work needed.
✅ Remove emailA from the campaign → Mystrika reassigns those prospects to emailB or emailC and continues. (Be careful to only remove emailA and not accidentally unselect the other addresses!)

𝗧𝗵𝗲 "?" 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝘂𝘀 (𝗨𝗻𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗻):

If a campaign goes a full week without sending a single email - due to disabled email addresses or everyone being stuck in a delay gap - Mystrika will auto-pause the campaign and show a "?" status. This is just Mystrika alerting you: "Nothing has moved in 7 days, please check!" It's a safety net so campaigns don't stall silently without you noticing.

𝗪𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗲𝗲 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗰𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗱𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴?

Go to Campaign Analytics → https://my.mystrika.com/analytics → click the ⋮ (three dots) on your campaign → select "Activity Stream". You'll get a detailed log of the last 1000 actions your campaign performed - so you can see exactly what's happening and why, step by step.

The two biggest reasons campaigns run slow: daily sending limits spreading emails over many days, and sequence delays creating idle gaps. Plan these carefully and you'll always know your real completion timeline. 🙂

reviews.title: Good Tool but Buggy
reviews.comment:
I purchased this tool for my YouStable Hosting campaigns expecting a streamlined solution to filter out fraudulent clicks—such as VPN traffic, proxy IPs, and high frequency device abuse. The overall concept is straightforward and aligns with what most advertisers should already be implementing as a baseline protection layer.

However, during practical usage, I experienced several operational issues that need attention:

	1.	There is no proper code or domain validation mechanism in place.
	2.	Profile updates frequently return an error.
	3.	The dashboard provides very limited actionable data.
	4.	Clicking on a campaign sometimes results in a 404 error.
	5.	The system displays all campaigns together — active, inactive, paused, and even deleted — which makes campaign management confusing.

While the idea behind the tool is relevant and necessary for performance marketers, the current execution feels unstable. With improvements in stability, validation systems, and dashboard clarity, it could become significantly more reliable for advertisers who depend on accurate click filtering

This went unnoticed for 10 days, resulting in a complete loss of leads across five campaigns, costing us thousands in wasted ad spend and lost sales opportunities.

Additionally, I suspect that some of the “blocked” clicks might have been legitimate visitors attempting to reload the page when it didn’t load properly, although I can’t confirm this. 

We manually removed the IPs it flagged, but I’m concerned about the potential long-term impact on our Google Ads campaign, especially given the high bounce rate this issue caused.

I’m deeply disappointed. We’ve used many AppSumo deals, and this is the first time one has cost us money rather than saving it. 

Sadly, this experience has set us back and left us out of pocket. I feel like I've been robbed of my money.

reviews.title: Still using this 6 years later — hard to beat for the price
reviews.comment:
I bought Switchy six years ago and have been using it across campaigns ever since. When I saw it back on AppSumo at the same price, that alone tells you something — tools that hold their value over that kind of timeline are not common.

What Switchy actually gives you is control over what happens after someone clicks. Custom domains, UTMs, retargeting pixels, and redirect logic mean you can control how links behave based on the channel, the audience, or the campaign stage. For anyone running traffic across multiple platforms, that flexibility has compounding value over time.

Where it is more limited is analytics. It functions as a monitoring layer — you can see what is happening at the link level — but it is not a full reporting solution. If you are expecting deep segmentation or campaign-level attribution, you will want to supplement it elsewhere.

The product feels more maintained than actively developed.

The core functionality is solid and does what it says, but do not buy it expecting a roadmap of new features. Buy it because what it does today is genuinely useful and the one-time pricing makes that a reasonable long-term bet.

If you care about tracking, retargeting, and control more than feature expansion, Switchy still holds up.

Full review: https://marketingwithdave.com/switchy-review/

Switchy vs Linko comparison: https://marketingwithdave.com/switchy-vs-linko-link-management-software-comparison/

reviews.title: Fantastic Product!
reviews.comment:
Switchy is an AMAZING product and probably one of my best AppSumo buys. I have bought a total of 10 codes (maxed out two accounts), and I might still want more codes in the future, because it's just so good!

The re-directs could be just a tiny bit faster and it would be even more amazing, but the slow down is hardly noticeable most of the time, and it really does EXACTLTY what you need it to do. It also offers so much flexibility in how you set up your links on your domains. You can for example set go.domain.com and then create endless links on that subdomain, or anything else you want to do.

I couldn't give a stronger recommendation, and if I built it myself (I have built my own link trackers in the past) I wouldn't change a single thing (other than perhaps upgrade the servers to be even faster)! If you have more than one website, just buy it and stop worrying about how you are going to deal with links and enjoy awesome tracking on everything.

reviews.title: Promising European email marketing tool with fair pricing
reviews.comment:
We bought InTouch because we were looking for an email marketing solution for three of our brands. Even though it was a Launchpad deal, we chose tier 3 so we could really try it out.
So far, the experience has been very positive. The interface looks great, everything feels clear, and I especially like the automation journey. It is still in beta, but it already makes building an email flow feel very visual and intuitive.

We chose InTouch for two main reasons:
First, we are planning to move to Italy next year, so it feels good to support an Italian business. It is also a European company, and we are trying to move more of our overseas subscriptions to European alternatives.
Second, I really like that their pricing is based on the number of emails sent rather than the number of subscribers. For us, that feels like a much fairer proposition. I am not an avid newsletter writer, and I have always found it frustrating to pay based on subscriber numbers when actual usage depends on how many emails you send.

Of course, there are still a few things that could be improved; it’s a new product, so that’s to be expected. The onboarding process, for example, currently uses a PDF form, which feels a bit clunky. That said, I could also smile about it, and the support team was quick to help us out. 
They addressed all our questions and minor issues promptly. I do hope the template builder gets a makeover at some point. It feels a little outdated, but it does work.

Overall, InTouch feels like a promising platform with a clear interface, a fair pricing model, and a responsive, helpful support team. We feel confident enough to purchase two more Tier 3 licenses for our other businesses.

children.comment:
Hi Nicolet,
thank you very much for your review! It's been great to read it! We will do our best to continuously improve inTouch. Any advice is more than welcome of course! We look forward to welcoming you in Italy! Let's stay inTouch :-)

questions.title: Is the 5,000 pages/project crawl limit per audit or a monthly quota?
questions.comment: Hi! Considering the LTD mainly for site audits. A few questions: 1) Is the 5,000 crawl pages/project a cap per crawl (max site size), or a monthly page allowance that resets? 2) How many re-crawls/audits per month are included in the LTD, and is there a credit limit? 3) Can I schedule automatic recurring audits (e.g., weekly)? Thanks!

children.comment:
Hi,

Thank you for reaching out.

The 5,000 pages per project limit refers to the maximum number of pages that can be added and crawled within a single project. It is not a monthly quota or a limit that resets after each audit.

For example, if your website has more than 5,000 pages, Screpy will analyze up to 5,000 pages of that project. You can then set the analysis frequency from your Project Settings according to your preference.

Whenever a new analysis runs, the pages within your selected limit will be crawled and checked again. There is no need for a monthly renewal because this limit is not based on credits—it simply defines the maximum number of pages that can be added and analyzed for a project.

If you have any other questions about the crawl limits or analysis frequency, please feel free to let me know. I’ll be happy to help.

Best regards,  
The Screpy Team

Stay well away from this plugin and find an alternative, unless you're fine with underhanded practices and egregious HTTP requests back to their own server. The plugin creators, WebFactory Ltd, go to lengths to silently add their own plugins to the first positions on the 'Add plugin' page on your dashboard. There's no indication that these have been added by a third party, and you have no control over this whatsoever as there's no option to control it. I poked through the plugin's code and there's not even a hook to stop this nefarious behaviour, it's astounding.

Sent them an email about this a while back and they never even bothered to reply. Here's the email, verbatim:

"1) It's absolutely disgraceful that you maliciously add two of your own plugins to the 'Add plugins' menu, in first and second position, with no disclosure that you're doing such. On a premium plugin, mind you.

2) What is with the insane HTTP requests to your API? That there's no setting for this and you's think this is okay is absolutely mental!"

I used this plugin for quite a long time, but never again.

questions.title: Uses for WP301 Redirects
questions.comment:
Hi, I'm new to this form of traffic redirections so I have 2 questions:
1) I have a few expired domains (local keyword exact match domains) with good Trust authority and DA, in checking WayBack on the site back when it was up, there are a number of blog articles that would still be relevant in today Search world.  Can you explain how using this tool might be able to help me keep the authority in Google's eyes (no 404s etc) and not lose clicks?
2) I have a few domains I've acquired after they were abandoned by YT Channel Creators that are no longer active on Youtube video channels, but their videos are still commanding lots of daily views, and I'd like to redirect those clicks to an affiliate product or signup page. Can this be accomplished with WP301 Redirects? E.g. www.cryptonet.com/cryptoprofits (made up URL)

children.comment:
Hi, 
Thanks for taking an interest in WP 301 Redirects!

1) Yes, you can do that. Just install the plugin on the site, and create new redirect rules. Since you say they're expired, you would of course have to renew the domains and install WordPress on the site, so you install the plugin in the first place.
The plugin will also help you identify 404s, so you can then redirect them.

You can also turn on automatic redirections, so people get automatically redirected if they enter the wrong URL. For example, if the try to open yoursite.com/contatc instead of yoursite.com/contact, the would be automatically redirected to the right page :)

2) Sure, it's a simple redirect rule you can create to redirect such a page from your site to any other page/site you want. However, note that you can't redirect a YouTube video; you can redirect a page where the video was embedded from your site.

questions.title: Does This Do Smart Redirects Now?
questions.comment: Can it detect a 404 and then 'smartly redirect' it to the most appropriate page?

children.comment:
Hi,
Thanks for taking an interest in WP 301 Redirects.

Yes, there's an autoredirect option which, when turned on, finds the most similar slug to a 404 page, and automatically redirects to it.

For example, if a user ends up on /your-pge, and you have a /your-page URL, it would be automatically recognized and redirected :)
Thanks. Do you also have a bulk delete if we need?
No, sorry, there's no bulk delete option.
If there is no bulk delete option, how do you handle regular clean ups and removals of old redirects?

You can manage redirects through the plugin and dashboard. It is possible to create/remove rules as you wish. You can also use the scanner to find problematic links; the only thing is that you can't manage/delete them in bulk, but you have to handle them one by one.

reviews.title: An ad agent that can go from analysis to action
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

A lot of AI marketing tools can look at your ad data and tell you what they think you should do. Soku is designed to continue past the recommendation and actually make the change.

You can connect Google Ads, Meta and TikTok, along with sources such as GA4, Shopify and Search Console so Soku has the conversion and revenue context behind the ad performance. It can then find things like wasted spend, ROAS drops, CPA spikes or campaigns that need attention.

You also don't have to hand over full control on day one. Read access is the default, so you can start by letting Soku audit the accounts and make recommendations. From there, you can enable actions that require approval and eventually let routine changes run automatically within the rules you set.

Soku can do things such as pause ads, move budget, add negative keywords and launch new ads rather than simply producing another report telling you to do those things yourself. Actions that could increase spend can still be held for approval, and the activity log shows what changed and the numbers behind the decision.

The automation side should also save a lot of checking. You can schedule daily and weekly briefs and set alerts for things like ROAS drops, CPA spikes and unusual spending, so you don't have to keep three advertising dashboards open waiting to notice something has gone wrong.

There are creative tools in the same platform too. You can take an existing ad and resize, localize, caption or modify it, or turn a product image into another ad variation without starting over.

During my testing, I also found the API and MCP connection available, along with BYOK under Integrations. I didn't run into anything that warranted an action item for the partner. Native webhooks would still be a useful addition for completed automations, approvals and credit thresholds, but that was more of a suggestion and a wishlist item from me.

One thing to understand with the AppSumo deal is how credits work. They are used for AI work such as analysis, creative generation and agent actions, reset each month and don't roll over. Additional one-time credit packs are available and those do not expire.

Overall, I think Soku's advantage is that it closes the loop between noticing a problem in an ad account and doing something about it. You can keep yourself involved in the decisions you want to approve while letting Soku handle more of the repetitive monitoring and execution.

children.comment: Thanks for the thorough review, Abe! You captured what we're going for: closing the loop between spotting a problem in an ad account and actually fixing it, while you stay in control of what needs your approval. Good call-out on how credits work too. Monthly credits reset, and one-time credit packs never expire. Native webhooks for completed automations, approvals and credit thresholds are on our list. Thanks again for taking the time to test Soku so carefully.

reviews.title: Not ready for prime time.
reviews.comment:
I bought this tool and tested it with a few different cases, but I was pretty disappointed for the following reasons, which is also why I am going to request a refund.

1. When you first log in, the tool forces you to connect something. There is no way to skip this step, which is annoying and frustrating. From a user perspective, this is not ideal and does not provide a clean experience.  

2. The AI is very slow, and having to use chats to go through every single step is not ideal either. You waste a lot of time.  

3. Regarding the chat, after connecting an ad account, I asked it to set up a simple boosted post campaign in Meta Ads. I gave clear instructions on how to name the campaign and ads, and provided a clear brief on the campaign objective, budget, audience, and more. It took 25 minutes and still was not able to set up 95% of the campaign. It kept running into issues. It only created the campaign but did not add any ad sets. All while I was talking to it and waiting for 25 minutes. At the same time, it used 3,000 credits without success, which was very disappointing. This type of tool will not improve my work or help me be more efficient when setting up campaigns for clients. If I set up the campaign myself, it takes five minutes. This AI tool took 25 minutes and did not set up anything for me.  

4. Claude can do all of this faster and costs less since I am not paying for credits. I did the same test with Claude, and instead of pausing or running into issues, Claude completed the entire process in about five minutes and set up the drafted, paused campaign in Meta Ads without stopping or reporting any issues. I really do not see the value in this tool. If you use Claude or another AI platform that has mcp, it can already set up the campaign for you if connected to your Meta Ads account.  

5. The tool seems like just a WRAPPER. It likely uses third-party tools + ai api's, but its capabilities are much more limited and it is much slower than using AI platforms like claude directly.  

6. The other features in the tool looked interesting, such as dashboards and some other sections. I tried to sync data into the dashboard, but nothing loaded after 30 minutes while it said it was still processing.

Overall, I did not enjoy my experience using this tool. I feel I can already do all of this using Claude, so I do not see the value of adding this to my toolset. It is very slow, and I do not have time to wait for a tool that makes mistakes, uses credits while I wait, and fails to complete tasks. For that reason, I do not like this and will request a refund.

Too bad, I had high hopes for this tool. It is always good to test tools you buy here with real use cases so you do not waste your money.

P.s. Maybe this tool is better suited for simple tasks like writing content for SEO blogs, as the person below my review mentions, but I would not recommend it for more technical tasks like meta ad/ google ad setup.

children.comment:
Thanks for testing Soku on a real client brief and writing this up in detail. I'm sorry it cost you an evening. Here's what we found when we went through your session:

1. Connecting: the Connect Tools step during setup is optional. The button at the bottom reads "Skip for now" until something is connected. If it didn't come across that way, that's on our wording and we'll make it clearer.

2-3. The Meta build: you're right that it was too slow. Soku created the campaign shell, then Meta rejected the first ad set because the campaign's bid strategy needed a bid cap. Soku retried with lowest-cost bidding and that ad set was created a few minutes later (paused, IL/IN/TX, 40-65+, $50 lifetime). It never got to the ad itself, the boosted post, and every step waited on an approval in chat. A 5-minute job taking 25 minutes and ~3,000 credits isn't acceptable, and we're fixing the bid-strategy default that caused the first failure.

6. Dashboard: the first sync for your connected Meta accounts took about 35 minutes to finish, so it was still loading when you checked. That's too long for a first impression, and speeding up first-time syncs is a priority for us.

On Claude + MCP: fair comparison. Soku's value is the parts around one-off builds: approval-gated changes across Meta, Google and TikTok, cross-channel reporting, and automations that keep running without someone in the chat. But that has to be fast to be worth it, and your session wasn't. Sorry again, and thanks for the honest feedback.

reviews.title: It's good. It's real good.
reviews.comment:
Soku is a game-changer. It is highly customizable and truly autonomous, as it quickly understands your business and begins executing marketing strategies on your behalf. Having purchased other marketing tools on AppSumo, I can confidently say that Soku beats them all hands down. It is one thing to have an app that provides real data, but it is entirely another to have one that acts on that data without needing constant direction. For instance, Soku has already begun writing and posting SEO-optimized blog content to my site without me having to lift a finger. This is an incredible tool for anyone looking to automate their marketing efforts.

The team is highly responsive, as you can see from the Q&A and the push are currently pushing updates very quickly. I'm floored by the experience thus far. Just waiting to see if this is campaign specific or true dedication to an amazing app and it's users.

children.comment: Thank you, TetanicRaptor! It means a lot, especially from someone who pushed us hard in the Q&A this week. Your feedback is the reason the canvas now has 11 video models in the app. On your last line: we're a small team that ships most days, and that pace isn't tied to the campaign. Keep the requests coming, we read every one.

children.comment:

2. Yes. All Tier 1 benefits are included with no extra subscription: 3 brands, 2 members and the Tier 1 credits.
3. Already done for your account: the license is now attached to your workspace, so a refresh should let you add your second and third brands. I've also replied to your support email.

We found two other buyers in the same state and fixed theirs too, and the sign-up path that caused it is being fixed now. If any other Tier 1 buyer still sees an upgrade prompt for brands 2 or 3, post here and we'll sort it right away.

reviews.title: Good entry point for SEO newbies
reviews.comment:
A SEO expert friend recommended such a tool so that I can gain clear insights into keywords positionning. I find writerzen very practical in its approach: from topic research, to keyword explorer and planner.

A feature I like is building keywords list that can be exported with keywords related ranking data such as the golden ratio or all in title results count, I used this to feed into ChatGPT in order to rewrite an article using those optimized keywords.

While I cannot say yet if the data is accurate enough to help ranking, I surely like the fact that topic research gives a good alternative to search engines and LLMs answers in order to discover hidden gems and see what topics resolve around keywords, in order to access less unbiased informations than what google or OpenAi wants to show !

reviews.title: From Research to Content Creation in One Dashboard
reviews.comment:
I found out about WriterZen and NeuronWriter when I attended SEOCON in Jakarta a few years ago. Both tools really caught my attention, and for about a year I used NeuronWriter for my daily office work. Recently, I started switching to WriterZen because not only does it have strong content creation features, but it also offers keyword and topic research in one platform, which I find very convenient. This also helps me reduce my use of SEMrush, which is quite expensive, especially for keyword research before turning it into content or articles.

For me, the main drawback of WriterZen is that its Google NLP feature still requires an additional payment, while in NeuronWriter this feature is already included in the package.

questions.title: Client Onboarding etc
questions.comment:
I run an agency and I am choosing a tool for Google Business Profiles and reviews for local businesses. Short answers please, five points:

Client onboarding: Can a client connect their Google profile with one link (no login sharing, no screen share)? How many clicks does it take for the client?
Geo map: Do you have a geo-grid heatmap per keyword? 
Review requests: Can I send requests by email and WhatsApp (or SMS) from the tool? Is there a drip setting (limit per day or week, follow-ups)?
AI review replies: Replies must never be posted automatically. The AI only suggests, and the business owner edits and posts. Is “suggest only” possible, and is it the default?
What else matters? What would you add that an agency should know before choosing (limits, extra costs, data hosting in the EU, German language)?

children.comment:
Client onboarding. The client never shares their Google password, and they can disconnect Google at any time. There is no standalone link they can open later on their own phone. Two ways: (1) You stay logged into Rating Captain Local and click Link Google account. On that same browser the client picks their Google account and allows Business Profile access — a few clicks on Google’s consent screen, no password shown to you. (2) The client adds your Google user as a Manager on the Business Profile in Google. You then connect your own Google account. No screen share and no login sharing.
Geo map. Yes. Each keyword has its own geo-grid rank map. The default grid is 9×9 (81 points) over a 5×5 km area, colored by position.
Review requests. Email: yes, from Rating Captain Reviews. WhatsApp: no. SMS: yes, but only with a separate SMS credit pack — base plans include no SMS volume. Drip: email follow-ups are none, one, or two extra sends, spaced 10, 5, or 2 days apart. There is also a daily cap and a monthly cap. This is not a long multi-step WhatsApp drip.
AI review replies. Suggest-only is the default. Generate reply fills a draft. Nothing is posted until a person publishes it. Automatic posting is a separate switch (“Enable AI Automatic Responses”) and stays off until someone turns it on. Leave it off and replies are never posted by themselves.
What an agency should know. AppSumo is Rating Captain Local (profiles, map, posts, AI replies). Review invitations are a separate product, Rating Captain Reviews. Local AppSumo tiers: locations 5 / 10 / 25 / 50 / unlimited; keywords per location 10 / 25 / 150 / 300 / 1000; AI credits per account 200 / 1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 15,000 (more can be added); rank history 90 days on tiers 1–2 and 365 days on tiers 3–5. Reviews email volume depends on that plan’s monthly and daily cap. SMS is extra. The app UI is available in German (Reviews also has Swiss German). AI replies can be written in the review’s own language, including German. Production hosting is AWS in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Team members can be added, and report links can be white-label.

questions.title: Tier 5: What exactly does “White label rank tracker URL” include?

children.comment:
Hi,

Thanks for asking before you upgrade. Tier 5 does not turn Rating Captain into a fully white-labeled client portal under your agency brand. The extra white-label piece versus Tier 4 is one custom domain for the shared rank tracker and for white-label report links.

Here is how each of your points works:

1. Your own domain or subdomain, for example local.myagency.com
Yes, on Tier 5. In White-label settings you add one hostname and point its DNS A record to the IP shown there. The shared rank tracker link then opens on that host instead of our shared host, trackwith.us. White-label report links use the same domain. It is one domain for the whole account, not a different domain per client. Login, settings, and the rest of the app stay on local.ratingcaptain.com.

2. Completely remove Rating Captain branding from the client-facing rank tracker
On the public rank tracker link, your uploaded logo replaces ours in the header. That page is a read-only view of one location, or of one location group. It is not a rebranded copy of the whole product. Your own login, and your coworkers' logins, still show the Rating Captain header on local.ratingcaptain.com.

3. Your own logo
Yes. Upload it in White-label settings (PNG or JPG, up to 2 MB). It is used on the shared rank tracker link, on white-label reports, and in the sidebar for guest accounts. The logo is already available on Tier 4. You do not need Tier 5 only for this.

4. Separate access for different clients
Tier 4 already includes guest accounts and coworkers. You can invite a guest and limit them to selected profiles or location groups. Those guests log into Rating Captain. They do not get a login on your domain. You can also copy a share link per location or per group. Anyone with that link can view that rank tracker, without an account. There is no separate branded portal or account per client on your domain.

5. Your own email domain for client-facing emails
You can verify your own sending domain and set a sender name and sender address. Scheduled report emails then go out from that address. A white-label report email uses your logo instead of ours. Guest invitations and account emails, such as a password reset, still come from Rating Captain. The email domain is in the same White-label settings and is not what Tier 5 adds.

What you already have on Tier 4
- White-label reports: your logo, and the report page hides the Rating Captain name and favicon
- A shareable rank tracker URL, on trackwith.us
- Coworkers and guest accounts
- Location groups
- 50 locations, 300 keywords, and 5,000 AI credits per month

What Tier 5 adds
- That same rank tracker URL, and white-label report links, on your own domain
- Unlimited locations, 1,000 keywords, and 15,000 AI credits per month

If you want a full client portal on your domain, with a separate login per client and your brand on every email, Tier 5 does not do that. If you want to send clients a rank tracker and reports on your own domain, with your logo, Tier 5 is the tier that adds the custom domain.

Happy to clarify any of these.
I only see Tier 1 through Tier 3—where do you see Tier 5?

To clarify: Tier 5 was available during our previous campaign, where we offered a 5-tier structure. In our current AppSumo campaign, we restructured the offering to include only 3 tiers (Tier 1 through Tier 3).

questions.title: CutMe Short Events - please explain
questions.comment:
Can you help me understand what "CutMe Short Events" are, what they can be used for and how they are set up?

We use HubSpot for sales, so I'm curious if this is lead/sales data that can be synced with HubSpot or whether it is completely separate/not integrated.

children.comment:
Hi, thanks for the question!!

What CutMe Short Events are - 
Events are our conversion tracking layer. A short link tells you who clicked, but Events let you see what happened after the click. You can record a Lead event when a visitor signs up, fills a form or starts a trial, and a Sale event when they actually pay, with the amount attached. Both get tied back to the original click, so you know which link, campaign or channel produced that lead or that revenue instead of just counting clicks.

Typical use cases-
Attribute signups and revenue to specific links, campaigns, affiliates or social posts. Track which creators or partners are driving paying customers, not just traffic. Measure the real ROI of a campaign from click to sale.

How they are set up

You enable conversion tracking on the link, then fire the Lead or Sale event from your app or website when the action happens. That can be done through our API or by adding our tracking snippet on your signup and checkout pages. 

<< Also very soon we are launching Shopify connector where with just a few clicks you will be able to make this setup >>

On HubSpot

Honestly, this is a good suggestion and something we want to explore. Right now there is no direct integration with HubSpot or other CRMs. What you can do today is export your Lead and Sale events and bring that data into HubSpot on your side. We are going to discuss a native HubSpot integration internally and will keep you posted.

Also feel free to reach out at [email redacted] we would love to work with you to setup this for you as currently we are working with user closely for this.

Thanks again.

Thanks for your detailed response. Awesome - yes please look at seeing what integration you can do to get this data into HubSpot :-) This is a huge opportunity for more exposure for you as they don't have a generic link tracking tool in the HubSpot stack - the integrate with other platforms for this eg Rebrandly (but their product/integration is awful)

reviews.title: A rare comprehensive SEO tool that gets the AI pricing model right
reviews.comment:
If you're a solopreneur or small business owner juggling multiple websites, you know the frustration of hunting for tools that actually fit your workflow instead of forcing you into theirs. After digging through at least a dozen SEO optimization tools, I finally found Labrika that solves a problem I didn't expect to be so hard to solve.

Most content optimizers on the market are "closed" systems - they want you to write inside their editor, using their templates, locked into their ecosystem. That's not how I work. I write articles across various platforms and tools, and I needed an optimizer that could take my own already-written content from anywhere and optimize it intelligently. Labrika is the only tool I found that does this properly. 

You can paste in an article written outside the platform, and it will analyze and optimize it just as well as if it were created natively inside the tool. This single feature alone made the search worth it, and it's the reason I would recommend Labrika to anyone who values flexibility over walled-garden workflows.

Beyond that core feature, the more I explored the platform, the more impressed I was. Labrika packs in a huge amount of SEO functionality, presented cleanly and logically, and crucially the usage limits on the lifetime deal are genuinely generous. This isn't a tool where you feel throttled the moment you try to use it seriously. For anyone managing several websites, this makes the AppSumo LTD an easy purchase.

The second thing that impressed me is how Labrika has handled its AI suite. Unlike the core SEO tools, the AI features aren't bundled into the lifetime deal and honestly, that's the right call, for two reasons:
1.It's credit-based, not subscription-based. You purchase AI credits that last a full year, and you can use them for AI audits, content writing, and similar tasks at a very reasonable cost. There's no monthly lock-in ; you buy once, use at your own pace.
2. It's fairly priced. The cost-per-credit feels genuinely affordable for the value delivered, especially compared to what many competitors charge.

This matters more than it might seem at first glance. We have all seen LTD tools hand out "lifetime" AI tokens, only to watch the company buckle under the weight of rising AI API costs a year or two later. That model is fundamentally broken; it's a race to the bottom that ends in either degraded service or the tool disappearing altogether. I actively avoid these kinds of deals now.

On the flip side, plenty of tools that do get AI pricing "sustainable" end up charging steep monthly fees that price out small entrepreneurs and solopreneurs.

Labrika has found the middle ground that most companies miss: affordable, non-subscription AI credits that still keep the business sustainable on their end. That balance is rare, and it's exactly what independent creators and small business owners need.

Another underrated aspect of Labrika's pricing structure is that limits are tied to the number of pages, not the number of websites. If you're running ten or fifteen smaller sites which is common for people managing multiple niche projects, this structure works heavily in your favour. You're not penalized for having several properties; you're only constrained by your total content volume.

On the core SEO side, I genuinely haven't found a missing feature yet. Whatever I've needed for optimizing my websites - technical audits, on-page analysis, content optimization, Labrika has covered it.

I haven't tested the full depth of the AI suite yet, but what I have tried so far is promising, particularly for GEO needs and AI-driven audits. For anything outside that scope, I simply lean on other tools already in my stack - no single tool can do everything.

Final Verdict: Labrika has earned a central spot in my toolkit. It combines a flexible, open approach to content optimization with an AI pricing model that's actually sustainable for both the user and the company - something surprisingly few SEO tools manage to get right. If you're comparing lifetime deals and want a tool that won't feel gutted a year from now, and you also need the freedom to optimize content written anywhere, Labrika deserves serious consideration.

reviews.title: Finally, a SEO / GEO Tool That Truly Delivers!
reviews.comment:
We've tested quite a few tools that promise actionable SEO and GEO recommendations. Nuwtonic outperforms them by a mile.

The recommendations are genuinely useful, and the content it generates is remarkably accurate and well-reasoned. That's particularly impressive for us, as we operate in a highly technical publishing environment where precision and factual correctness are essential.

The analyses are thorough and well-founded. There's a learning curve, but it's surprisingly gentle. I wouldn't call the interface entirely intuitive, yet it doesn't take long to find your way around. And once you do, there's an impressive range of features to explore.

Another plus: a fair and reasonable credit system.

This is becoming an increasingly important factor for us. Far too many AI tools, not just in the SEO space, consume credits at an alarming rate. Run three or four substantial analyses, and suddenly your entire monthly allowance is gone. Often, it's not even clear how those credits are calculated or consumed.

Nuwtonic takes a more reasonable approach. The credit allowance is fair and sufficient for meaningful work. More importantly, the quality of the results you get for the credits you spend is outstanding. And ultimately, that's what matters: getting real value for your money.

We're certainly not giving this one up anytime soon. We just hope the team keeps developing Nuwtonic with the same commitment to quality, without losing what makes it so good in the first place.

Already one of the best purchases we've made on AppSumo. And we've made quite a few.

Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Runs my whole content program across multiple sites
reviews.comment: I run a content program across several websites, and Nuwtonic has become the tool I plan everything around. My main site has 280+ guides, and the topical maps plus internal-linking logic are the standout — it builds topical authority the way search engines (and now AI engines) actually reward. The GEO tracking across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI answers is the other half: I can see where my pages get cited and where they don't, and plan content from that. Honest cons: you do have to plan credits across projects so you don't burn them on low-value generations, audits and prompt tracking are one-by-one rather than bulk, and the first session has a learning curve. Five tacos, and I'd buy it again.

reviews.title: The AI-visibility tracker I didn’t know I needed, but I am glad I have now!
reviews.comment:
I’m a Houston real estate broker, and more of my future clients are asking ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity who to hire before they ever call anyone. Nuwtonic is how I find out whether those tools are recommending me.

It runs my tracked questions (“Who is the best Realtor in Houston?”, “Recommend a real estate agent in Cypress TX”) across six AI engines and shows me who gets named, at what position, and which page on my site they cite. When I started in August, my brokerage barely showed up. Today, five of my main hire-intent questions cite my site on five of the six engines, and I can see which pages are earning it.

The GEO audit has become a standard step every time I publish a page or blog post. It scores how quotable and citable the page is, and the checklist tells me exactly what to fix. Pages I’ve reworked using it now score in the 90s.

The support is what pushed me to upgrade to Tier 5. When my audits got stuck, Samuel was on chat within minutes, escalated it to the tech team, and had it fixed the same morning. He also took the time to explain how the prompt quota works so I could plan my tracking properly.

If you care about showing up in AI answers, not just Google, this is worth every taco.

reviews.title: Erfahrungsbericht Nuwtonic: Modernes SEO- und GEO-Tool mit starkem Prompttracking für Profis
reviews.comment:
Ich nutze Nuwtonic seit einigen Wochen und schätze es als ein leistungsstarkes SEO- und GEO-Tool. Es verfolgt einen klar fokussierten Ansatz, der sich von bekannten All-in-One-Lösungen abhebt. Man muss keine Prioritäten im System definieren, sollte aber selbst genau wissen, welche Seiten für den eigenen Erfolg entscheidend sind.

Wer diesen Fokus mitbringt, erhält exzellent aufbereitete Fakten. Das Tool belässt es nicht bei der reinen Datenanalyse, sondern liefert sofort anwendbare Handlungsempfehlungen inklusive konkreter Textvorschläge und Offpage-Maßnahmen. Im Arbeitsalltag fungiert die Software dadurch als digitaler Kollege, der die Optimierung produktiv vorantreibt.

Einen hohen Mehrwert bietet der eigene Abschnitt für das Prompttracking mit seinen zahlreichen Funktionen. Er arbeitet wie ein Radar für branchenspezifische Informationen. Das System zeigt präzise auf, welche Quellen herangezogen werden und in welchem inhaltlichen Kontext Markenerwähnungen stattfinden.

Für WordPress-Nutzer gibt es eine direkte Schnittstelle. Das vereinfacht Prozesse erheblich, auch wenn in meinem Fall ein anderes CMS im Einsatz ist. Für Anfänger ist die Software nicht geeignet. Ein solides Grundwissen in den Bereichen SEO und GEO ist zwingend nötig, um die Funktionen sinnvoll zu bedienen. Wer diese fachlichen Voraussetzungen erfüllt, erhält ein effizientes Werkzeug für die Praxis.

reviews.title: Still using it after six months, but the analytics need work
reviews.comment:
I've been using SearchIQ for about six months and it remains one of the better AppSumo purchases I've made.
I originally bought it because site search data is one of the clearest signals of visitor intent. I wanted to know what people were searching for, which searches produced no results, and what content visitors were struggling to find. While some of this can be implemented in Google Analytics, it typically requires custom setup and ongoing maintenance.
SearchIQ makes that much easier. Installation is straightforward, the search experience is noticeably better than default WordPress search, and the analytics surface exactly the signals I was looking for.
The biggest benefit for me has been understanding what visitors are actually looking for in their own words. That kind of insight helps identify content gaps and opportunities that would otherwise be easy to miss.
The analytics do have real limitations though. They need longer data retention, better historical reporting, and internal traffic filtering. I flagged the last one to the team six months ago and it has not been implemented yet, which also raises questions about the pace of active development.
Strong value at $39 lifetime. The search experience is already excellent. The analytics just need to catch up. I cover all of this in more detail, including a full feature comparison and six months of hands-on findings, in my complete review at https://marketingwithdave.com/searchiq-review/
