reviews.title: An excellent and extremely fast tool for achieving results. Brilliantly implemented in JavaScript!
reviews.comment:
It’s true that we have Canva and many other much more complete tools, although they tend to be significantly more complex and time-consuming to achieve the results we get here so effortlessly. 

For quick editing jobs and screenshots, nothing beats this tool. It also includes a whole range of spectacular AI tools, from logo design, creating Pinterest pins, rapid infographics generation, and much more. 

It is absolutely a no-brainer tool to add to the tech stack, especially at the low price it currently offers, with unlimited AI usage (for now, until the quota runs out — which is fair and honest). Plus, the BYOK system is fair and flexible.

However, I have some suggestions:

- If using OUR API KEY, I believe you should include other AI models, particularly Google’s image models, even if the more advanced ones like “Nano Banana Pro” are more expensive. Sometimes I need to include Latin characters in infographics, and “Nano Banana Pro” is currently the only model that manages to render long texts with Latin characters perfectly — or nearly perfectly. I think having more LLM options could be very helpful and that should be brought in , not by STRAICO (which is limited) but simply implementing "OpenRouter", which includes all of them. It contains all possible image models and is always updated with the most recent/best image/text/video models.

- One essential missing feature that needs fixing is an extension that allows me to instantly capture and crop just a section of the screen. I know I can do this in two steps with Picbolt itself: first capturing the screen with the inline HTML5 web capture, then using the crop tool. But this is very rudimentary and disrupts the fast workflow you want. I think you should release, as soon as possible, a browser extension for Chrome/Edge — even if only to quickly capture sections or the entire screen.

I will definitely recommend this tool to everyone. It’s very useful. Five stars, no doubt!

children.comment:
Thanks so much for the kind words and the detailed feedback - really appreciate it! 

Both suggestions are great. We'll be adding OpenRouter and Google image models integrations for BYOK users in the next release, and a Chrome browser extension for quick screen capture is already in the pipeline.

questions.title: free WP alternatives - why should I buy it?
questions.comment:
Hi, 
in WP repository there are at least 2 credible, well working plugins with 5-star reviews, that works as your. Why should I buy this offer?

children.comment:
That’s a fair question.

To be completely transparent: given the current level of AI-assisted development and the maturity of the WordPress ecosystem, for simple UI enhancements like a reading progress indicator, it is often more practical not to buy a commercial plugin at all.

In many cases, generating a small, purpose-built script tailored to a specific website’s design and requirements is a better solution than installing a universal, highly flexible plugin. This approach avoids unnecessary overhead and gives full control over behavior and appearance.

So yes — if your goal is just a basic reading progress bar, there may indeed be no strong reason to purchase Reading Indicator. The plugin is offered mainly for users who explicitly prefer a ready-made, supported solution rather than custom implementation.

I appreciate the honest comparison and the question.
Thank you for fair answer.

reviews.title: Strong Topaz alternative that is almost there
reviews.comment:
I picked this up a while ago and have been putting it through its paces, so here is my honest take.

The upscaling itself is excellent. When it runs properly, the output quality sits right up there with Topaz and the other premium upscalers I have tried. Clean, sharp, no weird artifacts.

 Getting results like that at this price feels like a steal, and I think paying hundreds for the big-name upscalers is money down the drain when something like this exists.

There are a few things holding it back from five stars though. The sizing options are limited to 200% and 400%. I get it, this is still an MVP and upscaling is heavy on GPU resources, so I understand why more options are not there yet. But a couple of extra steps in between would make a real difference.

Then there is stability. When I upscale a single image (I have not tried batch upscaling yet), it sometimes takes a very long time, and every now and then it just stalls at zero and does nothing at all, which forces me to restart. Tightening up the reliability and processing speed would take this tool to another level.

The amount of ads is also a bit much. I understand the developer needs to fund the project, so I will not make a big deal of it for now, but somewhere down the line it could become a sticking point. The interface has room to grow too, and I am sure that will come with time.

Overall this is a really good tool and I can see it becoming something special. I am giving it four stars purely because of the long processing times I've experienced. Fix those things and you have a five-star product on your hands. I am rooting for it and hope the developer takes this feedback on board.

reviews.title: Good value, but with some flaws
reviews.comment:
This is no doubt a good value if you can use it. Unfortunately, for anyone doing portraits or even candids or any photos of people, it will fail to impress. People end up looking like wax figures (eyes are especially dead and skin and features too smooth to be human). This is the same issue with some textures in landscapes, but this program will serve sufficiently for many landscapes. 
If the program ditched the Digital Noise Reduction and allowed for preserving "grain" it would vastly improve both skin and nature textures. However, it would still prove a problem for eyes. It feels like the issue is that it upscales too broadly rather than pixel-by-pixel such that it saves on cost but trades fidelity.

reviews.title: 5 Tacos for sure!
reviews.comment:
Firstly, I'm still a novice where AI upscalers are concerned. But I've done enough research to see the value in this one.

Secondly, I did reach out to the owner using the support email he provided in his responses to comments here but never heard back. I did that about a month before I purchased it. I wanted to make sure this upscales large enough for my needs. I do want to add that about 20% of the emails I send go to spam. So maybe he never saw it. But I like to be transparent in all things.

Lastly, in spite of not hearing back I went ahead with the purchase about 2 weeks ago anyway. Why? Because it's an amazing value to have lifetime access to a true AI upscaler and it works the way they say.

I've used it a bit since purchasing and it's worked exactly as it should. It can upscale to double your original or 4X your original. You choose the radial button. I need a very specific output size in my work so I start with an image a quarter that size and upscale 400%.

Some notes:
The maximum this will go to is 16,000px on either side.  Just an FYI. Many folks don't need to go that big. That's 53.33" x 53.33" in 300DPI if you're printing. PRETTY BIG.  I only need a 10,800 long side but I did test larger files and they are definitely capped at 16,000px

Your starting image cannot exceed 10MB. Mine do not. But when I was playing with the larger images it stopped me on one that was 10.2MB

The maximum batch size you can do at one time is currently 8.  I'm Okay with that. I sometimes have 10 and just split them. 

The output image shows 72DPI when I inspect it (in case that matters to anyone) but from the research I've done this is just semantics as long as the pixels are correct? Again, I'm still learning and providing all my notes in case it helps anyone looking to buy this. The pixels are definitely correct and the image works perfectly for my needs. I do run it through a python script in an automation process I have which changes the actual DPI to 300 since all the required pixels ARE there. Maybe this is how all upscalers work? 

I'd like to repeat that this is an AMAZING value. If you need to regularly upscale images and have them upscale correctly there are other options out there. But they all cost a heck of a lot more and are subscription based. This product provides exactly what I need for my daily work and will pay for itself in just 6 months. At that point The subscription based product would leave me with an ongoing monthly bill.  Consider me a very happy customer!

reviews.title: Excellent. This product genuinely surprised me.
reviews.comment:
I have tried many AI image generators, both cheap ones as well as expensive ones. However, I only purchased this out of curiosity because of the volume of reviews. I was genuinely cynical, thinking at this price point, it's going to be terrible. 

It created some excellent images for me. However, I realised through testing that if I gave it a general prompt, it would create your standard, what I call plasticky, perfect teeth, perfect hair type of images. But if I gave it a good prompt, it created the styling that I needed that complemented my brand. I'm not going to claim it's perfect, but it's very close to the other platform I used, which was what I'd say perfect. The other platform was also a lot more expensive. So, given the price point, it was excellent. And even if I say so myself, I really expect high standards.

However, what I found was genuinely very surprising. It created some outstanding images, and the most important thing I noticed was the platform was very reasonable about the number of credits it took off you. Apart from a few AI models, in general, it took 2 credits from me per image, which I felt was fair. As as they don't get greedy and change the amount of credits they take from customers - then I feel this is definitely a keeper. 

I'll keep an eye during the rest of the 60-day period if things change, but so far, it has been a genuine surprise. 

One last thing I would say is I hope they have a sustainable business model planned, because if we are all honest with each other, lifetime deals are great for market awareness and getting feedback for your product at the initial stage. However, if you have to keep doing lifetime deals to get revenue, eventually things will catch up and the business won't be sustainable. So that's my only minor concern. But I'm sure the people behind the platform are smart and they know what they're doing.

Thank you.

questions.title: Has it been actively developed over the last couple of years? (It does not look like to me)
questions.comment:
I remember looking at BackgroundCut a couple of years ago and, to be honest, it didn’t feel very active at the time. Some features, like the Chrome extension, seemed to be stuck in “coming soon” for a long while.

I’m checking it again now, but I’m not immediately seeing what has changed or improved since then. I’d like to understand whether the product is still being actively developed.

Could you share a clear update on what has changed in the last 12–24 months? Roadmap progress, or any public changelog/release notes.

children.comment:
Hey,

Thanks for using BackgroundCut, and that's a fair question, let me give you an honest and clear picture.

You're right that visible development felt slow for a while, and I won't pretend otherwise. The Chrome extension and plugins are a good example, I did release Figma and WooCommerce plugins, but they never gained real traction, so I stepped back from actively updating or releasing new ones rather than sinking time into something few people used.

That said, here's what's genuinely changed in the last 12-24 months:

1. A brand new photo editor, with object selection for accurate cutouts, and an image matting feature (great for fine detail like hair). Both run on backend GPU compute rather than lightweight browser models, which is what gives the accuracy.

2. Reworked upload flow, the separate bulk remover page has been removed and folded into the main upload page. You can now do multiple uploads, select/replace backgrounds, and use auto-crop all from one place.

3. A new API v3, alongside the existing versions.

4. A lot of backend work, architecture changes and stability improvements that aren't directly visible but matter for reliability.

So the honest summary is: the product is actively developed, but a lot of the work over this period went into architecture, stability, and the new editor rather than flashy front-end features, so it may not jump out immediately.

On the roadmap, I'm currently working on an image generation model. The architecture is set up, and I'm mainly evaluating viability right now, since GPU compute costs for generation are significant. I'm also considering a BYOK (bring your own key) option, where you could plug in your own API key for background image generation, which would help keep it affordable.

Happy to answer anything more specific about any of these!

Thanks,
Harsh Ranjan
Founder, BackgroundCut

What’s even more impressive is the attention to detail. Need to extract dominant colors from an image for your next project? Done. If you’re looking for a tool that combines practicality with creativity, Watermarkup is worth exploring. It’s not just a tool; it’s a companion for your creative journey. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to save time, protect their work, and add a touch of magic to their images.

reviews.title: Essential watermark management functions are missing.

children.comment:
Hello,

We will try to improve the app based on your feedback.

At this time, our app is used for image watermarking purposes only, it is not a batch image editor. The existing features appear to be somewhat limited. But we have plans to develop it into a batch image editor soon. And you will find more features and editing options for your images.

The "Top Panel" will appear when you click on the logo/image object/text watermark. There are several options for you to choose:
 + remove the object
 + copy the object
 + if you have multiple text or logo or image objects, you can choose to select what will be on top (like stacking). We have "Bring Forward" and "Bring Backward"

Right now, text objects can't be saved, but you can upload and reuse your logos or image objects (designs, icons, emojis) in the app effortlessly.

In response to your feedback on free desktop software options, there are technical differences between web-based and desktop image processing. It is really different to edit 200 - 500 photos at the same time for web-based apps and desktop apps. 
I would also like to mention a few points about technical sides:

- Our app is processing multiple images at the same time. Single mode editing is not the same with multiple mode editing. While you may be familiar with single mode image editors, implementing all the features in a multiple mode editing app is nearly impossible. And the app is currently serving image watermarking purposes only.

- The number of photos you upload to the app will have different sizes and dimensions. So, even if we create a feature like setting dimensions of the watermark, the watermark will not be the same in different images because our app will have to resize the watermark proportionally.

- I understand that you may find the app not useful for your use cases, but some users still find some value in Watermarkup. I hope that with more features and plans to come, you will find the app useful for you again.

Thank you for giving Watermarkup a try. We will try our best to improve it and bring more features like what you mentioned to the app. Have a nice day.

questions.title: Questions
questions.comment:
1. ETA on video watermarking? And estimated length or file size supported? 
2. How customizable are the naming format for the bulk download images/files? 
3. Any webhooks/Zapier integration? 
4. Can I upload an image by image url? 
5. Any chrome extensions e.g, some image processing tools allow right click—>sync image to platform and get the task done automatically 
6. If bulk upload contains different aspect ratios, and I’ve got a few watermark templates already for these ratios, can it correctly identify these ratios and watermark accordingly? 
Thanks

children.comment:
Hi,

1. We cannot confirm the exact release date for our video watermarking tool. But we will try to release it soon in the coming months. We plan to create a tool to watermark short videos first. They can be in formats like Instagram Reels, TikTok videos, and YouTube Shorts. So, you can understand that the length of videos is limited, and we focus on MP4 first for the file type.

2. For the bulk watermarked images, we still keep the names of the original files. But when you download all the watermarked photos as a zip file, you can have a separate file or folder for all the watermarked photos. So, you can differentiate between your original and watermarked images.

For image editing apps, we currently set a different name for the edited image. If the original file is JohnDoe.jpg, the downloaded file might be tinted-image.jpg or embossed-image.jpg after users apply the Tint or Emboss effect.

3. Currently, we haven't thought about automation and webhooks/Zapier integrations. All the apps are mainly used by users directly on our website. But it is a good idea to have these features in the future.

4. Currently, you can drag and drop your images from your device or click the Upload button to upload your image. But it is a nice idea to upload images from a URL. We will try to implement that feature soon.

5. Currently, we haven't had any Chrome extensions to do that. But we will think about it and try to implement it if it is possible for our app and use cases.

6. Our app can handle different ratios of photos correctly and scale the watermark proportionally. For example, when you upload 50 photos at the same time, the sizes and ratios of your photos can be different. When you add a text watermark to all the photos, the text watermark is adjusted to suit each photo correctly. You can also have the option to adjust the watermark specifically for each photo. 

The same thing is applied to image objects, logos, icons, emojis, and etc.

You can add multiple watermarks or logos to your photos. In general, in the bulk upload, the app automatically adjusts watermarks accordingly. But sometimes, you will need to adjust for some specific cases to better suit your needs.

This month, we prioritize adding more tools for image editing. And we plan to add a background remover soon for all our Pro users.

We will think about your suggestions and try to implement the features we can develop.

Thank you for your questions and ideas. 

Have a nice day!

reviews.title: Redefining Lifetime Deal & Deceptive Remapping
reviews.comment:
FlexClip’s recent remapping of lifetime tiers has resulted in the removal and reduction of benefits that were part of my original purchase. The comany replaced my tier with a different plan classification, calling it "remapping" which now excludes lifetime customers from receiving the enhancements that should have been applied to the original tier.

AppSumo lifetime deals legally require that customers retain:
• The exact features and limits originally sold
• Plus any enhancements made to that same tier over time
• Without downgrading, reclassification, or replacement

FlexClip’s remapping violates these requirements. After multiple attempts to resolve this through FlexClip, AppSumo, and Candy, I received only repeated remapping explanations and no restoration of my original entitlements. Lifetime deals should be honored as sold, regardless of whether enhancements are made. Remapping is not grandfathering, and customers should not lose value after the original purchase.

Vendors should not be able to reclassify, rename, or replace lifetime tiers to avoid honoring upgrades. Yet FlexClip is doing exactly that, and support continues to repeat the same remapping explanation instead of restoring the original tier. This behavior violates the terms of the lifetime deal and leaves customers with less than what they paid for, but nobody seems to care and passes the buck to avoid accountability!

children.comment:
Thank you for your feedback, and I’m sorry for the confusion. If our earlier response came across as curt, I sincerely apologize.

I’d like to clarify a few important points:

First, this is not a “redefining” of the Lifetime Deal. The pre-2025 deal (V1) and the current post-2025 AppSumo deal(V3) are two separate deals, with different pricing, structure, and credits.

Second, for customers who purchased before 2025, their original tier benefits remain exactly as originally sold. No feature has been removed or reduced.

When we refer to enhancements to the same tier, we mean enhancements to the same official plan level on our website — not a comparison between different tiers across two different deals.

Your purchase is a Legacy Deal V1, bought before 2025. Those legacy tiers retain their original plan benefits and have not been reduced.

The current AppSumo deal is a completely new deal. Key mapping is as follows:
Old Tier 1 = Basic Plan
Old Tier 2 = Plus Plan
Old Tier 3 = Business Plan

New Tier 1 = Plus Plan
New Tier 2 & 3 = Business Plan

They are not the same official plan level, so they do not map directly to each other. The AI credit model is different too: legacy credits renew annually, while the new deal uses lifetime credits. So this is not a simple update to the same license — it is two separate deals.

That said, we do offer upgrade options for V1 users. You have two paths:

Stack new codes to move to the current (V3) deal structure:
V1 T1 + 1 code → V3 T2
V1 T1 + 2 codes → V3 T3
V1 T2 + 1 code → V3 T3

If you’d rather upgrade within the original V1 structure, please email [email redacted] for further help.

Thanks for your patience, and for giving us the chance to clear this up.

questions.title: API/MCP Security, Grok & Codex Integration
questions.comment:
Hi,
I'm using AdaptlyPost with Grok agents and Codex from research to strategy - to create and schedule branded content across multiple social platforms.

Could you clarify:
1. Can Grok, ChatGPT and Codex connect via MCP/API with workspace-specific access?
2. Is Contributor the safest role for AI agents?
3. Can agents upload media, create drafts and set future dates without publishing rights?
4. Can an Editor approve drafts for scheduled publishing?
5. Are API tokens isolated between brand workspaces?
6. Can agents prepare platform-specific posts, images, videos and carousels?
7. Are MCP/API calls and non-X posts unlimited without consuming credits?
8. Can tokens be revoked, rotated and given expiration dates?
9. Are content, credentials and brand assets private/ encrypted?
10. Any limitation when it comes to design?

Thanks!
Marcus

children.comment:
Hi Marcus, 
I appreciate your patience, and thank you for your questions! ImageDino is the image-generation piece of a setup like yours. It turns your branded templates into complete images, but it does not publish or schedule posts, so the questions about drafts, approvals and publishing rights are ones for AdaptlyPost.

Let me explain how ImageDino works! You design a branded template once in our visual editor and publish it. From then on, your connected agents generate finished images from that template by swapping in new captions, fonts, images, icons. Agents don’t have access to template creation or design change, so initial branding stays under your control.

Agents connect in two ways:
1. Our MCP server is documented for ChatGPT and Claude at https://docs.imagedino.com/docs/mcp, it also works with Codex, but we cannot promise Grok will work over MCP.
2. Any agent can use the REST API to connect - https://docs.imagedino.com/docs. Each API key belongs to one workspace and keys and connections can be revoked at any time, see http://docs.imagedino.com/docs/mcp#permissions for reference.

Output is PNG, JPG or WebP, and images are passed in by public URL instead of uploaded.

Every generated image uses credits: 1 for a standard-size image, or 2 if the agent needs it returned instantly (sync mode). Looking up templates, fonts and icons is free.

On privacy, data is encrypted in transit and API key secrets are never exposed. A finished image’s link can be opened by anyone who has it, which is what lets social platforms fetch it.

Let me know if you have any other questions!

questions.comment: how is this different from canva bulk apart from LTD?

children.comment:
Hi @VK, thank you for your question! 
Both ImageDino and Canva turn the design+data combo into many images; however, there is an important difference:

Canva Bulk is manual work: you upload a spreadsheet on a desktop, map the fields for hundreds of rows at a time, and you have to redo it every time the data changes.

ImageDino runs on its own. You connect Google Sheets to Make, or integrate our API once, and every new product, listing, or post gets its image automatically! Then the links are embedded directly into the design, and with Dynamic URLs, you can personalize an image on demand.

For example, for email banners, you cannot drop a Canva template into a campaign and have each recipient see their own image. With ImageDino, it's seamless! Paste one Dynamic URL into your email, add your tag for the name or offer, and every recipient gets a personal image, created when needed.

questions.title: Hi, what is Simple URLs and Signed URLs?

children.comment:
Hi Apesumo! 😄👋

Simple URLs and Signed URLs are both types of Dynamic URLs. You can use it for email visuals, opengraph images, personalized content – with no code!

– Simple URLs let you generate an image using a regular URL with parameters. You can pass your data directly in the URL, and ImageDino will generate the image automatically!

– Signed URLs work similarly, but the URL includes a secure signature. This helps prevent unauthorized users from modifying the parameters or generating images with your account.

You can learn more about Dynamic URLs, including Simple and Signed URLs, here: https://docs.imagedino.com/docs/dynamic-urls

I purchased and downloaded ScreenToVideo and tested it out multiple times on a back-up Windows 11 laptop. Despite an unnecessarily clunky interface and very limited saving options (no way to save any recording as MP3 unless you go outside of Quick Record and experiment alot), I was able to save short videos of my desktop screen doing back work or recording very brief videos on YouTube just testing it out. However, when I tried to record a much longer Zoom webinar taking place live it simply puttered out with the video that was finally recorded being unwatchable gibberish - the woman talking for an hour and a half couldn't say a single word since the screen locked while she was talking and wouldn't play so no sound and just a frozen video image of her in mid-sentence. 

When I tried to fast forward or rewind the video, it stayed locked. After trying multiple times, I gave up and accepted the video recording of the Zoom webinar was unwatchable. I tried again a day later after a replay had been sent and again, the same thing: screen freezing up, no sound, unwatchable. 

For now at least, this only seems capable of recording very short, very simple videos and that doesn't serve any real purpose for me personally or professionally. I've read other reviews with others having similar issues, especially with the other recording methods so I don't think this is something I can use or would want to try using again.

children.comment:
Hi,
Thank you for taking the time to try ScreenToVideo and for sharing your detailed feedback — we really appreciate it, even when the experience wasn’t what you expected.
From what you described, it sounds like the recording mode used might not have been the best fit for your use case. ScreenToVideo includes two different capture modes, each designed for a specific scenario. The Application Capture Mode is intended for short recordings where maximum visual quality is important. This mode captures at a higher quality but also uses more system resources and generates larger files. The Video Capture Mode is designed specifically for longer recordings such as webinars or Zoom sessions and is optimized for stability over longer durations.
In both modes, you can adjust the recording quality and frame rate, depending on your system capabilities and needs.
After recording, the content should be rendered in the editor. Playback issues such as freezing or missing audio can occur if the recording has not been properly rendered yet, and the rendering speed depends on the performance of the computer.
Regarding audio export, there are multiple options. You can export only the audio object or the entire project audio directly as MP3 from the editor. There is also the option to record audio only, which is saved as .m4a.
We understand that your experience was frustrating, especially when trying to capture a long webinar, and we’re sorry the app didn’t meet your expectations in this case. If you are open to it, we would be happy to help you configure the optimal settings for your specific use case.
Thank you again for trying ScreenToVideo.

reviews.title: Nice, Simple Template-Based Video Tool
reviews.comment:
At $25 for lifetime access to 10 HD downloads a month, this is a handy arrow to have in your quiver.
So, anyone expecting to make Oscar-worthy videos is looking in the wrong place - this is a collection of relatively basic editable templates into which you can upload your logo, different images, even a short audio track, depending on the template you choose. You can choose from a relatively small collection of fonts, although some templates don't allow this, and then change the colour of the text to match your brand. The system then uses the media and font/colour tweaks to modify the template to your specifications. Most of the templates are 5-20 seconds long.
There are plenty of templates to choose from - some just animate your logo, others make a slideshow of images, for when you add a new product to your e-commerce store, for example. Many of the templates are available in horizontal AND vertical mode, so you can be consistent over several platforms. The videos are simple but eye-catching, and they look quite professionally-made.
Considering the price, there's not much you can really complain about. The only annoyance I've found so far is that some of the vertical + horizontal templates have different levels of customization. For example, I liked a template called something like "Hand-drawn Logo Reveal" - thought it would be nice to add at the end of a longer YouTube/Instagram/TikTok video, so I customized the vertical version and spent 2 of my 20 monthly credits downloading it in HD only to find that the font can't be customized in the horizontal version of the same template, meaning that there will be inconsistency in the font if I choose to use it in the future. Annoying for a perfectionist, but not a fatal flaw.
So, overall, a nice little product. If you want to make a quick, low-effort Facebook Reel or an Instagram Story, you'll probably find a template you can use and get a ready-to-upload, respectable-looking short video in a few minutes that will look like you put a few hours' effort into it. And for $25 for 10 such videos a month, I recommend that absolutely anyone needing to do even just basic marketing consider signing up for this deal.

reviews.title: Animated videos without starting from scratch
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Wideo has been around for a while, and you can feel that in the parts of the product that work well. If you want to make a simple animated explainer, promo video, onboarding video, or social video from a template, Wideo is great for the job.

It works very well as a template based animation tool. You pick a video structure, replace the text and visuals, add voiceover, and turn it into an explainer, promo, onboarding clip, or social post without animating every scene from scratch.

Some of the newer AI pages needed clearer wording. During my retest, the blog to video tool only captured part of the article I tested. The team explained that the tool summarizes a post and creates a short promotional video meant to send people back to the original article. So I would describe it as a blog promo tool rather than a full article to video converter.

The AI Avatars page could have been clearer during my test. The team clarified that AI Avatars are a custom solution, not a regular dashboard feature users can create on their own. Since it still appears on the landing page, buyers may not immediately understand that difference.

The Text to Speech page also slightly confused me. It was branded as Wideo, but the main Try Now button sent me to Speechify through an affiliate link. The team clarified that Wideo does offer text to speech inside the editor, so buyers should look at the editor itself for the actual Wideo feature.

The team also said a new version of the app is close and that the current legacy dashboard dependencies will be replaced as part of that migration. They also confirmed the missing license notices in the bundled JavaScript file have been addressed.

Overall, I would look at Wideo for what it already does well: template based animated videos, simple explainers, promo videos, and branded social content. The main thing is to understand the difference between the regular editor, the AI features inside the app, and custom services like AI Avatars. For explainers, promos, onboarding clips, and social posts, the editor and template library are strong reasons to consider it.

children.comment:
Thanks for the detailed and thoughtful review! We really appreciate you taking the time to test Wideo thoroughly and also retest some features after our clarifications.

Your feedback around making the distinction between the core editor, newer AI tools, and custom solutions clearer is very valuable, and it’s something we’re actively working on as we continue updating the platform. Thanks again for giving buyers such a comprehensive perspective!

reviews.title: Promising Product - 2 Key Features Needed for 5 Tacos
reviews.comment:
The software is working well. The creation of videos is fairly easy and it has more/different features than other tools e.g. MapDirector (Freeware). From the tools I tried to create animated travel maps, AvoMap was the best so far. To make it really awesome (and for me to give 5 tacos) two important features are still missing:
1) Reordering of route segments.
2) Upload of GPX data to each route segment so that you truly can create completely custom travel videos or videos of sports activities like triathlon. Or hiking up a mountain and paragliding down. This feature would open up so many more possibilities and really make AvoMap stand out. It was wished for by users in the feature forum multiple times in different requests but so far rejected or ignored. :( I hope this changes!

Another thing that would be nice to have, is the upload of videos or images like in MapDirector, but I do not really need that feature for now.

reviews.title: Very Hard to Understand
reviews.comment:
I have been using this platform for several weeks and have found it to be lacking in several key areas. The folder structure is confusing and difficult to navigate, making it hard to locate or organize images. Additionally, the platform does not allow sharing an entire folder; when I copy a link, it only includes the last part of the URL, not the full path. This limitation severely hampers collaboration.

There is no Windows application available for download on the official website, despite an announcement on the AppSumo page in September 2025 that an application will be released soon. Until that release, users are forced to rely on the web interface, which is not ideal for many workflows.

Given the numerous alternatives available that offer better folder management, intuitive navigation, and robust sharing capabilities, I do not consider this platform a suitable option for shared image needs. I will be returning the product.

children.comment:
Thank you for taking the time to share your detailed feedback. We’re sorry to hear that the current experience did not meet your expectations.

We understand your concerns regarding folder navigation, sharing workflow, and the absence of the Windows desktop application. The platform is still evolving, and feedback like yours helps us identify the areas that need the most improvement.

Regarding folder sharing, we agree that collaboration features can be improved, and enhancements are already being worked on. The Windows app is also under active development, and we acknowledge the frustration caused by the delay after the earlier announcement.

We are actively working on all these improvements and aim to resolve these issues by 30th June 2026.

We genuinely appreciate you trying the product and sharing honest feedback.

reviews.title: BuzzHooks Review: Ok Results, but Expensive Credits and Questions About Future Model Access
reviews.comment:
Update: 10/16/26

upgraded from 3 stars to 4 stars as they have added image gen models that can do 4K.

Old Review:

BuzzHooks offers AI image and video generation, but its pricing is higher than some competing platforms I use. The video results are okay, but I feel the platform is only halfway there in terms of functionality.

1. Image Generation Limitations

Video generation lets you select individual models, resolutions, and durations. Image generation allows styles like Cinematic, but I couldn't find options to select individual image models or resolutions.

I'd like to see image models with 4K resolution options. These are important for character sheets, preserving details, and maintaining character consistency in AI videos. You absolutely don’t need 4K video, although it would be nice to have. However, 4K images are essential because they capture the pore-level skin detail and realism needed for high-quality character sheets, which can then be used to generate videos in 720p or 1080p. When using 1080p source images, too much fine skin texture and detail can be lost during video generation, especially in scenes where the character is farther from the camera. This is why 4K image resolution is so important, even when the final video is generated at a lower resolution.


2. Included Models vs. BYOK

Models like seedance 2.5 will not use your ltd credits. Other ltd deals outside this platform do not have this issue. I have ltds that give me access to use my ai credits with any model.

Models accepting included LTD credits:
WAN 3.0 Standard, WAN 3.0 Prime, Seedance 2.0, and Minimax H3. All support up to 1080p.

Models requiring BYOK:
Seedance 2.5, Seedance 2.0 Fast, and Seedance 2.0 Mini.

BYOK means Bring Your Own Key. You connect and pay an external API provider separately.

What the founder confirmed:

The founder explained that regular AI credits and BYOK credits are separate allowances. BYOK still uses BuzzHooks credits because of processing and workflow costs.

Tier 4 offers unlimited BYOK credits, but external API generation costs still apply.

He also stated that future supported models would remain accessible through BYOK. However, I haven't found confirmation that newer models will continue accepting regular included LTD credits.

**3. Future Models, API, and MCP**

My concern is that newer models could eventually require BYOK while regular LTD credits remain limited to older models.

The deal terms also indicate that future AI models may require additional purchases or discounted add-ons.

My questions are:

- Will newer image, video, and LLM models accept regular Tier 4 credits?
- Will future model upgrades require BYOK or add-ons?
- Will included credits work through API/MCP?
- What happened to MCP, which was estimated for release two weeks back in September?
- Is a public API still planned?

4. Video Generation Credit Pricing

I had trouble finding detailed pricing before purchasing. I manually went through the model dropdowns, durations, and resolutions to document the costs. I'm sharing them because I couldn't find another review with this information, and I don't want others to have to do the same work.

These models use regular included LTD credits, NOT BYOK.

WAN 3.0 STANDARD

10s 480p: 160 credits | 12s 480p: 190 credits | 15s 480p: 240 credits | 30s 480p: 470 credits

10s 720p: 290 credits | 12s 720p: 350 credits | 15s 720p: 440 credits | 30s 720p: 870 credits

10s 1080p: 520 credits | 12s 1080p: 630 credits | 15s 1080p: 780 credits | 30s 1080p: 1,560 credits

WAN 3.0 PRIME

10s 480p: 220 credits | 12s 480p: 260 credits | 15s 480p: 320 credits | 30s 480p: 640 credits

10s 720p: 410 credits | 12s 720p: 490 credits | 15s 720p: 610 credits | 30s 720p: 1,220 credits

10s 1080p: 730 credits | 12s 1080p: 870 credits | 15s 1080p: 1,090 credits | 30s 1080p: 2,180 credits

MINIMAX H3 (10s | 12s | 15s)

10s 480p: 120 credits | 12s 480p: 150 credits | 15s 480p: 180 credits

10s 720p: 180 credits | 12s 720p: 210 credits | 15s 720p: 270 credits

10s 1080p: 320 credits | 12s 1080p: 380 credits | 15s 1080p: 470 credits

SEEDANCE 2.0 (10s | 12s | 15s)

10s 480p: 200 credits | 12s 480p: 240 credits | 15s 480p: 300 credits

10s 720p: 400 credits | 12s 720p: 480 credits | 15s 720p: 600 credits

10s 1080p: 800 credits | 12s 1080p: 960 credits | 15s 1080p: 1,200 credits

Prices are from my account and may change.

5. Tier 4 and Final Thoughts

Because of the high credit costs, I'd consider Tier 4 for regular video generation, but even 10,000 monthly credits disappear quickly. One 30-second WAN Prime 1080p video costs 2,180 credits, allowing only four complete generations at those settings.

My 3-star rating mainly reflects the missing image model and resolution controls. Video generation offers more flexibility, but image generation needs improvement. I'd also like clarity about future models, included credits, API, and MCP. Hopefully, this detailed pricing helps other buyers make an informed decision.

children.comment:
Thanks for the detailed review and for putting together the credit pricing. This is useful feedback, especially about making model options, resolutions and credit costs easier to understand before purchasing.

For image generation, you are right that it currently has fewer model and resolution controls than video generation. We will add more image models, including the types of models you suggested, and improve the available resolution options.

On included credits versus BYOK: we have added newer models such as H3 Max, Wan 3.0 and Wan 3.0 Prime to the regular credit system. We are also considering making Seedance 2.5 available without BYOK. This is mainly an economic decision, as we need to make sure it can be offered sustainably with the included credits.

We cannot promise that every future model will be available with regular LTD credits, since this depends on the cost of the model and whether we can support it sustainably. BYOK gives users access to more providers and models when needed.

For Tier 4, regular included credits can be used with the models available in the platform. Unlimited BYOK credits means no BuzzHooks BYOK credit limit, but the external provider generation cost still applies.

MCP and a public API are not available yet. The original MCP estimate was too optimistic, and we should have communicated that better. We will update the public roadmap when we have a realistic release plan instead of giving another date that may change.

Thanks again for the honest review.

reviews.title: Great Potential, but Expensive Credits and Restrictive BYOK Hold It Back
reviews.comment:
BuzzHooks has potential, and I appreciate what the team is trying to build. However, after exploring its features and testing the real costs of video production, I'm lowering my rating from 3 to 2 tacos.

My biggest concern is the credit system.

For example, generating a single 15-second real estate commercial using Seedance 2.0 at 1080p costs 1,200 credits. That's almost an entire Tier 2 monthly allowance for one short video.

Professional video production rarely succeeds on the first attempt. It requires experimentation, revisions, testing and client approvals. At these rates, credits disappear before you have a commercially usable result.

The BYOK model makes this even harder to justify.

When I bring my own API key, I'm already paying the AI provider directly for generation. Yet BuzzHooks imposes an additional monthly platform credit cap, with unlimited BYOK reserved for Tier 4.

I understand that running a platform involves infrastructure costs. But charging against a second usage allowance while customers fund their own AI generation significantly undermines the value proposition of BYOK.

My second concern is the creative direction.

BuzzHooks offers an enormous library of viral hooks, gimmicky scenarios and repetitive templates. There's clearly a market for that content, but I question how much of it translates into credible, professional marketing.

For agencies, SaaS companies, real estate, e-commerce and established brands, realism, creative control and consistency matter far more than the number of available templates.

I'd rather have 50 thoughtfully designed, commercially useful workflows than thousands of variations on generic viral concepts.

What needs improvement:

Universal Brand DNA across all creative tools and workflows.

More sustainable credit allowances and affordable experimentation.

Unlimited BYOK across paid tiers, with transparent infrastructure fair-use limits.

Greater emphasis on photorealistic, brand-aligned commercial content.

Fewer generic templates and more professional, industry-specific workflows.

Better scene-level editing, reference control and consistency between generations.

The ability to revise individual scenes without regenerating entire videos.

BuzzHooks has a promising foundation, but right now, I see a significant gap between its marketing promise and its practical value for professional production.

The problem isn't the number of features. It's whether those features produce work clients would actually pay for, at a sustainable cost.

My 2-taco rating reflects that gap. Until the team addresses the credit economics, restrictive BYOK model and professional creative control, I find it difficult to recommend BuzzHooks for serious commercial use.

children.comment:
Thank you for the detailed and honest review.

You are right that high-resolution, longer videos can use credits quickly, and this makes experimentation harder—especially when you need several versions before reaching a usable result. We offer lower-cost model options and multiple BYOK providers, but we understand that this does not fully solve the credit concern.

Regarding BYOK, the provider charges for the AI generation, while BuzzHooks credits cover usage of the BuzzHooks platform and workflows. BYOK includes a larger monthly allowance, but we cannot offer unlimited BYOK on every tier at the moment and still keep the lifetime deal sustainable. We will continue reviewing the credit system based on feedback like yours.

Your point about creative direction is also valid. BuzzHooks currently has many hooks and viral concepts, but professional users need more brand-aligned, industry-specific workflows, stronger reference control, consistency, and better editing options. Brand DNA, scene-level editing, and revising individual scenes are important suggestions.

We appreciate that you see the potential while being clear about what is missing. This feedback is useful as we decide what BuzzHooks should prioritize next.

reviews.title: A complete localization workflow for multi-speaker videos
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What I like about Voicina is that I can take one video through the whole localization process without moving it between several different tools.

I uploaded a video and got a full transcript with speaker labels and timestamps. From there I generated subtitles, translated them into Spanish and Arabic, and Arabic was displayed correctly from right to left. I then created a French dub with a different voice for each speaker.

That multi-speaker workflow is especially useful for interviews, podcasts and other videos where more than one person is talking. Localization is not just about translating the words. You also need to keep the speakers separate and make the dubbed version easy to follow. Voicina handled that within the same project.

The editing tools worked well too. I could correct terms with find and replace, generate a summary, and export the results as SRT, TXT and JSON. I also exported a video with the subtitles burned in, and that worked as expected.

When I first tested Voicina, there was no developer access. The team has since added an API and webhooks, which makes it more useful if you want to automate transcription or localization workflows instead of uploading everything manually.

One thing to watch is credit usage. Transcription and subtitles use relatively few credits, but dubbing and voice generation consume considerably more, especially if you're translating long videos into several languages. I would choose a tier based on how many minutes you actually expect to dub each month rather than just the amount of video you plan to transcribe.

Also, the dubbing does not alter the speaker's mouth movements to match the translated language. It keeps the original video and adjusts the dubbed speech to fit the timing instead.

Overall, Voicina solves a bigger problem for me than simply generating subtitles. I can take one video, transcribe it, translate it, create subtitles and produce a multi-speaker dub without rebuilding the project in several different applications. For anyone regularly publishing the same content in multiple languages, that is the main reason I would get it.

children.comment:
Hi Abe,

Thank you for such a thorough and honest review. It means a lot to have Voicina’s first review on AppSumo come from someone who tested the full workflow so carefully.

You described exactly what we set out to build: one place to take a video from transcript to subtitles to a multi-speaker dub, without jumping between tools. It’s great to hear that speaker separation and right-to-left Arabic worked well for you, and that the API and webhooks are already proving useful.

Your point about credits is a fair one, and good advice for other buyers. Dubbing uses more credits than transcription because it involves translation and voice generation for every minute and every language. Choosing a tier based on your monthly dubbing minutes is the right approach, and if you ever need more, top-up credits are available and never expire.

On lip sync, you’re right. We’re looking into adding it if there’s enough demand. To be honest, though, lip sync is very expensive to run, so it would use a lot of credits for users. Even so, if our users ask for it, we’ll move quickly to add it.

Thanks again for taking the time to test Voicina so thoroughly.

Mojtaba
Co-founder, Voicina

children.comment:
Thanks for the feedback.

Lip sync credits: the first screen (upload) only shows the lip sync rate (150 credits per minute), and no credits are charged there. Credits are charged once, on the video page after you choose the voice. We agree this is confusing, and we’re looking into simplifying it.
Dubbing voice: right now, voice cloning needs a separate, clean voice sample, because the audio inside a video often contains noise, music or several speakers, which can lower the quality of the clone. Please consider adding automated stem separation (e.g., Demucs) during ingestion to isolate dialogue from background music and noise, ensuring clean voice clones directly from mixed-audio video without third-party editing. This would make Voicina significantly more versatile without requiring users to jump out into external audio editors just to prepare voice clone samples for video dubbing.

questions.title: Are the mouth movements adjusted to fit the new dubbed audio, or do they stay synchronized with the source video?

Voicina doesn’t change the video itself, so mouth movements stay exactly as they are in the original. There’s no lip sync.

What Voicina does is match the dubbed audio to the original speech timing: each line starts and ends where the speaker does, and the pacing is managed so the voice keeps a natural speed instead of being rushed to fit.

questions.title: Is it possible to burn the subtitles into an audio and have it generate a video?
questions.comment: So, is it possible to burn the subtitles into the videos and into the audios, or just into the videos? For example, for an audio that I upload, is it possible to burn the subtitles into the audio and it generates kind of video with the subtitles burned into?

children.comment:
Hi there! Thanks for your question!

Yes, this is possible with Voicina! You can upload an audio file in the Subtitles section, just as you would upload a video.

Since there's no video attached to the audio, Voicina will show a black frame by default. You can also add your own image to use as the visual background.

When you export the project using Burned-in subtitles (MP4), Voicina combines the audio with the black background or your chosen image and burns the subtitles directly into the resulting video.

This way, you can create a video with subtitles from an audio file alone, without needing an existing video.

I hope this helps clarify things!

reviews.title: Lacks Depth and Substance — Disappointing for Serious Learners
reviews.comment:
I purchased a lifetime subscription to Headway expecting high-density insights similar to what you’d extract from books like The 10X Rule or The Richest Man in Babylon—where even simple ideas carry depth, context, and practical weight. Unfortunately, the experience has fallen far short of that expectation.

Unlike the timeless principles in books like The Richest Man in Babylon, which reveal deeper value the more you reflect on them, these summaries feel surface-level and quickly forgettable.
The core issue is lack of depth. I understand summaries are meant to be concise, but they shouldn’t strip away the substance. Strong summaries should distill the most valuable insights—not reduce them to generic, high-level talking points. Instead, much of the content feels like predictable, diluted advice rather than the “intellectual meat” of the original books.
In fact, many summaries come across as if they were generated based on patterns rather than genuine understanding. They often feel mechanical, repetitive, and overly templated—more like approximations of ideas than thoughtfully curated insights.  
Another major disappointment is low information density. If a full book is condensed into ~7 short chapters, I expect each minute to deliver high-value insight. Instead, key ideas are often glossed over, while less relevant content is unnecessarily stretched—sometimes seeming like filler just to meet a time target.
 
Bottom Line
For a product centered around learning and key ideas, I expected depth, clarity, and high-value insights per minute—especially as a lifetime customer. Instead, the content feels superficial, repetitive, and overly dependent on automation.
There is potential here, but in its current state, this platform is better suited for very casual exposure rather than serious learners looking for meaningful growth. If you’re used to extracting real value from books like The 10X Rule or The Richest Man in Babylon, this will likely feel like a downgrade.

reviews.title: Finally! The Faceless Software Review Creator I've Been Searching For!
reviews.comment:
I've been searching for software like VideoMule for years, and I believe I may have finally found what I've been looking for!

As a content creator building Creators Academy IO, I've always wanted to produce professional software reviews, product demonstrations, and educational tutorials without having to appear on camera or record my own narration.

I've purchased other software, including Dale and Layerpath, hoping to accomplish this, but neither ultimately met my requirements.

**What makes VideoMule different?**

It's not simply another screen recorder. VideoMule is designed to handle much of the work that happens AFTER recording.

You can demonstrate software on your screen, have AI analyze the recording, generate a script explaining what's happening, synchronize AI narration, and edit everything into a professional video.

That's exactly the workflow I've been searching for!

After purchasing Tier 3, I spent time exploring the platform and studying its tutorials to better understand its capabilities.

**Here's what impresses me most:**

**1. AI-generated scripts:** Rather than trying to explain everything while demonstrating software, I can concentrate on showing the features and let AI help create the explanation afterward.

**2. Synchronized AI voiceovers:** VideoMule can align narration with what's happening on screen. The lifetime plan also advertises unlimited standard AI voiceovers.

**3. Custom script templates:** This is one of my favorite discoveries! I can create reusable templates for software reviews, product demonstrations, and educational lessons, with custom introductions, instructions, and conclusions.

**4. Script editing:** I can refine the AI-generated explanations and incorporate my own opinions, observations, pros, cons, and recommendations. That's essential because I want to create genuine reviews, not just generic tutorials.

**5. Video editing:** The timeline editor includes zoom effects, callouts, captions, graphics, branding, and other tools that help viewers follow along.

**6. Unlimited local rendering:** I appreciate being able to render videos locally without consuming monthly cloud-render credits.

**7. AI avatars and multilingual capabilities:** These offer additional opportunities to create educational content for different audiences without constantly appearing on camera.

**What I'd like to see improved:**

First, I'd love additional integrations with JoggAI and Unmixr AI.

Some longtime AppSumo customers purchased HeyGen when it was available as a lifetime deal. Many of us missed that opportunity and later purchased JoggAI as an alternative.

Likewise, many AppSumo customers already own Unmixr AI instead of subscribing to ElevenLabs.

Allowing customers to connect these alternatives, where API access permits, would make VideoMule even more valuable.

Second, I'd appreciate greater clarity around the one-time video-analysis minutes.

My Tier 3 license includes 60 monthly upload minutes but only 120 lifetime analysis minutes. Understanding exactly what happens when those analysis minutes are exhausted is important for creators planning to produce videos long-term.

I'd also love to see an official software-review template that helps structure feature demonstrations, pros and cons, and final assessments.

**My overall impression:**

VideoMule has one of the most promising approaches I've encountered for creating faceless software reviews.

What excites me most is the potential to transform a simple screen recording into a narrated, edited educational video without the traditional production process.

I've activated my Tier 3 license, explored the interface, and researched the available tutorials. I haven't completed my first full video yet, so this is an initial assessment rather than a final judgment of production quality.

However, I'm genuinely excited about what I've discovered.

If the finished videos deliver on the capabilities demonstrated in the tutorials, VideoMule could become one of the most important tools in my Creators Academy IO production workflow.

I'm looking forward to putting it through real-world testing and seeing how the platform continues to develop!

children.comment:
Thank you for such a thoughtful review and for choosing Tier 3! It’s great to hear how VideoMule could fit into your workflow.

A few points on your suggestions:

1. JoggAI and Unmixr AI: Thanks for suggesting these integrations. We don’t have an integration timeline yet.

2. Analysis minutes: Your Tier 3 includes 120 one-time analysis minutes and 60 monthly upload minutes. After the analysis minutes run out, you can still generate AI scripts and standard voiceovers by narrating your screen recordings. VideoMule uses your spoken transcript to create the script, so this workflow requires no video analysis or add-ons. The monthly upload allowance doesn’t replace analysis minutes for silent recordings.

questions.title: Why are you limiting BYOK minutes?
questions.comment:
Hi.
Why are you limiting BYOK minutes?
That makes little sense.

children.comment: we understand why a limit seems surprising when you are paying the AI provider yourself. BYOK covers the models running on your keys, but several parts of Tough Tongue still run on our infrastructure, including turn detection, noise cancellation, browser automation, and Google Meet automation. Those features still consume tokens and compute on our side when used, so we need a platform usage allowance to cover those ongoing costs. Fully BYOK sessions use the shared allowance at one tenth of the base rate, stretching it to up to 2,500, 5,000, or 10,000 BYOK minutes per month on Tiers 2, 3, and 4 respectively. I strongly believe that when you keep your ideal buyers in mind as you build your store and listings, Etsy will reward you with traffic and sales.

This goes back to your point about Etsy’s mobile-first, behavior-based algorithm. Let’s unpack that a bit. (1) Mobile-first means your store and listings need to be optimized for mobile such as using listing titles that display well on smaller screens and having high-quality images. On page 14, I included a helpful photo checklist for reference. On page 16, I cover how to write listing titles using both Etsy’s search data and Google Keyword Planner.

Behavior-based algorithm means Etsy now weighs post-click engagement metrics such as clicks, favorites, add-to-cart actions, dwell time, and conversions. This ties back to creating a helpful listing: a clear title that tells people exactly what you're selling, a description that answers common questions, and a variety of photos that give buyers a complete understanding of the product.

Most of the tactics in the ebook are foundational and still apply today. I wouldn’t consider them “black-hat hacks,” but rather evergreen strategies.

reviews.title: Strong Planning Depth with Room for Improvement
reviews.comment:
I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Our testing team found PrometAI easy to navigate overall, with a good loading experience, helpful guided walkthrough, and no functional bugs during the testing stage. Its strongest value is the combination of AI-assisted business planning, financial projections, valuation, scenario analysis, and pitch deck creation in one workflow. Classic Mode was noticeably clearer than the more crowded Journey experience.

During testing, our biggest concern was that generation happened with limited upfront control, which could produce a first draft that felt too generic for the intended audience. The Partner has since built an optional pre-generation step for details such as business stage, purpose, tone, differentiation, target customer, funding, and custom instructions, while deliberately keeping the faster generate-first workflow as the default based on its user research.

The version we tested also produced AI imagery that sometimes felt generic for investor-facing material and did not provide the depth of brand-system controls some professional users may want, so we would still recommend reviewing and tailoring generated output before using it externally. 

The Partner allows images to be regenerated or replaced, has deeper brand controls on its roadmap, and reported that a more standardized 14-section lender/SBA-style template was in final QA following the test.

children.comment:
Thank you for the depth and structure of this test. Concerns raised precisely enough that we could act on them while the review was still in progress is the most useful feedback a product team can get, and it shows in how fast the items below moved.

For anyone reading along, all three threads from the test are now resolved:

Upfront control: the optional pre-generation step is live. Before generating, you can set business stage, purpose, tone, differentiation, target customer, funding and custom instructions, and the draft is shaped around them. We kept generate-first as the default because our user research shows most founders prefer to see a complete plan in minutes and refine from there, but the steering is there for anyone who wants it before the first draft.

Lender-ready format: the standardized 14-section lender and SBA-style template has cleared QA and is live. You can see it without signing up: open any plan in our public template library at prometai.app/business-plan-templates and switch to the SBA format tab.

Imagery and branding: every generated image can be regenerated or replaced with your own, and deeper brand-system controls are on the roadmap. Your advice to give externally facing output a final review is advice we give ourselves. A plan going to an investor or a lender should always carry the founder's final hand.

We are glad the core held up under a professional testing team: business planning, financial projections, valuation, scenario analysis and pitch deck in one workflow, with no functional bugs found. The Classic versus Journey observation is a useful signal for where we simplify next.

Thank you for the four tacos and for a review that made the product better before it was even published.

Best Regards,
David at PrometAI

reviews.title: Powerful Strategy Tool, but the Financial Model Needs Better Synchronization
reviews.comment:
PrometAI is one of those tools that made me more impressed the deeper I got into it, but also more cautious.

I tested it using a fictional multi-location convenience-store company called Survival Stop. My goal was not to build a pretty startup pitch deck. I wanted to see whether PrometAI could handle realistic operating economics, multi-location P&Ls, margin pressure, labor, shrink, foodservice, CAPEX, valuation, and scenario planning.

There is a lot to like.

The strategic framework is excellent. PrometAI generated useful material around mission, vision, stakeholders, SWOT, PESTEL, VRIO, Porter’s Five Forces, risks, roadmaps, responsibilities, and task ownership. The assignment of responsibilities across CFO, COO, CIO, CPO, etc. was especially interesting because I can see this becoming useful for management training or even AI-agent training.

The tool also became much more relevant once I corrected the assumptions. I was able to build a much more realistic convenience-store model with roughly $18M in annual revenue, thin margins, operating expense pressure, and a $300K CAPEX baseline.

Where PrometAI lost points was financial consistency.

I found situations where updated assumptions were correctly saved in one part of the model but older assumptions remained in other parts of the generated presentation. For example, the recalibrated model reflected the corrected revenue and cost assumptions in some screens, while the downloaded PDF still contained older revenue projections and prior revenue-mix assumptions on several financial pages. That means you really need to audit the finished output instead of assuming that every section has refreshed correctly.

That is a serious limitation for a tool positioned around financial planning and valuation.
I also found that the AI regeneration feature can overwrite carefully entered assumptions with its own defaults. Once I learned that, manual editing worked better, but there is definitely a learning curve.

What I like:
•	Very strong strategic-analysis framework 
•	Excellent depth compared with a typical AI business-plan generator 
•	Good risk, task, responsibility, and roadmap structure 
•	Useful scenario and financial modeling concepts 
•	Potentially excellent for consulting, training, and management development 
•	Surprisingly adaptable to an industry it was clearly not built specifically for 

What needs improvement:
•	Financial recalibration needs to propagate consistently throughout the entire model 
•	Regeneration should not overwrite custom assumptions without warning 
•	Final presentations need stronger synchronization with saved financial inputs 
•	Some startup-oriented assumptions need manual correction for established businesses 
•	Users should not have to hunt for which version of a number is actually authoritative 

I’m giving PrometAI 4 tacos because there is a lot of depth and genuine value here. However, the financial synchronization issues keep me from giving it 5. If PrometAI can ensure that recalibrated assumptions flow consistently through every financial statement, valuation, and generated presentation, this could easily become a 5-taco product.

children.comment:
Thank you - this is exactly the kind of testing we want PrometAI judged by: real operating economics, thin margins, multi-location structure, and a reviewer who audits the output.

What you ran into is a trade-off we debate internally all the time, and you articulated its cost precisely. The design choice behind it: once you have entered or approved a number, PrometAI treats it as yours - we never silently rewrite other parts of the plan because one assumption changed, since we cannot know whether you are mid-way through a series of edits or consider the rest final. The price of that choice is what you observed: sections you have not regenerated keep the last version you approved, including in the exported presentation, and a full regeneration rebuilds a section rather than surgically preserving every manual entry. Your expectation is the right one though - when a serious assumption changes, the model should either carry the change through or at least tell you which sections are now affected. That middle path is where we are heading.

Concretely, the short-to-medium-term pipeline includes even deeper industry grounding - our default assumptions have always been built on industry benchmark data, and we are now taking that a level further in detail and granularity - alongside tighter mechanics on CapEx, working capital and depreciation. The larger direction is a planning copilot that understands which downstream sections a changed assumption touches and proposes the updates - so consistency stops being something you audit and becomes something the product shows you.

Your review is precisely the kind of input that shapes what ships next. We want that fifth taco, and we intend to earn it.

Best Regards,
David at PrometAI

Is that possible? Or are we forced to stick with company ACME once workspace 1 has been created for and assigned to company ACME?

children.comment:
Hi, thanks for digging in - the consulting angle is exactly the right one to press on.

Samples: yes. There is a public library at https://prometai.app/business-plan-templates with examples across dozens of industries - each downloads as a full PDF of the investor presentation, no registration needed. 
To see how a plan looks and feels on the platform itself, open the restaurant example here: https://prometai.app/business-plan-templates/restaurant-business-plan-template/business-plan - you can page through it and switch between the formats, including the SBA one.

On workspaces, a small terminology correction first, because it changes the answer: there are no workspace containers in PrometAI. What you would call a workspace is, for us, simply a business plan - your tier gives you a number of plan creations, and each creation builds the plan together with the connected financial model behind it. A created plan is not frozen to company ACME: every input can be edited and any section regenerated with your monthly AI requests, to whatever extent the business needs, pivots included. The one line we draw is fair use: evolving a client's plan is exactly what the product is for, while wiping a finished plan to reuse it for a completely different company is against our policies - a new case means a new creation.

That maps neatly onto how consultants already work with us: build the plan for a client, hand it over as a download or, from Tier 3 up, share it by link so the client reviews it online. When the next client comes, their plan starts fresh. The higher tiers exist exactly for that - they go from 10 up to 100 business plans, so there is never a need to recycle anything.

These are great questions - if you have more, or want us to share how we work with consultants in practice, we are happy to answer. We are also kicking off partnership programs and perks for consultants who do business planning; if you would like to learn more, feel free to write to us at [email redacted] and we will arange a meeting.

Best regards,
David at PrometAI

questions.title: Questions on the API and MCP and the following bits:
questions.comment: Hi PrometAI team—I’m evaluating Tier 5 for B2B relationship planning. My company would work with existing businesses—not merely startups—to define a bounded commercial collaboration: each party’s role and contribution, the process being improved, decision rights, deliverables, economics, risks, confidentiality, implementation options and eventual agreement. Can one Tier 5 project represent and continuously maintain the relationship between two or more existing companies, rather than only one company’s investor plan? Can each business be invited into only its own isolated workspace, with permissions and no access to other projects? Can the workspace preserve versions, approvals and partner-specific outputs, and later be transferred or left accessible to that business? Is this use covered by Tier 5 consulting rights?

children.comment:
Hi, thanks for asking this precisely. You deserve precise answers, and three
of the four are no, so let me get those out of the way first.

Can one project represent and continuously maintain a relationship between
two or more companies?
No. A project models one business. You can keep it updated indefinitely, but
it is one company's model, not a two-party relationship object.

Can each business be invited into its own isolated workspace, with permissions
and no access to other projects?
No. There are no seats, no invited members and no per-project permissions.
Sharing is a view-only link, not an account.

Can the workspace preserve approvals and partner-specific outputs, and later
be transferred to that business?
Partner-specific outputs, yes: run each side as its own project and export a
separate branded document for each. Approvals, no, there is no sign-off
workflow. Transferring a project into another company's account, no.

Is this use covered by consulting rights?
Yes. Nothing in this deal's terms restricts using PrometAI for client work.

Where we are strong is the layer underneath that negotiation: the economics of
the collaboration modeled properly, and a clean document each side can read.

I'm the co-founder and CEO of PrometAI, and I would like to hear about your
requirements in more detail. Let me know if you have 30 minutes to chat.

[email redacted]

Narek Abgaryan, CFA, FRM
CEO, PrometAI

questions.comment: If one business plan is deleted, does that free up space for another project?

children.comment:
Hi, thanks for the question.

A plan credit is used the moment you create a business plan, and deleting the plan afterwards doesn't return it. 

If you're planning more than one business, it's worth picking the tier that covers all of them.

Best,
Nare at PrometAI
If business cannot be changed then what would we do with monthly credits? 90% of business plans are submitted initially.

You can edit and change a plan, and that's what the monthly AI requests are for - rewriting sections, updating your numbers, reworking the financials after feedback.
Deleting the business plan won't free up the credit for a new one.

But, similar to Upmetrics, I could just delete all information from the business plan slot that's been created and use the new slot for a new business plan? I'm trying to get my head around this. There's been similar deals on here and some/most have gone the way of the Dodo, so I'm rather hesitant to cough up another $$$ for a business planning tool.

Honest answer: no, and the difference is what happens at creation. In most planning tools, a plan is simply a structured document - deleting and reusing a slot is easy because little stands behind it. Here each creation triggers real analytical work: market data, financial analytics, your inputs built into a connected model and deck. That cannot be undone, so credits count creations.

On the Dodo point: fair concern. For us this deal is additional distribution, not a wind-down - we run an active subscription business outside AppSumo, the product has been on the market for 3+ years, and our consulting branch for almost ten. We are here to stay for the long run. And the 60-day refund window means you can test all of it at zero risk.
