reviews.title: Misleading Product and Zero Transparency. Makes me wondering if all these 5 star reviews are legitimate
reviews.comment:
My experience with Kiwilaunch has been extremely disappointing and misleading from start to finish.

The features shown on their AppSumo product page simply do not exist in the actual version I received. The setup options and booking features they advertise, including the quote-style funnel shown in their screenshots are nowhere to be found in the real product. After spending hours trying to make it work, I’m still unable to recreate what was promised at the time of purchase.

What’s worse, Kiwilaunch expects customers to pay additional third-party developers to get the product properly configured, even though it was marketed as a lifetime deal (LTD) with “no technical setup required.” On top of that, they still charge a 10% commission on top of the LTD, which makes absolutely no sense.

I contacted support multiple times, but instead of providing clear guidance or accountability, I was told that assisted onboarding isn’t offered, even though the advertised setup experience was meant to be simple and self-guided.

This experience has made me seriously question the credibility of AppSumo’s listings and reviews. If AppSumo continues to promote products like this, it undermines buyer trust across the entire platform.

I’ve left my feedback publicly because it’s unacceptable for AppSumo and Kiwilaunch to market a product one way and deliver something completely different, all while wasting customers’ time and money.

In short: misleading marketing, missing features, poor support, and a complete mismatch between what’s sold and what’s delivered. I am leaving this review in Oct 2025. Hope this concern gets addressed!

>> My response to the developers 1st and 2nd responses

Thank you for responding, but your reply doesn’t address the real issue. My concern is not about technical skill or comfort with setup. The problem is that the features shown in your AppSumo listing simply don’t exist in the actual version of Kiwilaunch available to buyers. The product visuals and marketing clearly present a quote-style booking flow, yet the platform itself doesn’t include that functionality.

I work with a web developer, and even he couldn’t locate the options or tools required to recreate what’s shown in your product images. That alone should show this isn’t about the users technical experience but rather misleading advertising and unclear product tutorial information.

You mentioned Kiwilaunch doesn’t operate as a quote-style funnel, but that distinction was never made clear on AppSumo. The listing gives the impression that those features are included. Buyers should not have to hire a third-party developer to achieve what was promoted as a no-code, ready-to-use solution.

Your explanation about the 1% commission and assisted onboarding doesn’t change the fact that what was marketed and what was delivered are not the same. My feedback stands: Kiwilaunch and AppSumo should update the product page to accurately reflect the platform’s actual capabilities so future buyers are not misled and do not waste time on something that is listed as a no code LTD.

So far they did not offer a genuine solution, only explanations and justifications.

children.comment:
Hello! I must admit I was quite surprised by this review.
While I understand everyone has different levels of technical comfort, I’d like to clarify a few things for anyone reading.

What you refer to as “step-by-step technical support” is actually what we call assisted onboarding — typically a 2–3 hour guided session. Kiwi, like any content creation platform, does assume a very basic level of web familiarity — essentially filling out forms and navigating simple menus. I understand this can feel challenging for some users, which is why many AppSumo buyers are actually agencies who resell and implement for their clients.

Since it wasn’t possible to provide the assisted onboarding in your case, I suggested external help — not out of indifference, but out of practicality and goodwill. It was the most efficient route for you to get going, and I would have given the same suggestion for software you wanted to buy and use.

Kiwi is consistently praised for its simplicity and ease of setup by hundreds of verified users, but of course, experiences vary — and your review is a useful reminder that no matter how easy we make it, it will never be easy enough for everyone


——

Hello again, and thank you for updating your review.

Just to clarify a few points for anyone reading — Kiwi doesn’t operate on a quote-style funnel; it’s a direct booking platform, which is clearly stated on the deal page.
We also don’t charge any 10% commission (obviously) — our fee is 1% only, and it’s fully transparent.

Kiwi has never required users to pay third-party agencies. For anyone with even basic experience using webforms, setup is entirely self-service. My earlier suggestion for external help was simply an attempt to tailor support to your comfort level — not to dismiss you. I can see how it might have come across differently, and my takeaway is to avoid sounding dismissive even when my intent is to be pragmatic and solution-oriented.

Every single review here is genuine, many from users with dozens of verified AppSumo purchases — people who understand how to evaluate a product fairly.

I do apologize once again if my suggestion offended you; it wasn’t condescending, just a genuine effort to help you get results faster. Your reaction makes it clear that it felt personal, and I respect that. Still, it’s uncommon to see such a harsh review simply because onboarding couldn’t be completed — most would have taken a refund and moved on.

Even in our third year, I’m still learning — and this, too, is part of the journey.

reviews.title: Missing key features for coaching  (see list of competitors in review)
reviews.comment:
Almost all or all therapy and life coaching platforms support 1) self scheduling, 2) comprehensive intake forms, 3) esigned paperwork, and 4) client portals. I can do workarounds for a few of these, but I found it odd that self scheduling, a key feature on competitors' platforms, is not only missing, but will not be considered in future. 

I also found it odd that the founder will not consider a WYSIWYG or rich text editor for confirmation and reminder emails, which was the dealbreaker for me.

See, kiwilaunch can't support intake forms that have conditional logic (and I have my reasons for needing this). That is fine, I can direct the client elsewhere to fill out. They also can't support esigned documents and again, that's okay since I can do the same redirecting. But what I am not going to do, is send the client a block of plain text wedged at the top of a confirmation email that looks like a run on sentence because I need to give instructions as to where to go because certain features are not available. It not only looks unprofessional, but limits accessibility. Some people may be fine with being on the phone to provide information but some will need clear and styled written emails to know what is going to happen next.

It's a shame since there is a lot of great stuff here. I just don't think its a competitor in the life coaching/therapy space. Or maybe that's just me and my business. I can see the value of the platform for other business types though, and for people who don't mind doing the manual work!

--
Edit update: coaching platforms that have 1) self scheduling (including client's ability to cancel and reschedule without admin), 2) dedicated client portal, 3) e-signature agreements,  and 4) customizable confirmation and reminder emails.
- Practice.do
- Honeybook
- Paperbell
- Satori
- CoachVantage
- Practice Better
- Simply.Coach
- Dubsado
- Bonsai

Also wanted to note that the response time is... uneven. It can take 2 hours or 2 days. Not a huge issue, but I wish it was more clear. The chat says it will take a "few hours" and yet 2 out of the 4 times I messaged, that wasn't the case.

Just a small clarification: you're right that we don’t currently offer a WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) editor or built-in e-signature support.

Regarding the reminder emails, they aren't sent as unstyled plain text. I believe what you meant is that the visual style of the template isn’t customizable — while you can modify the subject line and body content, the overall layout stays the same.

Lastly, for the benefit of other potential buyers: coaches are actually our core customer segment, and your review will likely carry weight with them. If you're open to it, sharing the names of competitors that offer the features you mentioned would be really helpful — both for prospective users and for us. It would allow others to better evaluate the overall value and pricing in context.

questions.title: EU client site: is data EU-hosted? Do you offer a GDPR DPA? Does the embed load Google Fonts/Stripe before consent?

children.comment:
Hello! 
- Hosting: Your data is hosted on AWS eu-west-2 (London). Despite Brexit, the UK still holds an EU adequacy decision, so this doesn't conflict with EU GDPR — that's the latest guidance from our consultant.
- Stripe: Stripe only loads at the payment step, after the user has shown clear intent to purchase, so it's strictly necessary at that point. We use Stripe Connect (Standard), and card data flows directly from the browser to Stripe — it never touches our servers. Stripe is the payment data processor and is GDPR-compliant (SCCs / EU-US Data Privacy Framework) (considering your STripe account is EU merchant, not non-EU)
- DPA: We provide a DPA covering our role as your data processor, so we're covered on our side for how we handle your and your clients' data. Note that for your clients you are the data controller — so you still need your own privacy policy, which you can set in the Kiwi admin panel. Our providing a DPA doesn't remove your own obligations toward your clients.
- Google Fonts: This is the one open item. For widgets we previously used "inherit from CSS" (which loaded no external fonts), but it was glitching so we reverted to loading fonts. Thanks to your message I've added "Self-host Google Fonts" to our roadmap — I appreciate you flagging it.

To set it up, add the second host to a team, create a booking type in that team, set "Team booking type" to Collective and tick both hosts. children.comment:
Hello, thanks for reaching out!

No, you don't need to buy anything on top of Agency Lifetime. Agency includes everything in Individual Lifetime plus the team features, and your team member doesn't need a paid plan either: she can join your team with a free TidyCal account, and on your team's booking types she gets your plan's features (her own personal booking types follow her own plan). Agency bought today includes up to 4 team seats, counting you.

Yes to both. Each of you keeps your own booking types, so clients can book either of you on your own, and for joint meetings you can create a team booking type set to Collective, which only shows the times when both of you are free. For your webinar, group bookings (several people booking the same slot, up to a capacity you set) are included in Agency too. Team booking types are covered here: https://help.tidycal.com/article/742-team-booking-types

On future changes: when the Agency deal changed on 1 September, people who had already bought it kept the limits they bought, and the new limits applied only to new purchases. One charge has been added to the lifetime plans, including Agency: a 1% platform fee on payments you take through Stripe, which your bookers pay by default. questions.title: Can I manage scheduling for more than one business or brand from one TidyCal login, without creating a new account?
questions.comment:
I run a few separate businesses and want to manage all of their scheduling from one TidyCal login, without creating a new account and email address for each one.

Before I upgrade to Pro, can you confirm the following:

1. Can I create multiple separately branded booking pages under one account? For example, one page for Business A and another for Business B, each with its own name, logo, colors, and booking types.
2. Can each of those pages use its own custom domain (book.businessA.com and book.businessB.com), or does Pro include only one custom domain per account?
3. If I use a team page as a workaround for a second brand, can it have different branding and a different custom domain from my personal page?

If this works, I'm ready to upgrade. Thanks!

children.comment:
Hello, thanks for reaching out!

Yes, on Pro you can run several brands from one login, with one difference from how you described it: an account has a single personal booking page, and each additional brand is set up as a team.

1. Your personal page carries your own name, photo and bio. A team has its own name, logo, description and URL, and its page lists only that team's booking types. So Business A can be your personal page and Business B a team, or each business can be its own team.

2. Pro isn't limited to one custom domain. You can connect one domain to your personal page and one to each team, so book.businessA.com and book.businessB.com can both run from the same account.

3. Yes for the name, logo and custom domain: a team's are separate from your personal page's. Colors work differently. A team page uses the same theme as the team owner's personal page, so the page-level colors are shared. Each booking type can have its own theme though, so the pages your clients book on can still match each brand.

Custom domains: https://help.tidycal.com/article/1000-custom-domains---use-your-own-domain-for-booking-pages

Teams: https://help.tidycal.com/article/732-teams

Themes: https://help.tidycal.com/article/748-booking-theme-editor

If you have any other questions, feel free to reach out to us at [email redacted] and we'll be happy to help!
Thanks, Luka! That's exactly what I needed to know. Running each business as its own team with its own domain covers my use case. Appreciate the quick and detailed answer!

children.comment:
Hello, thanks for reaching out!

Not at the moment: the BreezeDoc API doesn't have an endpoint that accepts a PDF upload, so a new file can only be uploaded in the app itself. It's a fair request, and https://breezedoc.com/feedback is the right place to log it so our product team sees it and other users can vote it up.

What the API can do today is work from templates. Upload the PDF once in BreezeDoc, place the fields and save it as a template. From then on your assistant can call the API to create a new document from that template and send it to the recipients you pass in (name and email), and they get their signing link by email.

That covers documents that reuse the same layout, such as a standard contract or NDA. A different PDF each time would still need the upload step in the app.

The API is included in every paid plan, and you create your token at https://breezedoc.com/integrations/api

API docs: https://breezedoc.com/developer/docs/

If you have any other questions, feel free to reach out to us at [email redacted] and we'll be happy to help!

children.comment:
ResumeUp adds no watermarks or hidden characters to your documents.

We use GPT models, and ChatGPT does not currently watermark text output. Some newer Claude models may embed a statistical text watermark, not hidden characters.

Editing or rewriting can make such marks harder to detect, and AI detectors are generally unreliable for short, bullet-point resumes.

reviews.title: Vibe coded for 1 week and then abandoned?
reviews.comment:
I have to say I'm genuinely disappointed by what I need to write as a review for this application. 

👉🏻 Xinterview has nothing to do with Prospect'In (Waalaxy)

Contrary to what he claims on his roadmap, the founder of Xinterview has absolutely no connection with the Prospect'In/Waalaxy team, which is highly successful and therefore very reassuring. I reached out to one of Prospect'In's co-founders and he confirmed that he has no affiliation with Xinterview whatsoever.

👉🏻 False G2 awards 

On their website, they claim to have received numerous awards on the G2 platform, which is not the case at all. When I purchased a lifetime license on AppSumo for this software, these awards displayed on their website obviously played a significant and reassuring role in my decision. Since then, lies and suspicious behaviors have gradually accumulated.

👉🏻 False promises about platform updates

The first lie was claiming in February 2025 and in October 2025 that a major update was being prepared with advanced AI integration on the platform. More than two months have passed and there hasn't been the slightest evolution of the platform. Absolutely none. Not a single email from the company to its users either. Nothing at all.

👉🏻 Questionable team composition

But that's not all. I tried to contact the founder and realized that there are no other employees for this company on LinkedIn. None. Yet they wrote to me saying that nine developers were working on this platform, which is particularly surprising when you see that the platform isn't evolving at all.

I tried contacting the founder on LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and by email 2 months ago. Same thing—nothing at all. Not a single response.

👉🏻 Unresolved technical issues

The last and biggest disappointment is, of course, the fifty or so bugs I've identified on this platform. I've systematically reported them with screenshots and maximum detail to technical support—though I'm not sure you can call it technical support since it's just the software's chat feature. Not a single bug has been fixed in the past two months and they confirmed to me last night that none of the 30+ bugs I reported to them will be fixed.

All of this together convinces me that this is an application that was probably quickly coded in a week and is no longer being developed at all today, and probably hasn't been for a very long time, possibly since its launch. There's therefore a huge discrepancy between the image being projected by what is certainly the sole person behind this company and what it actually is.

I'm therefore naturally starting to doubt the reviews that have been published here and there, because I can't believe for a second that this accumulation of bugs hasn't caused problems for other users as well.

Finally, I want to clarify that a phone call or screen-sharing session wouldn't fix all the bugs on your platform. I'm not a user who doesn't know how to use the software. I know perfectly well how to use it. Everything I've reported to you consists mainly of bugs that need to be resolved urgently on your end (around 35 to 40 bugs) and 10 to 15 suggestions to improve the application.

children.comment:
We respectfully disagree with this characterization and would like to clarify several important points.

👉🏻 Regarding G2 awards:
All G2 awards displayed on our website are legitimately earned and published by G2 in their quarterly reports. These reports are publicly available and can be independently verified directly on the G2 platform. We would never claim or display awards we have not received.

👉🏻 Regarding platform updates and AI integration:
We have been actively improving the platform, with updates typically released every 15 days. While some updates may not always be highly visible on the surface, they include backend improvements, bug fixes, performance optimizations, and feature enhancements.

👉🏻 Regarding team composition:
This is not a one-person company. Developing a product is not an easy task—it requires significant effort, dedication, and continuous work day and night from the entire team. Team size does not define the quality, legitimacy, or capability of a product. We are a highly motivated team, full of energy, and actively building, maintaining, and improving the platform on an ongoing basis.

👉🏻 Regarding communication and support:
Our support team has consistently offered to arrange a one-on-one call or demo with the founding team to address concerns in detail, including technical issues and the product roadmap. Unfortunately, we did not receive confirmation to proceed with a call.
We also found no record of LinkedIn messages or emails reaching the founding team. Founders do not publicly share WhatsApp numbers, so contact through that channel would not be possible. It is likely there was a misunderstanding or an attempt to contact an incorrect account.

👉🏻 Regarding reported bugs:
No platform is perfect—every product improves over time, and we continuously work on enhancements. We genuinely appreciate the time and effort taken to share feedback. After reviewing the feedback, the majority of reported already present on the platform, feature requests, or future enhancements rather than critical bugs. That said, we have been actively fixing issues and rolling out improvements.

👉🏻 Regarding professional images:
Using AI to enhance professional images is a common and widely accepted industry practice and does not indicate anything misleading or suspicious.

We value all user feedback and remain fully committed to improving our product. Our team is always available through our official support channels, and we remain open to a direct conversation to address any concerns in detail.

Best regards,
The XInterview Team

reviews.title: Super esignature software
reviews.comment:
BunnyDoc Review

I'm the founder of a naturopathy educational institute in Quebec, Canada. We needed an e-signature solution to collect consent forms from students and clients before appointments — roughly 100 documents per month. After researching DocuSign, eZsign, and BreezeDoc, I purchased the BunnyDoc Lifetime Plan 3 on AppSumo.

What works well:

• Public Form Links are the standout feature. We generate a unique URL for each consent document and embed it in our appointment reminder emails (via Acuity Scheduling). The client clicks, enters their name and email, receives the signing request, signs, and we're done. Zero manual work on our end. This alone justified the purchase.

• The signing request email arrived instantly and landed in the inbox (not spam) on our first tests with Gmail. This was our biggest concern going in, given reports from other users about deliverability issues.

• The client-facing form is clean and professional. Our logo appears at the top, the title is clear, the interface is in French (a pleasant surprise for our Quebec clientele), and the reCAPTCHA adds a layer of security.

• The field editor is intuitive. Placing signature fields, text fields, auto-fill name, and signed date on our PDF took minutes. Once you understand the drag-and-drop system, it's fast.

• Entrust digital certificates (AATL) embedded in the signed PDFs give real legal weight — important for us.

• The plan includes 1,500 web signatures/month, 10 public form links, and 10 team members — more than enough for a small company.

• Google Drive integration for automatic backup of signed documents is a smart safety net.

What could be improved:

• The confirmation page after the client submits the public form link is in English only ("Action Required - Follow Instructions in the Email"). For a bilingual or French-speaking clientele, this is jarring. A language option or customizable confirmation message would help.

• Templates and Links are separate workflows. You'd expect to create a template once and generate a public link from it, but instead you upload the same PDF twice — once for the template, once for the link. Minor inconvenience, but it feels redundant.

• No custom email domain (sending from @yourdomain.com instead of @bunnydoc.com). This would significantly improve deliverability and brand trust. I hope this feature is on the roadmap.

• The "Powered by BunnyDoc" footer on the client-facing form can't be removed on the Lifetime plan. Not a dealbreaker, but white-labeling would be appreciated.


Bottom line:

For the price of a one-time lifetime deal, BunnyDoc delivers serious value. The Public Form Links + appointment reminder workflow is exactly what small clinics and educational institutes need. The digital certificates give it an edge over simpler alternatives like BreezeDoc. If email deliverability holds up across a broader range of recipients and the team addresses the language/localization gaps, this could be a long-term solution. Hope the company will stay alive. We never know with startup. Still, very promising.

Thank you.

Is it the perfect DocuSign replacement? No. Is it close? Maybe. Does it do what I need? Absolutely. I’m excited to see how it improves over time, but for now, it reliably gets the job done when it comes to signing documents.

As mentioned previously, our team is currently building a new version of the system, which is expected to be released by mid-April. While it had some limitations when it first launched, it has improved dramatically over the last couple of years as the founder has been very receptive to feedback. I am especially happy with the ability to now allow guest access to individual roleplays so that no account setup is needed (though this is only suitable if you don't need subsequent lessons to be personalized based on the learner's progress with previous lessons). You can assign credit limits for guest access to roleplays to ensure credits aren't abused, and you can also set up time limits to ensure the duration is suitable based on the skill being practiced and to avoid any possible AI hallucinations when context capacity has been reached.

Overall, I am very happy with Personeo as it is invaluable for providing roleplay practice.

reviews.comment: A focused product that's intuitive to use; it's very helpful for simulating interviews and conversations. This AI has a well-defined purpose and does its job very well.

reviews.title: Wow - Expectations surpassed!
reviews.comment:
I nearly refunded this app due to a lack of time and also because I thought it wouldn't suit one of my use cases which was interviews, but I decided to challenge it with a quick test. 
The test was a probing Behavioral interview with the CEO of a large company for a new role as Commercial Finance Director, this is not a waffle and wing it situation but one that requires deep technical experience backed up with strong factual evidence and with great communication. 
The prompt took me 25 minutes and the interview itself was only 30 minutes, but much to my surprise the questions were pretty good, possibly the interviewer was too easily satisfied, or maybe my answers were just awesome!! But normally I would expect at least 2-3 questions probing deeper into the first answer but to be fair I am a detail guy (ok verbose!) so possibly one question was enough. Regardless it was certainly not a waste of time and actually very good as a process.
Outcome: The feedback too was very helpful in the most part, a few things I didnt agree with but 90% plus was both fair and helpful, so Im keeping it - to be fair the vendor said its not yet optimised for interviews but I hope they will do it. 
AI certainly seems to be progressing now, I know I could just use typing into AI but the voice and transcription features and prompt enchancement just make this far more efficient and useful to me. 
Well done Personoai, please do donsider optimising for interviews and consider the usual stuff such as "ummm" spotting. Im expecting even better results for its core jobs of pre sales meetings too. For this stage it is a solid 5 for now from me, more improvements and development will be needed for a secure future of course

reviews.title: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Excellent AI Role-Play Training Tool — One of the Most Unique LTDs on AppSumo
reviews.comment:
I’ve reviewed a lot of AI tools on AppSumo, and Personeo stands out because it’s actually built for VARIOUS (interchangeable) AI role-play training, which is something most other AI tools only do loosely or indirectly.

What I like most is how flexible the role simulation is. With Personeo you can easily simulate conversations between different roles, such as:
	•	customers
	•	employees
	•	managers
	•	interviewers
	•	sales prospects

You can even switch roles during the conversation, which makes it very powerful for training scenarios.

For example, you can set up situations like:
	•	An angry customer calling about a defective product
	•	A skeptical buyer questioning a salesperson
	•	A support agent dealing with complaints
	•	A manager coaching an employee

The AI can challenge you and make the interaction feel very realistic.

What really makes Personeo valuable is the training framework around the AI, not just the AI conversation itself. The platform includes:
	•	scenario templates
	•	defined roles
	•	performance feedback
	•	scoring and evaluation
	•	structured training modules
	•	team training possibilities

This turns it into something closer to a conversation training simulator, rather than just another AI chat tool.

Many other AppSumo AI products are:
	•	chatbot builders
	•	prompt tools
	•	automation assistants

Those can sometimes role-play if you push them with prompts, but they usually lack structure, analytics, scoring, and training design.

Personeo fills that gap really well.

Compared to enterprise platforms that do AI sales or negotiation simulations (which often cost hundreds or thousands per year), this LTD is actually very affordable for what it offers.

I also see interesting possibilities beyond just sales training. For example, it could be used for:
	•	customer service training
	•	ethical sales practice simulations
	•	consumer education
	•	product transparency conversations
	•	coaching and counseling scenarios

Overall, if you are looking for a structured AI role-play training platform rather than just another AI chatbot, Personeo is one of the more unique and useful tools I’ve seen on AppSumo.

Definitely worth trying if you want to practice realistic conversations, training simulations, or customer interaction ("customer coaching") scenarios. That's very impressive. 

I just hope they come out with an iOS app and allow this to speak in Japanese by 2027 if not sooner ( ^.^)(^.^ )/.

*****Warning: This tool is primarily intended for training, experimentation, and conceptual work, and should not be treated as a strict fact-checking proof-of-concept type of work. If insufficient data is provided, the AI may attempt to fill in gaps by generating very convincing examples or illustrations that may appear factual but are actually inferred or hypothetical.  Still, exceptional in flow. 

This behavior seems to be part of its design, allowing users to have a smoother and more creative training experience when working through conceptual scenarios.

Despite this limitation, I still find the platform very useful and plan to continue using it. In the future, it would be great to see an option or toggle that allows users to restrict or override fictional assumptions, characters, or unsupported claims when factual accuracy is required.

One additional strength I noticed is that the system appears capable of handling significantly larger data inputs in a single upload than what I’ve typically experienced with ChatGPT. Wow! Good stuff there! Thanks

reviews.title: A thoughtful API-first document workflow tool with strong governance ideas
reviews.comment:
We use PlutusDoc as a lightweight, document-first execution option alongside our broader client-operations platform.
What stands out is not simply e-signature. There are plenty of tools that can send a document for signature. The interesting part of PlutusDoc is the control model around the document lifecycle: scoped access, API/MCP support, idempotent writes, lifecycle states, audit/readback, and the ability to preserve a human approval boundary before consequential send/sign actions.
That architecture is a strong fit for how we work. We want automation to be able to prepare, inspect, correlate, and track a document, while keeping the actual external commitment under deliberate human control. PlutusDoc is clearly designed with agent/API operation in mind rather than having automation bolted on afterward.
We also like that it has a distinct role from a full CRM/client portal. PlutusDoc is attractive when we want a lighter, document-centric execution layer with deterministic IDs, readback, and integration behavior.
Our testing did uncover areas that could be better. The largest is least-privilege MCP/OAuth interoperability. We saw clients request broader scopes than the very narrow document-read scope we intended, even though PlutusDoc can issue API keys with exact read scopes. I would like the MCP path to make the same least-privilege behavior straightforward and consistent across clients.
We also encountered a UI-state edge case around a voided document where a signing control could remain visible. Lifecycle state should be absolutely unambiguous in a document/signing product, so I would like invalid actions to disappear or become clearly disabled immediately when the underlying state changes.
Overall, I like the product direction a lot. It is focused, developer/agent friendly, and takes idempotency, scopes, auditability, and lifecycle state more seriously than many document tools. We kept our Tier 1 license because that combination gives it a useful place in our stack even though there is still integration hardening I would like to see.

questions.title: Should all signing actions disappear immediately after a document is voided?
questions.comment: In lifecycle testing we encountered a state where a voided document could still present a signing control. We did not treat the control as authority, but for a signing workflow the UI should ideally make invalid actions impossible or unmistakably disabled. Is this expected behavior, a known UI-state bug, or already fixed? We would also like the API/MCP/UI lifecycle state to stay visibly consistent after void/decline/completion transitions.

questions.title: Can MCP clients request only exact document-read scopes without expanding the grant?
questions.comment: We verified that PlutusDoc API keys can be created with exactly the narrow read scopes we need, but MCP/OAuth testing with more than one client requested broader read or write-related scopes than intended. What is the currently supported way for a client to request only workspaces:read and documents:read with no additional contacts/reminders/teams/calendar or write/send scopes? A current Codex/ChatGPT/Cursor example would help us validate least-privilege behavior.

reviews.title: AI assisted automation for systematic traders
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

TradeSgnl is built for traders who want to connect trading signals, strategy testing, risk rules, and execution into one automation workflow.

I’ll be honest, this one had a learning curve for me because I was not already familiar with some of the MT5 concepts. Once I understood how the pieces fit together, the product became much clearer.

The interesting part is how it helps move a trading idea from signal to execution with more structure. You can bring in alerts, use AI to interpret trading messages, apply risk rules, map symbols, test ideas in Strategy Lab, and choose whether to run execution locally or through the cloud option. The benefit is that you are not just reacting to alerts manually. You can build a more automated and controlled workflow around how trades are interpreted, tested, and executed.

The biggest value is for traders who already have a strategy, follow Telegram providers, or use TradingView alerts and want a more automated way to execute. Instead of manually watching alerts and copying trades, TradeSgnl gives you a way to turn those inputs into rules, execution, and monitoring.

A few things buyers should be aware of. This is not a casual trading app. You need to be comfortable with MT5, broker setup, risk rules, and trade automation. If you want to trade from the cloud, you connect your MT5 account during onboarding. If you want to run it locally, you have to install the TradeSgnl EA on MT5, which is Windows only.

I also asked about MT5 credential handling because MT5 does not offer an OAuth style connection. The team confirmed that credentials are sent over encrypted HTTPS, are not stored on their end, are not accessible to staff or third parties, and are wiped when the terminal is deleted.

Overall, TradeSgnl is worth considering if you are already an MT5 trader and want AI assisted automation around TradingView alerts, Telegram messages, strategy testing, and risk controlled execution. It is probably not the best first trading tool for a beginner, but in the hands of someone who wants to get better or someone who understands MT5 and automated trading, there is a lot here to work with.

reviews.title: TradeSgnl (Tier 3)
reviews.comment:
I picked up Tier 3 to test the TradingView integration and the strategy development side, and overall I'm pretty happy so far. The documentation is comprehensive, Market Analyst gives a fast, useful read on structure across timeframes, and Strategy Lab is a real time-saver for turning a plain-language idea into working Pine Script.

A few suggested improvements / comments:

1. I think there is a bug in Market Analyst. ASX tickers like CBA and WOW show up in the search, but running them just returns "The analyst is experiencing high demand right now." I waited and retried a few times before realising it does it every time, so I don't think it's actually load-related.

2. Market Analyst itself is good but a bit narrow. It's mostly EMA, MACD, RSI and ATR, and you pick one trading style per run. I'd love to see day, swing and scalp together in one go, and export would be handy too. Kavout offers more in this regard, with near-term and swing setups, entry, stop and target levels, plus a confidence read. That said, that's one of Kavout's main features, whereas TradeSgnl offers a much wider range of trading tools and automation.

3. The model behind Strategy Lab handles simple strategies well, but it starts to struggle once you're combining several indicators or stacking conditions. I have experienced it stalling partway or producing a Pine Script that encounters some errors when you upload it in TradingView. 

4. There's also no backtesting built into Strategy Lab, so there's no real build-test-refine loop. You can generate a strategy in one place and test it somewhere else, but you can't iterate in a single flow. Even a rough, clearly-labelled quick test inside the Lab would make a big difference.

5. It would be great to have access to a TradeSgnl API or MCP server, so we could use our own AI to build, test and save strategies into the application, then use TradeSgnl to deploy them.

For completeness, I haven't yet tried the MT5 integration or the Telegram copier, which are arguably the main features of the app, so I can't comment on those.

Overall, a good tool that has potential.

Hi @skinspec,

Thanks for reaching out!

Setup & Hosting: Yes, TradeSgnl runs on a Windows environment (typically a Windows VPS). It listens for incoming webhooks from TradingView or signals from Telegram and executes trades automatically.

reviews.title: A Fast, User-Friendly Platform with Accounting Gaps
reviews.comment:
Invoiless positions itself as a streamlined invoicing solution, and in many aspects, it absolutely delivers on that promise. However, its approach to financial reporting might not suit every business.

Pros: Invoiless is incredibly fast and easy to use, with a snappy, responsive interface that makes invoicing a breeze. The white-labeling, customer portal, and multi-language support are excellent features for a professional, international-facing business.

Cons: The reporting is basic, and the biggest drawback is its cash-basis accounting. Unpaid invoices don't count as income, which is problematic for anyone needing to use accrual accounting. This limits its usefulness as a complete financial tool. 
The tax report has two main issues:
    - It shows a combined total for all taxes, with no breakdown between provincial and federal amounts.
    - It groups total sales and expenses, instead of listing each individual line item and its corresponding tax."

I'm eager to adopt and recommend this platform, but its current reporting shortcomings are a significant barrier. To be viable, the reports must provide the comprehensive data and flexibility our accountant needs to prepare accurate business tax returns.

reviews.title: Capital Connector AI: Promising Concept, Significant Execution Issues
reviews.comment:
Capital Connector AI presents an intriguing proposition: leveraging artificial intelligence to connect organizations, including non-profits, with potential funding sources. The idea of streamlining the often-complex process of finding financial support is certainly appealing, particularly for resource-constrained entities like small non-profits.

However, the current reality of using this product appears to fall significantly short of its potential. A critical drawback is the apparent lack of adequate customer support. We made multiple inquiries regarding the company's stated offer of free access for non-profits. They went unanswered, forcing a supporter to purchase the product independently. This lack of responsiveness is a major concern, especially for users who may require assistance or clarification before committing financially.

Furthermore, the absence of tutorials or instructional materials poses a significant barrier to effective utilization. Without clear guidance, users are left to navigate the platform through trial and error, which can be time-consuming and frustrating. A tool designed to simplify a process should not, in itself, become a source of complexity due to a lack of user support.

While the underlying technology of Capital Connector AI may hold promise, the current lack of customer service and user guidance severely hinders its practicality and value. For non-profits and other organizations seeking efficient funding solutions, these shortcomings represent significant obstacles. Until these fundamental issues are addressed, potential users may find themselves better served by seeking out more established and user-friendly alternatives. The core concept is innovative, but the user experience needs substantial improvement to make Capital Connector AI a viable and reliable tool. I will be asking for a refund.

questions.title: Questions about HoneyBill

Hello,

Can I switch the entire backend interface to German?

Can I also communicate with the AI in German to create an invoice?

On which servers and in which country is the data stored?

Does HoneyBill also work without an active internet connection?

children.comment:
Hey Torben,

German interface: Not yet, the app itself (menus, buttons, settings) is English only today. Full UI translation is something we're working towards but not live yet.

German with HoneyAI: Yes, this works today. You can speak or type to HoneyAI in German (or any language) to create invoices, and it'll understand and generate accordingly.

Data storage: Hosted in the EU with Hetzner, so your data sits on German servers.

Offline use: No, HoneyBill is a cloud-based web app and needs an active internet connection to work.

Editing sent invoices: Once an invoice is sent, it's locked to protect the audit trail, only drafts are editable. If something needs correcting after sending, the usual path is to cancel it and issue a new one.

Let me know if anything else comes up.

John

reviews.title: Finally, a simple WordPress payment solution

reviews.title: A very smart Plugin Indeed

questions.title: Credits - what does total exactly mean?
questions.comment:
Is it monthly renewed or you just purchase access for - let's say - 100 USD and for that amount you can generate X reports?
And if so, what then?

children.comment:
**Equitest isn’t a typical software deal on AppSumo.** 
Rather than focusing on credit limits, consider the direct ROI: a single professional business valuation usually costs thousands of dollars on the market. With Equitest, you can run a full valuation for your company at a fraction of that cost—or, if you offer valuation services, generate thousands of dollars in revenue for your practice.

---

### Credit Breakdown

**"Total credits" means a single, lifetime pool of credits included with your purchase—they do NOT renew monthly.**

When you purchase Tier 1 ($100 for 250 Total Credits), those credits are added to your account immediately and do not expire. You draw down from that balance as you perform actions:

* **Standard Business Valuations (⚡ 10 credits):** Up to **25 full valuations** (250 / 10).
* **409A Compliance Reports (⚡ 25 credits):** Up to **10 reports** (250 / 25).
* **Group Valuations (⚡ 5 credits):** Up to **50 portfolio company evaluations** (250 / 5).
* **PDF/DOCX Exports & First 2 Audits:** Completely **FREE** (0 credits).

---

### Is 250 Credits Enough?

For most business owners, advisors, and founders, 25 full valuations cover several years of work.

**What happens if you run out?**
We have been serving users on AppSumo since 2020 and are committed for the long run. If you ever use up your pool:

* **During the active deal:** Upgrade your tier or stack additional codes to expand your lifetime credit balance (e.g., Tier 2 = 550 credits, Tier 3 = 900 credits).
* **After the deal ends:** Purchase top-up credit packs directly inside the platform whenever needed—no forced recurring monthly subscriptions.
how much the top up costs afterwards?

If you run out of credits, you have two flexible options:
1. Upgrade or stack AppSumo Tiers: While the AppSumo deal is active, you can simply upgrade your tier directly on AppSumo to instantly expand your lifetime credit pool .

reviews.title: Support that actually builds what you ask for
reviews.comment:
I run a small UK e-commerce business and take customer calls through a softphone on my PC. I use Hedy to record and summarise those calls, and its webhooks send the transcript and recap straight into our own customer system, so every caller's history is there next time they ring.

The one gap was starting and stopping sessions automatically, since meeting detection only covers Zoom, Teams and Webex. I asked support. They gave me a clear, honest answer about what was and wasn't possible, then came back to say they'd built it for the next release: links to start and stop a session, so my phone system can control Hedy itself. They even made it off by default for safety.

The recap plus full transcript is what makes it useful day to day, and the webhook data is clean and easy to work with. For a lifetime deal, being listened to and having a feature request picked up this quickly is rare.

Highly recommended if you want call or meeting notes that plug into your own tools.

reviews.title: Promising, With an Astonishing Number of Failure Modes
reviews.comment:
❯ No messages in {my email} with "robo" per Hostinger.

● No reply in your inbox yet — noted, matches Robomotion's own track record of slow/no maintainer response on filed issues (#57/#58 went 5 days with zero response, per prior session notes).

  Here's what the investigation actually turned up, and my honest read:

  What I found

  No changelog for the version actually running. GitHub's release feed for robomotionio/robomotion-next stops at v26.5.0 (published 2026-04-30). Every robot in this repo — including the one that just failed — runs v26.9.2, confirmed live in the connect logs.
  That's ~5 months of shipped changes with zero public release notes, including whatever changed in exactly the area that broke (robot auth/reconnect). There's no way to check "did they push a breaking change to token validation" because they don't publish what changed between .5 and .9.2 at all.

  No usable status/incident page. status.robomotion.io renders client-side with nothing in the initial HTML — no incident history retrievable without a real browser session.

  No idle/heartbeat visibility, which cuts against "quiet spin-down for non-use." I pulled the full journal across the ~26-hour
  silent window before the outage. There is zero log output of any kind — no heartbeat, no keepalive, no periodic status line — the
  entire time. The very first log line after 26 hours of total silence is the moment we sent the stop signal. That means the client
  emits no signal distinguishing "still genuinely connected" from "connection quietly died hours ago and nobody would know." So I
  can't confirm or rule out a silent idle timeout — the product gives you no telemetry to check either way. That absence is itself
  the finding.

  What the evidence does support: the reconnect attempt with the old, previously-working token failed twice with two different
  rejection codes (not_allowed, then auth_failed) before you regenerated it in the console, and the new token connected on the first
  try. A token that was fine yesterday and dead today, with no client-side change, no expiration warning, and no way to inspect why
  server-side — that's consistent with either a silent idle-timeout policy nobody documents, or a backend change that invalidated
  live sessions. Robomotion's opacity means there's no way to tell which from our side.

  Is the tech impressive?

  The Designer/AI-assistant/flow-authoring side is genuinely capable — the action-compiler approach this repo built on top of it
  works, and Robomotion's throughput (a real 48.9s/application proof-of-concept) is fine. But the operational substrate is fragile in
  a way that matters more for a production system: this is at minimum the 6th distinct live-reproduced defect in about 48 hours
  across this account (auth login/whoami rejecting valid sessions, misleading vault-not-found errors, a deterministic Timer bug, no
  self-healing after a node error, silent poll-loop death, and now a silently-dying robot token) — filed as issues #59–#64, none
  acknowledged by a maintainer within the same window. A platform whose core promise is "runs your robot reliably, unattended"
  shouldn't have this many ways to go silently dark with zero telemetry to diagnose it after the fact. That's the accurate
  characterization: capable authoring tool, hyper-fragile runtime, near-zero observability into its own failures.

Put together with everything else: the monitoring page being empty isn't a bug you're hitting, it's very likely just unpopulated for a self-hosted "Local Run" robot — Robomotion's metrics/monitoring plumbing appears built for their managed Cloud Run robots,
  and a self-hosted one like Filler 1/2 probably never reports into it at all. That's consistent with everything found today: no heartbeat in the local logs, no changelog for the version you're running, no accessible incident history, and now no monitoring data either. There's no single smoking gun proving "they pushed a breaking change" — there's something arguably worse, which is that the product gives you no instrumentation anywhere to even ask the question. You're flying blind on a self-hosted robot by design, not by misconfiguration.

children.comment:
Hi Ken,

Sorry about the issues you’ve experienced.

One thing that would help us a lot: the reports are currently very detailed and include a lot of assumptions and debugging. For us, it is much easier to investigate if you simply tell us:

* What you expected to happen
* What actually happened
* The steps to reproduce it
* A few screenshots or relevant log lines

There is no need to diagnose the root cause on your side. We can investigate that. Adding assumptions about the cause can sometimes make the reports harder for us to process and understand.

From your message, should I understand that the robot token generated under Admin Console → Robots stopped working and you had to generate a new one?

If so, this is not behavior we have seen before. It may be related to an older token, but we need to investigate before drawing any conclusions.

Regarding release notes, we are developing and shipping Robomotion very quickly, and our public changelog has fallen behind the actual releases.

Most updates are currently shared through Discord. Please check the #product-updates channel, which is much more up to date. In the latest versions, we also added a “What’s New” section directly inside the product, so when you open Designer, you can see the latest changes.

This is an area we know we need to improve. In earlier years, our documentation was also behind the product, and since then we have invested significantly in our documentation and especially to our Robomotion Academy videos.

You can also follow and subscribe to our YouTube channel for updates:
https://youtube.com/robomotion

We are now working on improving release communication in the same way.

There are constant updates going into the platform, and unfortunately the public changelog sometimes falls behind. We try to keep the updates current, especially through Discord.

There have been several major additions recently, including Build with AI, Robomotion Apps, and Agent Teams (early preview). Please also check out our Agent Hub also.

Robomotion can now build apps, and we have already developed three apps as demonstrations. You can clone these apps and modify them yourself as well.

As these features mature, we will also publish more videos on our YouTube channel, which we try to keep up to date.

For now, Discord and YouTube are the best places to follow the latest Robomotion updates.

Best,

questions.title: Compare with GrokBot
questions.comment: How does robomotion compare to the recently launched GrokBot?

children.comment:
Hi,

There is definitely some overlap, especially now that both products have agents, but they come from very different directions.

Robomotion started as an automation platform and RPA is still at its core. It was built to automate browser and desktop applications, APIs, files, databases, and other business systems. Automations can run locally, on your own servers, or in the cloud, and they do not require AI.

What has changed is how you can build and use those automations.

Today, you can describe what you want and let AI build the automation for you. But the result is still a real Robomotion flow. You can open it on the canvas, see every step, manually change it, debug it, or continue developing it with AI. Once it works, it can run repeatedly without requiring an AI model to figure out the process again each time.

Grok Bot takes more of an AI-first approach. Each Bot is a persistent AI agent with access to a cloud computer, browser, filesystem, terminal, connectors, skills, and routines. You give the Bot an outcome, and the model decides how to accomplish it. Grok Bot also supports multiple Bots collaborating and handing work to each other.

Robomotion combines both approaches.

You can build deterministic automations for the parts of a process where you want exact control, and use AI agents for the parts that require reasoning. Those automations can then become tools that your agents use.

With Robomotion Agent Teams (early preview), you can create teams of humans and agents that collaborate, communicate, delegate work, and use your automations as tools.

And with recent Robomotion Apps, any flow can become the backend of an application. You can build the UI and the automation behind it with AI, then use the app directly through its UI or expose its capabilities to agents through MCP.

You can already see examples in our store.
The apps and agents there are free to install and use. If you want to customize one, you can clone it and modify the workflows behind it. We are also adding many more.

Currently, we have:
- Stageline, a CRM app with MCP support, so your Agents can also do outreach
- Ad Cracker, which helps you analyze ads from your competitors, get inspiration from what is working, and use AI to create similar concepts for your own campaigns.
- Inkwell, an AI-powered book creator.

So I would summarize the difference like this:

Grok Bot starts with an autonomous AI agent and gives it a cloud computer and tools.

Robomotion starts with controllable automation, then lets you combine those automations with AI agents, Agent Teams, and applications. You can create deterministic automations with AI and then when these automations run you do not pay anything.

For open-ended tasks where you want to tell an AI what to achieve and let it determine the steps, Grok Bot is very interesting.

For business processes where you also want repeatability, local execution, desktop application automation, visibility into every step, and the ability to decide exactly where AI should and should not be involved, that is the problem Robomotion is designed around.

Best,

questions.title: What are the licensing, external-user access, and commercial-use limitations of Tier 6?
questions.comment:
Hi Robomotion team,

I'm considering Tier 6 and would appreciate clarification on its licensing terms.

1. What qualifies as a user under the Unlimited Users allowance?

2. Are external users permitted, and what access restrictions apply?

3. What commercial-use rights are included with the lifetime license?

4. Are there any additional licensing fees, usage restrictions, or limitations when using robots and AI agents for commercial purposes?

5. Are self-hosted execution, API access, and queues included in Tier 6 without additional subscription requirements?

Thank you!

children.comment:
Hi,

1. The main limits are actually the robots, not the number of users. You can invite users to your workspace and assign them roles such as Owner, Admin, Developer, or Guest.

For example, Admin users can access the Admin Console, while Developers can access Flow Designer and the Agents dashboard.

For operational and non-technical teams, we often build Chat Assistants or apps in front of the automations. These users simply log in and interact with the Assistant or app, while the robot performs the actual work in the background.

2. Yes. You can invite external users to your workspace using any email address. Their access is controlled by the role and permissions you assign to them.

3. You can use your Tier 6 license commercially. Robots can run on your own VPS, server, or computer and effectively act as the execution layer for your applications and automations. Chat Assistants, Forms, and Robomotion Apps can provide the user interface, while the robots handle the actual processing and automation behind them.

4. There are no additional Robomotion licensing fees for using your robots or AI agents commercially. You can use your own AI API keys and proxy APIs, and you can run robots on your own machines without paying additional execution fees to Robomotion. Any third-party services you use, such as AI providers or proxy services, may have their own usage costs.

5. Self-hosted robot execution is included. You can install and run your robots on your own machines or VPS. API and webhook-based automations are also supported. Incoming HTTP requests are tunneled through Cloudflare directly to your robots. Queues are included in Tier 6.

Best,

reviews.title: An Automation Factory for Serious Builders
reviews.comment:
If you’re serious about leveraging automation—(or combining it with AI)—RTILA is the tool to get. It’s not for everyone, but for those who see its potential, it’s a game-changer.

I picked up RTILA through AppSumo about six months ago: 6 codes (100 machines) for $594, unlocking standalone bot compilation—a massive feature. Later, RTILA offered backend upgrades for Sumolings, so I upgraded to unlimited machines for $396 directly through their team. Total: $990 for what’s listed at $4,999 on their website. Lifetime licenses, no recurring fees.

RTILA isn’t Zapier. It’s closer to Puppeteer, Selenium, or Playwright—but with a simple UI and a fraction of the learning curve. 

If you don’t know those tools, here’s the gist: RTILA can do almost anything a human can do with a mouse and keyboard.

If you can map out the steps, RTILA can automate them. But it’s more than just a tool—it’s a factory. It lets you build bots, chain them into workflows, and even compile them into standalone software you own and can rebrand and sell (insane).

RTILA is versatile, but these are some of its strongest use cases:

Data Scraping: Extract public data—like pricing, reviews, or contact info—and organize it into CSVs, Google Sheets, or databases.

Lead Generation: Automate scraping leads, verifying emails, initiating outreach, and importing cleaned data into a CRM.

Chaining Automations: Stack bots by feeding the output of one into another or have them collaborate on a single project (e.g., updating a shared Google Sheet). 
Example:
Bot 1 scrapes leads.
Bot 2 verifies emails.
Bot 3 sends the data to your CRM.
Bot 4 triggers an outreach campaign.

Building SaaS Tools: While not fully ready yet, you’ll eventually be able to host RTILA Studio on a VPS and integrate it with GPU-powered PCs for local AI models.

AI-Powered Automations: Pair RTILA with AI to unlock exponential potential. Think sentiment analysis on scraped reviews, AI-enriched lead insights, or bots that dynamically adapt to changing web content.


RTILA isn’t “set it and forget it.” To use it effectively, you’ll need to learn:

1. CSS Selectors: RTILA interacts with webpage elements (like buttons, forms, or text) using CSS selectors. It’s straightforward to learn with a bit of practice.

2. BPMNs (Business Process Model and Notation): These flowchart-like visuals help you map out workflows and create reliable automations.

3. The Blank Canvas Problem: The hardest part? Deciding what to automate. RTILA gives you the entire internet as your playground, and that sheer freedom can feel overwhelming. But for those who know how to use it, it’s an incredibly powerful tool.


The tool is fantastic, but the team makes it exceptional.

Mohamed, RTILA’s CEO, is one of the most thoughtful, hardworking founders I’ve come across. He (& the team) have bootstrapped RTILA, delivers regular updates, and directly engages with users. Got a question? He’ll answer it. Stuck? He’ll hop on a call to help.

Mohamed isn’t just building a company—he’s building a community. The team actively involves users in shaping RTILA’s direction, and their dedication to delivering value is unmatched.


If you’re dabbling in automation, RTILA might be overkill. But for serious builders, it’s a no-brainer.

The Price: Through the AppSumo deal and backend upgrades, I got a lifetime license for unlimited machines and standalone bot compilation for under $1,000. That’s insane.

The Potential: RTILA is a factory for automations. You can build bots, stack them into workflows, and sell them as standalone products—or use them to enhance your current offer.

The Future: RTILA’s roadmap includes AI-generated bots, It’s not here yet, because they need enough templates (think pre-built automation blocks) to train it on, but it’s coming.


The Bottom Line

RTILA is a tool for serious builders. It’s powerful, flexible, and built for those ready to automate and scale. If you’re willing to learn, it can save you hundreds of hours, unlock new revenue streams, and help you create products to sell.

For some, it’ll sit on a shelf. But for those who see the opportunity, RTILA is a no-brainer.
And at this price—lifetime licenses, unlimited machines—you’re either in, or you’re missing out.

reviews.title: Best tool of 2021
reviews.comment:
Hello, I'm Roberto from Spain.

I have been working with automation and scraping tools for around 20 years. Sometimes I coded my own, at early times with C++, later on python, PHP...

For commercial software, I have been using a ton of tools, I could name a ton of them: WebHarvy, Web Content Extractor (newprosoft), scrapebox, WinAutomation, UBot...

You can figure I have spent thousands on licenses, plugins, maintenance, distribution tokens...

I found RTILA the best desktop scraping tool by far. The price is a real bargain.

If you never had to do a scraping, the process need a small learning curve. Not because the tool, it's just because to scrape a site sometimes is very easy, and sometimes could be more complicated.

No other tool has RTILA features for the price. You own a multiplatform tool, and you are free to use it to scrape as much as you can. Some saas tools could charge you 300$ for 30k records, but you can achieve those numbers in one day (just don't be too much aggressive scraping, be gentle).

You will be using a sandboxed real browser while scraping, based on chromium. The targeted site will see a "real user" navigating.

The automation actions are quite powerful, you can configure almost every detail, change the user agent, clear cookies, set timings, fill forms, clicking, scrolling, use variables, loops.

The project is configurable, define how many instances, tabs, proxies, timeouts.. whatever you need will be there.

For many projects the default settings are perfectly fine.

You can get alerts or get the results by email, FTP, csv/excel, HTML, JSON, Google Sheets or webhooks.

Don't be focused on the initial appearance, this is not a toy at all.

I have build around 400 projects with this tool, probably 50 were for clients. The results are insane, the core engine of RTILA is very well coded.

The mac and Linux versions are less tested, probably there are less users with those.

I usually go with the windows version, I run one on my computer to create the projects and a second one in my VPS.

Of course you can use proxies, or captcha solvers. You can install chrome extensions on the project, for example an ads blocker or some free vpn.

The projects can be scheduled, it has their own scheduler. They can be executed from command line if you need.

The inspector module is very complete, you could be intimidated a bit. There is no need of coding/programing on the 90% of the projects, but in case you need, all can be done with JavaScript.

For the selectors, it's point and click. Just define the elements you want to grab and give them a name.

This is a real gem, being honest, I recovered my investment on the first week after purchase this. Usually I do scraping and automation services.

Now this software is my first choice, you can get scraping projects in no time. My biggest project was to scrape 130k pages. 

Many features to comment but this review don't let me write more... you can get an idea about how much I love this tool.

questions.title: RTILA X standalone bot architecture
questions.comment:
Hi there!

With the current RTILA X standalone bot architecture, the executable uses its snips_id to fetch the encrypted configuration from the RTILA Snips server at runtime.

If RTILA Corporation or the Snips service were ever discontinued, would already distributed standalone executables continue to work?

Specifically:

1. Is there currently any option to embed the complete automation configuration inside the executable so it can run permanently without contacting RTILA servers?

2. Can Plan 6 / Enterprise users self-host the Snips backend and point their standalone bots to their own server?

3. If none of these are currently possible, is an offline/self-hosted fallback planned, and would existing AppSumo Plan 6 customers receive it?

Thanks for your answer!

children.comment:
Thank you for the clear message!

The initial architecture implementation used the snips.sh publish service to guarantee functionality. However, after a lot of tests the team found that the best secure option without having to force any SSH-related tasks on user machines is to have a custom service coded entirely from scratch. In few days, a new marketplace dedicated to hosted and ready-to-use templates following this same logic will launch.

Regarding offline and self-hosted fallbacks, the related code may be published as open-source. Although we believes that will still maintain a strong market position, allowing users to host and customize the remote destination host is an idea that will be considered and supported after finishing the official marketplace.

All AppSumo customers who got the standalone bot will continue to receive it just like what was done for the RTILA X version and the same policy will follow for upcoming upgrades. The team is currently focusing heavily on the standalone feature, so please don't hesitate to reach out to us directly if you need any help with that.

reviews.title: Powerful Product and a Founder Who Listens
reviews.comment:
SheetXAI is one of the best AI tools I have purchased on AppSumo. It is much more than an AI formula generator. It can clean data, research companies, organize information, extract data from documents, create reports, and automate multi-step spreadsheet work using plain English.

Yesterday, I had a two-hour meeting with David, the founder of SheetXAI. He personally walked me through a complete commercial real estate underwriting workflow using my CRE Value-Add Underwriting Model.

During the demonstration, SheetXAI:

• Analyzed multiple worksheets and identified a formula error
• Created a deal-comparison sheet with live calculations
• Imported and organized property-listing data
• Extracted information from an offering memorandum PDF
• Reconciled the rent roll against the OM
• Compared reported operating expenses with stabilized assumptions
• Flagged missing information instead of inventing numbers

That last point is especially important when analyzing commercial real estate deals. SheetXAI clearly separated reported information from items that still needed verification.

The meeting also showed me how committed David is to the product and its users. He listened carefully to my ideas about connecting SheetXAI with Wyn Intelligence, autonomous agents, MCP tools, voice input, and AI headphones. We discussed how someone could eventually speak a command and have SheetXAI update a spreadsheet or complete a workflow without sitting at a computer.

The new mini-app and workflow features add even more value. You can turn existing Google Sheets into interactive dashboards, prospecting tools, property trackers, broker directories, and lightweight CRM systems. You can also save repetitive tasks as workflows and schedule them to run again.

There is a learning curve, and structured prompts produce better results than vague instructions. David was transparent about this and showed me how to improve the workflow. That level of direct support from a founder gives me confidence in the product’s future.

I plan to use SheetXAI for commercial real estate underwriting, broker and property research, lead lists, personalized outreach, and my broader AI workflows with Codex, Hermes, and Wyn Intelligence.

SheetXAI combines a useful product, a strong development roadmap, and a founder who actively listens to customers. Five tacos from me.

questions.title: Detailed structure of credits on all plans
questions.comment:
Please guide us about the credits given in each plan offered in appsumo.
Also what is one time 5000 credit and what is access to Excel AI Agent

children.comment:
Hey!

The main difference between the plans is how many people can use SheetXAI:

Tier 1: 1 person
Tier 2: 3 people
Tier 3: 5 people
Tier 4: 25 people

Tier 1 is the basic version.

Tiers 2, 3, and 4 include all the extra features, including unlimited automations and the ability to build interactive mini-apps directly in Sheets.

With Tier 2 or above, you can generate content in cells, do bulk research, create bulk content, categorize data in bulk, upload documents, and automate workflows across your spreadsheet.

If you are familiar with Clay, this gives you the ability to do that same type of work directly in SheetXAI.

The license gives you access to SheetXAI for life, but the AI itself needs either your own API key or credits.

The 5,000-credit add-on is a one-time purchase, not monthly. You can assign it to one person, and they can use SheetXAI without setting up their own API key until the credits run out.

The Excel AI Agent is also a one-time add-on. It lets you use SheetXAI inside Excel too, not just Google Sheets.

TL;DR:

Get Tier 1 if it is just you and you mainly want help chatting with your spreadsheet, analyzing data, and automating basic spreadsheet work.

Get Tier 2 or above if you want automations, interactive mini-apps in Sheets, content generation, bulk research, bulk categorization, document uploads, or multiple people using it.

Get the one-time credits if you want the easiest, fastest way to start without setting up an API key. You can use SheetXAI right away after the credits are assigned.

These are not monthly credits and do not renew. Once they are used up, you can either buy more credits or add your own API key.

If you are already familiar with API keys and prefer to bring your own, you can do that instead from the start.

Get the Excel add-on if you want to use SheetXAI in Excel as well as Google Sheets.

Full guide:
https://www.sheetxai.com/help/appsumo-ltd-setup-guide

reviews.title: Not always usefull
reviews.comment:
I originally bought WizWrite to transcribe speech from videos, for example, on YouTube. When I speak directly into the microphone, WizWrite transcribes the text relatively accurately. However, recording speech from a distance, such as from a television, or recording a YouTube video played back through an external device, works very poorly. A large portion of the speech is either not recorded at all or transcribed completely incorrectly. If the recorded speech is also to be translated into another language, the translated text often bears no resemblance to the original, resulting in a complete loss of meaning. I get the same result when I upload a pure audio file from a video or podcast.

The automatic speaker detection doesn't work at all; everything is lumped together into an endless stream of gibberish.

So, for directly recorded speech that needs to be transcribed—which is what WizWrite is actually designed for—it's quite good, but unsuitable for other purposes.

So far I've connected:

- Google Sheets 
- Gmail 
- Google Analytics

Today, a large part of my business runs automatically because of Apix-Drive.

I'm genuinely grateful that I discovered this tool through AppSumo. It has saved me time, reduced manual work, and allowed me to automate processes that would otherwise cost much more through other platforms.

If you're on the fence: just try it. For me, this has been one of the most valuable AppSumo purchases I've ever made.

reviews.title: Plug-and-play automations — just wish it looked newer
reviews.comment:
Bought Tier 3 on AppSumo (May 2025) to replace a patchwork of Zapier + Make tasks. 
Wizard had my first flow (Hedy → Gmail → Notion) live in under 5 min—no docs needed. 

Why I’m keeping my code
	•	Zero learning curve: step-by-step builder makes even non-tech teammates look like automation pros. 
	•	Instant triggers—webhooks push data in seconds, not 15-min polls
	•	AI actions (ChatGPT, Claude) now let me enrich leads or draft replies mid-flow without extra tools.

Room for improvement
	•	Old-school UI: tiny dropdowns, no dark mode, and activity log feels 2016.

Verdict
ApiX-Drive nails the “set-it-and-forget-it” promise for real-time automations, earning 5 tacos. If you can live with a retro UI and a growing (but not yet exhaustive) connector list, snag a code before pricing climbs—your future self will thank you when Zapier invoices shrink.
