reviews.title: Four issues, but I'll keep the app.
reviews.comment:
After using this for a while, I came to a conclusion and I'm writing my review. The first thing that I don't like is that the prompt can only be called at the start of the chat. You cannot add a prompt in the middle of the chat or even at the end; you need to be at the start. This is something I would not expect from this app.

Second, the smart tags have a mind of their own. They include a few default tags that most of us won't even need, and they are extra in the workflow. If you add your own custom tags, the system might find a post that is two months old but will not find a post you have just written a few seconds ago. This is a second main hurdle.The way the search is organized, you don't know which chat is the earlier one or the later one. It would be advisable to add a date with that particular chat name to give a view of what date we are actually dealing with. 

The third issue is that when you make folders and refresh your page more often, the folders are not completely loaded and they miss their content. To get that working you need to refresh the page until you see all. This again is something that needs to be solved.

The fourth thing is that it needs a stronger PC. For example, my desktop PC is an i9, so it takes about 4 to 5 seconds to load. When I am on a slower laptop like an i3 or i5, it takes about 12 seconds to load. Imagine the pain when you have to spend 12 seconds just to browse in between.

The most important question, even besides all of this, is: will I keep this app? Yes, I will. Great things take time to build, and we have to support the developers for this purpose. That's why I'll keep this, and I hope these issues will be resolved and this will become one of the best apps. That's what I pray for it. I request the developers to please solve these issues.

children.comment:
First, thank you. This is the kind of review we actually learn from - specific, fair, and generous enough to stick with us while we improve. And thank you for keeping the app; that means a lot. Let me answer all four honestly, because you have earned a straight response.

1. Prompts only insert at the start. You are exactly right, and it is a real limitation, not your setup. Today inserting a prompt replaces the composer instead of dropping it in at your cursor, so it always ends up at the top. That is not the behavior we want either. Inserting at the caret (middle or end, keeping what you have already typed) is now on our fix list.

2. Smart Tags. Three fair points, three honest answers:

The default tags: you are right that a built-in set is forced on everyone. We are going to add a way to hide or turn off the built-in tags so they do not clutter your workflow.

A brand-new chat not being found while an old one is: this is a sync-timing issue. Smart Tags read from the extension's local copy of your history, and a chat written seconds ago has not been pulled in yet. We are working on making new chats index faster so this gap closes.

Dates in results: in the main Search you already get a date next to each chat, so ordering is visible there. You are correct that the Smart Tags results list does not show a date yet - we will add it there too so you always know which chat is earlier or later.

3. Folders not fully loading on refresh. Confirmed, and it is on us. On refresh the folder tree renders from a single fetch and can come back partial (and the chats inside can still be catching up), which is why repeated refreshes "complete" it. We are adding proper retry and quicker reconciliation so it fills in on the first load instead of making you refresh.

4. Load time on slower machines. This is real and we take it seriously. Most of that time is the first-load sync of your history plus some tag recomputation that currently runs more often than it should. We are moving that heavy work off the critical path and making the recompute far leaner, which should especially help i3/i5 machines like the one you described.

None of these are excuses - they are our to-do list, written down because you took the time to lay them out clearly. Thank you for the patience and for betting on us early. If you ever want to talk through any of it directly, we are at [email redacted].

reviews.title: Decent utility - shame about the UX (and all the different UIs).
reviews.comment:
The top 3 reasons to get this toolbox are:
1. Global Search
2. Tag-based search
3. Chat management

Top reason not to get this toolbox:
* Fragmentation

It feels like this was 4 different vibe-coded projects.  The clunky UI is completely different for each AI platform.  There is global search, but there are no global folders, no global tags, etc.  You have to recreate each one on every platform.

Not a lot of thought seems to have been put into how the user interacts with the features. Smart tags in chatgpt show up as a single line of tags in the sidebar.  
* Want to see your tags? You have to side scroll until you get to the right tag - wait - you scrolled too far - remember you can only see 1 or two tags at a time.  Scroll slower! ;)
* Want to search for your tag? Can't do it from the sidebar.

If you want smart-tag search, you have to click on the icon and then click on the smart-tags menu.  Then you get to a useful smart-tags interface.  But the order in which the ui components are presented is baffling.  Why are the statistics (Conversations, categories, tags) the first thing you see "above the fold" so to speak? Who cares about that stuff when you just want to interact with your tags?  It's noise. Put it at the bottom or as a tooltip.

If you select a chat or chats, there's no way to manually assign tags. You have to rely on the "smart" search system.

To be honest, all tag and folder functionality should just be rolled into the global search.  You should be able to manage every aspect from the search menu.  Adding different interfaces for each is very non-DRY and messes up the ux.  search for your chats, multi-select them, drag onto a tag, or hit a button to move them to a folder.

Not only does it feel like each AI platform has been vibe-coded separately, it feels like each and every _feature_ has been vibe-coded completely separately. 

It's one thing if you are vibe coding stuff for yourself, but when you go to sell the "system" for 60 dollars? That's a more challenging proposition and requires more engineering and UX discipline.

... all that said - the utilties are GENUINELY USEFUL.  Sure, you could get 2 or 3 free utilities on  the webstore and it would make a similar toolbox. But this toolbox puts many of the important ones in one place.

AI Toolbox has a ton of potential. The ideas are great. The utilities are good. It's just the user experience  that needs work. If I were the developer, I would stop chasing features.  Curtail the technical debt and code rot.  Instead,  work on cleaning house.  Minimize the number of clicks and scrolling. Minimize distracting noise on the screen. Don't force the user to move their eyes and mouse all over the screen. Bring similar functionality into one interface panel. Unify the code.  Unify the interface. 

TBH, it might almost be worth rewriting instead of refactoring. 

YAGNI + DRY -> Clean.

children.comment:
Thank you for this - genuinely the most actionable review we've received on any platform.

Here's the part worth knowing: most of what you asked for is already on our public roadmap at ai-toolbox.co/roadmap, written before this review - which we hope reads as agreement rather than coincidence:

1. "No global folders" - Cross-platform folders is in the "working on now" section: one folder holding chats from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok together.
2. "No global tags" - Cross-platform Smart Tags: tag rules written once, applied on every platform.
3. "Recreate everything per platform" - same section covers a cross-platform prompt library, so nothing is created twice.
4. The sidebar tag strip you (fairly) mocked for its scrolling - a wrap-into-rows setting is in "working on now" too.

One respectful correction on the "vibe-coded" read: we're two full-stack engineers with a combined 12+ years building SaaS products - one of us leads product and frontend architecture, the other backend architecture, algorithms, and LLM systems (more at ai-toolbox.co/about). The product runs on a shared core - one search engine, one export engine, one account-isolation layer - with thin adapters per platform. Where the UI differs between platforms, much of that is deliberate: each module lives inside a host page we don't control, and blending into each site beats imposing one foreign UI on four. Some of it is honest debt from reaching four platforms in a year - which is exactly what the unification work above is retiring. We have plenty to improve; engineering discipline isn't the missing piece.

Two things that already exist today, with the honest caveat that you not finding them is its own lesson for us: from global search you can multi-select results and, right from the bulk bar, move them to a folder or tag them - nearly the exact flow you sketched. And manual tags don't depend on the smart system: you can assign your own from Manage Chats and from search. Discoverability is on us.

Stats above the fold in the Smart Tags view: agreed, it's noise where it sits. It's moving.

If you're open to more of this, [email redacted] reaches the two of us directly. Feedback this specific shapes what ships.

reviews.title: A very useful and promising tool
reviews.comment:
I’ve been testing AI Toolbox for a few weeks now. After a lukewarm first impression—mainly because it wasn't immediately clear what it could do or how to launch it—I started finding it genuinely useful once I located the floating button.

My main use case so far is the cross-platform search across multiple AI tools, which currently feels like its most valuable feature. However, I plan to dive deeper into the rest of its capabilities, as I see a lot of untapped potential that I’m not fully exploiting yet.

On the downside, there are a few limitations that hold it back at the moment:

1. Indexing issues: Some platforms never finish indexing (ChatGPT in my case), making them unusable for cross-searching.

2. Web-only integration: It only integrates with the web versions of AI platforms, not their installed native apps. This is a bit of an annoyance—while it can be partially bypassed by saving Claude and ChatGPT as PWAs/web apps (Gemini already is), it's still far from ideal.

3. Lack of Perplexity integration: Perplexity is currently not supported.

I hope these limitations will be addressed in future updates. Overall, though, it’s a promising and great productivity tool.

children.comment:
Hi, thank you for such a thoughtful review - this is exactly the kind of feedback that shapes what we build next.

You're right about the first impression, and it's fair criticism. We've been improving onboarding, but "I didn't immediately get what it does or where to start" is something we still hear and still owe a better answer to. Noted, seriously.

On your three points:

ChatGPT indexing that never finishes: please email us at [email redacted] with roughly how many conversations your ChatGPT account has. On very large accounts, ChatGPT's own service can stop returning the oldest conversations, which can look exactly like indexing that never completes - we have fixes for related syncing issues in an update that's about to ship, and a workaround for the large-account limit is in active development. Your case would genuinely help us, and we'll get your account indexing properly.

Native apps: being a Chrome extension, AI Toolbox can only run where Chrome runs - browsers and, as you discovered, PWAs. The PWA route (installing ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini as a web app) is the right workaround, and the extension works fully inside them. Native desktop apps don't allow extensions to run inside them, so that boundary unfortunately isn't ours to remove.

Perplexity: it's on our ideas list, and we prioritize by demand - your request just moved it up. Grok was our fourth platform this year precisely because users kept asking, so this is a real path, not a polite deflection.

And you're right that there's more under the hood - since cross-platform search is your main use, folders with subfolders, Smart Tags, and bulk export as TXT/Markdown/JSON/PDF are probably the next things worth two minutes of your time.

Thanks again for the detailed writeup. Email us about that ChatGPT indexing - we want your account working end to end.

questions.title: Question
questions.comment: Hi, could we, when we pull up manage chats, have the conversation we are on and clicked your widget on be at the top and highlighted? Also, did you say that when I do an export, it gets sent to your servers?

children.comment: I forgot to mention: for users like me who turn off indexing, can we add an Index now button somewhere in Manage Chats so our convo appears?

Right now Manage Chats doesn't single out the conversation you opened it from, and showing that chat at the top and highlighted would make it a lot quicker to find. We've added it to our feature requests.

On exports, only PDF goes through our server:

- TXT, Markdown and JSON exports are created entirely in your browser. Nothing is sent to us.
- PDF exports send the text of the conversation to our server, which builds the PDF and sends the file back to you. The conversation is held only in the server's memory while that happens. It is never saved to a database, to disk or to our logs, and it's gone once your file has been delivered.

If you'd prefer nothing to leave your computer, the TXT, Markdown or JSON exports are a good choice.

questions.title: Theft
questions.comment: How do I know this doesn't let you steal my ideas, chat and artifacts? Does it run offline?

children.comment:
Good question to ask before installing anything that can see your chats, so here is exactly what happens.

AI Toolbox has to read your chats to search them, file them and export them, but that reading happens in your own browser, and your conversations and Claude artifacts are stored on your computer, not on our servers. Search and Text, Markdown and JSON exports are all done locally.

What our server does see is limited and listed in our privacy policy: your folder names and which chats are filed in them (not the chats themselves), your saved prompts (unless you choose to keep them on your device in Settings), and a short preview of any message you bookmark. Three features send one conversation you pick, only when you use them: PDF export, summarizing a long chat with @@, and carrying a chat into a new one. That conversation is processed and discarded, never stored or logged.

On offline: the AI sites themselves need an internet connection, so AI Toolbox does too, but the work on your chats runs on your machine rather than ours. The full details are at ai-toolbox.co/privacy-policy, and you can remove the extension at any time, which deletes everything it stored in your browser.

reviews.title: My Honest Kortex Review: Great for Research, Better for Content Workflow
reviews.comment:
I’ve been using Kortex mainly to move my AI research into NotebookLM faster, and overall I’d say it’s one of those tools that feels incredibly useful once it clicks. 

If you want a quick walkthrough before trying it, watch this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mrrbh1QrGBU

The biggest win for me is how easy it is to grab conversations from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and web pages without the usual copy-paste mess.

That alone saves a lot of time. I also really like the podcast feed feature because it turns research into something I can listen to later, which is surprisingly practical.

That said, it hasn’t been perfect. Looking through user feedback, the main complaints were reliability issues early on, especially around notebooks not loading properly or things feeling buggy. 

A few people also called out PDF export formatting and the extra Kortex branding in exports as frustrating. So it’s definitely not a flawless product.

Still, what gives me confidence is that the founder has been very active in responding, fixing issues, and shipping updates. That matters a lot with a tool like this. 

If you use NotebookLM seriously and want a faster way to collect AI chats, notes, and sources in one place, Kortex is genuinely promising and already very useful — just with a few rough edges that seem to be improving over time.

reviews.title: Three important fixes that need to be done
reviews.comment:
The extension is working, but a few key issues remain:

Brief Placement: "Generate Brief" claims to save to Notes, but briefs end up in Artifacts instead.

PDF Formatting Bug: Bold text exports as raw stars (**) in PDFs instead of actual bold text.

Branding Removal: Paid users should be able to disable the "Made with Kortex" footer label on exported PDFs.

Currently, the raw markdown stars and forced branding make exported PDFs unshareable without manual editing. Please fix the PDF formatting and add an option to remove branding.

There are other similar extensions just don't have these issues.

reviews.title: Good and Valuable Tool
reviews.comment:

This has always been a headache as GN made it difficult to go through every notebook to see what had generated. That problem is now gone.

So, I'd advise that that part of this description be eliminated. I did find a good one to utilize it through, however. Pocketcasts seems to work flawlessly.

reviews.title: Finally, the missing knowledge management layer for NotebookLM
reviews.comment:
I love NotebookLM, but what always frustrated me was the lack of organization—no folders, no real structure, and no easy way to manage multiple notebooks. Kortex solves that problem and takes the NotebookLM experience to a whole new level.
The second reason I bought it was knowledge management. I use Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini every day, and over time I've built a huge library of valuable AI conversations. Finding and organizing them later was always a challenge. Now I export my most valuable chats to NotebookLM, and with Kortex I can organize them by topic and quickly find the information I need.
For me, Kortex doesn't replace NotebookLM—it unlocks its full potential by making knowledge truly organized.
Highly recommended for anyone who uses NotebookLM as a serious knowledge management tool.

reviews.title: Not as simple or always straight forward, but has potential
reviews.comment:
I've never had to use an AI API key before, but i was having a really hard time setting this up to get it to work. 

I wanted to use a free/low cost API key as I tested this out, so i figured google gemini. I encountered error after error, and was even having the gemini web app attempt to help me in another tab. The chat also didn't work well with the free model through openrouter (eventually gemini 3.5 worked alright).

In my process of trying to get gemini to work through openrouter, imagine my surprise when i saw that my short chat messages just testing whether things were working were eating away at my small credit balance on Openrouter (and were calling claude 4.5 through Amazon Bedrock and pi). 

I can fully recognize that perhaps someone well-versed in AI api keys and doesn't mind paying up for their LLMs might have had an easier time than me setting up, but this was not a simple ready to build stuff in 90 seconds for me. 
I spent nearly 100 credits trying to make sure that everything was going through the LLM that I wanted through chat, but also a lot of the chats would fail for one reason or another. 

Eventually, I finally, finally was ready to build something and my agent told me it built a feature/automation/crm thing based on my prompt but it wasn't under apps anywhere. The agent was trying to help me find where it put the app, but it was possibly referring from an older gui design? Idk, for something that claims to be really simple, this made me feel quite dumb. 

I did put a ticket in so we'll see what happens, but since everyone is claiming how easy and seamless everything seems to be I feel like I should add a bit of contrast. 

To be fair, if this does work as intended,  this sounds like a cool tool to have. I feel like Tier 2 (for small use-cases) and Tier 3 make the most sense, and I might upgrade to Tier 3, but I'm still not sure about it overall.

children.comment:
Julia, thank you for this. Feeling lost in a tool that promises “simple” is the exact opposite of what we’re building, and I’d rather hear it from you now than have you quietly walk away.

Why API keys, and why that’s changing

A lifetime deal can’t include unlimited AI usage forever without quietly becoming a subscription. With your own key, you pay your provider directly, we never add a markup, and the deal stays truly lifetime.

But you’ve shown me the other side of it: for someone who just wants to build, a key is a wall before you’ve even started.

So here’s what we’re working on: top up and go. You add a small balance, say $5, and your agent uses Claude, Gemini or GPT straight away. No key, no provider accounts, no monthly plan. You pay a few cents per message, with a spending limit so nothing runs away from you. Your own keys will still work for anyone who prefers them.

The rest is on us

The credits you spent just testing and the app the agent sent you looking for are our mistakes, and I’d like to fix both with you directly.

Can we get on a call?

Email me at [email redacted] and I’ll set up a call. We’ll look at your setup together and get your first agent doing something useful for you. If it still doesn’t click after that, I’ll understand. But I’d love the chance to show you what it’s meant to feel like.

reviews.title: A real proposal agent running in one evening
reviews.comment:
I started on Tier 3 and moved up to Tier 5 after a few tests. In one evening I built an MVP: a custom skill with Python scripts that generates sales proposals as PowerPoint files. You request it via Telegram, the agent asks for missing data, builds the deck, sends it back to the chat, and emails me a control copy with the file attached. It worked better than I expected.

Things worth knowing:

Skill uploads have a size limit (a 7 MB ZIP was rejected, 2.7 MB was fine), so keep large files compressed.
In my tests, Telegram didn’t pass files I sent to the agent, so I forward them to the agent’s Gmail instead. Sending files from the agent works using the Bot API.
Secrets must be declared in the skill’s Credentials, or the scripts won’t receive them.

No servers, no Docker, and support answers fast. Excited to see what comes next.

children.comment:
This is incredible. A proposal agent that takes a Telegram request, asks for what’s missing, builds the PowerPoint and emails you a control copy, all in one evening. We built the skill system hoping someone would do exactly this, and you did it on day one.

Tier 3 to Tier 5 after a few tests? Best compliment we could get :)

And thank you for the notes. The 3 MB skill upload limit is a known one, and we’re raising it to 10 MB. The Credentials requirement is going into the docs this week. 

If you ever want to share that skill with the community, we’d love to feature it. Watch this space.

reviews.title: A Promising Tool for Turning Lectures and Academic Discussions into Structured Knowledge
reviews.comment:
As a university lecturer and school teacher, I see real potential in Prismical beyond its usual role as a meeting-notes tool. It can become valuable for students, teachers, and researchers, particularly for recording lectures, academic discussions, and seminars, then turning them into structured text that can be reviewed and used later.

What I appreciate about Prismical is its privacy-oriented approach and technical flexibility. The option to transcribe locally with Whisper, rather than relying entirely on the cloud, is especially valuable in a university context. Recordings may contain research discussions, student data, or sensitive information that should not leave the institution. The ability to work without a bot joining the meeting is also a practical and professional advantage, especially in lectures and academic meetings where participants may not want external tools to appear in the session.

I also see clear value in live transcription, speaker identification, and summaries that extract key points, decisions, and action items, as well as MCP support and integration with AI tools. These functions can help a faculty member quickly return to an earlier discussion, prepare an initial meeting summary, or organize voice-recorded research ideas. For students, a recording can become a useful starting point for revision instead of relying on scattered notes or replaying an entire long lecture.

From an educational perspective, however, the current summary templates appear closer to the business-meeting model: decisions, action items, and next steps. This is useful, but it is not enough for lectures. I would love to see dedicated academic and educational templates, including learning objectives, new concepts and terminology, key definitions, examples, questions raised during the lecture, revision questions, suggested references, and points that require clarification. It would also be extremely helpful to generate flashcards, short questions, or a quick quiz directly from a lecture summary.

My most important observation concerns Arabic-language support. It is good that Arabic is available as a transcription language, and I will test this more deeply in real use. However, simply selecting Arabic for transcription is not sufficient to create an appropriate experience for Arabic-speaking users. The application needs native and complete RTL support across the interface, transcripts, summaries, editor, and exports: correct right-aligned Arabic text, a natural reading direction, punctuation appearing in the correct position, proper display when Arabic is mixed with English or German, and clear, comfortable fonts for Arabic text. These are not merely visual refinements; they directly affect whether text can be read, reviewed, and used effectively in education.

I would also encourage the team to test Arabic transcription across a range of dialects, especially Modern Standard Arabic used in lectures, as well as foreign names and academic terminology. It would be very useful if users could select the summary language independently from the recording language. A lecture may be delivered in Arabic while the student or researcher needs a summary in German or English, or the other way around.

Compared with Voicenotes, Prismical appears stronger in privacy, local transcription, and its no-bot approach to meetings—advantages that matter greatly in universities. However, Voicenotes offers quick PDF export. I therefore hope Prismical will develop professional Word and PDF export in print-ready formats, because teachers often need to turn lecture content into worksheets, summaries, or materials that can be shared with students.

One positive point that deserves mention is that the Prismical developer is very open to feedback and professional and easy to communicate with. In my communication with the team, I found a genuine willingness to listen to users’ needs—especially educational and academic needs—and to engage seriously with suggestions. The team does not merely receive feedback; it shows a clear interest in considering it and working on it as part of the product’s development. For me, as an educator, this is very important, because successful educational tools are not built only on strong technical features, but also on a team that understands real-life use cases and responds to them continuously.

My first impression is very positive: Prismical is not just another voice recorder, but a promising project that could become an excellent tool for education and academic research if the team invests in genuinely educational templates, practical academic export options, and native right-to-left Arabic support. I will continue testing it in real teaching contexts, especially in Arabic and German, and I look forward to sharing more detailed feedback with the team.

reviews.title: Meeting notes without the bot
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Prismical got my attention for a very convenient reason: it can take meeting notes without putting another bot in the call.

It records the audio already playing on your computer, along with your mic, so it can work with calls, lectures, demos, interviews, and voice notes. Prismical does not join the call as a visible meeting participant, so the other people do not see a bot, get a bot notification, or have the call feel like it is being monitored by another attendee.

In my test, Prismical gave me a live transcript with speaker labels, then turned the recording into a summary, decisions, and action items accurately. This is what makes it unique for me: useful notes after the meeting without making the meeting itself awkward.

The local first setup is another big reason I like it. Prismical can transcribe locally with Whisper, supports local models and BYOK, and lets you choose when to use cloud providers. For client calls, internal discussions, interviews, or anything sensitive, I like having that control.

It is also built for people who already use AI in their workflow. MCP, API, webhooks, and integrations are part of the product, so your notes can connect to tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Obsidian, Notion, Zapier, n8n, Make, Activepieces, or custom workflows.

During my early test, I ran into a few issues around integrations, model availability, and app version confusion. The team pointed me to the newer build, and I retested using a newer version from the correct download page. The MCP OAuth redirect worked properly with Notion, Gemini had been added, the previously coming soon model options were cleaned up, and Zapier, n8n, Activepieces, Make, and Notion integrations were available. Slack, Linear, HubSpot, and Attio were still listed as coming soon.

Overall, Prismical is worth considering if you spend a lot of time in meetings and want notes without inviting a bot to every call. Its best fit is someone who cares about privacy, local transcription, and AI workflow hooks, and is comfortable with a product that is moving quickly.

reviews.title: The “Goldilocks” of Data Viz: Powerful, Fast, and UI-Focused
reviews.comment:
If you’ve ever felt like Excel is too basic but Power BI is a full-time job just to learn, InstaCharts is your new best friend. It occupies that perfect middle ground where professional design meets extreme ease of use.

The Sharing Controls are “Fab” This is a huge standout for me. When you share a chart via a public link or iFrame embed, you aren't just dumping data. You have granular control:

Privacy & Scope: You choose if the end-user sees just the chart or the underlying data table too.

Look & Feel: You can lock down the aesthetic so it matches your brand perfectly, keeping your reports looking cohesive and high-end.

UI/UX & Founder Support The interface is a breath of fresh air—clean, snappy, and zero clutter. But what really seals the deal is the human element. The founder, Bart, is incredibly active and actually listens. It’s rare to buy a tool where you feel like your feedback could literally shape the next update.

The "BI Tool" Reality Check Is this a replacement for a £100/mo enterprise BI tool? Not yet. It’s missing a few "big league" components like:
- API-driven data collection (for pulling live app data automatically).
- Advanced Dashboards with multi-chart drill-down capabilities.
- Complex Team Permissions for large-scale orgs.

But here’s the kicker: If it had those features, would it be on a Lifetime Deal for this price? Absolutely not. You’d be paying a monthly subscription that would make your eyes water.

The Verdict: For 90% of business owners, marketers, and researchers, InstaCharts does exactly what you need it to do: it makes data look beautiful, instantly. It’s a "speed-to-insight" tool that pays for itself in saved time within the first day!

questions.title: Once we embed the charts on our website, will readers have the option to apply filters and explore the data?

children.comment:
Hello! Thanks for reaching out and asking a question. I've broken out the answer into two parts:

 1. Will readers be apply to apply filters to an embedded chart?  
If the reader opens the embed into a full view window, they will see the share screen. If "Show Editor Controls" is on for the share, the users will be able to fully "edit" the chart, including setting filters. https://instacharts.io/docs/guides/share-chart/#show-editor-controls  So readers can apply filters in the full share view but not the embedded view.

 2. Will readers be able to view the data of an embedded chart? 
 Yes. On the share settings page, make sure "Show Embed Toolbar" is on, and select at least one data view under included views (plotted data or full dataset). A toolbar will appear at the bottom of the embed, and the reader will be able to switch between the chart view and the data views that are included) https://instacharts.io/docs/guides/share-chart/#share-settings

I hope this helps to answer your question!
Bart

I'm frustrated that a lot of tools that come to appsumo lately don't support Windows, which blows my mind considering windows/nvidia is leading that race and can handle larger LLMs for AI infrastructure.

The layout is different from the default Android keyboard, so it will take a little bit of muscle memory unless they could examine the Samsung keyboard and make layout options to switch to. The question key comes on the Samsung KB by default as a standalone button; it doesn't in Acti, so it's one extra step to use a very common question mark. All of the common symbol keys you would use, such as @, %, $, ', ", #, and! etc are all inside a button that you hold down, whereas on the Samsung KB, they are all visible on your main keyboard to hold down and click as a secondary key. 

I communicate in GIFs and emojis; I was glad to see the AI skill for being able to analyze our text and pick a relevant GIF. The problem is you can't see the GIF until you send it. That's a big trust to an AI that might misread a typo and send your girlfriend a GIF of a big sausage by accident, and nobody wants to see that. It makes me wonder what GIF it would choose if I used a bad word in my text. So I'd like to see some sort of preview for GIFs, as well as other GIF options if I don't like the one it picked- maybe a retry button or a GIF gallery. 

The Acti keyboard on my Samsung Galaxy S26 could use some improvement in visuals. The keys don't have much effect on them to look like real buttons. Looking forward to the Windows app so I can see what this tool is really made of, but even without it currently, it seems like I'll get good use out of it.

reviews.title: AI that follows you wherever you type
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What stood out in Acti is that the AI is built into the keyboard itself. I don't have to leave the app I'm using, open a chatbot, ask for something, copy the answer, and then come back.

I tested it on iOS in Gmail, Notes and Messenger, and it worked as advertised. I could use the main action from the space bar, and I also assigned a specific action to a letter key and triggered it directly from the keyboard.

This is what differentiates Acti from a normal AI keyboard. It can help with writing, dictation and translation, but the bigger idea is turning any text field into a place where you can ask a question or run an action without leaving the app you're already in. Just imagine how much time this could save.

I'm finding that there are a surprising number of little app switches throughout the day that add up. You're chatting with someone and need to look up an address. Someone makes a claim and you want to check it before replying. You need a quick answer or a bit of research while writing an email. Normally that means leaving the conversation, opening another app or AI tool, finding the answer, and coming back. Being able to do those things from the keyboard saves more time than I expected.

You can also create your own Acts by describing what you want in plain language. Act Builder Agent can turn that into a reusable workflow, and you can refine it through conversation until it does what you want. There are also thousands of existing Acts you can add and personalize instead of making everything yourself.

Acti can connect those Acts to apps and APIs too, so they can do more than manipulate the text in front of you. The current deal includes connections across 300+ apps and APIs, with integrations such as Gmail, Slack, Notion and custom APIs.

One thing to understand about the credits is that normal voice dictation does not use them. AI actions and workflows do, with basic workflows currently using one credit per execution. The monthly credits reset rather than rolling over, and BYOK is not currently available.

For me, the biggest advantage is still where Acti is located. The keyboard is already there in almost every app I use on my phone, so the AI comes to me instead of making me change apps every time I need it.

One drawback I've run into is that the keyboard can occasionally feel less responsive, especially when I'm typing quickly. It isn't constant, and it hasn't stopped me from using Acti, but there are moments when it feels a little sluggish compared with the standard iPhone keyboard.

I've actually kept Acti on my iPhone since the original test and I still use it. The more I use it, the more I notice how much time is normally wasted jumping between apps for small questions and tasks that can now happen right where I'm already typing.

children.comment:
AbeChallah, thank you for such a thoughtful and thorough review! It means a lot to me and the team.

You’ve captured what makes Acti special: it brings AI right to where you’re typing. What takes this further is being able to call up AI with instructions and workflows you’ve already set up. Our editor lets you create your own Acts in plain language, customize them around your needs, and share them with the community. We’re excited to keep expanding this, with plans to support private APIs and even connections to your own agents.

Our next focus is making Acti more proactive, so it can offer relevant AI help at the moment you need it. Getting this right is challenging, but I believe it’s a big part of the future of agentic keyboards.

I also want to highlight the everyday typing experience. From what I’ve seen, many AI keyboards still fall short as keyboards you can comfortably use throughout the day. We’ve worked hard to make Acti a capable everyday keyboard, alongside everything it offers through AI. There’s still a small gap to close with the native iOS keyboard, and we’re working hard on those remaining improvements.

I believe our voice typing is also top tier and already very close to Wispr Flow in quality. We offer it free to everyone on mobile, and I’d encourage you to try them side by side and let us know what you think.

And here’s a fun little feature to try: dictation with emoji! Just speak, and Acti can automatically pick emojis that fit what you’re saying and add them to your text. It’s a small touch that makes everyday messages more expressive.

Thanks again for your support. I’d love to hear more of your feedback as you explore Acti!

reviews.title: More Than Another AI Chatbot — A Promising AI Workspace for Business Owners
reviews.comment:
What initially attracted me to WorkLLM was the idea of having more than just another AI chatbot. As a business owner building Creators Academy, I'm always looking for practical ways to bring AI research, content creation, business knowledge, and automation together without constantly switching between different platforms.

WorkLLM caught my attention because it approaches AI as a complete business workspace rather than simply offering access to different language models.

**What I Like**

One of the biggest strengths is the five-layer memory system. Having organizational, personal, project, folder, and conversation memory creates a foundation for keeping business knowledge organized and accessible. This is especially valuable when managing multiple projects that need consistent context.

Access to 200+ AI models is another major advantage. The ability to choose and compare models for different tasks offers flexibility without being tied to one AI provider.

I also appreciate the support for BYOK, MCP, and integrations with popular business applications. These capabilities give WorkLLM the potential to work alongside existing software rather than requiring businesses to replace everything they already use.

The workspace setup was straightforward. I was able to establish my business identity, upload branding, configure my administrator profile, and access the workspace without unnecessary complications. The interface is organized, with dedicated areas for AI chat, memory, integrations, agents, administration, and usage reporting.

Another feature I appreciate is the visibility into credit consumption. Having reports that break down usage by model, provider, and task is important for managing AI expenses.

**What Really Stands Out**

What impressed me most was the founder's communication.

I asked a detailed question about whether WorkLLM could eventually replace platforms such as Genspark AI for digital-product research, multi-agent workflows, browser automation, and product creation.

Rather than giving a generic marketing response, Dhimant addressed each capability individually, clearly explaining what WorkLLM supports and where its limitations are.

He also shared details about Agent 2.0, including multi-agent orchestration, reusable workflows, scheduling, event-based triggers, and approval checkpoints.

I particularly appreciate that he was transparent about browser automation and full application deployment not being supported. That kind of clarity helps customers make informed decisions.

**Where I'd Like to See WorkLLM Grow**

I'd love to see WorkLLM continue developing toward more complete, end-to-end business automation.

reviews.title: A Multi-Model AI Workspace With Real Value for Education
reviews.comment:
As a teacher and university lecturer in language education , I purchased WorkLLM and have used it daily for lesson preparation, worksheets, and research. Here is my assessment from an educational perspective.

Key strengths:

- Model comparison: over 200 models in one place, with the option to send the same prompt to four models at once.

- Chatting with files: I uploaded lengthy PDFs (including a roughly 90-page curriculum document) and extracted summaries, exam questions, and differentiated worksheets with high accuracy. Here WorkLLM clearly outperforms WritingMate, whose "chat with files" feature is very poor — it struggles with large files and loses track of details.

- The five-tier organization memory and shared threads: I stored my templates and curriculum standards, so outputs now stay consistent with my style, and colleagues can build on each other's work.

For Arabic-speaking users: the experience is positive overall. The app fully supports right-to-left writing, and the developer is extremely cooperative on this topic and listens to feedback remarkably well. Arabic quality depends on the model chosen, and the comparison feature helped me identify which model writes the most polished Modern Standard Arabic. The only remaining flaw is export: it does not yet work well, and the font in exported PDFs is unfortunately poor — but given the developer's responsiveness, I expect this to improve.

My suggestions: improve export to Word and PDF (top priority), ready-made educational agents (lesson plans, quizzes with answer keys), LMS integration. I also hope an iPhone and Android app is released soon — that would greatly enrich the user experience and make it possible to keep working on the go.

Conclusion: WorkLLM is a fully fledged collaborative workspace, not just another AI chat app. worth every penny you pay for it!

And it means a lot that organization memory and shared threads are actually helping keep consistency across your work and your colleagues' work, that was very deliberately designed for exactly this kind of collaborative, ongoing use.

Thank you also for the honest breakdown on Arabic and RTL support, glad the writing quality comparison across models has been genuinely useful for finding the best fit for Modern Standard Arabic. And you're right to flag export quality, especially PDF fonts, as the current weak spot, that's a fair callout and something we're actively working to improve.

Your suggestions are noted, ready-made educational agents, LMS integration, and mobile apps are all things we're thinking seriously about, and feedback like yours from someone actually using this in a classroom setting genuinely shapes where we prioritize next.

questions.title: Is Coding and File work capability envisioned?
questions.comment:
Hi, 

I am contemplating on getting this product but still a few questions:

1) In my work I use a mix of chat, but also heavily rely on coding capabilities of Claude code and Codex. Do you plan on extending the tool so it can directly work on code-bases and folders or that was never the plan? 

2) One way to get a combination of chat but also coding ability would be to allow calling models available in WorkLLM through API, and then use OpenCode or other harness, while using the credits in WorkLLM. Is that a functionality that could be supported?

3) I haven't bought WorkLLM and thus not tested it. Does "the work" run in the cloud, or do I need to have my computer running for it to perform work. If it is in cloud, what are the space, bandwidth and compute limitations?

4) Do you add all newer models from big providers (Astra, Fable?)

children.comment:
Hi,

Thank you for your questions, and for considering WorkLLM. I will answer each one clearly, so you can decide with confidence.

1) Do you plan on extending the tool so it can directly work on code-bases and folders? & 2) Could models be called through an API, so you can use a harness like OpenCode with your WorkLLM credits?

I will answer these two together, because the answer comes from the same idea. WorkLLM includes strong coding models, so you can write, review, and edit code in your workspace, and you can import code to work on it. It is not a professional coding tool, though, and it does not work directly on code-bases and folders the way Claude Code or Codex do. Replacing those tools is not part of our roadmap, and we do not plan it in the near or long term.

Our purpose is different. We want to raise the productivity of general users who do not want to learn technical skills or build technical workflows. They simply describe what they need in plain English, and an agent gets ready. This is our whole vision, and it is how we want to operate. So if coding is your core need, and you rely on tools like Claude Code and Codex, I would recommend keeping them. WorkLLM is a good companion to them, and it does not replace them. For the same reason, we are not building WorkLLM as a coding backend for other harnesses.

3) Does the work run in the cloud, or do I need my computer running? What are the space, bandwidth, and compute limits?

WorkLLM is a web app that runs in the cloud, and it does not work offline. When you create an agent with a simple prompt in English, with a time-based or app-based trigger, the agent does all of the job in the cloud. You do not need your computer to be running. Right now, there are no space, bandwidth, or compute limits for you to manage. It works well for all of the customers we have today.

4) Do you add all newer models from big providers?

Yes. We add the new models directly from their original providers. All of them are zero data retention (ZDR) compliant, so your data is not kept by the model providers.

What WorkLLM is designed for

WorkLLM is designed to improve your productivity across your daily work. For example, along with your coding work, you could create an agent that checks your Jira tickets and updates them, and automate other workflows like this one. You can also keep one Organization Memory, where the AI remembers your company’s work, brand guidelines, and templates. It then gives every employee in the workspace the same standard answers. You also get 200+ models in one place, so your team does not need to buy individual subscriptions. They can use all of them and automate their daily workflows. This is the main design and use of WorkLLM.

If you have any other questions, please ask here, and I will be happy to help.

Dhimant

Great answer and thanks for that.
Since AI credit is included in the Tiers, would it be a big ask to be able to use the same AI credits over API calls? I mean I would not be using more credits, and it would solve my coding issue since standard models like Sol, Opus already code really well with any harness. Then I would have a "one product for all work" type of scenario.

Other questions I hope is okay:

- Can you interactively write and work on a document, file, slide-deck directly inside WorkLLM with collaboration from AI models. Similar to big-name LLM models allow a working Canvas or notebook?

- Reasoning for Opus, Sol etc. is adjustable to same levels as provider allow?

- For WorkLLM custom agents, can you select the model yourself (Haiku, Opus, Sol).

Thank you. Today you cannot call WorkLLM models through an API or an MCP server. We are working on it, and it is prioritized. ETA: approx 1 month but not confirmed yet. When it is available, it will use the same credits you have in your workspace, so you would not need to buy anything extra. I hope that answers your first question.

A canvas-style editor is on our roadmap, but it is not prioritized yet, and I will let you know here when we prioritize it. What you can do today is share a chat thread, so several people can work with AI together in the same thread. They can ask the AI to update the same document (generated in chat thread) as you go, right from the chat.

you can adjust the reasoning level for every model that offers it, including Opus and Sol, the same way the provider allows. WorkLLM has 200+ models, and not all of them offer detailed reasoning. For the models that do, you can choose the level that fits your task, such as Low, Medium, or High, so you can balance quality and credits.

Yes, you can choose the model for your agents. You can even do it for each step of the agent. For example, if one step does detailed research, you can pick a strong model for only that step, and use a lighter model for the other steps. This helps you get good results and keep credit use low. You can also use your own BYOK model for any step.

questions.title: Few Questions
questions.comment:
1. Can you please confirm if we can build nodejs site and it can connect to github and connect to VPS via SSH.
2. Can it connect to web and do live research?
3. Can you connect it to image/video generation models via API and automate the process?

children.comment:
Hi,

Thank you for your questions, and for considering WorkLLM. I am happy to go through each one.

Can you please confirm if we can build nodejs site and it can connect to github and connect to VPS via SSH?

You can work on a Node.js site in WorkLLM. We have strong coding models, so you can create, edit, and review Node.js and HTML code right in your workspace. You can also connect to GitHub and work on your repositories from your workspace. However, WorkLLM is an AI workspace, and it is not a platform like Lovable. Everything happens in your workspace, and nothing is hosted or run on the server side. You take the code and deploy it with your own hosting and tools.

Can it connect to web and do live research?

Yes, of course. WorkLLM can search the web and do live research for you. You can also point it to specific websites and ask it to research them. This works well for market research, competitor checks, and keeping up with the latest information.

Can you connect it to image/video generation models via API and automate the process?

For images, yes. WorkLLM has image models built in, with full capabilities for creating, editing, and modifying images. You can also connect your own image models through BYOK, and these are fully supported. With our new Agent 2.0, you can then automate image tasks too.

For video, WorkLLM natively can understand video content. At this stage, it does not create, edit, or modify videos, and it does not stream video. This means video generation models are not supported through BYOK as well for now.

If you tell me more about what you would like to build, I will be happy to suggest the best setup for you. Please feel free to ask any other questions here.

Best,
Dhimant

questions.title: Can WorkLLM help me in my website design and development business.
questions.comment: I design and develop websites for my clients. Can I create an AI agent in WorkLLM, which can help me in my website design and development workflow?

children.comment:
Hi,

Thank you for your question. Yes, WorkLLM can help with your website design and development business, and you can build agents for many parts of your workflow.

Let me start with design. WorkLLM can create website mockups, page layouts, and interactive, clickable prototypes in HTML, so your clients can see and click through an idea before you build it. You can refine the design with the AI, step by step, by describing what you want to change. It can also write the page copy and generate images for the design. You can export your work as HTML, PDF, Word, or PPT, so it is easy to share with a client or hand over to your developer. WorkLLM is not a development tool like Lovable, so it does not build and deploy full websites or apps. Mockups, designs, and prototypes are where it works best.

With our new Agent 2.0, you can describe a task in plain English, and WorkLLM creates an agent with the steps. For example, you could set up an agent that starts when a new client inquiry arrives by email. It reads the request, researches the client’s business, and prepares a draft reply and a first proposal outline for you to review. Another agent could prepare a weekly project update for each client and send it by email every Friday. You can also build agents for page content, review checklists, and client onboarding tasks. Agents can run on a schedule or when an event happens, and each step can use a different model from our 200+ models.

Memory and projects can help you keep each client organized. You can create a separate project for each client, and keep their brand guidelines, content, and requirements in that project’s memory. The AI then always has that client’s context, so you do not need to explain it again each time, and one client’s information stays apart from another’s. You can also store your own standards and templates in Organization Memory, so every project follows the way you work.

To set expectations clearly, WorkLLM can help you plan, write, design, and prototype, but it does not replace your coding tools. Most developers use it alongside them, for the planning, content, and client communication around the build.

If you tell me more about your workflow, I will be happy to suggest a good first agent for you. I can also show you a quick demo with your own use case.

Dhimant

questions.title: A couple of questions for you
questions.comment: On AppSumo Tier 2, can I build and sell tools to my consulting clients under my brand? Which tier is needed for (1) custom domain, (2) giving each client their own workspace or sub-account, and (3) unlimited knowledge bases?

children.comment:
Hi there, 

Yes, on Tier 2 you can build tools and sell them to your clients under your own brand. Every tier includes branded portals with your own theming, end-user login, built-in checkout with your own pricing tiers, and per-user credit allowances.

On your three points:
Custom domain: custom domains come with whitelabeling. Tier 3 and Tier 4 include whitelabeling (no "Powered by FormWise" badge) and up to 2 connected custom domains. On Tier 1 and Tier 2, whitelabeling is a $49/mo in app add-on, which also includes 2 custom domains.

A space for each client: on any tier, you can give each client their own login to your portal, and each client gets their own private knowledge base that other clients can't see. If you run GoHighLevel, Tier 3 and Tier 4 also include our GHL integration, which syncs your GHL sub-accounts. A fully separate FormWise workspace per client is a separate account with its own plan, so it isn't covered by a single AppSumo license.

Unlimited knowledge bases: Tier 4 only. Tier 2 includes 3 and Tier 3 includes 10.

For branded client work with a custom domain, Tier 3 is the minimum. If you want unlimited knowledge bases (plus advanced gating such as allowed email domains and IP restrictions for your portals), Tier 4 is the best fit.

questions.title: Can you guarantee no bait and switch like Pickaxe?
questions.comment:
Your listing positions this as an alternative to Pickaxe.co, which launched on AppSumo a few years ago and later significantly cut back the value of its lifetime plans for existing customers (https://appsumo.com/products/pickaxe/).

What assurance can you give that the same won’t happen here? Specifically, will the tiers and future updates keep equal or greater value over time? Many of us bought into Pickaxe, only to find a year later that our paid plans were effectively no better than the free tier...

children.comment:
Totally fair question, and thanks for asking it directly. We'd rather be upfront about how this deal works than have anyone surprised a year from now.

Lifetime deals usually go wrong when a company sells unlimited or monthly-refreshing AI usage for a one-time price. AI models cost real money every time they run, so that promise eventually stops adding up, and the company ends up cutting plans it already sold. We built our AppSumo tiers specifically to avoid that.

Here's how it works:

- Your credits are a one-time lifetime allotment, not a monthly refresh. You get your tier's full credit balance up front, and it's yours to use at your own pace. We tell you that clearly now so we never have to change it later.
- Platform access is lifetime. Building agents and flows, your knowledgebases, Suites, portals, and the features and limits included in your tier stay with your license.
- On Tier 2 and above, you can bring your own API key. When you run on your own key, the model costs go to your provider account and not to your FormWise credits, so you can keep running after your allotment is spent.
- AppSumo tiers are their own plans. They're defined separately from our monthly plans, so changes to monthly pricing don't change your license. Since launch we've added to the AppSumo tiers (the MCP server is now included on every tier) rather than taking anything away.

We were very deliberate about how we designed our plans and specifically chose the current offer we have today because it is sustainable for us to continue providing long-term. Thank you for the question!
Great answer, thanks!

Lots are very similar. Some offer something different. Hello Aria is one of those, and it’s very, very close to what I need.

I particularly like getting reminders through WhatsApp. It’s something I already use throughout the day, so having reminders appear there makes sense for me. An organisation tool has a better chance if I actually remember to look at it!

There are still a few things missing that I’d normally expect, such as subtasks. Sometimes “sort the garage" is several steps, and I’d like to tick those off as I go.

I’d also like more control over the order of tasks and task lists. Certain things belong in my morning routine, and being able to rearrange them would make it easier to see what’s next.

I fed these suggestions back and received very quick responses. The team understood exactly what I meant and said they’d logged them for the roadmap. That doesn’t mean they’re available yet, but it’s encouraging to feel that your feedback is being heard.

I’ve hit a couple of bugs during early testing too, so I wouldn’t pretend everything is polished. What has impressed me is how willing the team has been to investigate and keep the conversation going.

My impression is that the founder really wants to improve this in ways that help people manage their lives. That matters to me, because I’m looking for something I’ll actually keep using.

Five tacos, partly for where it’s headed rather than just where it is today. There’s work to do, but this feels close enough to what I need that I want to stick with it and see how it develops.

Why are “Create and manage lists” and “Custom integrations” excluded? ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity already help me with these tasks. What organization and connections would I be missing?

Meeting notes and summaries are my main reason for considering Aria. How many meetings or minutes does Tier 2 include? Is there a recording length limit? Do long voice notes use that allowance? Are there extra charges?

Does Aria record Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, and in-person meetings, or must I upload audio? Does it provide transcripts, speaker identification, detailed notes, summaries, decisions, and action items with owners and deadlines?

Can Aria turn meeting action items into assigned tasks and recurring reminders, even without list management in Tier 2?

children.comment:
Great questions — let me go through them honestly.

EXCLUSIONS (Lists & Custom Integrations)
• "Create & manage lists" (Tier 3) is purely an organisation layer — it lets you group to-dos into separate named lists (e.g. "Invoices", "Clients") each with their own deadline. On Tier 2 you still get full to-dos and reminders; they just aren't grouped into named lists.
• What Tier 2 DOES include: Google and Microsoft calendar, Gmail, Drive and Meet integrations, bring-your-own-AI-key, internet search, and Circles. For a meeting-notes use case, Tier 2 has what you need.

MEETING ALLOWANCE
• Tier 2 isn't metered on meeting minutes — no per-meeting or per-month cap, and no extra charges. Voice notes and image analysis are unlimited too.
• Per recording, the only limit is file size (up to ~2GB), which comfortably covers multi-hour meetings. Long voice notes are fine and don't eat into any separate allowance.

RECORDING & OUTPUT
• Aria does not auto-join or record Zoom/Teams/Meet/in-person calls — you record the meeting (or export the call's audio) and send it to Aria.
• From that audio you get structured, executive-style minutes: identified participants/speakers, an executive summary, key discussion topics, decisions made, and action items with owners and due dates, plus critical dates and follow-ups.
• One honest note: it produces polished minutes, not a raw word-for-word transcript — the actionable version rather than a verbatim line-by-line copy.

ACTION ITEMS → TASKS
• Yes — you can turn action items into to-dos and reminders and assign them to people in your Circle, all on Tier 2 (Tier 3's lists would just let you group them into named lists). Recurring reminders are supported on daily / weekly / monthly schedules.

Hope that helps you decide — happy to clarify anything!

questions.title: Hello, I have four questions.
questions.comment:
These four — the ones I couldn't verify from the AppSumo page and reviews:
1. **Recording length:** "Unlimited minutes of meeting" — but is one single recording unlimited, or is there a per-recording limit?
2. **Transcripts:** Do you get a complete word-for-word transcript, or only a summary with action items?
3. **Circle members:** Do the people getting your reminders need Hello Aria or WhatsApp, or can they be any phone contact?
4. **Smart speakers:** Does it work with Alexa or Google Assistant / Google Home?

children.comment:
Straight answers:

1. Recording length: There's no per-recording minute limit — a single recording can run for hours. The only ceiling is a 2GB file size per upload, which is far more than even a long multi-hour meeting would produce, but on Whatsapp its 45mins due to WhatsApp limits. So one continuous recording is effectively unlimited in length.

2. Transcripts: You get professionally formatted meeting minutes — an executive summary, key discussion topics, decisions made, and action items — rather than a raw word-for-word transcript. So it's the structured, actionable version of the meeting, not a verbatim line-by-line copy. On the Ios app- you get transcriptions + minutes document.

3. Circle members: They need their own Hello Aria account (on an active plan — a trial counts) to receive the reminders you assign them. Aria won't send to someone who isn't a user, so it's not a way to text any phone contact — it's designed for people who are also on Aria (your team or family).

4. Smart speakers: Not currently — there's no Alexa or Google Assistant / Home integration. Aria runs through WhatsApp, the web dashboard, and our iOS/Android apps (and you can connect it to Claude or ChatGPT). You can capture things fairly hands-free by sending a WhatsApp voice note, but there's no native smart-speaker skill today.

Hope that helps — happy to clarify anything further!

Thank you.  Is there any plan for the To Do list to be able to show in the Task list on Google Calendar?   Will the ring feature available now on iPhone be available for android?  I understand the is a beta version for android.  What does that mean? Different features?

Great questions!

1. To-Dos in Google's task list: not yet — to-dos stay inside Aria, only calendar events sync to Google. I've logged it for the roadmap.

2. Ring feature: it's iOS-only for now. The Android app is in beta and we're building toward the same features, so it should come across — no date I can commit to yet.

(part 2 of 2 to follow)

3. What "beta" means: it's the same Aria — same account, same data, synced with WhatsApp and the dashboard — not a different or cut-down product. It just means the Android app is earlier in development than iOS, so a few features (like the ring feature) aren't there yet and you may hit the odd rough edge. Your feedback while it's in beta genuinely helps us prioritise.

Happy to help with anything

questions.title: Tier 3 Lists, Circles, and Knowledge Management
questions.comment:
1. Am I correct in my understanding that only tier 3 has access to create to do lists? Does that mean Tiers 1 and 2 are only for reminders?

2. Do people in my Circle need their own subscription to Hello Aria?

3. Beyond capturing tasks and setting reminders, how well does this perform as a second brain? Would I be able to feed it extensive information and recall/search through it easily?

children.comment:
Great questions!

1. Lists vs to-dos: Not quite — all three tiers can create both reminders AND to-dos, so you're never limited to just reminders. What Tier 3 adds on top is dedicated, named to-do lists you can organise and set deadlines on — e.g. a separate "Invoices" list, a "Certificates" list, etc. — instead of one general to-do pile. So: Tiers 1–2 = reminders + to-dos; Tier 3 = that, plus managed lists.

2. Circles: Yes — to receive the reminders/tasks you assign them, people in your Circle need their own Hello Aria account on an active plan (a trial counts). Aria won't message someone who isn't a user. So it's great for a team or family who are all on board, but it isn't a way to send reminders to people who don't use Aria.

3. Second brain: Yes — that's exactly what the Notes feature is for. You can feed Aria as much information as you like as notes, and then recall or search it anytime just by asking (e.g. "what did I note about the Henderson job?"). It holds that context and pulls it back on demand, so it works well as a lightweight second brain alongside your tasks and reminders.

Hope that helps — happy to go deeper on any of these!

questions.title: Hello Aria: Long-Term Memory, WhatsApp Reminders, Reliability, and Tier 2 vs. Tier 3 Lifetime Deal Benefits
questions.comment:
I am considering Hello Aria’s lifetime deal. My primary use case is a WhatsApp-based personal AI assistant that remembers facts, preferences, and ongoing matters over time, retrieves them accurately, and reliably delivers scheduled and recurring reminders. Can it also capture and retrieve information shared through text, voice notes, and images? Which of these features are fully operational today versus still on the roadmap?

I would also appreciate a clear comparison of Tier 3 ($199) and Tier 2 ($99). What additional features or usage limits does Tier 3 offer, particularly for memory, WhatsApp, reminders, and integrations? Finally, what ongoing product development and customer support can lifetime-deal customers expect?

children.comment:
Great questions — straight answers:

LIVE TODAY: WhatsApp-first assistant with AI memory (facts/preferences you share are remembered and used in later conversations), one-time AND recurring reminders delivered on WhatsApp (with automatic retry + redelivery if WhatsApp delays a message), capture via text, voice notes (transcribed + acted on), and images (analyzed — e.g. send a photo of an appointment letter and it extracts the details), Google Calendar/Gmail/Drive/Meet integrations, internet search, meeting minutes, and a web dashboard + iOS app synced with WhatsApp. Bring-your-own-API-key is live too.

ROADMAP (not live yet): subtasks, task reordering, multi-account/multi-calendar, deeper notification customization — public roadmap at helloaria.io/roadmap.

TIER 2 vs TIER 3 — honestly: for memory, WhatsApp, reminders, and integrations there is NO difference — both get unlimited messages, unlimited voice notes, unlimited image analysis, AI memory, recurring reminders, Google integrations, and circles. Tier 3 adds managed Lists (live today) plus upcoming extras: unlimited meeting minutes, custom integrations, and advanced security features. So for your described use case, Tier 2 covers it fully; Tier 3 is for Lists + those upcoming capabilities.

ONGOING DEV & SUPPORT: we ship weekly (you can see the cadence on the roadmap), lifetime buyers get all updates within their tier, and support is direct email with the founding team — most issues get a same-day response, and Sumolings' bug reports regularly turn into fixes within days.

questions.title: What Features are available
questions.comment:
Android user & solo electrician. Can you confirm: 1. Does it work smoothly with WhatsApp & WhatsApp Business app ? 
2. Can a messy post-walkthrough voice note  such us,  need t replace light and switch bedroom 1 , only socket bedroom 2, kitchen 2 spot lights(address, pricing, certificates) automatically parse and populate Google Calendar event descriptions with all details? 
3. How do Android reminders work—can I set custom advance alerts (20–30 mins or a day before to quote), and can it send automated text reminders to clients? 
4. What exact features/limits does Tier 3 add over Tier 2 for a trade business? Thanks!  
Is there any storage available, for the messages , photos, videos etc. so in bried how can my business benefit, as i like the idea behind but still unsure if it provides what i really need to speed my work. Thanks

children.comment:
Great questions — and honestly, a solo trade is one of the best fits for Aria (capture by voice/photo, let it do the admin). Straight answers:

1. WhatsApp + WhatsApp Business app: Yes, both. You just message Aria's number — works the same whichever WhatsApp app you use. As an Android user you'd run everything through WhatsApp + the web dashboard; no app install needed.

2. Messy post-walkthrough voice note → calendar: Yes. Aria transcribes it, puts the site address in the event's location, and files the rest (what to replace in each room, quantities, pricing notes, certificate mentions) into the event description as readable detail. It won't create separate structured "price" or "certificate" fields, but nothing you dictate gets lost.

3. Reminders (to YOU): Yes — you can say "remind me a day before to send that quote" or "remind me 30 min before the job" and it sets a reminder at that time; recurring (daily/weekly) works too.
   Automated texts to CLIENTS: here's the honest limit — Aria reminds YOU on WhatsApp, but it does not send messages directly to your clients' phones. Client-facing reminders only reach people who are themselves Aria users, so it's not a client-SMS tool today.

4. Tier 3 vs Tier 2 for a solo trade: honestly, Tier 2 already unlocks nearly everything — unlimited messages, unlimited voice notes, unlimited image analysis, Google Calendar, recurring reminders, and bring-your-own-AI-key. There's no word-limit or "team seat" difference between the tiers. Tier 3 adds Lists management now, plus a few coming-soon items (unlimited meeting minutes, custom integrations, advanced security). So Tier 2 is plenty for a solo operator unless you specifically want Lists or those upcoming extras.

In short for your business: after a walkthrough you just talk or snap photos, and Aria turns it into calendar events, your to-do list, and timely reminders to yourself — and keeps the paperwork in one place. The one thing to set expectations on is that it reminds YOU, not your clients directly. Happy to help you get set up.

reviews.title: Persistence is valuable, expecting tacos to increase
reviews.comment:
I originally purchased FuseBase (1 year ago) for an online education use case: onboarding students, creating portal rooms for individual learners and groups, sharing session documents, and supporting collaborative project work. The vision was compelling—a flexible client and student portal that could bring learning materials, communication, recordings, and project collaboration into one place.

My experience has been mixed, largely because I joined during a major period of product transition. FuseBase was moving from more basic AI features toward a much more agent-driven product direction. During that shift, there was a noticeable drop in communication and continuity for early users like me. It sometimes felt like we were caught between the former platform and the future version still being built.

That said, I chose to stay engaged. I joined the community spaces, followed product updates, watched videos, and learned from power users willing to share how they were using the platform. That has helped me see both the current limitations and the longer-term opportunity.

One feature that did not work reliably for me was the webinar recording extension. It failed to record an important consulting call that was under an hour long. I later tested it with a much shorter call, under five minutes, and it worked correctly—but that was not a meaningful test for the type of client meetings I need to capture. Reliable recordings are central to my intended use of FuseBase within a client portal, so this was a significant disappointment.

I do not see this as a permanent product flaw so much as a maturity and documentation issue. The platform is evolving quickly, but the training materials and documentation do not always appear to keep pace with what is actively being built and changed. There is a large amount of educational material available, yet it can be impractical when it does not reflect the current product experience.

Despite these frustrations, I am giving FuseBase four tacos because I believe in Pavel and the team. They have invested heavily in the platform’s transition, and their development experience is visible. I expect the current turnaround to produce meaningful benefits for the broader user base—not only customers who receive high-touch, white-glove support.

I also had a one-on-one conversation with Pavel when I first decided to onboard (April). His advice was candid: unless I needed an immediate solution, I should give the product a few months to develop and, in the meantime, become more comfortable with VS Code for general AI upskilling. That was some of the best advice I have received in this space. It increased my ability to work with tools that are less dependent on a simple user interface and more capable under the hood.

In some ways, that captures FuseBase’s current challenge. Highly technical users may find parts of the platform insufficient and wonky while it continues to add deeper capability. At the same time, non-technical users may feel that the product is becoming more complex faster than its documentation and training can support.

Still, the progress so far is impressive. The transition is not finished, but it is already showing real promise. The user community is generally helpful and supportive, and I remain optimistic that FuseBase can become a powerful solution for client portals, education programs, collaborative workspaces, and knowledge-driven businesses.

Bottom line: FuseBase is not yet a fully polished, plug-and-play platform for every use case. But for users who can tolerate some change, stay engaged with the community, and grow with the product, it has substantial potential that is being realized in real-time.

I am very impressed with FuseBase as an all-in-one solution that includes pages, apps, automations, databases, customer portals, and AI agents. For me, a big plus is that all these components are connected and interact with each other in a shared environment. 
The monthly limits (e.g., for AI requests or automations) are in my view pleasantly generous, and I have personally had very good experiences with the support (I received timely responses that helped me).

reviews.title: A comprehensive, modern platform that stays on the cutting edge of tech
reviews.comment:
FuseBase has successfully evolved from a simple workspace into a versatile operational platform built to drive value across the entire organization. Its greatest asset is how fast it adopts cutting-edge technology—integrating white-labeled client portals, databases, and autonomous AI agents to automate workflows and consolidate tools into a single dashboard.
Because the platform advances so quickly, there is an unavoidable learning curve, and the official documentation occasionally lags behind new releases. However, the product's forward-looking direction and active development more than compensate for it. For any team looking for an all-in-one ecosystem that scales alongside modern tech innovations, FuseBase is an outstanding long-term asset.
