reviews.title: Problem Solved !
reviews.comment:
-
Garmingo Voice has solved a long-standing problem for me.  

I have to access an hour-long or more recording of a meeting that occurs on a daily basis outside of my time zone, and in the past I’ve listened to it with half-an-ear and scrabbled to make notes of anything that will affect me or my team.  The same where I’ve been asked to listen to lengthy podcasts or videos.

I’ve tried many locally installed transcription apps and they’ve all been hugely disappointing.  The issue has only been resolved by paying $$$ to a service that allows lengthy audio files to be uploaded and transcribed.  Garmingo Voice has allowed me to now do this locally on a barely-used and aging Intel Power Mac, and their ‘ultra’ model transcription is comparable to the paid service that we are currently using.

I had a few initial issues during installation, namely I couldn’t install the driver.  I raised this with support, who were incredibly helpful, and issued me with a driver file to be loaded via terminal.  Then 48 hours later I was notified that there was a new update where this issue had been fixed, and having checked, the in-app installation of the driver now works fine.

I haven’t tried their cloud service as this is what I’ve been attempting to get away from !

There are a few things I’d love to see in future updates: 

* The ability to upload a file in the Meetings panel to group by speaker in the transcription.
* .mp4 uploads along with .pdf and .docx outputs.
* Dropbox connectivity.

If you have similar transcription needs then definitely give Garmingo Voice a try.   In my use case, this one is a definite keeper.

questions.title: Teams app + workflow
questions.comment: I use an application called Teams almost daily at work. I can make full transcripts if I receive a call on my cell phone or we start a conference on the computer. How is the workflow? Is the app always listening? Do I have to start it first? Or can I do something to start it at the same time as the Teams app starts? Could you explain a little more how it works? And if we are on average 15 participants in the meeting, how can I assign a name to it so that it detects the type of voice or differentiates them from each other?

children.comment:
Hi Arnold,

Thank you for your interest in Garmingo Voice. The setup process is actually very simple:

The app installs a virtual speaker that you can link to your Teams application. In Teams, you select your output device—the Garmingo Voice speaker—and your audio is then routed through Garmingo Voice before being played back through your system speaker or the one you’ve selected in the app.

Currently, there is no automatic detection if a Teams meeting is running, so you’ll need to manually press the "Start Meeting Recording" button in Garmingo Voice.

For differentiating participants, we use a diarization algorithm that automatically detects and distinguishes speakers. Afterwards, you can assign names to them.

If the number of participants is incorrect or if a transcript segment is wrongly identified, you can easily adjust these details later.

questions.title: privacy and security
questions.comment:
Hi! A few questions about privacy and security on macOS:
1. Accessibility permission request: When using local AI models, can you confirm that no dictated text or other accessible content is transmitted to external servers? Is this permission used only for dictation and text insertion, or can the app read content from other applications?
2. Telemetry: Does the app transmit any usage or diagnostic data, even in local mode?
3. Enhanced driver: What data can it access? Can you confirm it doesn't transmit dictated text, app content, or sensitive data externally? Is it fully removed upon uninstallation, along with any background services?
Thanks for clarifying!

children.comment:
Hi Aleit,
Security and Privacy is very important for us. And therefore no data about your usage of the app is saved except the cost of your cloud usage. This means we never know what you dictate or transcribe neither in cloud nor in offline mode. All operation of offline models is happening without any connection to our services, no data is transmitted at all.

To your questions:
1: The accessibility permission on Mac is requested to check which app you are focusing during dictation and then to correctly insert the text. All of that happens locally and none of the information is ever saved or logged on our servers. If you are using a local model our services are not even contacted at all. No text or content is ever read from your applications.
2: The app does not transmit any usage or telemetry data with two exceptions: a) crash/diagnostics reports (an upcoming feature were you will be able to manually send a diagnostics log to us in the case of errors - which will not contain any sensitive data) and b) when you use a cloud model the token consumption and equivalent credit pricing is saved for billing, again no actual content is saved on our end.
3: The driver does not transmit any data at all. If you are only using the app for dictation, it is not required to install the driver at all. It is used for a) Microphone enhancement and b) Meeting recordings. And it works fully offline. If you uninstall the driver (which is also possible from within the app) it is fully removed and no background services remain installed on your Mac.


I really appreciate your interest in our app and our privacy standpoint. For us privacy is important and we will never collect any sensitive data about our customers.

Best regards,
Alex

reviews.title: Loving this App
reviews.comment:
I've been using this app for over a year now, and it's the best tool I have found to help keep me organized and not forget things. I have ADHD and always forget things that are not right in front of me. 

I had tried many tools previously, but none of them worked very well and were abandoned within a few weeks. With browser-based tools, you need to have a browser open and a connection to the internet in order to use them. I would pin the tab so I would always see it, but often I would close the wrong browser window first and lose all my tabs and would forget about the tool, and end up missing important deadlines or appointments. Or sometimes I might not be connected to the internet or have the browser open and would then not get the notifications. Some other apps could only installed on one device; they wouldn't sync, or you would need an active internet or cell phone connection, which I don't always have, or they just didn't have the features I needed. 

Physical planners rarely worked unless I made a point of always carrying them around, but would often then lose them or just forget to open them to look. Often the way they were set up didn't work for me either, and I would abandon them after a couple of weeks of use.

Chaos Control was fairly easy-to-use right from the start, but it took a little trial and error to figure out exactly how to use all the features in a way that worked for me. I have installed it on my home desktop system, my laptop, my tablet and my phone, so no matter where I am, one of these devices has it right there, and the notifications alert me so I don't forget appointments and deadlines very often now. Also having the app set to start as soon as your device starts up is a big win for me, so I don't forget to start it.

You can set tasks with repetitions, so they pop up daily, weekly or however often you set them to. 

You can create projects with different tasks for them and set start dates and deadlines up for each task so it will appear in your daily task to do list only when applicable, and you can create a checklist inside each task in case you want to break them down into smaller steps. You even have a folder structure so you can put different projects and tasks into different categories and organize them in a way that makes sense to you.

I love the timer that tracks the time you spent on each specific task so you can check back later to see the total time it took and time spent for each individual session. There are also options for tagging your tasks by priority, color, or other means. The app has different themes you can use to customize it. You can also bookmark certain tasks or projects in order to find them more easily. 

I really like that you can store files and images right in the app and have it synced with your other devices.

The most important things for me are that it can still be used when you are offline or out of cell service (which is often for me), and will sync as soon as you get back online, and I can install it on as many devices as I want and they will all sync, so I rarely forget important tasks and appointments now.

Since I've been using the app, there have been several upgrades, and each one keeps getting better. There is now the ability to use AI right in the app and to record voice, although I haven't used them yet, so I can't comment on how it works.

The only thing I would like to see added is something like a habit tracker that you can click each time you do something that might be something you do several times a day or a couple times a week but not at any specific times, so you can see how often you are doing the desired task (or bad habit). For instance, I ate healthy 4 times this week, and ate junk food 3 times this week, or drank 7 glasses of water today. 

Overall, if you've tried other ways to organize your life and they haven't worked, then give Chaos Control a try to see if it's right for you.

children.comment:
This is awesome review Lucy! 
Thank you so much. Love the habit tracking idea.

reviews.title: Nice "To-Do" List/Task Manager
reviews.comment:
It took me a minute to figure out how to set up my Categories, Programs and Tasks, but once I got the Jest of it, I put everything that came to mind in and I now have a long, manageable list.  
Prioritize by date, schedule by day, week, month, time, or have one time tasks. Track or limit time spent on tasks by using the timer. You can schedule your days and track your progress in Chaos Control. I even started setting up a recipe bank that I can schedule for family meals. You can do a lot with Chaos Control if you think outsoutside the box. I requested a blog article to test the AI feature, and it returned a succinct article with citations. -- Of course I need to fact check it, but the references are half of that battle. Otherwise, it looks like it needs minimal editing. I also made a test voice recording and it was crystal-clear. I uploaded a PDF file and easily accessed it in the app. Chaos Control is a 5* app. What is lacking for me is clear instructions. They do have links in the app that walk you through setup and use cases. Something is missing for me because I still fumbled around to connect some of the dots, so I am giving 4*s. Once I got going, I really enjoyed the ease of using the app to manage life. I highly recommend this purchase.

reviews.title: Does everything as promised and better but navigation and interface can be improved.
reviews.comment:
Pros:
1) Creating mind maps were quick and simple from a prompt/file/text. Very easy to implement and see.
2) You can add images easily for better understanding.
3) Interface is beautifully designed, intuitive, and aesthetically pleasing.
4) AI explore and AI chat is very useful, you can chat with it, use it to create child nodes/parent nodes as well as choose to expand on a particular part. It helps a lot when you need to go in depth rather than just a brief sentence. 
5) Rearranging is very easy, just drag and drop it on any node and it'll auto attach. Helps when you made a mistake/want to rearrange.
6) Pitch mode is an interesting feature that I've never seen before, love it.
7) Exporting or importing mindmaps are very easy.

Things to improve on:
1) AI often replies in other languages. Was given the reply of Chinese text as well as french text before when asked in English.
2) Fit to window is trash, if you expand the mind map to be in depth, it'll become huge and hard to read. 
3) Dragging the mindmap around using space+right click and hold is an awful way to move around. (Personally I got around that by using outline view.)
4) To get useful child nodes, you can't just press a node and add it, you have to first AI explore before scrolling to the bottom and using the add as a child node button. If you don't your child nodes would be really simple and not be as in depth. 
5) Dragging multiple mindmaps to a single folder isn't possible too so I have to do it one by one.
6) Folder settings are annoying, I do not want to see my recent mindmaps, I want them gone from app.amymind.com/home. I only want to see them in my sidebar. The main page can just be https://app.amymind.com/mindmap/guide. That would be much more cleaner. 

TLDR; Pros: Fast and simple mind map creation, easy image support, beautiful interface, useful AI chat/explore for depth, smooth drag-and-drop rearranging, easy exports and imports of mindmaps and unique pitch mode.

Cons: AI sometimes replies in wrong languages, poor “fit to window” scaling, clunky navigation controls, extra steps needed for detailed child nodes, can’t bulk-move maps to folders, and messy homepage with unwanted recent mindmaps.

Updated review: 17 March 2026

Reduced it by one star to 3 stars for lack of customer service.

reviews.title: Great Tool, deserves more than 5 Tacos!
reviews.comment:
I created my first mind maps with AmyMind and I am absolutely thrilled! Whether I created new mind maps completely frm scratch with AI or automatically from a Word document or PDF – AmyMind delivers! Usually, the mind maps are more than good on the first try, but if needed, I can also have the AI generate additional subpoints after creation or, of course, add them myself.

The handling of the tool is really well-developed, so that it can be used very well as a standalone mind map program, independent of the AI functions. Whether automatic rearrangement of the mind maps, expanding and collapsing individual branches, adding images or notes (the latter even automatically with the AI), or exporting in a variety of formats – AmyMind can do everything I need. The mind maps also look very appealing. In my case, I had the mind maps created in German, which worked flawlessly.

What I would still wish for:
- You can move the mind map back and forth by holding down the spacebar and left-clicking. This works very awkwardly on a (at east my) laptop. It would be nice if you could just hold down the mouse button to move it back and forth.
- Expanding and collapsing is done via a small menu directly on the entry. In my opinion, a dedicated symbol would be better (as long as clarity does not suffer).
- Although there is a presentation mode (which is great), it would be amazing if it showed the mind map overview and then zoomed in and out of the individual branches, so you always know where you are in the mind map. Currently, the view is text-based.

Apart from that, AmyMind is one of my favorite tools here on AppSumo and gets an absolute recommendation from me!

children.comment: I'm very glad you like AmyMind, and your suggestions are very reasonable. We will seriously evaluate them and consider adding them to the development plan. Thank you again!

questions.title: Will the user-friendliness be further improved?
questions.comment:
Hello,

Unfortunately, AmyMind can not be used, if:
❯ a professional user is working just with the keyboard to be fast 😢
❯ or if a disabled user is not able to use the mouse. 😱
Do you have any plans to improve the usability?

For example:
❯ Edit a node: The F2 key 
(F2 is used in all well-known desktop mind-mapping apps)

❯ Moving the focus from node to node: Cursor Keys

❯ Moving the View: Ctrl + Cursor Keys   
(Is the same as Control + Cursor Keys)

This would make it very easy for people switching from desktop mind-mapping apps, because they could get right back to work.

And people with disabilities could also configure their control panel using the keys. (Mouse control isn't practical for many people because many can only give a single impulse and thus press a key.)

Thanks a lot, kind regards,
Thomas

The platform is ok-ish, support? Non-existent.
I bought several deals here on AS, and got other ones outside, never experienced such absence of support. You ask the same thing over weeks, zero human answers.
And the bot answer is even one of the worst: the bot answers and you cannot basically answer anymore, cannot send any more messages. I mean in other platforms the bots says something like: "hey a human will be in touch soon, if you wanna add something else, just message.."
but no, in Stackby you cannot.

And other bugs like misleading UI: you create API calls in the columns, there is nowhere a number showing how many runs you did.

You bought the lifetime here on AP, and you wanna buy the other one-time packages? You cannot becuase wheen you go in your account settings they show the YEARLY prices, you click the button and the stripe page is shown with the subscription for the powerups or whatever you clicked.

AI credits number: inside the settings it continues to remain 0/500 for each stack. So it's repeated 0/500 for each stack. Then, somewhere else, can't remeber where they say that these credits are total across all stacks, another ui misleading info, and on top of that, you use the ai credits but it still shows 0/500 in the account settingss, but when you are in the home and click at the bottom left the ai credits button then it shows 433 left out of 500.

Then they increased the price of the one-time packages over and over, that's fine, it's not a bug, but it just adds on top of all these things.

Then, they just decide like they want: this feature is on the base terms, and then this other let's put it in the power ups, just like they woke up in the morning almost. Import CSV -> base tier, but Add from CSV -> power up, because why not.

Overall, I can't seem to find reason to trust them.
Airtable is better and I ran an analisis and you need to spend 2000$ to get the same base features that aritable gives you for 20/month

reviews.title: Feature-rich tool, but no real branding
reviews.comment:
Feedbeo shines when it comes to live engagement: unlimited polls, Q&A, and word clouds all update smoothly, and presenters pick it up within minutes. Attendees join via a short code, moderation is simple, and the interface performs reliably—ideal for meetings, workshops, or internal events.

However, calling the logo upload + preset colour swatches “branding” feels misleading. Real branding includes custom palettes, fonts, backgrounds, branded or neutral URLs, and the option to hide a vendor badge. With Feedbeo, the large logo remains fixed on every screen, and the session link always resides on the Feedbeo domain—this undermines the event’s identity, especially in brand-sensitive environments.

The UI can be confusing: the “Event Settings” control sometimes appears greyed out and feels inactive, making navigation harder for new users. If deeper branding options existed—like custom links, full theme controls, or a badge toggle—I’d gladly pay for them. As is, Feedbeo occupies a strange middle ground: it’s loaded with great interactive tools but falls short in the branding department. Minimalism is admirable—but not at the cost of essential features.

reviews.title: UX feels illogical and key features are gated
reviews.comment:
It's hard to like  Worklenz, as the UX design feels far from logical, especially during project setup.

The flow focuses on metadata like status, health, estimates, and categories before the purpose of the project is even defined. That’s the wrong order. A project should start with a clear goal and intent, then move into structure and execution, not the other way around.

Projects are driven by purpose, and different types of work (research, product, marketing) require different workflows. Here, everything is treated the same and pushed into configuration too early, which creates friction and breaks the natural way of working.

There are also structural gaps. File management lacks proper folder organization, making it harder to scale and manage assets inside projects.

On top of that, important features seem to be locked behind higher-tier plans without clear upfront visibility. Capabilities like client portals, finance tracking, and advanced scheduling are positioned as premium add-ons, even though they are core to real project workflows.

The UI looks clean, but the underlying UX logic is not aligned with how work actually happens. It feels built for tracking and reporting rather than thinking, planning, and building.

Overall: lacks a solid foundation. Needs a purpose-first setup flow, proper file structure, and clearer feature accessibility to be usable at scale.

A Project tools should help with a clear overview and control of the different process, what this is not!

children.comment:
Thank you for taking the time to share such a detailed and thoughtful review — this kind of feedback is incredibly valuable for us as we continue improving Worklenz.

You’ve raised a very important point about the project setup flow being too configuration-heavy upfront, and we agree that this can feel counterintuitive. Projects should indeed start with a clear purpose and evolve naturally into structure. We’re currently working on refining this experience toward a more “purpose-first” approach, where users can define intent quickly and configure details progressively as needed.

Regarding workflows, you’re absolutely right — different types of work (research, product, marketing, etc.) require different approaches. We’re actively exploring project-type templates and flexible workflows to better support these variations without forcing a one-size-fits-all structure.

On file management, we acknowledge the limitation around folder organization. This is already on our roadmap, and we’re working toward introducing a more scalable and structured file system within projects.

About feature visibility and plan limitations, we understand how this can be frustrating. Our goal is to strike a balance between keeping the product sustainable and ensuring core workflows remain accessible. Based on feedback like yours, we’re currently revisiting what should be considered “core” vs “advanced” features, and improving how this is communicated upfront.

Lastly, your point about Worklenz feeling more geared toward tracking rather than thinking/planning is insightful. Our long-term vision is to support the full lifecycle — from idea → planning → execution → reporting, and feedback like this helps us close those gaps.

We truly appreciate your honesty. If you’re open to it, we’d love to involve you in early feedback on upcoming improvements — your perspective would be extremely valuable.

Thanks again for helping us build a better product 🙌

What we appreciate most is that Worklenz strikes the perfect balance between power and simplicity. It’s robust enough for serious operations, yet clean enough that it never becomes a burden. That’s a hard balance to achieve—and they nailed it.

After a full year of real-world use, we can confidently say this isn’t just another project management tool—it’s an operational backbone. If you’re managing teams, clients, or complex projects and want visibility, accountability, and flow in one place, Worklenz delivers.

Highly recommended.

Hi there, thank you for your question! yes, Worklenz gives you full control over who sees what. You can set up privacy at three levels:

Organization level: Manage who is part of your workspace and their roles.
Team level: Group people into teams so each team only works within its own space.
Project level: Add each person only to the projects they need. Members can only see the projects they are added to.

reviews.title: Project management with gamification and WhatsApp built in
reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Most project management tools are good at telling people what they need to do. Syncupp tries to give them another reason to actually do it.

The gamification is a big part of that. Completing work can earn coins and XP, build streaks and move people up a leaderboard. Those coins can then be tied to rewards you define yourself, so the reward system becomes part of the everyday work instead of something a manager has to run separately.

I tested creating and completing tasks and awarding coins, and that worked well. I can especially see this working for agencies, sales groups or other environments where a little friendly competition can make routine work more engaging.

Syncupp also brings a lot of the day-to-day work into the same place. There are project boards, tasks, chat, meetings, time tracking, attendance, roles and permissions, along with the leaderboard and rewards. You can work in kanban, list or calendar views and break tasks down with subtasks, dependencies and recurring schedules.

The other big advantage for me is the native WhatsApp integration. Task assignments, deadline reminders and daily summaries can go directly to WhatsApp, and some approvals can be handled just by replying without opening Syncupp. For groups that already rely heavily on WhatsApp, that could make the product much easier to adopt because people can see what needs attention where they are already communicating.

I also like that WhatsApp and the gamification are included across the AppSumo tiers rather than being reserved for the higher plans. The tiers mainly change how many people and workspaces you can have, along with the amount of AI usage included.

During my test, the leaderboard did not update immediately after coins were awarded. The team reproduced the issue and said they were adding real-time updates. The current AppSumo listing now describes it as a live XP leaderboard with real-time rankings, so that appears to have been resolved.

I also found a visitor-tracking script running inside the logged-in application during the original test. The team removed it completely after I reported it, which I appreciated.

There are also integrations with Slack, Zapier, Make and Pabbly, plus Claude MCP if you want to bring Syncupp into an AI workflow.

Overall, I think the reason to choose Syncupp over another task manager is the combination of gamification and WhatsApp. The project management side is familiar, but coins, streaks, rewards and native WhatsApp updates give people more reason to stay engaged with the work and less reason to miss what needs to get done.

reviews.title: Inflated User Claims, Glaring Bugs, and Hidden Server Risks (Refunded)
reviews.comment:
Syncupp is a great concept, but is just not ready for prime time. There are too many issues with its underdeveloped UI and buggy functionality. I just can't see this being used with a serious client or team without some frustration on their end. Built-in AI is very limited (currently only responds to a very small number of questions, which seems to be a bug), and if you plan to rely on it and chat across multiple users even just a handful of times a day, the allotted credits are highly insufficient and will run out quickly within days. Also, it severely limits the types of files you can attach to a task, and it won't even allow you to delete files, which shows just how poorly it was designed and the lack of proper QA. This is simply not a mature enough product to take seriously, as it poses too many risks from an implementation standpoint. 

It is also a huge red flag that they refused to answer how many organizations are using this platform publicly on AppSumo, and instead asked me to have this conversation via email. I was then shocked when they claimed to have over 150 organizations and 2,500 active users (all pre-AppSumo), even though I later saw that their site prominently claims 3200+ companies worldwide. This huge discrepancy in numbers raises clear suspicions, especially given the persistence of glaring functionality issues that are hard to ignore due to their impact on the overall user experience. Based on these numbers, it is impossible that so many other users did not encounter the same basic issues earlier and report them. Because of this, their exaggerated customer numbers lose all credibility and reflect misleading practices. This is not how you build trust with your users, especially on AppSumo.

Along with the app bugs, you also have to worry about how well their servers hold up. Because their data is hosted in India and tied to outside tools like WhatsApp, it is tough to tell how secure our information is or if the system will slow down under heavy use. When you add in the fact that they aren't being fully transparent about how many real users they have and make unbelievable claims about their size, it is tough to trust that this app will stick around for the long run.

————————
UPDATE:
In response to the founder, I found myself spending more time than I would’ve liked right from the start, reporting too many glaring issues to the point where I lost any further interest in the platform. Also, my AI credits wouldn’t even work properly, as I was only given 150 credits rather than the 1,000 I was supposed to get on Tier 2. To make matters worse, there is no public roadmap and no feature request page. For a business touting the importance of effective project management, with either +3200 or even just 150+ organizations using its platform (not sure either number can be trusted at this point), it’s ironic how poorly its own operations are being managed.

children.comment:
I’ll separate what’s true from what isn’t.

True. You were given 150 credits instead of the 1,000 Tier 2 entitles you to. Our bug, fixed within 30 minutes of you raising it. File deletion and wider attachment support are already shipped. Three legitimate hits.

Not true, and stated with a confidence the facts don’t support:

The numbers. 3,200+ is total companies signed up since launch. 150 organisations and 2,500 users was active usage at the time you asked. Two different metrics, both accurate. You didn’t ask which was which — you jumped to “misleading practices,” “lose all credibility,” and “not how you build trust,” and then built half your review on top of that leap. Our site copy should have been explicit; it will be this week. Your accusation still doesn’t survive the question you never asked. This is in very poor taste. 

“Impossible that so many users didn’t hit these issues earlier.” They did. That’s what a tracker is for, and it’s why several of these are already queued for release. You’ve constructed a conspiracy out of a product having a backlog.

The servers. Files on AWS Mumbai. Database on MongoDB Atlas. Data never sold, never shared, never used to train any model — when you use an AI feature, only that request’s text goes to Gemini, or to your own API key if you connect one. WhatsApp runs on Meta’s official Business API, the same infrastructure your bank sends OTPs over. “Hosted in India, therefore unclear if it’s secure” is not a security finding. It’s a guess dressed as one, and it’s the weakest paragraph in your review.

What I’ll own. Moving your customer-count question to email was the wrong call. There was nothing to hide, but it looked like there was, and that one decision is why everything after it in your review reads as suspicion. Numbers are public in the Q&A now, and a public roadmap and feature-request page go live by 31st October.

Where we actually stand. Syncupp has been in business three years. We’re not an AppSumo flip — we’ll be here until Syncupp is the best project management tool on the market, and we’re building something genuinely different: AI that runs your workspace from WhatsApp and Slack, not another Trello clone with a chatbot bolted on.

That vision isn’t for everyone. You spent a few hours, decided we were inflating numbers and hiding something, and refunded. That’s a fair outcome for both of us. Everyone else reading this can check the roadmap against what we ship, and judge us on that rather than on either of our opinions.

— Ritwik, Co-founder, Syncupp

1. Credits
Great question! Credits work the same on WhatsApp, Slack and the dashboard chat:

Chat message: 1 credit
Info reply: 2 credits
Task executed: 3 credits

Monthly workspace pool (resets every month): 300 (Tier 1), 1,000 (Tier 2), 2,500 (Tier 3), 5,000 (Tier 4).

Want unlimited usage? Connect your own API key in Settings, and your Syncupp credits stay untouched. 🙌

2. Client access
Yes! You can add clients as Viewers. They only see the boards you share, and you choose their access per board:

View: see tasks
Comment: see tasks and add comments
Edit: update existing tasks

Everything else (attendance, team chat, leaderboard, rewards) stays private to your internal team.

All your data is stored in India. Files are on AWS (Mumbai), and the database is on MongoDB Atlas. 🇮🇳

Your workspace data resides in India. Files are hosted on AWS (Mumbai), and the database runs on MongoDB Atlas.

5. Privacy
Your tasks, chats and files stay private to your workspace and are never used to train any Syncupp models. When you use AI features, only the text of that specific request goes to Google Gemini, or to your own API key if you’ve connected one. 🔒

Tasks can be assigned to workspace members, who then mark them complete. Want to keep a client in the loop? Add them as a Viewer so they can follow progress and comment.

questions.title: Questions to: Custom branding, Email-white labelling & Active requests
questions.comment:
I want to send the questionnaires to my customers traditionally, with a direct email from my email client (Outlook); therefore, my question is: why do I need these two features: Custom branding & Email-white labelling? 
Active requests: If I understand this correctly, an active request is 1 client even with 2 or 3 forms with different questionnaires? If I have a project finished and I delete this request = client, does it mean I have this slot free again? 
Last question: as a small agency in the e-commerce sector (mostly online stores & SEO) with around 2-3 projects each month, is there a reason to choose a higher plan than 1?

children.comment:
Hi Johannes,

Thanks for your questions Happy to clarify.

If you plan to send invitations directly from Outlook, you can absolutely do that. Simply copy the client portal link and include it in your email.

Custom branding lets you add your own logo, colors, and branding to the client portal, so it looks like an extension of your agency rather than OkaySend.

Email white-labeling lets you customize the emails sent automatically by OkaySend, such as some notifications, so they match your brand and use your email address instead of mail.okaysend.com. If you handle all communication yourself through Outlook, this may be less important to you.

Branded links let you use your own domain, so the links you share and the URLs where your client portals are hosted reflect your brand (e.g., your-company.com?id=request-uid-123).

An active request represents a live client portal. You can send unlimited requests a month and have an unlimited client list. Once a project is finished, you can mark the request as Done or Archived. This revokes the client's access and frees up your active request quota, so you can use it for another project. You don't need to delete the request.

Based on what you've described Tier 1 is perfectly fine. That said, higher tiers offer additional features, including features we'll release in the future, that may be useful as your needs grow. These are nice to have, but there's no reason to pay for a higher tier until you actually need what it offers.

I hope this helps you choose the right plan!

Order Management: You currently can't edit existing orders directly to add or remove products post-purchase. Adjusting customer orders requires a few roundabout workarounds.

questions.title: vs. Base44 vs. Shopify
questions.comment: Hi guys.  I had someone recently sign me up to try their AI storebuilding process, which includes Shopify and Base44.  Is this a solution to both of those, in one place?  New to ecommerce, and planned to sell a clothing brand from it with vendors fulfilling the orders.

children.comment:
Hi appking,

Thanks for your question, and welcome to ecommerce! Yes—for the clothing business you described, Selldone brings your storefront, ecommerce operations, and vendor management together, with AI tools to help you build and manage your store.

You wouldn’t need Shopify to run a Selldone store. Whether you need Base44 would depend on any additional custom application you want to build. Selldone already provides the core commerce system: products, sizes and colors, inventory, checkout, payments, discounts, customers, and orders.

For vendors fulfilling your clothing orders, there are three possible setups:

- Print-on-demand: Connect providers such as Printful or Printify to sell clothing featuring your designs. The provider produces and ships the items, allowing you to start without buying inventory upfront.

- Your existing suppliers: If you work with clothing suppliers who ship directly to customers, the workflow depends on how they receive orders and share inventory and tracking information. We can help you assess the integration options.

- A multi-vendor marketplace: Independent vendors can use their own panel to manage products, inventory, and fulfillment, while you manage the marketplace and commissions. Stripe Connect supports vendor payouts where available. Marketplace functionality is included from AppSumo Tier 3 upward.

You don’t automatically need a marketplace just because a supplier handles shipping—a regular branded store may be sufficient.

For AI-assisted building, you can connect Claude or ChatGPT through MCP. Supported actions include creating and organizing products and categories, preparing descriptions and SEO content, and building landing pages. Selldone provides the commerce infrastructure behind what you create.

How to connect Claude:
https://selldone.com/help/191

How to connect ChatGPT:
https://selldone.com/help/192

Here are three stores whose owners joined Selldone, built their ecommerce websites, and have already made sales:

https://skyward.supplies/

https://andara-creations.voicesofthelighttribe.com/

https://printinthebag.co.uk/

Since you’re starting out, I’d recommend choosing your fulfillment model first. Are you planning to use Printful/Printify, work with existing clothing suppliers, or invite independent vendors? Share a little more about your plans, and we’ll help you choose the right setup and tier.

Best,
Alireza

reviews.title: Flowlance is a great way to sell products and services
reviews.comment:
We purchased Flowlance a few months ago and we have nothing but positive things to say about the product. The features and functionality available in Flowlance are amazing, and when you consider the price point, it is an easy recommendation!

The features included on the Teir 3 option we purchased include:
--- Flowie - AI product, store and ad content creation
--- Sales Dashboard
--- Orders - Order Details
--- Helpful CRM - Track every session spent with a customer, every invoice sent, every product they purchase, and any notes you take about this customer. You have one place to manage and automate customer records. You can also import a current customer list.
--- Use your own URL - You can set up your store using your own URL. 
--- Communities - Want to provide a space where customers within the same or similar category can network, share ideas, etc.? Create a community.
--- Courses - Simple-to-use LMS that enables a business to offer training as a feature add-on or as a primary product. We may use the Communities section to promote a course following a customer purchasing a specific product. 
--- Calendar - Customers have the ability to schedule an appointment with you during the time frame you identify as available [Consultation/Coaching/etc.]
--- Email Sequencing and Broadcast Emails- this is very helpful.
--- Direct Sales - Send a customer a link for a one-off or even recurring charge
--- Funnels [BETA] - And they are adding more features. We have not created a funnel yet, but I can assure you we will check out this feature when we are ready.
--- Referral/affiliate link - If you refer one of your customers [or anyone] to Flowlance and they subscribe, Flowlance will pay you 20–30% commission monthly [based on your plan]. Seriously… automatic PayPal payouts every month. There is no minimum payout amount, no sales limit, and you can track your revenue in real time. 

In full transparency, on two occasions, support didn't respond within a day… one request took two days, and the other took three. And I still have nothing but positive things to say about Patrik Kruntorad, his team, and the product they have brought to market. Both times the issues were resolved. Only after the fact did it occur to me that we were probably prioritized lower than customers who were already live with products. I am also hoping my fellow entrepreneurs residing in the U.S. remember that 9:00 AM in Prague is 3:00 AM in New York and midnight in Los Angeles. Likewise, 2:00 PM in LA is 8:00 PM in Prague… you get the idea. 

Patrik and his team may want to consider adding a KnowledgeBase and a ticketed support system/workflow that doesn’t begin with “send an email to support”. An automated acknowledgment when a support request is submitted could include a link to the KnowledgeBase, especially if Flowlance is experiencing a higher-than-usual support request volume. This helped us a lot almost three years ago when a promotion/ad campaign produced a lot of inquiries and sales and also significantly increased support requests. It was a great problem to have; however, we could not keep up with support. We hired two freelancers to categorize support requests, build a basic Knowledgebase, and automate an acknowledgment email that inserted links based on keywords in the "issue description" and/or selections from a category drop-down menu. When the next advertising push launched, purchases and support requests spiked again; however, this time over half of the support requests were closed by the customer that submitted the request. A surprisingly high percentage of customers visited one or more of the Knowledgebase links included in the support request acknowledgment email. Anyhooooo…. I am sure there are solutions being considered and Flowlance will land on the right solution.

The key takeaway here is that without hesitation, everyone on our team would recommend Flowlance. Flowlance, like the other products we have purchased on AppSumo, was conceived, created, and coded by a founder/business owner [and if they were lucky... a small team] genuinely trying to help other business owners navigate the sticking points we crawl over every day. So everybody, keep crawling until we can zoom and glide!

Thank you!
Jan J.

reviews.title: Exceptional for Speed and Conversion, But Limited by Architecture and flexibility
reviews.comment:
Flowlance is excellent for stripping away friction and launching a high-converting storefront instantly. It removes technical bloat, making it perfect for lean, purpose-driven brands.

However, its "one-pager" constraint is a major trade-off. It lacks the capacity to build out deep site architecture—like dedicated "About" or "Portfolio" or "Product (w categories)" pages—natively. 

This forces you to cram everything into one scroll, which over-populates the page and creating a messy, untidy offer that dilutes your authority. You are forced to treat this as a final transaction destination rather than a cohesive home base. BUSY, BUSY FAR TO BUSY!

Additionally, from a white-labeling perspective, the standard subscription cost paired with an extensive custom build can be a disproportionate layout to on-sell to an emerging coach or consultant. It feels a bit ambitious for the current feature set.

This architectural limitation is why it doesn't get a higher rating from me. If the roadmap updates to allow for more flexible site depth and a more sustainable white labelling, I maybe inclined to "taco up."

If your goal is a high-performance checkout experience that prioritises revenue over site depth, it is a solid tool.

children.comment:
Hi Gene,

Thanks for the detailed feedback and for highlighting how excellent Flowlance is for speed, friction-removal, and conversions!

You are completely right about the architecture. We intentionally built Flowlance as a high-converting, link-in-bio style storefront. Our entire philosophy is minimizing buyer friction and getting them to the checkout as fast as possible.

If you are looking for a multi-layered, deep website architecture with dedicated sub-pages, we are definitely not the right tool for that. To be completely transparent, rating Flowlance down for not having multi-page site depth is a bit like giving a boat a lower rating because it can't drive on the highway! (just kidding 😄) We are built specifically to be the ultimate checkout and delivery engine, not a traditional website builder.

For things like an "About" section or a "Portfolio," our most successful creators simply use the store bio text, or they add a free "Video Introduction" as a standalone product card right at the top of their page.

Also, while the frontend is simple by design to reduce clutter, the backend is anything but. You can massively increase your revenue per customer by stacking order bumps, one-click upsells, and custom post-purchase redirects. It has very deep use cases for revenue generation.

Regarding the white-labeling many of our competitors don't even offer full white-labeling on their $99/month subscription tiers. With this deal, you can secure full white-labeling for a single one-time payment and have it forever. If you are on-selling to clients, that gives you incredible lifetime margins. And I'm not even talking about 0% transaction fees! 😎

Thanks again for the review and for recognizing that if the goal is high-performance checkout and revenue, this is a solid tool.

Hopefully, this gives you a bit more context on why we built it this way, and maybe helps with reconsidering your rating. If not, that is totally okay too - we respect your feedback and appreciate you giving us a shot!

Take care 💙,
Stepan

questions.title: Can Flowlance protect a paid PDF with download limits, expiring links, and buyer-specific watermarking?
questions.comment:
Hi! I plan to sell a copyrighted PDF publication through Flowlance and need clarification on digital protection:
1. Does your copyright/protection feature only display a usage notice, or does it technically restrict sharing/redistribution?
2. Can I limit each purchase to exactly 1 or 3 downloads?
3. Does each buyer receive a unique download URL?
4. Can that URL expire automatically? If so, can I choose the timeframe?
5. Can Flowlance dynamically stamp/watermark each PDF with the buyer’s name, email, order number, or purchase date?
6. If a buyer forwards their download URL, can someone else download the file?
7. Can I manually reset access for a legitimate customer?
My goal: unique buyer access + 3-download limit + expiring link + buyer-specific PDF stamping.

children.comment:
Hey ThePortal! Great questions, let me give you straight answers on each. 🙏

1) Download limits. No, there's no download cap. What you can do is keep the product safely behind the paywall, or create products as drafts and publish them only when you need them.

2) & 3) Unique URLs and expiry. After a successful payment, the file is delivered via link. That link isn't unique per buyer and doesn't expire.

4) Buyer-specific watermarking. Not possible right now. No dynamic stamping with name, email, or order number.

5) Forwarded links. Yes, a forwarded link can be downloaded by someone else. Courses are different though — those are protected by a cookie session and will only open for the email that actually purchased.

6) Resetting access. Easy. You can resend the product to a legitimate customer anytime, even for free, using our Direct Sale feature.

7) The protection side. Access is gated at purchase, not locked at the file level.

One honest thought from watching thousands of creators sell here: the creators who win rarely win by locking things down. They win by building real trust and delivering so much value that sharing feels wrong. When buyers feel genuinely looked after, piracy mostly stops being a problem on its own. Heavy DRM tends to cost you more in friction with honest customers than it saves you from the few who'd never have paid anyway.

So my advice: pour that energy into the offer and the relationship. It pays back far better.

Happy to go deeper on any of these!
Steven

questions.comment: I created an account, but I can’t find an option to connect Stripe because I’m not from the USA, Mexico, or Canada? Let's say ... I make sales, will the option to connect Stripe appear? The "Account Setting">"View my earnings">“Manage Deposit” button is grayed out. Will I be able to withdraw my earnings in the future?

children.comment:
The deposit option is grayed out because Commissions, markups, and Stripe payouts are based on where you legally reside. These features are currently only available in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Making sales won't change that — it's tied to residency, not activity, so the Stripe option won't appear just from selling.

Without Stripe connected, markup isn't available, since we're not able to hold funds on your behalf without a way to pay them out. So earnings won't quietly build up in the background for a later withdrawal.

You can still use Pro and all the Pro tools, and while availability on earning features can change over time, we can't promise if or when.

questions.title: whitelabel or custom domain or custom branding?

children.comment:
Your store lives at stickermule.com/yourname and appears in Sticker Mule search and feeds, with products featured in the marketplace at stickermule.com/marketplace. It also works as a standalone storefront, you drive traffic to yourself, and you can set it to private to hide it from search and feeds while keeping your store URL working.

On branding: you get a custom banner, avatar, display name, bio, and a link to your own site. No custom domain today.

On fees: no platform fee, no listing fee, no monthly cost beyond Pro. Each product has a base price, you set a markup, and the difference is yours. Earnings go to your bank through Stripe five days after an order ships, with no minimum payout.

With Notify, you pay per send. There's no subscription and no list-size pricing — email is $0.005 per recipient and SMS is $0.03, with a $5 minimum per campaign.

reviews.title: Solid Platform with Great Potential but Needs Improvements!
reviews.comment:
I wanted to give this product a full 5 tacos, but after thoroughly exploring 99% of the Tier 3 features, I found a few limitations and shortcomings. My primary goal for purchasing this LTD was to sell digital products and subscriptions, and it shows promise in those areas. It’s also a great addition to my portfolio of cart platforms like WooCommerce, ThriveCart, and SamCart. I truly hope the team delivers on their roadmap and remains around for the long haul.

PROS ("The Good")
*Digital Products & License Keys: The standout feature for me is the ability to sell digital products and generate license keys for activation. While manual activation may be required on my end, I'd appreciate clarity on tracking and managing license keys—especially for refunds and deactivations.

*Customizable Landing Pages & Checkout Features: Offers a variety of options for customization, including the ability to add images, videos, and custom code.

*CNAME/Custom Domain Setup: Straightforward setup with clear instructions.

*Coupon Functionality: Ability to create fixed or percentage-based discounts is a nice touch.

CONS ("The Bad & The Ugly")
*White Label Limitations: The CNAME feature falls short when Zylvie branding is still visible in headers and footers. Charging extra to remove branding, especially for top-tier LTD buyers, is a poor practice.

*Outdated Design: The landing page design options feel stuck in the 90s, with limited flexibility.

*Brand Management Restrictions: There’s no option to delete and replace brands while preserving the inventory limit.

*Domain Linking Issues: After setting up a custom domain, the "view my store" link in the admin dashboard still points to the Zylvie site, leading to an error page.

*Cart Abandonment Disclosure: This valuable feature is locked behind Tier 5, which isn’t made clear in the AppSumo listing.

*Affiliate/Referral Limitations: Affiliate links can only be created manually via email invitations. The absence of a self-service affiliate registration (like Partnero) is a missed opportunity.  Please refer to these screenshots: Refer to these screenshots: https://prnt.sc/yV4P7Wfbiii9, https://prnt.sc/KP_seoF5uvnq

*Coupon Date Errors: Coupons with specific start and end dates arbitrarily change when revisited for editing.

*In the cart, when customer selects the bump offer, the cart total does not add up correctly.  There's also no option to "continue shopping" or go back to the home page if customer wants to select more products.  

*Sales Volume Uncertainty: It's unclear what happens after reaching the stated $1 million sales cap for Tier 3 users.

Final Thoughts
This platform is a strong and cost-effective alternative to other cart platforms, but there’s room for significant improvement. Addressing the issues outlined above could make this a 5-taco contender.

children.comment:
Hi there,

We definitely appreciate that you took all the time to provide us with both sides of the coin.

That's a very long list of cons (of course, can't fault your honesty), some are valid, some are a matter of opinion, and a few I also dare say are user error/misunderstanding.

All feedback are taken seriously and will be worked on.

It's really a lot, so I won't address all of them here, plus it goes beyond the scope of a review response (and AppSumo are quite strict about what goes into the reviews section).

But one thing I will definitely respond to here and now:

"Gating features"  (cart abandonment) -- We submitted a change to the deal terms to AppSumo like 3 weeks ago now. We're trying our best here. I can't force AppSumo to move faster as there's a queue even just to fix 1 typo, let alone add features.

This is how it works behind the scenes: It's not like we can just edit the deal page independently. We submit a form, they decide "in their discretion" if they want to approve it, and then they make the change. This can take weeks -- hell, in this case, this HAS taken weeks.

Now. The reason we offer cart abandonment to Tier 5 users for now is not because we hate Tier 4 users and below. Let's make that absolutely clear; we love all of our users.

It's because cart abandonment is a very new featurre, and it's also computationally expensive just to run the cronjob 24/7 to monitor the status of carts and send out emails reliably and in a timely manner.

We want to know we can handle the load and volume on our servers before we open the feature up to all. You can double-verify this with anyone in IT or any LLM out there.

Plus it's our Tier 5 users who have the most sales volume right now, so the data gathering will be most efficient with them.

questions.title: Hi, I'm based in Egypt and want to sell digital products to customers in the US and Europe.
questions.comment: Hi, I'm based in Egypt and want to sell digital products to customers in the US and Europe. Since Stripe isn't available to me, can your platform accept customer payments and allow me to withdraw my earnings through Payoneer, similar to Amazon or Etsy? If not, what payment and withdrawal options are available for Egyptian sellers?

children.comment:
Hi — thanks for the clear question.

Zylvie doesn’t work like Amazon or Etsy. We’re not a merchant of record, so we don’t collect customer payments on your behalf or pay you out via Payoneer (or any other withdrawal method).

Instead, you connect your own payment processor, and customer payments go directly to that account:

1. Stripe — best option if available where you’re based, but Stripe isn’t available in Egypt.

2. PayPal — if you can receive business payments with a PayPal account in your situation, you can connect it to Zylvie and get paid that way. Availability and receiving rules in Egypt depend on PayPal’s own policies, so please confirm with PayPal that your account can receive commercial payments.

3. Manual / off-platform payments — you can enable this at checkout and instruct buyers to pay you outside Zylvie (e.g. Wise, bank transfer, Payoneer, etc.). You then mark the order as paid so fulfillment runs. This is the most flexible option if Stripe/PayPal don’t work for you, but payment collection is handled by you, not by Zylvie.

So in short: we can’t accept payments for you and withdraw to Payoneer. For Egyptian sellers, the realistic paths are PayPal (if your account can receive) and/or manual payments with your own payout method.

If you want, tell me whether PayPal receiving currently works for you in Egypt and I can suggest the cleanest setup.

With thanks,
Jay

questions.title: Hi - I have a few questions :)
questions.comment:
1. Can visitors register for a new customer account on my website?
2. Can customers log in to their existing account?
3. Is there a "Forgot Password" or password reset feature?
4. Can customers change their password after creating an account?
5. Does every customer receive a permanent account after purchasing?
6. Can customers log in later and see all of the products they have purchased?
7. Does each customer have a personal library that grows as they purchase additional products over time?
8. Can access be controlled on a per-product basis so customers only see the products they own?
9. Can this be embedded into an existing website rather than replacing it?
10. Is there a customer dashboard or "My Library" page where users can access their purchased products?
11. Is there a limit to the number of customer accounts that can be created?

children.comment:
Hi there,

1. No — visitors don’t sign up for a customer account on the storefront. The account is created automatically when they buy, using the email they enter at checkout.

2. Yes. They go to your store’s /account page (“My purchases”), enter that same email, and we send a login link.

3. There’s no buyer password, so there’s no “Forgot Password” form. Requesting a new login link to the purchase email is how they get back in.

4. Same as #3 — buyers don’t set or change a password.

5. Yes. After a purchase they can return anytime via /account + the email they used at checkout.

6. Yes. That page lists the products they bought.

7. Yes. Later purchases on the same email are added to the same library.

8. Yes. They only see products they own.

9. Checkout, yes — embed it inline or as a pop-up on your existing site. You don’t have to replace your website. The library itself is a page on your Zylvie store (or custom domain), not an embeddable widget.

10. Yes — that’s the /account “My purchases” page.

11. No limit on buyer/customer accounts.

Hope this clarifies!

With thanks,
Jay

**Regarding your Tier 2 allocation:**
The Tier 2 plan includes **10,000 credits per month**, which is equivalent to **up to 2,000 leads**, since each lead consumes 5 credits.

If you're using the SmatLeads default API, it's possible to consume your allocated credits relatively quickly. However, if you're using your own API key, you can spread your searches across the month without being restricted by our shared API's daily safeguard.

So, your Tier 2 allocation is still available as specified—we are not reducing the 10,000-credit allowance.

You also mentioned averaging **60–120 leads per search** and approximately 650 leads per month. **Regarding the filters:**
The filters are functional, but we understand that some of them may not behave exactly as expected if the search parameters aren't configured correctly. That's precisely why we offer **free onboarding sessions for new users**. This is also mentioned in the welcome email sent after signup.

We'd much rather spend 15–20 minutes helping your team configure the searches correctly than have you spend hours fighting with the platform.

**Regarding your unanswered support request:**
We're sorry to hear that you feel your message went unanswered. Since you've already established contact with our support team, the quickest route would normally be to continue on that existing support thread. We've also checked our support channels, and we don't currently see any unanswered tickets or emails from your team. It's possible your message didn't reach us successfully.

reviews.title: Average platform with good potential, but severely outdated data
reviews.comment:
It is a pretty average B2B contact database when it comes to the interface and core features. It does what it claims to do, but the major drawback is the data freshness. Based on my usage, the records seem to be at least four years old.

In the B2B space, data that old leads to high bounce rates and requires way too much manual verification before you can actually use the leads. I am giving it 2 tacos because the platform itself is a data platform but UI functions fine for what it is, but you should be prepared to spend significant time cleaning and verifying your lists if you rely on this tool.

reviews.title: Yes! Love this Leads App! Only 1 New Feature that is Needed
reviews.comment:
I love this app! Purchased Tier 2 to get the email outreach included. The leads are accurate, easy to grab, and simple to organize within the app. 

The only feature missing is the ability to import emails directly from our lists when setting up an outreach email campaign, instead of having to import from a CSV file.

Why? This way, the system could notify us if a person from the list has already been included in the campaign. When uploading CSV files, if the same email appears in multiple files and outreach campaigns, we can’t easily identify duplicates.

Can you connect our lists directly to Outreach Campaigns? If this feature is possible, it would greatly help ensure we’re not sending duplicate emails or including contacts in more than one campaign unintentionally.

reviews.title: Good Idea, But the Data Quality Didn't Meet My Expectations
reviews.comment:
I purchased two lifetime licenses because I was looking for a reliable B2B lead database. After using the platform, I don't feel it delivers enough value for my use case.

The first issue I encountered was my account only showing 50 monthly credits instead of what I expected based on my purchase. I'm still waiting for clarification on that.

I also attempted to contact support using the email address that sent my login PIN, but my email was returned as invalid.

From a product standpoint, my biggest concern is the data quality and search experience.

When searching for businesses in the United States, there is no option to filter by state, even though state/province filters are available for other countries. For anyone targeting specific U.S. markets, this makes prospecting much more difficult.

I also noticed that many search results pointed to the same company website, which made the results feel repetitive rather than providing unique prospects.

Most importantly, I was searching for medical practices and expected to find owners, CEOs, or decision-makers. Instead, many of the contacts were simply employees. For B2B outreach, having a list of staff members instead of the people who make purchasing decisions significantly reduces the value of the platform.

I'm not expecting any lead database to be 100% perfect, but I do expect accurate, actionable data that helps me reach decision-makers. Right now, I don't feel the product delivers on that expectation.

I hope the team continues improving the database, search filters, and overall data quality because the concept has potential. If those areas improve, I'd be happy to revisit my review.

reviews.title: Stay away.
reviews.comment:
I bought 3 codes and yesterday I pulled 10,445 contacts in the venture capital and private equity industry and all of them passed their email verification. 

Then I moved them into Bitscale (a Clay alternative) and removed the ones that had no website, had no email, had a team size of 0 and that were not in the venture capital and private equity industry (there were still some strays from other industries). 

After those filters, I had 1,235 leads left. 
Then I verified the remaining emails with Reoon and I had 389 leads left. 

So quick math, that's 3.724% of the contacts I pulled and I hadn't even applied an ICP filter yet. 
So if you buy, just understand you'll probably only get about 3% of the leads the plan states and even if the credits renew, the lists don't. 

I can't pull a fresh set of 10k leads in the vc & pe industry because the platform ran out of new contacts.

I'd stay away but at least be aware.

reviews.title: I'm willing to up my tacos to 5, but I don't think this does what I thought it did...
reviews.comment:
NOTE: I've got an appointment to talk with Tom next Friday, and that may adjust my feelings strongly, so Take this review with a grain of salt...

At a glance, this SEEMS to be far more manual than I expected... I've been using LinkedIn (and *ahem* potentiallyusingautomationtoolsthatareagainsttheirtermsofservice *ahem*) for the better part of 15 years at least, if not longer.  I've used a lot of different tools - some cost $1500 to $3500/year to use, some were more in the $29/month range, some were appsumo purchases that didn't pan out (and one upsold me into a 5 year contract that I'm ready to part ways with) which lead me to Fl*w, which seemed like an elegant solution...

On the face of it, it looked like it would do full campaigns for me, but it seems more like an "automatic send connection requests" platform that does NOT subsequently keep up the conversation, going, but which requires manual effort to monitor connections.

What I WANT is a system that lets me manage different profiles DIFFERENTLY, and set up structured campaigns for DIFFERENT THINGS.

EG: 

1 campaign is my main account, connect me with my clients, help me make introductions, and give them a reason to book with me.

1 campaign is my assistant, who invites people to my podcast who are a good fit

A third campaign for my other assistant who promotes Service X.

Each campaign can START with connection request, then once they connect AUTOMATICALLY read their page, know the best strategy that fits that person, and reaches out once they connect to invite them to move forward.  

In an ideal world, it'll connect with my X and Email at least, and also reach out to them too via those channels, potentially in a multi-step process. 

However, I think Fl*w is far simpler than that, alas. 

It seems that you pull a group of contacts, they all go into a bucket, with one outreatch message with mabye SOME personalization, but...then... you have to monitor it daily to see who has connected, then you have to TRIGGER IT  to write a follow up manually... 🫩

Ain't Nobody Got Time For That... or again at least that's how I feel currently (almost feels like a bait-and-switch)... but it has great reviews, so I'm willing to be patient... so... stay tuned... I'll give it a week or so, and a conversation with the founder to make sure I'm using it in the optimal way...

Hey there! Thanks so much for sharing this, and there are some really good points here.

I just wanted to clarify that the full automation you're looking for is entirely available. We just need to do a better job of making it clearer in our documentation and onboarding.

I'm looking forward to our call on Friday, when I can take you through some personal use cases where I have Claude running a daily scheduled task to check my daily connections, send them an automated, personalised intro message, and manage my follow-ups if they don't reply after a certain amount of time - this is in addition to having it feed leads into other tools like Apollo, HubSpot, Instantly and more. 

Again, really appreciate you sharing this. Again, we can do a much better job of making this clearer when you sign up. Looking forward to our call on Friday because I think you'll be pleasantly surprised by the full capabilities of what you can do :)

reviews.title: My Reason using FlowAI
reviews.comment:
I see ChooseFlow.ai as a practical option for anyone who relies heavily on LinkedIn for finding clients or booking sales meetings. What I like most is that it brings lead search, outreach campaigns, follow-ups, inbox management, and AI-assisted replies into one place. That can save a lot of time compared with using several separate tools.

In my view, it is best suited to consultants, agencies, and sales teams that run consistent outreach campaigns. The unified inbox and campaign tools make it easier to stay organized, especially when handling several prospects at once.

The main downside is the price. Starting around $79 per month, it may feel expensive for someone who only sends occasional LinkedIn messages. I would also recommend testing account connections and lead-search quality during a trial before fully committing.

Overall, I think ChooseFlow.ai is a strong choice for serious LinkedIn outreach. It is not the cheapest tool, but its all-in-one approach can be worth it if it helps you run campaigns more efficiently and keep conversations from slipping through the cracks.

questions.title: Does flow support RTL languages like Hebrew or Arabic?
Difference between tier 1 and tier 2?
questions.comment:
Hi Tom, deciding between Tier 1 and 2:

 1. Does "1 campaign" let me run 2 lists (different audiences/DMs) at once, or is that Tier 2?

 2. Besides accounts/campaigns, do tiers differ on database exports, team logins, agents, API/MCP or daily limits?

3. Is 15 invites/day the cap on all tiers? Higher with Sales Nav? Message/visit limits?

4. Can I upgrade T1 to T2 later by paying the difference? Only while the deal is live?

5.Will webhooks, voice notes, workspaces and post-engagement import come to all tiers free?

6. Can I import a CSV of my own LinkedIn URLs straight into a campaign, and is there any limit on imported leads?

children.comment:
Hey there,

Thanks for reaching out, and great questions.

1. Yes, you can run both at once. There's no cap on campaigns or lists on any tier, so two audiences on one account is fine.

2. The tiers only differ on LinkedIn accounts (1, 3 or 10). Agents, API/MCP, the lead database and safety limits are the same on every tier. 

3. Every account gets 15 connection requests, 80 profile visits and 80 post likes a day, whatever the LinkedIn seat. We keep DMs to about 30 a day. Need a higher invite cap? Just ask support or update them in Settings if you have Sales Nav or a Recruiter licence

4. Yes, you can upgrade through AppSumo and pay the difference while the deal is live.

5. New core features roll out to every tier at no extra cost.

6. Yes. Import a CSV of LinkedIn URLs straight into a list, with no limit on leads.

Hope that helps! Any other questions in the meantime, please just holler :)

Bye for now,
Tom

questions.title: How does Flow protect LinkedIn accounts from restrictions or bans?
questions.comment:
Hi Tom,
I've read your explanations about private IPs, human-like pacing and the 15 daily connection-request limit. However, LinkedIn explicitly prohibits unauthorised automation, regardless of activity limits.

Before purchasing, could you clarify:

1. Beyond mimicking human behaviour, what safeguards prevent account restrictions or permanent bans?
2. Have any users experienced warnings, temporary restrictions or reduced visibility, even without permanent bans?
3. Can I use Lead Finder, AI-generated replies and the inbox without automated LinkedIn actions?
4. Does connecting my account alone introduce any risk?
5. If an account is restricted despite following your recommended settings, what support or remedy do you provide?

Protecting my established LinkedIn account is my primary concern.

Thanks!
Marcus

children.comment:
Hey Marcus,

Thanks for reaching out, and great questions. 

Good news is that Flow does a lot more than pace things like a human. The limits are hard limits. Flow enforces them itself. Each account also gets its own dedicated IP, and Flow runs in the cloud, so there's no browser extension.

We've never had an account banned for anyone using Flow. Now and then, LinkedIn asks someone to verify their ID, mostly when their profile isn't verified. 

And yes, you can use Flow without any automated LinkedIn actions. The Flow Database is our own 300M+ profiles, so searching it doesn't touch LinkedIn at all. 

If you search LinkedIn itself, that does run through your account. Nothing goes out unless you start a campaign or send a message.

Connecting your account is just a normal LinkedIn sign-in, so LinkedIn sees it like a new device. Having LinkedIn's verification badge on your profile really helps here.

If anything did happen, you'd have Darren and me working with you directly. We can lower your limits as far as you like too.

Nobody can honestly promise zero risk, as LinkedIn never shares exactly what it checks. What we can promise is that Flow is built to keep your account safe first.

Hope that helps! Any other questions in the meantime, please do holler :)

Bye for now,
Tom

questions.title: Hi, I'm looking to replace Woodpecker with Warmy.
questions.comment:
Do emails stop being sent automatically to anyone who has genuinely replied? How about out-of-office responses? How does it handle these?

Also, does Warmy have sentiment tagging for replies so that these can be filed accordingly - interested, OOO, not interested etc..

Looking forward to your reply

children.comment:
Yes: in WarmySender a genuine reply stops that contact's sequence automatically, an out-of-office doesn't, and every email reply is tagged by sentiment so you can file it.

Genuine replies stop the sequence. "Stop on reply" is on by default in every campaign. When someone writes back, their remaining follow-ups are cancelled, and any pending LinkedIn, Instagram or WhatsApp steps for that person stand down too, so nobody gets chased on another channel after answering. The campaign keeps running for everyone else. A reply asking to be removed ("unsubscribe", "remove me") is handled as an opt-out, and the address goes onto your suppression list.

Out-of-office and other auto-replies don't. WarmySender recognises automatic responses from the hidden markers mail systems add, and from common out-of-office wording in English, Dutch, German, French and Spanish. Holiday notices, "we've received your ticket" acknowledgements and "no longer monitored" messages don't stop the sequence or count toward your reply rate, so follow-ups go out as scheduled. If one is ever filed the wrong way, relabel it and the contact continues from their next unsent step. Nobody gets the same email twice.

Every reply is tagged. In the inbox, each email reply is labelled automatically as Interested, Neutral, Negative, Auto-Reply / Out of Office or Spam, and you can change any label by hand. The Needs Reply view leaves out auto-replies and spam, so it only shows people who are waiting on you. If you run WarmySender through an AI agent, it can pull replies by label too, for example "show me today's Interested replies."

Details: https://warmysender.com/documentation/how-stop-on-reply-works-across-channels and https://warmysender.com/documentation/does-an-out-of-office-reply-stop-my-campaign. Questions: https://warmysender.com/support

The WarmySender team

questions.title: API
questions.comment: Hello, a quick question: can I send emails via the API from the mailboxes I’ve created, and is there a sending limit? Thanks.

children.comment:
Hi marlonfer, thanks for the question!

Yes. Through the API you can send from the mailboxes you've connected: create a campaign with your email steps, choose which of your mailboxes send it, add your contacts and launch it. Our scheduler then sends each email from those mailboxes. You can do the same from an AI agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent) in plain language. There's no endpoint that fires a single one-off email instantly: every email goes through the scheduler, so your mailboxes stay within safe pacing.

Sending limits:
- Your tier's monthly email allowance (shown on the deal page), spread evenly as a daily cap of about one thirtieth of it per day.
- A daily limit per mailbox and a gap between sends, plus the sending days and hours you pick for the campaign.

Sent emails, replies and stats can be read back through the API or webhooks.

If you get stuck setting it up: https://warmysender.com/support
